issue.title: Tighten the universal machine: O(t log t) time and O(s) space overhead
issue.body:
Posted by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` (Claude) at Samuel's direction. **Tighten the universal machine.**

**Today.** `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Universal/ResourceBound.lean` bounds the simulation of `J` steps of a machine with description size `B` by **time `O(B⁵ · J³)` and space `O(B² · J)`**. That is about `J²` per simulated step. It is worse even than the naive approach of packing all simulated tapes onto one tape (`O(t²)` total), and far from the textbook bounds:
- time `O(c_M · t log t)` (Hennie–Stearns; Arora–Barak Thm 1.9);
- space `O(c_M · s)`.

**Why it matters**
- **Hierarchy theorems.** Their gaps inherit this overhead. A tight universal machine gives the standard `DTIME(t) ⊊ DTIME(t log t · ω(1))` and a tight space hierarchy.
- **Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity (#798).** Invariance with a small time slack, and Liu–Pass in its "every `t ≥ (1+ε)n`" form, need a near-linear simulation. The design's decision D1 works around the current overhead by counting steps of the described machine.
- **Every diagonalization argument:** Ladner, constructibility, the oracle and relativization results.

**Milestones**, each landing on its own and tightening the stated bounds of the existing theorems:
1. **U1: per-step cost independent of `t`.** Bring the per-step cost down from `O(J²)` to `O(poly(B) · J)` at worst, the naive tape packing, so time is `O(poly(B) · t²)`. Bring space down to `O(poly(B) · s)`.
2. **U2: same tape count, linear overhead.** When the simulated machine uses no more tapes than the universal one, give a **linear-time** simulation, `O(poly(B) · t)`. This is the case time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity needs.
3. **U3: Hennie–Stearns.** Simulate an arbitrary machine in `O(poly(B) · t log t)`, the classic oblivious-tape construction.
4. **U4: tighten the consumers.** Restate the hierarchy theorems, Kolmogorov invariance and the other diagonalization results with the new bounds. Statements only get stronger, and in-repo clients are updated, with no aliases.

**Constraints**
- **Upstream.** The machine is vendored from `crei/tidy-universal`. Credit Christian Reitwiessner's construction, keep the upstream relationship in `UPSTREAM.md`, and decide with the Machines owner whether this is a new construction or a revision of the vendored one.
- **Plain-first.** Public resource statements are plain; the construction's internals may use tidy, as allowed in the machine layer (#456 rule).
- **Sequencing with the sweep.** The construction is in the allowlisted machine layer. Coordinate with S1 (#671) and the Machines sweep to avoid double conflicts.
- **Owner:** `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8` (Machines). A design note comes first: the encoding of simulated tapes, how heads are tracked, and whether U2 is a separate machine or a specialization.

issue.title: perf(tactic): reduce repeated local-call matching in polytime search
issue.body:
## Scope

Reduce the elaboration cost of the `polytime` (and, where shared, `ppt`) Aesop search without changing which goals it proves.

Observed in `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.lean`: every structural rule is wrapped in `withoutLocalCall`/`withLocalCall`, each of which re-runs the full local-routine matcher (`applyKnownCall`: a scan of the local context, `reduce` + `isDefEq` per candidate, and a trial application) only to test applicability. For one goal this matcher can run up to nine times (four guarded fast rules, four alternatives, and the rule itself).

Planned work:
1. Measure: profile `polytime`/`ppt` call sites in the library and the tactic tests (heartbeats / wall time per call) to establish a baseline.
2. Replace repeated applicability tests by a cheap, side-effect-free pre-check (head match on local certificates) and/or a per-goal cache, keeping the existing alternative structure.
3. Look for further generality gaps exercised by existing clients (e.g. constructor/projection decomposition, fold encodings) and add regression tests for any new case.

## Completion criteria

- No change to tactic semantics on the existing library: all six checks pass.
- Measured before/after numbers on the tactic test modules and representative heavy clients, recorded in the PR.
- Regression tests in `ComplexityTests/` for any added capability.
- Theorem-index assessment recorded (expected: no impact).

issue.title: doc(authors): credit Karn Seth on rational hitting and binary integer files
Quality program: a uniform, library-wide overhaul of interfaces, structure and documentation
issue.body:
**Program charter.** Samuel has made a sweeping, uniform improvement of the library's quality the top priority, run top-down by both coordinator fleets. The governing idea, from #577: reduce what a future user, developer or agent has to know, remember or repeat.

**Leads.** `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` (program lead and integration) with `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8` (co-lead). Areas are not owned or locked (Samuel, 2026-10-24): any agent may work in any area, staying aware of ongoing plans, issues and PRs, and any independent, non-authoring reviewer may approve any PR. See §4.

## 1. The standard (applied identically everywhere)
An area is in great shape when:
1. **Surface:** public declarations are the intended API. Helpers are `private`, and `@[expose]` appears only on definitions whose bodies downstream proofs must unfold.
2. **Statements:** user-facing statements use mathematical notions and plain computability (#456). No proof machinery (tidy certificates, internal encodings of proofs) appears in them, and names follow Mathlib conventions.
3. **Placement:** no duplicates, narrow topic modules, and consumers import what they use rather than hubs (#569, #572).
4. **Documentation:** module docstrings' "Main definitions/results" match the real public API; every public definition and headline theorem has a docstring; the area has a Verso guide chapter (#585).
5. **Proofs:** hygiene passes (CI-enforced), there are no avoidable outliers in proof length or heartbeats, and certificates are proved with automation rather than plumbing.
6. **Tests:** nonvacuous checked examples of the area's main API, which the guide reuses.

## 2. Instruments (one shared report, built first)
`scripts/quality_report.py` extends #584's measurement into per-area metrics:
- public declarations never referenced outside their module;
- public declarations referenced only by tests;
- tidy predicates in public statements;
- public definitions without docstrings;
- module-doc drift (listed names that are missing or private, and public API that isn't listed);
- duplicate statement types;
- hub fan-out;
- proof-length outliers.

The baselines go in the table below, and the report reruns after each area PR.

## 3. Phases (bottom-up through the import graph)
- **Phase 0 (now):** land the #456 wave (#559, #560, #568); build the report (#584); land the standard (a short CONTRIBUTING section); get decisions D1 and D2.
- **Phase 1, Foundations (structural changes first, because they ripple):** hub splits (#573 List, then BitString and PMF), Foundations/*, Probability, Languages/Probabilistic.
- **Phase 2, in parallel by area:** the areas in the table, each running the same loop: report → surface → statements → placement → docs and guide chapter → proofs → report.
- **Phase 3, upstream:** areas that meet the standard submit their stable foundational layers to cslib (1,826 modules are `candidate`, 17 `submitted`).

## 4. Areas
| Area | Modules | Checklist issue | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Foundations (Data, Combinatorics, BooleanAnalysis, other) and Probability, Languages | 316 | #614 | 1 |
| Machines and the polynomial-time calculus (Computability/Machines, Probabilistic) | 283 | #592 | 2 |
| Complexity classes, problems and reductions (Computability/Complexity, PCP, Communication, DecisionTree, QueryComplexity, TreeEval) | 446 | #610 | 2 |
| Circuits (Computability/Circuit) | 402 | #590 | 2 |
| Crypto (Crypto/*, incl. FHE) | 160 | #593 | 2 |
| Logics (FirstOrder, Propositional) | 98 | #596 | 2 |
| WordRAM and Algorithms | 158 | #591 | 2 |

**Area rules** (revised 2026-10-24 at Samuel's direction; areas used to have owner fleets).
- **No locks, only awareness.** Nobody locks an area or a set of files. Before starting and while working, read the ongoing plans, issues and open PRs, and make sensible choices: build on in-flight work, avoid needless duplication, and coordinate in the relevant issue or PR when changes overlap. Most overlap is cheap; rebase on what lands first. AGENTS.md task claims, with the three-hour takeover rule, say who is working on what. They are not a reservation.
- **Review by any independent reviewer.** Any non-authoring reviewer's verdict at the exact head is sufficient. A delta review confirms that every earlier change request is resolved. No area reserves a "final verdict" to a particular coordinator, though anyone may still request changes.
- PRs stay within one area where practical and stay reviewable (roughly ≤40 files). Cross-area interface changes are announced on this issue before editing; the rest of the library adapts in the same PR, or the change keeps compatibility.

## 5. Decisions for Samuel
- **D1, removing public helpers.** AGENTS.md requires a deprecated alias for every removed public name. Applying that to thousands of helpers no outside module uses would defeat the purpose. **Proposal:** a helper never referenced outside its module, and not named in a module doc, an abstract, the guide or the README, may become `private` without an alias. Anything with outside references keeps the existing compatibility rule. The measurement is evidence, not an automatic rule; a reviewer still judges intended API.
- **D2, capacity.** **Proposal:** quality comes first. Feature work continues on the current FHE tasks (#528, #543) and Sigma protocols (#581) with one worker each, and new feature work must meet the standard from day one.

Progress, baselines and per-area status are tracked in this issue's table, updated by the leads.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/MAC): add message-length schedule msgLen, reindex, and composition helpers
issue.body:
## Summary

Supplier PR 1 for #1000 Step 2 ([confirmed design comment 6398462902](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1000#issuecomment-6398462902)).

To authenticate ciphertexts of an IND-CPA symmetric cipher whose ciphertext length `ctLen n > n` exceeds the security parameter `n` (since zero-expansion deterministic encryption cannot be IND-CPA), `MACScheme` needs to support a polynomial-time message-length schedule `msgLen : ℕ → ℕ` together with schedule reindexing (`MACScheme.reindex`) along any strictly monotone polynomial-time schedule `ℓ : ℕ → ℕ`.

### Main additions (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/GeneratorReindex.lean` and `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean`)

1. **`MACScheme.msgLen` generalization with backward-compatible defaults:**
   - Adds `msgLen : ℕ → ℕ := fun n => n` and `msgLen_polyTime : ComputableInPolyTime msgLen encUnary encUnary := by exact ComputableInPolyTime.id'` to `MACScheme`.
   - Updates `MACScheme.verify_sign`, `eufCmaGame`, `eufOneTimeGame`, `sufCmaGame`, and the unique-tag equivalence hypotheses to use `M.msgLen n` instead of `n`.
   - Because `msgLen` defaults to `fun n => n` and `msgLen_polyTime` defaults via `autoParam` to `ComputableInPolyTime.id'`, **every existing `MACScheme` user compiles unchanged**:
     - `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean` (`prfMAC`, `PseudorandomFunction.sufCma_prfMAC`, `PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC`, `PseudorandomFunction.oneTimeEUFCMA_prfMAC`)
     - `ComplexityTests/Crypto/MAC.lean` (`echoPrfMAC`, `twoTagMAC`, `randomizedTagMACScheme`)
     - `ComplexityTests/ProgramCertificateDiagnostics.lean` (`testMACScheme`)
2. **Public plain-first composition certificates on `MACScheme` (`#733` item 2):**
   - `MACScheme.computableInPolyTime_msgLen_comp`: `M.msgLen_polyTime.comp hn`
   - `MACScheme.isPPTOn_keyGen_comp`: `M.keyGen_ppt.preprocess hn`
   - `MACScheme.isPPTOn_sign_comp`: `M.sign_ppt.preprocess (hsk.prod hmsg)`
   - `MACScheme.computableInPolyTime_verify_comp`: `M.verify_polyTime.comp (hsk.prod (hmsg.prod htag))`
3. **Schedule reindexing (`MACScheme.reindex`) reusing `GeneratorReindex.parameter`:**
   - `GeneratorReindex.parameter_apply_of_strictMono`: for `StrictMono length`, `GeneratorReindex.parameter length (length n) = n`.
   - `MACScheme.reindex M ℓ hℓ : MACScheme` with `(M.reindex ℓ hℓ).msgLen n = M.msgLen (ℓ n)` and `(M.reindex ℓ hℓ).keyGen n = M.keyGen (ℓ n)`.
   - `MACScheme.reindexForger ℓ adversary : Forger` using `GeneratorReindex.parameter ℓ m` and its `IsOraclePPT` certificate `MACScheme.isOraclePPT_reindexForger`.
   - Exact game identities `MACScheme.sufCmaGame_reindex`, `MACScheme.eufCmaGame_reindex`, `MACScheme.eufOneTimeGame_reindex` and security transfers `MACScheme.SUFCMA.reindex`, `MACScheme.EUFCMA.reindex`, `MACScheme.OneTimeEUFCMA.reindex` (using `Negligible.comp_of_polynomial_bound` with `hmono.tendsto_atTop` and `hmono.id_le`).

### Source pins and verbatim quotes

Pinned to Boneh–Shoup v0.6, Section 6.1 (*Message integrity: definition and basic properties*, printed pp. 217–219):

- **Definition 6.1** (printed p. 217):
  > Definition 6.1. A MAC system I = (S, V ) is a pair of efficient algorithms, S and V , where S is called a signing algorithm and V is called a verification algorithm. Algorithm S is used to generate tags and algorithm V is used to verify tags.
  > • S is a probabilistic algorithm that is invoked as t ←$ S(k, m), where k is a key, m is a message, and the output t is called a tag.
  > • V is a deterministic algorithm that is invoked as r ← V (k, m, t), where k is a key, m is a message, t is a tag, and the output r is either accept or reject.
  > • We require that tags generated by S are always accepted by V ; that is, the system must satisfy the following correctness property: for every key k and every message m,
  > Pr[V (k, m, S(k, m)) = accept] = 1.
  > As usual, we say that keys lie in some finite key space K, messages lie in some finite message space M, and tags lie in some finite tag space T . We the say that I is defined over (K, M, T ).

- **Attack Game 6.1 and Definition 6.2** (printed pp. 218–219):
  > Attack Game 6.1 (MAC security). For a given MAC system I = (S, V ), defined over (K, M, T ), and a given adversary A, the attack game runs as follows:
  > • The challenger picks a random key k ←$ K.
  > • A queries the challenger several times. For i = 1, 2, . . ., the ith signing query is a message mi ∈ M. Given mi , the challenger computes a tag ti ←$ S(k, mi ), and then gives ti to A.
  > • Eventually A outputs a candidate forgery pair (m, t) ∈ M × T that is not among the signed pairs, i.e.,
  > (m, t) ∉ {(m1, t1), (m2, t2), . . .}.
  > We say that A wins the above game if (m, t) is a valid tag on m under k; that is, if V (k, m, t) = accept. We define A’s advantage with respect to I, denoted MACadv[A, I], as the probability that A wins the game. Finally, we say that A is a Q-query adversary if A issues at most Q signing queries.
  >
  > Definition 6.2. We say that a MAC system I is secure if for all efficient adversaries A, the value MACadv[A, I] is negligible.

*Library specialization:* At unary security parameter `n`, the finite message space `M` is specialized to `msgLen n`-bit strings (`msg.length = M.msgLen n`), defaulting to `n`-bit strings (`msgLen := fun n => n`).

### Framework friction

Previously `MACScheme` hardcoded `msg.length = n` in `verify_sign` and `out.1.1.length == n` in `eufCmaGame`, `eufOneTimeGame`, and `sufCmaGame`, which prevented `MACScheme` from authenticating expanding ciphertexts of length `ctLen n > n` at security parameter `n`. Adding `msgLen : ℕ → ℕ := fun n => n` and `MACScheme.reindex` resolves this without breaking any existing caller.

### Abstract impact

None — no files in `ComplexityAbstracts/` are modified or affected.

### Verification

- `lake build Complexity.Crypto.Computational.GeneratorReindex Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MAC ComplexityTests.Crypto.MAC ComplexityTests.ProgramCertificateDiagnostics` (0 errors, 0 warnings)
- `python3 scripts/check_changed_files.py --base origin/main --no-build-check`
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
- `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py --no-build-check` (1289 public tidy statements, 0 new)

Refs #1000, #723, #733

issue.title: perf(polytime): make fun_prop fail fast and cover common plain/tidy mixes
issue.body:
Follow-up from #456 (found while migrating classes in #557): automation around the plain `ComputableInPolyTime` (#554) has three rough edges that make migrated proofs worse than they should be.

1. **Slow failure.** `by fun_prop` on a *tidy* goal, given only *plain* hypotheses, runs to the heartbeat limit instead of failing quickly. This happened in `Classes/WPP/Robustness.lean` and `Classes/WPP/TwoSided.lean`. Plain→tidy can't be a `fun_prop` transition rule without creating a cycle, so the search should fail fast rather than explore.
2. **Tidy-only rules don't accept plain hypotheses.** Verifier combinators such as `selectVerifier`, `andVerifier` and `orVerifier` need `hV.tidy` or `mem_X_iff_tidy.mp` first.
3. **Plain goals `fun_prop` can't decompose.** Two arithmetic or test shapes still need `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`: the threshold `3 * (k a * 2 ^ q n)` in `inter_mem_SBP_of_mem_BPP`, and the `sharpTest` verifier in `Classes/Toda.lean`.

**Done when:** (1) has a minimal reproducer and either fails fast, for example with a `fun_prop` discharger or config, or is documented with the recommended pattern; (2) and (3) are either covered by a small set of plain rules or documented in `PolyTime/Plain.lean`, each with a test. Before/after examples should come from the files above.

issue.title: docs(site): keep the API docs under the Pages size limit and fix broken internal links
issue.body:
Found while publishing the API docs (#583, https://www.cslib.io/complexitylib/):
1. **Site size.** The generated site is 973 MB uncompressed, 90.6% of the 1 GiB Pages limit: 807 MB on Oct 18, 962 MB on Oct 22. Mathlib pages are 570 MB; `Complexity` pages about 106 MB, Std 94 MB, Init 74 MB, the search index 48 MB, Lean 46 MB. #583's size check fails before deploying above 1 GiB, and Pages then keeps serving the previous deployment, so overflow means stale docs rather than an outage. Measured quick wins: `DISABLE_EQUATIONS=1` saves about 48 MB, and dropping Lean/Std/Lake modules the library never imports saves about 37 MB. Together that's roughly two more weeks. The lasting fix: link dependency declarations (Mathlib, Lean core, Std) to their official doc sites instead of hosting them, if doc-gen4 supports it; otherwise host elsewhere. Investigate and recommend.
2. **Broken internal links.** 404 links on 323 library pages point at pages that don't exist, e.g. `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.html` → `Cslib/Tactic/PolyTime.html`. That suggests a module-to-namespace mapping assumption (the `Complexity.` → `Cslib.` prefix convention), worth fixing at the source or in the doc config.

**Done when** the site has durable headroom (or alternative hosting), and the internal link check is clean. Available.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/Homomorphic/Leveled): unified base reduction and exact concrete security loss (#1104)
issue.body:
## Summary

Implements the unified concrete-security reduction and advantage loss for leveled bootstrappable encryption from Item 3 of #1104 ([Gentry2009], Section 2, Theorem 4, p. 171, up to a constant factor).

Previously, `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Security.lean` proved asymptotic IND-CPA security (`Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.indCPA_keyGen` and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.indCPA_scheme`) via a three-reduction triangle inequality summing the advantages of `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.linkAdversary` (at `false` and `true`) and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.zeroLinkAdversary` scaled by `(dyadicSize (2 * budget n) : ℝ≥0) * dyadicSize (capacity n)`. Because that bound referenced three distinct base reductions rather than a single base IND-CPA adversary, it did not package Gentry's Theorem 4 into one explicit reduction algorithm.

This PR replaces the three-reduction triangle inequality with a single unified base IND-CPA reduction `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.leveledAdversary` that samples two fair coins `(first, second)` plus dyadic indices via `sampleDyadicCoin (depth n) 1` and `sampleDyadicCoin (capacity n) 1`:
- On branch `(false, false)`, it runs `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.linkAdversary` on `publicKeyGame E adversary false`.
- On branch `(false, true)`, it runs `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.linkAdversary` on `publicKeyGame E adversary true` with its two challenge messages swapped (`swapLeveledChoice`), which negates the signed acceptance gap in the challenge world so the intermediate all-zero-link hybrids `publicKeyChainHybrid n (2 * budget n) 0` at `false` and `true` cancel identically in `gap_leveledAdversary`.
- On branch `(true, false)`, it runs the zero-key / challenge-experiment step of `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.zeroLinkAdversary` at the dyadically sampled index `(i, j)`, outputting `false` if `depth n + 1 ≤ i ∨ capacity n ≤ j` (`rejectLeveledChoice`) so out-of-range indices have equal acceptance probability in both challenge worlds and acceptance gap scales by `(dyadicSize (depth n) : ℝ)⁻¹ * (dyadicSize (capacity n) : ℝ)⁻¹`.
- On branch `(true, true)`, it outputs `false` immediately (`rejectLeveledChoice`), contributing zero to the signed advantage gap.

### Main definitions and theorems

* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.tagLeveledChoice`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.swapLeveledChoice`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.rejectLeveledChoice`: two-bit branch tagging and message swapping for `leveledAdversary`.
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.leveledAdversary`: the unified two-stage base IND-CPA reduction.
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.isPPT_leveledAdversary`: uniform native strict-PPT certificate for `leveledAdversary` when `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.keyGen`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.encrypt`, `adversary`, `depth`, and `capacity` are polynomial-time in the unary security parameter.
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.eval_leveledAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.succProbability_leveledAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.gap_leveledAdversary`: exact distributional and signed acceptance-gap identities for `leveledAdversary`.
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.advantage_game_eq_leveledAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.advantage_scheme_eq_leveledAdversary`: exact unsigned advantage identity for this dyadic reduction
  $$\mathsf{Adv}_{\text{leveled}}(\mathcal{A}) = 4 \cdot \mathrm{dyadicSize}(2 \cdot \mathrm{budget}(n)) \cdot \mathrm{dyadicSize}(\mathrm{capacity}(n)) \cdot \mathsf{Adv}_E(\mathrm{leveledAdversary}).$$
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.advantage_game_le_mul_leveledAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.advantage_scheme_le_mul_leveledAdversary`: polynomial loss bound with factor $16 (2 \cdot \mathrm{budget}(n) + 1)(\mathrm{capacity}(n) + 1)$, matching Gentry's Theorem 4 loss $\ell(d + 1)$ up to a constant factor.
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.computableInPolyTime_secretWidth`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.isPPT_leveledAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.advantage_leveled_eq`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.advantage_scheme_le`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.advantage_leveled_le`: instantiation at the leveled GSW parameter family in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/GSW/FullyHomomorphic.lean`.

### Abstract impact (`gsw-fhe`)

No change to `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/GSWFHEAbstract.lean` in this PR: the `gsw-fhe` abstract states asymptotic `INDCPA` for the leveled GSW scheme, whereas the concrete-security reduction and advantage loss remain at the library surface (`Leveled.Security` and `GSW.FullyHomomorphic`).

## Source Statement & Notation Mapping

- **Source & exact locator:** Craig Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices*, STOC 2009, Section 2, Theorem 4, p. 171.
- **Verbatim source statement ([Gentry2009, Section 2, Theorem 4, p. 171]):**
  > Theorem 4. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algorithm that breaks the semantic security of $\mathcal{E}^{(d)}$ with advantage $\epsilon$. Then, there is an algorithm $\mathcal{B}$ that breaks the semantic security of $\mathcal{E}$ with probability at least $\epsilon / \ell(d + 1)$, for $\ell$ as in Definition 4, and time $\mathrm{poly}(\ell, d)$ times that of $\mathcal{A}$.
- **Scope and comparison with Gentry's Theorem 4:**
  - *Advantage loss (up to a constant factor):* Because strict-PPT coin sampling draws dyadic power-of-two indices (`dyadicSize m ≤ 2 * (m + 1)`) and our De Morgan circuit compilation doubles the depth budget to `2 * budget n` NAND layers, `leveledAdversary` achieves exact factor `4 * dyadicSize (2 * budget n) * dyadicSize (capacity n) ≤ 16 * (2 * budget n + 1) * (capacity n + 1)` rather than Gentry's `ℓ(d + 1)`.
  - *Running-time claim:* `isPPT_leveledAdversary` proves that `leveledAdversary` is a uniform strict-PPT adversary (`Encryption.Adversary.IsPPT`) whenever the depth budget `budget`, secret width `capacity`, base encryption scheme, and leveled adversary `adversary` are polynomial-time in the unary security parameter, rather than formalizing a multiplicative runtime bound `time(B) ≤ poly(ℓ, d) · time(A)`. The exact constant and multiplicative runtime formulation remain open in #1104.
- **Notation & convention mapping:**

| Source (`[Gentry2009]`, Theorem 4, p. 171) | Lean statement (`advantage_scheme_eq_leveledAdversary` / `advantage_scheme_le_mul_leveledAdversary`) |
|---|---|
| Security parameter $\lambda$ | `n : ℕ` encoded in unary (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.encUnary`) |
| Base bootstrappable encryption scheme $\mathcal{E}$ | `E : Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme` (instantiated with `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.scheme`) |
| Leveled scheme $\mathcal{E}^{(d)}$ at depth budget $d(\lambda)$ | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.scheme D budget` (with $2 \cdot \text{budget}(n)$ transition layers for NAND-augmented compilation) |
| Secret-key bit length $\ell(\lambda)$ | `capacity : ℕ → ℕ` (instantiated with `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.GSW.DepthParameters.secretWidth`) |
| Leveled CPA adversary $\mathcal{A}$ and advantage $\epsilon(\lambda)$ | `adversary : Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.Adversary` (`adversary.IsPPT`) and `Cslib.Crypto.Game.advantage` on `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.game (Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.scheme D budget).keyGen (Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.scheme D budget).encrypt adversary` |
| Unified base CPA reduction $\mathcal{B}$ | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.leveledAdversary E (fun n => 2 * budget n) capacity adversary` (`isPPT_leveledAdversary`) |
| Advantage loss factor (Gentry: $\ell(d + 1)$) | Exact dyadic factor `4 * Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.dyadicSize (2 * budget n) * Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.dyadicSize (capacity n)`, bounded above by `16 * (2 * budget n + 1) * (capacity n + 1)` |

Refs #1104

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`

- `python3 scripts/check_changed_files.py`

issue.title: refactor(api): add plain polynomial-time computability with tidy bridges
issue.body:
Milestone M1 of #456: a plain polynomial-time predicate that definitions and public statements can use, with tidy bridges so proofs keep the existing automation.

**Scope**
- Define `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime f encIn encOut := ∃ t s : ℕ → ℕ, Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded t ∧ Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded s ∧ ComputableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength f encIn encOut t s`. This is the form both abstract bridges already use. It depends only on upstream cslib declarations, so put it in a new `-- upstream: candidate` module that could be submitted without `crei/tidy-universal`. The vendored `PolyTime.lean` must not grow.
- In the local companion `PolyTime/Plain.lean`, add bridges both ways: an iff with `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, plus one-step `.tidy` / `.of_tidy`-style shortcuts. Also record "polynomial time alone suffices" for a plain machine as a lemma. Names follow Mathlib conventions; propose them in the PR.
- Transport the basic closure API (identity, composition, pairing/`ite` as used by class proofs) and decide whether to `@[fun_prop]`-register the plain predicate. The design commitment is that computability predicates stay automatable. Show a before/after client: a public `ComputableInPolyTime` goal discharged directly, or through one bridge rewrite.
- Document the convention (M5): tidy notions are proof devices; definitions and public results use plain computability.

**Out of scope:** changing any class or reduction definition (M2 batches); plain space/`O` counterparts (M1b); switching the abstract bridges (waits for #497 to avoid conflicting with #497/#541).

**Done when:** the six gates pass, `ComplexityTests` covers the bridges and a nonvacuous client, and the M2 batches can start from this branch.

issue.body:
Addresses Item 3 of #884 (F2, F3, F9 `tableInstance`, and `getD_beq_self_eq_true_iff`).

### Summary of Changes

1. **Generic Certificate Verifier Pipeline (F2)**:
   - Defined `Cslib.MCSP.checkCertificate (accept : List Bool → Bool → Bool) (m S : ℕ) (w : List Bool) : Bool` in `Complexity/Computability/MCSP/NP.lean`, parameterizing certificate checking over the acceptance condition on circuit output.
   - Proved generic soundness `Cslib.MCSP.exists_circuit_of_checkCertificate`, completeness `Cslib.MCSP.exists_checkCertificate_append`, and polynomial-time verification `Cslib.MCSP.computableInPolyTime_checkCertificate`.
   - Added table-level polytime rule `Cslib.MCSP.computableInPolyTime_checkCertificate_table` generic over `encT : List α ↪ List Bool`, unifying polytime verification across truth-table encodings and making `MCSP.computableInPolyTime_tableVerifier` and `PartialMCSP.computableInPolyTime_tableVerifier` thin callers supplying only `haccept`.
   - Refactored `MCSP.verifier` and `MCSP.tableVerifier` to call `checkCertificate`, preserving definitional equality for `#print axioms` and `by decide` test coverage.
   - Replaced `PartialMCSP.verifier` and `PartialMCSP.tableVerifier` with calls to `checkCertificate`, eliminating duplicated circuit decoding, code checking, and enumeration logic across `MCSP/NP.lean` and `MCSP/PartialNP.lean`.
   - Added generic `getD_boundedBinaryValue_reverse_ofFn` deduplicating `tableValue_ofFn` and `tableEntry_ofFn`.

2. **PartialMCSP Embedding & Bounds (F3)**:
   - Defined `Cslib.PartialMCSP.toRaw : Instance ↪ List (Option Bool) × ℕ` and refactored `enc` and `encBinary` to factor through `toRaw.trans ...`.
   - Generalized bounds `two_pow_le_length_enc_of_encT` and `certLength_le_enc_of_encT` parameterized by `encT : ℕ ↪ List Bool`, inlining directly at callers and deleting dead wrappers.

issue.title: refactor(classes): define probabilistic, counting and hierarchy classes with plain computability
issue.body:
**Stacked on #554** (base `refactor/plain-polytime-545`); retarget to `main` once #554 merges.

Closes #547 (milestone M2b of #456).

`BPP`, `RP`, `ZPP`, `PP`, `SBP`, `MA`, `AM`, `SigmaP`, `PiP`, `SharpP`, `WPP` and `LWPP` now require their verifier (for `SBP`, `WPP`, `LWPP`: their threshold or target function) to be `ComputableInPolyTime` instead of `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`. This is refactoring of the definitional presentation, not new mathematics: the two predicates are equivalent (`computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime`), so each class is the same set. Every class is defined directly; there was no shared helper to change. Classes defined through these ones (`coRP`, `PH`, `GapP`, `UP`, `FewP`, `US`, `ModP`, `CeqP`, `SPP`, `AWPP`, `PWithSharpPOracle`) become plain with no textual change.

Every name is kept. `mem_X` is still the definitional unfolding, now plain, and each class gets `mem_X_iff_tidy` so a proof that composes machines switches with one rewrite. The class modules publicly import `PolyTime/Plain.lean`, so clients have `.tidy`, `.of_tidy` and the iff. Broken proofs in 46 other library files and 8 test files were fixed locally with `.tidy`, `.of_tidy`, `mem_X_iff_tidy` or `fun_prop`. The complement proofs of `BPP`, `SigmaP`/`PiP` and `SharpP.exists_two_pow_sub_mem` now close plain goals with `by fun_prop`.

**Public statements whose shape changed**
- The twelve definitions.
- `mem_BPP`, `mem_RP`, `mem_ZPP`, `mem_PP`, `mem_MA`, `mem_AM`, `mem_SigmaP`, `mem_PiP`, `mem_SharpP`: the machine hypothesis is now plain. Names are unchanged, so there are no deprecated aliases (as #547 specifies).
- New: `mem_X_iff_tidy` for all twelve classes, and `mem_SBP`, `mem_WPP`, `mem_LWPP` (`Iff.rfl`), which did not exist.
- The private `exists_inter_verifier` in `PH/Closure.lean` is now stated plainly.

**Limitations**
- **Left for M3.** 52 public theorems in `Classes/` still state membership or closure with tidy hypotheses or tidy right-hand sides. They remain valid. Examples: `mem_BPP_iff_forall_decidesWithErrorExponent`, `mem_RP_iff_forall_decidesWithOneSidedErrorExponent`, `mem_MA_iff_exists_forall_errorExponent`, `mem_AM_iff_forall_errorExponent`, `mem_SBP_iff_exists_pos_threshold`, `exists_SBP_gap_pow`, `mem_PP_iff_decidesByNonstrictMajority`, `SharpP.of_polyTime`, `SharpP.comp_mem`, `GapP.comp_mem`, most of `WPP/*` and `SharpP/{Aggregation,Products,Power}`. The same holds for `mem_UP` and `mem_FewP`.
- **Overlap with #546.** `P`, `NP` and `PolyTimeReducible` are still tidy here. Proofs that mix them with these classes therefore convert with `.tidy` or `.of_tidy`, for example `RP_subset_NP`, `SigmaP_one`, `P_subset_SigmaP_zero`, `P_subset_BPP`, `NP_subset_PP`, `BPOp_P`, `mem_NP_iff_exists_SharpP` and the `PolyTimeReducible.mem_*` lemmas. Whichever PR lands second removes those conversions.
- **`fun_prop` friction** (relevant to #554):
  - `fun_prop` cannot use a plain hypothesis for a tidy goal. Tidy-only rules (`selectVerifier`, `andVerifier`, `orVerifier`) therefore need the hypothesis converted first. In `WPP/Robustness` and `WPP/TwoSided`, such a call hit the heartbeat limit instead of failing quickly.
  - Two plain goals are still beyond plain `fun_prop` after #554's `trans`/`fst'`/`snd'`: the threshold in `inter_mem_SBP_of_mem_BPP` and the `sharpTest` verifier in `Toda.lean`. They use `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`.

No other bridge changed. `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes.

issue.title: feat(counting): prove LWPP reduction closure and multiple-target robustness
issue.body:
## Summary

Implements polynomial-time many-one reduction closure for `LWPP`, unary-indexed target normalization, and finite-family multiple-target robustness for `WPP` and `LWPP` (#26).

### Main additions
- **[`Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Int/Binary.lean`](Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Int/Binary.lean)**:
  - `Int.size_natAbs_prod_le`: binary length bound on the magnitude of a list product of integers.
  - `@[fun_prop] theorem Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.intBin_prod`: polynomial-time list product of binary integers (`encList encIntBin → encIntBin`), proved via `foldlWith_of_bounded_growth`.
- **[`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/WPP.lean`](Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/WPP.lean)**:
  - Subclass containments: `UP_subset_LWPP`, `UP_subset_WPP`, `coUP_subset_LWPP`, `coUP_subset_WPP`, `FewP_subset_LWPP`, `FewP_subset_WPP`.
  - Remaining Boolean closures: `diff_mem_WPP`, `symmDiff_mem_WPP`, `diff_mem_LWPP`, `symmDiff_mem_LWPP`.
  - Finite multiple-target robustness (`mem_WPP_of_finset_targets`, `mem_LWPP_of_finset_targets`): if a `GapP` function takes `0` outside `A` and one of a fixed finite family (`s : Finset ι`) of nonzero polynomial-time binary-integer targets on `A`, then $\prod_{i\in s} f_i - \prod_{i\in s}(f_i - g) \in \mathsf{GapP}$ witnesses membership with single nonzero target $\prod_{i\in s} f_i$.
  - Unary-indexed target normalization (`mem_LWPP_of_polyTime_index`) and many-one reduction closure (`PolyTimeReducible.mem_LWPP`): if a `GapP` function takes `0` outside `A` and $f(k(a))$ on `A` for a nonzero unary-input target $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and unary polynomial-time index $k : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$ bounded by $p(|a|)$, multiplying the gap by the filtered product $\prod_{i \le p(|a|),\, i \ne k(a)} f(i)$ normalizes the target to $\prod_{i \le p(|a|)} f(i)$, yielding reduction closure for `LWPP` by taking $k(a) = |r(a)|$.
- **[`ComplexityTests/WPP.lean`](ComplexityTests/WPP.lean)**:
  - Nonvacuous tests (including length-altering reductions and signed multiple-target families) and `#print axioms` guards for all headline theorems.
- **Documentation & Theorem Index**:
  - Updated [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md), Section 4.15 ("Wide counting gaps") of [`paper/sections/randomness.tex`](paper/sections/randomness.tex) pinned to `f2409a4a13c9e6b67a22ede3eb3ef963ddf9401c`, and rebuilt [`paper/main.pdf`](paper/main.pdf).

### Scope & Limitations
- Uses the library's verifier-based `#P` and `GapP` definitions; nondeterministic counting-machine characterizations and oracle lowness of `WPP`/`LWPP` are not claimed.
- `mem_WPP_of_finset_targets` and `mem_LWPP_of_finset_targets` cover fixed finite target families (`s : Finset ι`), while `mem_LWPP_of_polyTime_index` normalizes a polynomial-time unary-computable target index $k(a)$; polynomial-cardinality target families where the accepting target index is not polynomial-time computable from the input (`Poly-LWPP = LWPP`, `Poly-WPP = WPP`) remain open in `ROADMAP.md`.

### Validation
All six checks in `scripts/check.sh` passed on `0180e770`:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

issue.title: feat(stateful): certify adaptive RAM controllers and charged calls
issue.body:
Stateful operation budgets previously left client control flow, initialization, and argument delivery outside the RAM execution. This adds fixed-code `Refines` certificates with charged sequencing, branches, pure results, preparation and initialization, plus a uniform word-valued RAM-time predicate. Named certificates are reusable through `stateful`, `polytime`, and the demonstrated `fun_prop` registration.

The complete adaptive client reuses the existing bounded stack: push/pop the input, observe the answer, and push/pop one if it was zero. One fixed nine-register program returns `max n 1`, leaves its stack empty, and takes exactly 49 instructions for zero or 29 otherwise, including setup, argument writes, dispatch, control and halt. Every input fits its stated logarithmic numerical-magnitude width threshold. Standard input placement is the machine convention; arbitrary continuation synthesis, general allocation, Turing-machine simulation, and vEB remain subsequent work.

Closes #280. Follow-up to #278 and #160; supports #273.

issue.title: refactor(api): add plain counterparts of tidy space, big-O and FPT computability
issue.body:
Milestone M1b of #456. The remaining tidy resource notions get plain counterparts with the same bound parameters, so space and FPT statements can be restated without tidy machines. Each one is built on upstream `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`, with time and space as independent bounds.

| Tidy (proof device) | Plain (for definitions and public statements) |
|---|---|
| `ComputableTidilyInO f encIn encOut T S` | `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInO f encIn encOut T S` |
| `ComputableTidilyInSpace f encIn encOut S` | `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInSpace f encIn encOut S` |
| `ComputableTidilyInPolySpace f encIn encOut` | `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolySpace f encIn encOut` |
| `ComputableTidilyInFPTTime f encA encB κ` | `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInFPTTime f encA encB κ` |

Each bridge is an equivalence with the **same** bounds, `computableInX_iff_computableTidilyInX`. #545's shortcuts are mirrored: `ComputableInX.tidy`, `ComputableInX.of_tidy` and `ComputableTidilyInX.computableInX`. The linear overhead of the tidy normal form disappears because every notion is up to constants. The core lemma is `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableTidilyInO`. A machine within time `t` and space `s` whose values fit in `s` is tidy within `O(t)` and `O(s)`. Without that lemma the normal form's time `2t + 3s + c` would mix the two bounds. The lemma first replaces `s` by `min s (k t + k)` (`space_linear`), so each bound grows only by a constant factor.

**Placement.**
- `MultiTape/ResourceBounds.lean` holds the three plain definitions. It imports only upstream cslib, like #545's `MultiTape/PolyTime.lean`.
- The bridges are in companion files `Complexity/{BigO,InSpace,PolySpace}/Plain.lean`, following `PolyTime/Plain.lean`. No vendored file changed.
- `ComputableInFPTTime` and its bridges are in `Parameterized.lean`, a local candidate file and not a vendored one. They sit beside `FPTReducible`, so #549 can switch that definition.

**Design choices to check.**
- `ComputableInO`, `ComputableInSpace` and `ComputableInPolySpace` also bound the length of `encOut (f a)` by the space bound, as their tidy counterparts do. This is what gives the same-bound equivalence with tidy. For `ComputableInO` and `ComputableInSpace` it departs from the textbook convention (Arora–Barak Ch. 4, Papadimitriou §2.5) and from `ComputableInLogSpace`, which charge only the work tapes. At sublinear bounds they are therefore strictly stronger than transducer space. A test pins this: the identity is in `ComputableInLogSpace` but not in `ComputableInSpace` at `log n`. The docstrings say so and point to `ComputableInLogSpace` for transducer space. For polynomial space the condition is the usual polynomial-length requirement. The coordinator chose to keep the condition and document it.
- `ComputableInPolySpace` is `∃ (t : α → ℕ) (s : ℕ → ℕ), PolynomiallyBounded s ∧ ComputableInTimeAndSpace f encIn encOut t (s ∘ length ∘ encIn) ∧ output length ≤ s (length)`. It uses upstream `Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded`, not the vendored `PolyBounded` adapter. The time bound is arbitrary, as in `ComputableInLogSpace`.
- `ComputableInFPTTime` bounds time and space by `F (κ a) * (|encA a| + 1) ^ c`, as the tidy notion does, and has no output condition: the output never exceeds the time. The new `ComputesInTimeAndSpace.length_output_le` and `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.length_le` sit beside `space_linear` in `PolyTime/Plain.lean`. Bounding the space costs nothing: `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInFPTTime` gives fpt time from a time bound alone, mirroring #554's `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInPolyTime`.

**Limitations.** This PR adds no closure API and no `fun_prop` registration for the four plain notions; proofs reach the tidy combinators through `.tidy`/`.of_tidy`. #556 tracks the registration, starting with `ComputableInPolySpace`. It restates no class lemmas (`mem_PSPACE_iff_…`, `mem_FPT_iff_…`): that is M3. No class definition changes; that is M2.

**Tests.** `ComplexityTests/ResourceBoundsPlain.lean` covers both directions for each notion:
- Upstream's copy machine and almost-constant machine, which are not tidy, satisfy the plain notions. Through the bridges they give tidy certificates, membership of a problem in `PSPACE`, and membership in `FPT` for every parameter.
- Library certificates give plain ones, including plain deciders for `TQBF` (polynomial space) and `SAT` (fpt time in the number of variables).
- Negative checks show that the output condition has force: the identity is not in `ComputableInSpace` with a constant bound, or with a `log n` bound, although it is in `ComputableInLogSpace`.
- `#print axioms` guards cover the core lemma and the four iffs.

**Validation.** `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates at `cb551548` (base `main` @ `fe7bc578`).

**Abstract impact.** None. No existing definition or statement changes, and no selected abstract or bridge mentions these notions.

**AI disclosure.** Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5), worker `worker-claude-551-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Not yet independently reviewed.

Closes #551

issue.title: CCA security track: KEM–DEM, encrypt-then-MAC, Cramer–Shoup
issue.body:
Posted by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` at Samuel's direction (2026-10-25). Part of #640.

## Goal
Chosen-ciphertext security, in increasing difficulty. The steps can be claimed separately.
1. **KEM–DEM hybrid encryption:** #881 (Boneh–Shoup v0.6, Exercise 11.9 (modular hybrid construction)), open to claim.
2. **Authenticated encryption by encrypt-then-MAC:** CPA-secure symmetric encryption plus a strongly unforgeable MAC gives authenticated encryption, and hence CCA security. This reuses the MAC API, including strong unforgeability (#723), and the PRF and Carter–Wegman work.
3. **Cramer–Shoup:** CCA2-secure public-key encryption from DDH in the standard model. Use the hash-proof-system presentation (Cramer–Shoup 1998 and 2002) or Boneh–Shoup's chapter, whichever M0 pins. It reuses `DiffieHellman`, `DDH` and `ElGamal`.

## Process
For each step, post a short design (exact statements and source locators) before any Lean. Keep PRs reviewable, under about 1.5k lines. Security statements need certified efficient reductions with explicit losses (#733), and public statements are plain-first (#456).

issue.title: feat(crypto): multi-hop evaluation for fixed-key and leveled FHE (#1104)
issue.body:
## Summary

Implements Item 2 of #1104: multi-hop homomorphic evaluation (reusing evaluated ciphertexts as inputs to subsequent circuit evaluations) for both the fixed-key (circular-secure) scheme and the depth-budgeted leveled scheme ([Gentry2009], Section 2, pp. 171–172; [GentryHaleviVaikuntanathan2010]).

Previously, `Scheme.Correct` (`decrypt_evaluate`) took `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.FreshInputs` (`List.Forall₂ (fun bit c => c ∈ (ProbComp.eval (E.encrypt n pk bit)).support) bits inputs`), so it covered only a single evaluation call starting from freshly encrypted bits (`encrypt`). While the low-level layered evaluator (`Scheme.encryptedWires_evaluateLayers`) and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.FixedKey.evaluate_spec` on `main` already accepted `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.EncryptedWires`, the scheme-level `FixedKey` and `Leveled` interfaces did not expose two-hop composition theorems or level-indexed hop evaluation along the leveled key chain.

This PR adds multi-hop evaluation support for both constructions:
1. **Fixed-key (unbounded-depth self-loop) scheme (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/FixedKey/Correctness.lean`):**
   - Under the $i$-hop definition of [GentryHaleviVaikuntanathan2010], the fixed-key result is multi-hop for `(FixedKey.scheme D).evaluate` itself and is a thin corollary of the existing `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.FixedKey.evaluate_spec` on `main` (which already accepts `EncryptedWires` inputs):
   - `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.FixedKey.encryptedWires_of_evaluate`: any list of ciphertexts produced by `(FixedKey.scheme D).evaluate` on `EncryptedWires` inputs again satisfies `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.EncryptedWires ciphertextWidth n keys.2 midBits mids`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.FixedKey.evaluate_twoHop_spec`: evaluating a batch of inner circuits $c_i$ on `EncryptedWires` inputs via `(FixedKey.scheme D).evaluate` and feeding the resulting ciphertexts `mids` directly into an outer circuit `outer` via `(FixedKey.scheme D).evaluate` produces a ciphertext of width `ciphertextWidth n` that decrypts under `(FixedKey.scheme D).decrypt` to $outer(c_1(x_1), \dots, c_m(x_m))$.
2. **Depth-budgeted leveled scheme (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Basic.lean`, `Leveled/Correctness.lean`, `Leveled/PolyTime.lean`):**
   - `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop`: original adaptation providing a level-indexed family of evaluators (analogous to Gentry's sub-scheme $\mathcal{E}^{(\delta)}$ over part of the key chain on [Gentry2009, p. 171]). It evaluates a circuit `c` of depth at most `step` starting at key-chain level `offset` (consuming the sub-chain slice `[2 * offset, 2 * (offset + step)]` via `List.drop (2 * offset)`), stripping the leading input tags and tagging the output with `true`. At `offset = 0` and `step = budget`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_zero` shows `evaluateHop D n 0 budget = evaluate D n budget`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.ValidLinks.drop`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.encryptedWires_evaluateLayers_drop`, and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.encryptedWires_evaluateCircuit_drop`: generalize `Scheme.encryptedWires_evaluateLayers` to `layers.length + 1 ≤ keys.length` and lift layered and padded circuit evaluation to an arbitrary offset along a generated key chain. Both `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.encryptedWires_evaluateCircuit` and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluate_spec` are derived as the `offset = 0` specialization.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_spec`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.encryptedWires_of_evaluateHop`, `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_final_spec`, and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_twoHop_spec`: hop-by-hop invariant preservation using `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.EncryptedWires` on stripped ciphertext payloads (`inputs.map List.tail`), endpoint decryption when `offset + step = budget n`, and two-hop composition across `step₁ + step₂ = budget n`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.isPPTOn_evaluateHop`: uniform strict-PPT certificate for `evaluateHop`, from which `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.isPPTOn_evaluate` is derived at `offset = 0`.

### Existing notions considered

* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluate` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Basic.lean`): remains single-hop, starting at key index `0` and padding the compiled schedule to `2 * budget` layers so a single hop lands at the final endpoint key `2 * budget`. Multi-hop evaluation goes through `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop`, with the caller tracking `offset`; because the secret key retains only the two endpoint secrets (`0` and `2 * budget n`), only a hop ending at `offset + step = budget n` produces a ciphertext that `(scheme D budget).decrypt` can decrypt.
* `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.EncryptedWires` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Basic.lean`): reused directly on `inputs.map List.tail` at key `(chain.getD (2 * offset) ([], [])).2` in `evaluateHop_spec`, `encryptedWires_of_evaluateHop`, and `evaluateHop_final_spec`, avoiding any separate wrapper predicate.

### Abstract impact (`gsw-fhe`)

No change to `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/GSWFHEAbstract.lean` in this PR: the `gsw-fhe` abstract states scheme-level `Correct` for single-pass circuit evaluation, whereas multi-hop composition (`FixedKey.evaluate_twoHop_spec`, `Leveled.evaluateHop_spec`, `Leveled.evaluateHop_twoHop_spec`) is exposed at the library surface.

## Source Statement & Notation Mapping

- **Source & exact locator:**
  - Craig Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices*, STOC 2009, Section 2, pp. 171–172 (`[Gentry2009]`).
  - Craig Gentry, Shai Halevi, and Vinod Vaikuntanathan, *$i$-Hop Homomorphic Encryption and Rerandomizable Yao Circuits*, CRYPTO 2010, pp. 155–172 (`[GentryHaleviVaikuntanathan2010]`).
- **Source statement (paraphrase, not verbatim):**
  In [Gentry2009, Section 2, pp. 171–172], the leveled construction $\mathcal{E}^{(d)}$ chains level keys and sub-schemes $\mathcal{E}^{(\delta)}$ over parts of the key chain (note that Gentry indexes keys in reverse from $pk_d$ down to $sk_0$ with $\mathsf{Recrypt}$ stepping from $pk_i$ to $pk_{i-1}$, whereas this library indexes forward from $0$ to $2d$), and the self-loop modification reuses a single key pair $(pk, sk)$ across all recryption layers. [GentryHaleviVaikuntanathan2010] formalizes $i$-hop / multi-hop homomorphic encryption, in which outputs of homomorphic evaluations are fed as inputs to subsequent evaluations. In this PR, `FixedKey.evaluate_twoHop_spec` provides two-hop composition for `(FixedKey.scheme D).evaluate` itself (as a corollary of `FixedKey.evaluate_spec`), while `Leveled.evaluateHop` and `Leveled.evaluateHop_twoHop_spec` are original adaptations providing a level-indexed hop evaluator and two-hop composition over slices of the forward key chain.
- **Notation & convention mapping:**

| Source (`[Gentry2009]`, Section 2, pp. 171–172; `[GentryHaleviVaikuntanathan2010]`) | Lean statement |
|---|---|
| Two-hop evaluation in the fixed-key self-loop scheme ([Gentry2009, p. 172]; [GentryHaleviVaikuntanathan2010]) | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.FixedKey.evaluate_twoHop_spec` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/FixedKey/Correctness.lean`) |
| Intermediate ciphertext wire invariant under secret key $sk$ | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.EncryptedWires` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Basic.lean`) |
| Level-indexed hop evaluator (original adaptation of Gentry's sub-scheme $\mathcal{E}^{(\delta)}$ over a slice of the forward key chain, [Gentry2009, p. 171]) | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Basic.lean`) |
| Hop correctness from key $sk_{2 \cdot \text{offset}}$ to $sk_{2 \cdot (\text{offset} + \text{step})}$ (original adaptation) | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_spec` and `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_final_spec` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Correctness.lean`) |
| Two-hop leveled evaluation across $\text{step}_1 + \text{step}_2 = d(\lambda)$ (original adaptation) | `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.evaluateHop_twoHop_spec` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Correctness.lean`) |

Refs #1104

## Verification

- Hosted CI run: https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40230382255

issue.title: refactor(calculus): prove the canonical plain core directly
issue.body:
Plain PT/O/Degree/linear proofs now use canonical machine-witness rules directly, with existing entry modules reexporting their names. The included closure and primitive rules preserve generic encodings, complete callback contexts, independent time/workspace/output bounds and the distinction between charged O and uncharged time/space bounds. Superseded same-name plain wrappers are removed.

Both composition alternatives live in the raw-free core. Inner-first inference avoids the original Extraction test's 12,000-heartbeat timeout; outer-first inference remains available to standalone clients. One private Liu–Pass certificate explicitly composes arithmetic after that ordering exposed expensive search. Its program, statement and resource limit are unchanged. Claude's #1039 supplies direct binary-index lookup without expanding a binary index to unary.

**This is a core milestone; S1 and S4 remain open.** Decoder/Native/StepMachine field and API changes, strict PPT activation and the whole Crypto public-surface sweep are a subsequent delivery with their consumers. Tidy codec capability fields, four conversion bridges and framed-word conversion proofs remain transitional. No mirror attribute, derivation command, registry or compatibility alias ships here.

The sole allowlist addition is the exact `Internal/NormalForm.lean` path: five statements return bare normalized machines, rather than a high-level tidy calculus. [Boundary rationale](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6400704445). There is no wildcard or baseline increase; the final zero boundary remains #862's objective.

<details>
<summary>32 legacy plain wrappers still deferred</summary>

All names below are in `ComputableInPolyTime`:

- Basic: `bool_or`, `decide_eq'`, `beq`.
- List: `anyWithInput`, `bitsAppend`, `bitsTakeWithInput`, `encoding_length`, `filterWithInput`, `flatMapWithInput`, `headD`, `length_list`, `length_bits`, `bitsDropWithInput`, `length_bits_comp`.
- Nat: `unary_add`, `unary_eval`, `unary_mul`, `unary_pow`.
- Nat/Binary: `binary_bitwise`, `binary_and`, `binary_or`, `binary_xor`, `binary_and'`, `binary_or'`, `binary_xor'`, `binary_size`, `binary_min_unary`, `binary_min_unary'`, `binary_shiftRight`, `binary_shiftRight'`, `binary_mul'`, `binary_two_pow`.

`bits_encList_polyTime` and `trans_encList_polyTime` also retain raw construction dependencies. `PairEncoding`, `ListEncoding` and `OptionEncoding` still expose tidy linear capability fields. This is not a claim of transitive plain compliance.

</details>

**New definitions: existing notions considered.** The existing plain `ComputableInTimeAndSpace`, `ComputableInBigO` and `ComputableInDegree` remain the resource vocabulary. `ComputableInLinearTimeAndSpace` specializes the existing plain asymptotic notion. Internal normalization constructs witnesses for those notions; it does not define a competing efficiency model.

**Framework friction.** Unresolved intermediate encodings made composition search expensive. Keeping both inference directions in the shared core removes the need for client-local composition rules; the original budget and generic/missing-evidence controls remain. Deferred proof views and field migrations are tracked in #608/#862, with Crypto follow-ups on #733.

**Validation and review.** Current source is `6ec5c21090adb92f8f79d7fceff274297ba1eee6`, a normal merge of preserved130e6ae3 with actual main197b4098. [Exact-head refresh evidence](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/671#issuecomment-6400942827) records all six local gates and the normal freshness-aware ratchet passing on this merge; hosted checks and outside current-head confirmation remain required. [Consolidated local evidence and freshness-aware ratchet](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6400726286) records exact revisions and reused checks. [Earlier outside core review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6399594564), [resolved facade/registration findings](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6400324902) and [lookup approval](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1039#issuecomment-6399407467) retain their stated coverage limits. Final exact-head delta review and hosted checks are required; no earlier verdict approves this whole head automatically.

**Abstracts and source moves.** Selected headline statements, models and bounds are unchanged. Encoding/frame data and machine helpers move to their shared homes with original reexports; declaration-link origins change, and the abstract-origin fixture follows `Encodings.Nat.Bits` without weakening its assertion. No new rendered-PDF claim.

issue.title: Frontier track: quantum computation foundations, BQP ⊆ PP and the Grover/BBBV bounds
issue.body:
**Status: `available`.** M0 and M1 can be claimed now.

## Targets
- **BQP ⊆ PP:** L. Adleman, J. DeMarrais and M.-D. Huang (1997).
- **The Ω(√N) quantum query lower bound for search:** C. Bennett, E. Bernstein, G. Brassard and U.
  Vazirani (1997).
- **Grover's algorithm**, which meets that bound.

This is a new area for the library. It starts with finite-dimensional semantics, then connects to
the existing counting classes.

## What's already here
- **Counting classes:** GapP, PP and #P (`Classes/{Counting,PP,SharpP}`), which BQP ⊆ PP reduces
  to.
- **Query complexity:** `QueryComplexity/`.
- **Mathlib:** matrices, `Matrix.unitaryGroup` and inner-product spaces.

## Milestones
- **M0, design.** Circuit and measurement semantics, uniformity, gate set, and approximation
  conventions. Reuse CSLib or Mathlib quantum foundations if any exist.
- **M1, quantum circuits.** Finite quantum circuits with unitary semantics and measurement
  probabilities.
- **M2, BQP.** Defined with uniform families, plus amplification.
- **M3, BQP ⊆ PP** via a GapP representation of acceptance amplitudes, plus an abstract.
- **M4, the BBBV lower bound** (hybrid argument).
- **M5, Grover's algorithm** with its success probability.

## Rules for every track
These follow the frontier program umbrella issue and AGENTS.md.
- **M0 is a short design milestone,** posted as a comment here before any Lean. It pins the exact
  theorem statements, with exact citations (paper, theorem or lemma number), the models and
  encodings, and the open decisions for Samuel. Later milestones follow the design.
- **Faithfulness.** Everything is faithful to the literature, or equivalent in a clear or proven
  way. Label original lemmas. Never state more than is proved.
- **Plain-first (#456, #862).** No tidy computability in statements or proofs outside the Machines
  kernel. Lower the tidy baseline if counts move.
- **PRs.** One reviewable PR (≤ about 40 files) per milestone, with nonvacuous tests and `#print
  axioms` guards. Headline results get a curated abstract under the AGENTS.md rules.
- **Claims.** Claim a milestone with an `active` status comment before starting. Nothing is locked;
  rebase onto whatever lands first.

issue.title: Review findings: certificate registration, degree domain, and reuse fixes
issue.body:
Posted by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` (Claude) at Samuel's request. These are the triaged findings of two source reviews of `main` at `c139c8d` that Samuel ran with other agents. Both were source-only reviews, so the proposed Lean replacements have not been compiled. I re-checked the locations on `main`. Neither review found a false theorem. The recurring pattern: shared facts exist, but their visibility, placement or registration stops the next proof from using them.

## Defects (fix first)
**D1. `[program_certificate]` silently mishandles plain certificates.** Owner: `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8` (Tactic/PolyTime). **High priority**, and it bears on S1.
- **Where:** `Signature.lean:117` and `MAC.lean:141` register `verify_polyTime : ComputableInPolyTime …` with `[program_certificate]`.
- **What goes wrong:**
  - `efficiencyKey` (`Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean:71`) extracts the function argument only for `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`. For a plain certificate it takes the last argument, the output encoding.
  - The consumer looks up only tidy certificates, and the `fun_prop` branch skips the plain predicate.
  - So the registration is inert: it seems to work but contributes nothing.
- **Fix:**
  - Support plain certificates, by generating a tidy companion internally or by registering the existing bridge.
  - Give unsupported predicate shapes a useful error.
  - Add a regression: a plain certificate from another module, for a function that can't be solved by unfolding.

**D2. `MaxDegreeLE` and `width` treat infinite degree as 0** (`Circuit/Frontier/Multigraph.lean:112–115`). Owner: Circuit, Codex.
- `Set.ncard` of an infinite set is 0. With vertices `Bool` and edges `ℕ`, every edge joining `false` and `true`, the definitions give `MaxDegreeLE 0` and width 0.
- The finite layout endpoint assumes `[Finite V] [Finite E]`, but the exported definitions are unrestricted.
- **Fix:** require `[Finite E]` for the natural-valued API (smallest change), or switch to `encard` and an extended-natural width.

**D3. The quality report can certify an incomplete inventory as current.** Owner: `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`, as a follow-up to #649.
- `output_differences()` compares artifacts under `Complexity/`, `ComplexityTests/` and `ComplexityAbstracts/` but skips the root files (`Complexity.ilean`, …).
- `load_ileans()` builds the inventory from those roots' imports. So a stale root can pass the freshness check and silently drop modules. The review reproduced this.
- **Fix:** compare the root artifacts for all `REPORT_INPUTS` extensions, with a regression where only a root `.ilean` differs.

## Public API (plain-first, #456)
**A1. Crypto constructors take tidy hypotheses.** `OneWay.of_inversion_negligible` takes a tidy certificate and immediately converts it back. Its client `PRGToOneWay.lean:151` passes `hgenerator.polyTime.tidy`. `ComputationallyIndistinguishable.map` has the same problem.
- **Fix:** take `ComputableInPolyTime` and use `.tidy` inside the proofs.
- Owner: Crypto, Codex. This can land ahead of the Crypto sweep.

## Reuse and placement
- **R1. One shared `containsWithInput` certificate** beside `anyWithInput`/`countWithInput`, using `List.contains_eq_any_beq` and registered for automation. It replaces the private copies in `Signature.lean:142–155` and `MAC.lean:124–137`. Owner: Machines and Crypto, Codex.
- **R2. One public `splitAlternatingBlocks` certificate.** `PH/Closure.lean:107–122` and `BooleanHierarchy/Kadin.lean:124–139` have identical proofs, both private. Expose one with a plain statement and use it in both. Owner: Classes, Claude area, open to Jetski or Antigravity.
- **R3. WPP should use Mathlib.** `WPP.lean:342–368` and `WPP/Lowness.lean:463–489` duplicate `prod_map_ne_zero` and `mul_prod_filter_range_ne`. Use `List.prod_ne_zero`, `List.prod_map_erase` and `List.Nodup.erase_eq_filter`. Owner: Classes, Claude area, open to Jetski or Antigravity.
- **R4. One single-threshold change lemma.** It is proved privately in `WeightedThreshold/CapacityCircuit.lean:79–95` and again in `Menus.lean:238–258`. Put it beside `Foundations/Order/Changes.lean` and derive both uses with `ChangesAtMost.comp`, `comp_monotone` and `comp_antitone`. Owner: Circuit with Foundations, Codex, with Claude review of the Foundations part.
- **R5. One one-time-query proof.** `run_limitToOneQuery_eq_oneTimeSigningOracle` is about 95 lines, duplicated in `Signature.lean:579–674` and `MAC.lean:387–483`; #732 already hit a heartbeat limit because of it. Prove it once, parameterized by the callback and its length bound, in a small neutral oracle module. Owner: Crypto, Codex, under #710.
- **R6. Split Commitment from OneWayToPRG.** `Commitment.lean` publicly imports `OneWayToPRG` only for two OWF existence corollaries. Move those to `Commitment/OneWay.lean`. That cuts 74 local modules from the closure of Commitment, `GMW.Protocol` and `GMW.Simulator` (267 → 193). Owner: Crypto, Codex.
- **R7. Generic circuit counting in its own module.** `Iteration/CircuitCounting.lean` publicly imports `Iteration.Optimization`, but its first section is generic finite-signature counting. Narrow the import (closure 41 → 4 modules), then move the generic part to `Computability/Circuit/Counting.lean`. Owner: Circuit, Codex.

## Smaller follow-ups
- **S1.** Prove the stronger estimate `lowerBudget_description_margin` once, beside the budget definition, and derive `lowerBudget_description_exponent` from it (`CircuitCounting.lean:223`, `ModulusCounter.lean:170`). Owner: Circuit, Codex.
- **S2.** Fix the affine-disperser foundational doc: it says the affine-map/subspace correspondence is "not formalized here". Cross-link the proved direction (`IsAffine.toAffineMap`, the image-dimension theorem, the disperser bridge). Owner: Foundations, Claude area, open to Antigravity.
- **S3.** The `CollisionResistant.lean` introduction (lines 23–35) argues by hardcoding a collision. Scope that to a fixed accepted collision, as distinct from the length-indexed compression case, where a fixed pair works at most at one parameter. Documentation only. Owner: Crypto, Codex or the #678 author.

**Process:** claim each item here before working on it, one PR per item, with reviews per area ownership. Each PR follows the plain-first rule (tidy in proofs only) and the #733 friction note where it is a crypto PR.

issue.title: feat(parameterized): Buss polynomial kernel for vertex cover
issue.body:
## Summary

Proves that `VertexCover` parameterized by the target cover size `k` has a polynomial kernel (`Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover_hasPolyKernel`), strengthening `VertexCover_hasKernel` to an explicit polynomial bound `g(k) = 40 (k + 1) ^ 6` via Buss's kernel [BussGoldsmith1993, DowneyFellows1999, FlumGrohe2006, CyganEtAl2015].

- **Degrees and high/low partition (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Parameterized/VertexCover/BussKernel.lean`)**:
  - `VertexCover.Buss.degree G v`: counts distinct declared neighbours of `v` in `G`.
  - `VertexCover.Buss.high x`, `VertexCover.Buss.low x`: partition `G.distinctVertices` at `cap x = min n k`.
  - `VertexCover.Buss.mem_of_isHigh`: any declared vertex of degree `> k` belongs to every vertex cover of size `≤ k`, so `|high x| ≤ |S|` (`length_high_le_card`).
  - `VertexCover.Buss.active x`: low vertices with at least one low neighbour; `VertexCover.Buss.length_active_le` proves `|active x| ≤ k (k + 1)` whenever a cover of size `≤ k` exists.
- **Relabelling and isolated-vertex padding**:
  - When `cap x = k`, `|high x| ≤ k`, and `|active x| ≤ k (k + 1)` (`VertexCover.Buss.accept x = true`), the `m = |active x|` active vertices are relabelled to `0, …, m - 1` (`VertexCover.Buss.edges x`), the reduced target is `param x = cap x - |high x|`, and the vertex list `List.range (numVertices x)` where `numVertices x = min |low x| (m + param x)` pads with up to `param x` isolated vertices so that exact-size covers are preserved (`VertexCover.Buss.graph_mem_iff`, `VertexCover.bussKernel_mem_iff`).
  - Rejected instances (including `k > n`) map to `VertexCover.Buss.noInstance = (([], []), 1) ∉ VertexCover`.
- **Size and polynomial-time bounds**:
  - At most `k (k + 2)` vertices (`VertexCover.length_bussKernel_vertices_le`), at most `(k (k + 1)) ^ 2` listed edges (`VertexCover.length_bussKernel_edges_le`), and encoded length and output parameter at most `40 (k + 1) ^ 6` (`VertexCover.length_encode_bussKernel_le`, `VertexCover.isKernelization_bussKernel`).
  - Certified tidy polynomial-time computability (`VertexCover.computableTidilyInPolyTime_bussKernel`) using `fun_prop` and `polytime`.
- **Tests (`ComplexityTests/VertexCoverKernel.lean`)**:
  - Nonvacuous concrete tests for the high-degree rule, active relabelling, isolated-vertex padding on a star graph, rejection cases (`|high| > k`, `|active| > k (k + 1)`, `k > n`), and `#print axioms` guards.

## Headline declarations

```lean
def Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.bussKernel (x : Graph × ℕ) : Graph × ℕ :=
  if accept x then (graph x, param x) else noInstance

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.Buss.mem_of_isHigh {S : Finset ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ u ∈ x.1.1, ∀ v ∈ x.1.1, x.1.toSimpleGraph.Adj u v → u ∈ S ∨ v ∈ S)
    (hcard : S.card ≤ x.2) {v : ℕ} (hv : v ∈ x.1.1) (hhigh : isHigh x v = true) : v ∈ S

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.Buss.length_active_le {S : Finset ℕ}
    (hS : ∀ u ∈ x.1.1, ∀ v ∈ x.1.1, x.1.toSimpleGraph.Adj u v → u ∈ S ∨ v ∈ S)
    (hcard : S.card ≤ x.2) : (active x).length ≤ x.2 * (x.2 + 1)

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.bussKernel_mem_iff (x : Graph × ℕ) :
    bussKernel x ∈ VertexCover ↔ x ∈ VertexCover

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.length_bussKernel_vertices_le (x : Graph × ℕ) :
    (bussKernel x).1.1.length ≤ x.2 * (x.2 + 2)

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.length_bussKernel_edges_le (x : Graph × ℕ) :
    (bussKernel x).1.2.length ≤ (x.2 * (x.2 + 1)) * (x.2 * (x.2 + 1))

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.length_encode_bussKernel_le (x : Graph × ℕ) :
    (encPair encGraph encNat (bussKernel x)).length ≤ 40 * (x.2 + 1) ^ 6

@[fun_prop]
theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.computableTidilyInPolyTime_bussKernel :
    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime bussKernel (encPair encGraph encNat) (encPair encGraph encNat)

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover.isKernelization_bussKernel :
    IsKernelization (encPair encGraph encNat) Prod.snd VertexCover bussKernel
      fun k => 40 * (k + 1) ^ 6

theorem Cslib.Complexity.VertexCover_hasPolyKernel :
    HasPolyKernel (encPair encGraph encNat) Prod.snd VertexCover
```

## Automation notes (`fun_prop` / `polytime`)

1. **Compositional `Graph.adjBool` rule**: `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_adjBool` is stated on uncurried `((Graph × ℕ) × ℕ)`. Adding the compositional `@[fun_prop]` wrapper `computableTidilyInPolyTime_adjBool_comp` for `fun c => (G c).adjBool (u c) (v c)` allowed `fun_prop` and `polytime` to discharge `degree`, `isActive`, and `edges` directly.
2. **Mixed `encUnary`/`encNat` equality and output coercion**: When a helper is `@[fun_prop]`-registered with output encoding `encUnary` (such as `cap : Graph × ℕ → ℕ`, `param : Graph × ℕ → ℕ`, or `List.range` producing `encList encUnary`), `fun_prop` does not automatically insert `unary_to_binary` (or `map unary_to_binary`) when comparing against an `encNat` value in `decide (cap x = x.2)` or when packaging into an `encNat` / `encList encNat` output in `graph` and `bussKernel`. Minimal reproducing goal:
   ```lean
   example (f : α → ℕ) (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc encUnary) :
       ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f enc encNat := by fun_prop -- fails without unary_to_binary.comp
   ```

## Validation

No Lean MCP server was available in this session; iterated with targeted `lake env lean` / `lake build` and ran `./scripts/check.sh` once at the end:

- `lake build --wfail --iofail`: passed
- `lake exe mk_all --check`: passed
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`: passed
- `lake lint`: passed
- `lake exe lint-style`: passed
- `lake exe checkInitImports`: passed
- `python3 scripts/build_paper.py`: built `paper/build/main.pdf` cleanly at `a437d35a7e69181e1b712801ac86a60684776928`

## Theorem-index assessment and remaining limitations

- Updated `paper/sections/completeness.tex` to remove the limitation that Buss's kernel is not covered from the existing `Kernelization and parameterized vertex cover` entry and added a dedicated entry `Buss's polynomial kernel for vertex cover` pinned to `29c6c5e0ed7b97de51a4cb18276f3a2b72b07036`.
- Updated `ROADMAP.md` in the fine-grained/parameterized complexity row and the search/parameterized complexity bullet.
- Remaining limitations: crown-decomposition and LP-based $O(k)$-vertex kernels for Vertex Cover, and the computable-$g$ variant of `IsKernelization`, are not covered.

Closes #270

AI assistance: Antigravity agent (Claude and Gemini), worker `agy-worker-f29e46b2` / `agy-worker-f29e46b2/buss-kernel`. Requesting independent correctness, API, and theorem-index review from a coordinator.

issue.title: feat(tm2): compile multi-tape machines to finite stack machines
issue.body:
Closes #602.

Compile every fixed finite-state deterministic binary multi-tape machine to an actual finite-alphabet Mathlib `FinTM2`. The direct two-stack simulation handles bounded input heads, two-sided blanks, the final halting action, output order, and complete canonical `haltList` cleanup. For `k` work tapes it proves time `n + (k + 1) * (t + 1) + o + 3` and total stack length at most `n + s + o` at every target step, including initialization, cleanup and padding after halting.

`computableInPolyTime_iff_tm2` and `mem_PSPACE_iff_tm2` establish the resource equivalences under the original binary encodings, with finite alphabets on every stack and no computable-inverse assumption. The space transfer has no polynomial runtime assumption. General functions require polynomial output length, already included in `ComputableInPolySpace`; storing the input adds linear space. The forward space overhead remains polynomial.

Validation: `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2 scripts/check.sh` passed all six repository gates, including the global and named axiom audits. `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp` also passed. [Independent agent review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/654#issuecomment-6377328692) covers the final revision.

Selected abstract assessment: no impact on statements, catalogue, bridges or rendering; no PDF review needed. Documentation records the proved comparisons and remaining space-convention limits.

AI assistance: Codex implemented and checked the development, with independently delegated Codex agent reviews of semantics, API quality, resources and the final plain-API integration. This is agent review, not human approval. Existing tape-proof source credit is preserved. Coordinator review requested.
