issue.title: perf(tests): evaluate materialized circuits and drop slow ppt searches
issue.body:
Refs #622. This is a test-only PR: six of the seven slow test modules named in #622 drop by 80–93%, and no library module changes.

**Circuit tests (WordRAM/Algorithms, #591).** `BatchLookup`, `Routing`, `KeyedSort`, `DuplicateFlags` and `BatchOr` spent 90–98% of their time interpreting their exhaustive `#eval` checks. `Line.mapWires` and `Circuit.comp` store wires as composed closures, so compiled code re-resolves the whole wire-map chain on every read, in every evaluation. On the padded `batchLookupCircuit`, one `evalVector` call took 369 ms; on a copy with stored wires it took 15 ms.
- The new helper `ComplexityTests/CircuitMaterialize.lean` rebuilds a circuit with each line's wires and its outputs in `Vector`s. It proves `materialize_eq : materialize c = c`.
- The exhaustive checks evaluate `materialize (theCircuit …)` with the library's own `Circuit.evalVector`.

**`Crypto.ZeroKnowledge` (Crypto, #593).** Three `ppt` calls cost about 92.7M heartbeats each, roughly 10 s apiece. All three closed `IsPPTOn _ encBits (fun p => Prod.fst <$> GMW.runTwoRound …)` with the local `hrun` certificate already in context. Each becomes `exact hrun.map (by fun_prop)`, at about 20k heartbeats.

**What each test still proves.**
- **Circuit tests:** every input set, table, padding and empty-dimension case, gate count, weighted cost and `#guard_msgs` expectation is unchanged. The checks still exercise the library circuits, through a copy proved equal to each one.
- **`ZeroKnowledge`:** the two `ZeroKnowledgeProof` nonvacuity instances, the Naor and GMW concrete checks, and all six `#print axioms` guards are unchanged.
- **Coverage lost:** `ZeroKnowledge` no longer exercises the `ppt` tactic on this goal shape. The slow search is reported to the `ppt` owner on #592, so a dedicated regression can go in `PPTTactic` if wanted.

**Timings.** Each module was compiled alone with `lake env lean` on the shared 24-core machine, two runs each, between 23:47 and 23:59 UTC. The table gives the mean wall time; user+sys CPU tracks it. CI times are from the cold run 40034532326 on 4 cores.

| Module | CI before | Local before | Local after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BatchLookup` | 154 s | 86.4 s | 7.6 s |
| `Routing` | 122 s | 55.9 s | 7.6 s |
| `KeyedSort` | 77 s | 37.3 s | 5.3 s |
| `PolyTimeContracts` | 59 s | 30.8 s | unchanged |
| `DuplicateFlags` | 52 s | 30.0 s | 5.0 s |
| `Crypto.ZeroKnowledge` | 44 s | 29.0 s | 4.2 s |
| `BatchOr` | 41 s | 20.3 s | 3.4 s |

**Estimated effect on CI.** The six changed modules fall from 259 s to 33 s locally. On the cold CI runner that is about 490 s → 63 s: roughly 7 of the 38.8 test minutes, or 4% of the 169-minute total. It also lowers the `lake test` step's span from 156 s (`BatchLookup`) to about 60 s; the critical-path analysis is on #622.

**Not changed: `PolyTimeContracts`.** Its cost is the `polytime` searches themselves:
- 27% is the `CapturedFold` example with seven `fail_if_success (clear h; polytime)`;
- 14% is the failing "small final projection" search;
- the rest is spread over the joint-inference examples.

Those negative searches are what the test checks, so shrinking them would weaken it. The per-example breakdown is on #592.

**Follow-ups.**
- **Library fix (#590):** `@[csimp]` replacements for `Line.mapWires` and `Circuit.comp`/`append` that store wires at construction. That would make `materialize` unnecessary.
- **Other circuit tests:** `SortingTrace` (31 s), `BitonicSort` (16 s) and `Broadcast` (15 s) also evaluate composed circuits and could use the same helper.

**Validation.** `scripts/check.sh` (all six gates), `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` (127 tests) and `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only`.

issue.title: feat(crypto): prove Naor bit commitment and GMW zero knowledge for NP
issue.body:
Advances #324; the universal-instance/arbitrary-auxiliary-input endpoint remains open.

## Result and scope

Adds Naor bit commitments and computational zero-knowledge interactive proofs for every language in `NP`, in the library's uniform polynomial-time-family model, from a uniform one-way function. The concrete protocol is a three-copy masked-3SAT truth-table commitment adaptation of Goldreich–Micali–Wigderson, using Naor commitments and the existing HILL and Cook–Levin developments. Mathematical sources: `[Naor1991]`, `[GoldreichMicaliWigderson1991]`, `[Goldreich2001]`, and `[AroraBarak09]`.

- `BitCommitmentScheme` packages polynomial-time commitment/verification, statistical binding, and computational hiding over deterministic polynomial-time receiver-string and bit families. `PseudorandomGenerator.naorBitCommitment` requires `3 * n ≤ length n`. The binding error is at most `2^(2n - ℓ(n)) ≤ 2^(-n)`; the one-way-function construction supplies stretch `3n+1`.
- The concrete `GMW` protocol has perfect completeness and soundness at most `1/8 + 2^(-(n+8)) ≤ 1/3` against arbitrary computationally unbounded stateful provers. Honest verification and interaction have strict oracle-PPT/PPT certificates.
- For every uniform strict oracle-PPT malicious verifier, one uniform strict-PPT simulator works for all deterministic polynomial-time-generable instance/witness/auxiliary-input families. The proof uses an actual PRG-to-uniform hybrid, witness-free challenge guessing, and `n+1` attempts with failure `(7/8)^(n+1)`. `zero_knowledge_const` recovers fixed-instance security.
- The bundled witness predicate has no separate polynomial witness-length bound. For the NP construction it is `ThreeSAT.verifier (f a, w)` after the Karp reduction; this does not provide a witness-level Levin reduction from an arbitrary NP verifier.

The stronger universal-instance/arbitrary-auxiliary-input zero-knowledge formulation, hiding against randomized receivers carrying state into the distinguisher, witness-level Levin reductions, and sequential soundness amplification remain open in `ROADMAP.md`. This PR does not claim those endpoints.

## Implementation and review fixes

The development is split across `Commitment.lean`, `GMW/{Protocol,Soundness,PolyTime,Simulator}.lean`, and `ZeroKnowledge.lean`. Generic CNF, bit-string, probability, negligible-function, and hybrid helpers live beside their existing APIs. Internal protocol helpers are private or descriptively named.

The latest source resolves the scope and roadmap overclaims raised by `coordinator-crei-dc679113` and `coordinator-jetski-90c7e6c8`, documents the missing witness-length bound, adds unconditional empty-language and inhabited universal-language examples, and retains headline axiom guards. It is rebased onto main `3e54050f944f13592e75ccc68135d045f73e0e11` with the prior withdrawals preserved.

issue.title: feat(mac): strong unforgeability with pair freshness
issue.body:
Closes #720

## Summary

Adds **strong existential unforgeability under chosen-message attack (SUF-CMA)** for message authentication codes in `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MAC`, alongside the quantitative and asymptotic hierarchy connecting SUF-CMA, EUF-CMA, and deterministic/unique-tag MACs.

### Mathematical Definitions and Results

- **Pair-logging tagging oracle and SUF-CMA game**:
  - `MACScheme.signingPairOracle`: stateful tagging oracle (`ProbOracle (List (List Bool × List Bool)) (List Bool) (List Bool)`) that signs a queried message `m`, appends `(m, tag)` to the transcript, and returns `tag`.
  - `MACScheme.sufCmaGame`: samples `sk ← M.keyGen n`, runs the oracle-PPT adversary against `M.signingPairOracle sk`, and outputs `true` iff `!(queriedPairs.contains (mStar, tagStar)) && M.verify sk mStar tagStar`.
  - `MACScheme.isPPTOn_run_signingPairOracle`, `MACScheme.isPPTOn_sufCmaGame`, `MACScheme.isPPT_sufCmaGame`: plain public PPT contracts.
  - `MACScheme.SUFCMA`, `MACScheme.SUFCMA.negligible`, `MACScheme.SUFCMA.of_negligible`: asymptotic SUF-CMA security definition.
- **Shared pair-history bridge & hierarchy**:
  - `MACScheme.eval_run_signingOracle_eq_map_fst_signingPairOracle`: `ProbOracleComp.run` against `M.signingOracle sk` equals mapping `List.map Prod.fst` over the pair transcript produced by `M.signingPairOracle sk` (via `ProbOracleComp.run_interpret_map_state`).
  - `MACScheme.eval_eufCmaGame_eq_signingPairOracle`: factors `M.eufCmaGame` through `M.signingPairOracle sk`.
  - `MACScheme.succProbability_eufCmaGame_le_sufCmaGame`: for every `n`, `M.eufCmaGame A n ≤ M.sufCmaGame A n` (`!(queriedPairs.map Prod.fst).contains mStar → !queriedPairs.contains (mStar, tagStar)`).
  - `MACScheme.SUFCMA.eufCma` and `MACScheme.SUFCMA.oneTimeEUFCMA`: `SUFCMA → EUFCMA → OneTimeEUFCMA`.
- **Unique-valid-tag equivalence**:
  - `MACScheme.eval_sufCmaGame_eq_eufCmaGame_of_unique_tag`, `MACScheme.succProbability_sufCmaGame_eq_eufCmaGame_of_unique_tag`, and `MACScheme.sufCma_iff_eufCma_of_unique_tag`: under unique valid tags (`hSignVerify` + `hUniqueTag`), any valid pair `(mStar, tagStar)` whose message appears in `queriedPairs.map Prod.fst` must equal the queried pair in `queriedPairs` (established via `ProbOracleComp.run_interpret_invariant`), so `sufCmaGame` and `eufCmaGame` have identical distributions and `M.SUFCMA ↔ M.EUFCMA`.
- **Transfer to `prfMAC`**:
  - `eval_sufCmaGame_prfMAC`, `sufCma_prfMAC_iff_eufCma`, `eval_prfRealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher_eq_sufCmaGame`, `succProbability_sufCmaGame_prfMAC_le`, and `PseudorandomFunction.sufCma_prfMAC`.
- **Strictness witness (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MAC.lean`)**:
  - `randomizedTagMACScheme` appends a fresh random nonce bit `b` to an otherwise constant tag (`0^n ++ [b]`), and `sameMessageNewTagForger` (`isOraclePPT_sameMessageNewTagForger`) queries `0^n`, receives `0^n ++ [b]`, and outputs `(0^n, 0^n ++ [!b])`, achieving `eufCmaGame = 0` and `sufCmaGame = 1` (`succProbability_eufCma_lt_sufCma_sameMessageNewTagForger`).

## Framework friction

- Pair-history freshness reuses the existing generic `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.decide_mem` from `PolyTime/Membership.lean`, followed by the Boolean membership equivalence. The duplicate private pair-list scan proof has been removed; no new shared machinery was needed (#750 R1).
- Shared state-projection and state-invariant lemmas (`ProbOracleComp.run_interpret_map_state` and `ProbOracleComp.run_interpret_invariant`) were already extracted into `Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.OracleSimulation` in #677 and reused directly here.

## Abstract Assessment

issue.title: Signatures from one-way functions: Merkle trees to Rompel
issue.body:
Posted by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` at Samuel's direction (2026-10-25). It leads to the ROADMAP landmark **Rompel's signature theorem**.

## Current state on `main`
`OneWayToSignature.lean` proves that one-way functions are equivalent to one-time signatures (Lamport), and that EUF-CMA signatures imply one-way functions.

## Milestones
- **M0, design:** exact statements and locators. Candidates are Merkle (CRYPTO 1989); Naor–Yung (STOC 1989); Rompel (STOC 1990); and Goldreich, *Foundations of Cryptography* Vol. 2, Chapter 6, pinned in M0.
- **M1, many-time signatures from one-time signatures and collision-resistant hashing:** authentication trees for a polynomial number of messages, as a stateful scheme first. The security reduction has an explicit loss.
- **M2, stateless signatures:** derive the tree nodes with the existing GGM PRF, the usual Goldreich construction.
- **M3, universal one-way hash functions:** Naor–Yung from one-way permutations, then the hash-and-sign extension to arbitrary polynomial-length messages.
- **M4 (long-haul), Rompel:** UOWHFs from any one-way function, which completes OWF ⇔ EUF-CMA signatures.

## Rules
The #897 shared rules and #733 apply. Reuse the `SignatureScheme`, `OneWay`, GGM and collision-resistance APIs.

issue.title: feat(tm2): bridge Mathlib stack machines to polynomial time and space
issue.body:
Mathlib’s TM2 model describes computations using stacks and finite control states. Complexitylib’s complexity classes use CSLib’s multi-tape Turing machines. This PR connects the two, so computations proved using Mathlib’s TM2 API can receive Complexitylib complexity certificates.

It provides two transfers:

- A Mathlib polynomial-time certificate gives a polynomial-time multi-tape computation.
- A terminating Mathlib computation with polynomially bounded stacks gives a polynomial-space multi-tape computation, without requiring a runtime bound. For Boolean deciders, this also proves membership in `PSPACE`.

The simulation represents source configurations using the existing binary encodings and certifies transitions through the existing list-operation calculus. It adds reusable finite-table operations whose entries may have different types, allowing stacks to retain their own alphabets.

The polynomial-space proof counts possible configurations to derive an exponential runtime bound, then executes the simulation using a binary clock. It also exposes a lower-level simulation theorem for clients supplying their own clock.

Typed input and output encoders must be injective, and every working alphabet must be finite. Input and output alphabets may differ or be empty. Space bounds include the input and output stacks. The result establishes polynomial space overhead; linear overhead, sublinear work-space conventions and converse comparisons remain open.

Updates `ROADMAP.md`, `UPSTREAM.md`, and the theorem index with these results and limitations.

Before merging current `main`, validation passed the strict library build, all 358 test modules, the global axiom audit, lint and import checks. Regression examples cover termination-only certificates, exponential binary clocks, heterogeneous and empty alphabets, and Boolean answer conversion.

The merge preserves all TM2 source and test contents. On the merged tree, the three PR regression modules pass strict compilation, and focused environment lint, import-generation and style checks pass with documented Windows Lake workarounds. Full merged-tree validation remains pending in CI; the broader local rebuild encountered Windows runtime/resource failures. The rebuilt theorem-index PDF was independently reviewed. API documentation generation remains blocked locally by a missing native `cc` compiler.

Developed with OpenAI Codex, including independent API, correctness, test and theorem-index reviews. Findings were resolved and re-reviewed.

issue.title: feat(crypto): add Encrypt-then-MAC and PRF-plus-XOR cipher (Boneh-Shoup Theorems 5.2, 9.2)
issue.body:
### Summary

Resolves Step 2 of #1000 (PR 3 of 3, following merged #1028 and #1026; [confirmed design comment on #1000](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1000#issuecomment-6398462902)) by formalizing the generic **Encrypt-then-MAC** composition (`encryptThenMAC`) and Boneh–Shoup Theorem 9.2 ([Boneh and Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Section 9.4.1, printed pp. 367–368), together with the concrete randomized **PRF-plus-XOR cipher** (`prfCipher`, Section 5.4.1, Example 5.2 and Theorem 5.2, printed pp. 183–189) and the end-to-end non-vacuous **PRF Encrypt-then-MAC instance** (`prfEncryptThenMAC`):

1. **Generic Encrypt-then-MAC construction and Theorem 9.2 (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/EncryptThenMAC.lean`)**:
   - `Cslib.Crypto.encryptThenMAC E M hctLen`: combines any `E : SymmetricCipher` whose ciphertexts on `n`-bit plaintexts under supported keys at security parameter `n` have length `M.msgLen n` with any `M : MACScheme` authenticating `M.msgLen n`-bit messages. Keys and ciphertexts are framed via `encPair encBits encBits (ke, km)` and `encPair encBits encBits (c, tag)`, and `decrypt` checks canonical pair framing, `(unframe ct).length == M.msgLen n`, and `M.verify`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.etmToMACHandler`, `Cslib.Crypto.etmToMACForger`, `Cslib.Crypto.isOraclePPT_etmToMACForger`, `Cslib.Crypto.eval_sufCmaGame_etmToMACForger`, and `Cslib.Crypto.succProbability_ciGame_encryptThenMAC_eq`: exact CI-to-SUF-CMA reduction proving `Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval ((encryptThenMAC E M hctLen).ciGame adversary n)) = Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval (M.sufCmaGame (etmToMACForger E M tagBound adversary) n))`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.etmToCPAHandler`, `Cslib.Crypto.etmToCPAAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.isOraclePPT_etmToCPAAdversary`, `Cslib.Crypto.eval_cpaGame_etmToCPAAdversary`, and `Cslib.Crypto.advantage_cpaGame_encryptThenMAC_eq`: exact CPA reduction proving `Game.advantage ... ((encryptThenMAC E M hctLen).cpaGame adversary false n) ... = Game.advantage ... (E.cpaGame (etmToCPAAdversary M adversary) false n) ...`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.ciphertextIntegrity_encryptThenMAC`, `Cslib.Crypto.indcpa_encryptThenMAC`, `Cslib.Crypto.authenticatedEncryption_encryptThenMAC`, `Cslib.Crypto.indcca_encryptThenMAC`, `Cslib.Crypto.authenticatedEncryption_encryptThenMAC_prfMAC`, and `Cslib.Crypto.indcca_encryptThenMAC_prfMAC`: asymptotic `AuthenticatedEncryption` and `INDCCA` security of Encrypt-then-MAC (Theorems 9.2, 9.1, and 6.2).
2. **Concrete non-vacuous PRF-plus-XOR cipher and end-to-end PRF Encrypt-then-MAC instance (`prfCipher`, `prfEncryptThenMAC`, Boneh–Shoup Example 5.2 & Theorem 5.2)**:
   - `Cslib.Crypto.prfCipher family hpoly hlen`: encrypts an `n`-bit plaintext `msg` under an `n`-bit key `k` by sampling a uniform `n`-bit nonce `r ← BitString.sampleList n` and returning the `2 * n`-bit ciphertext `r ++ List.zipWith xor (family k r) msg`, with `Cslib.Crypto.prfCipher_ciphertext_length` certifying `ct.length = 2 * n`.
   - `Cslib.Crypto.cpaToPrfHandler`, `Cslib.Crypto.cpaToPrfDistinguisher`, `Cslib.Crypto.isOraclePPT_cpaToPrfDistinguisher`, `Cslib.Crypto.eval_prfRealGame_cpaToPrfDistinguisher`, `Cslib.Crypto.advantage_cpaGame_prfCipher_le`, and `Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.indcpa_prfCipher`: quantitative and asymptotic `INDCPA` security of `prfCipher` via `OracleComp.IdenticalUntilBad.advantage_le` between the lazy random-function game (Game 2, "faithful gnome", printed p. 186) and the fresh one-time-pad game (Game 3, "forgetful gnome", printed p. 187).
   - `Cslib.Crypto.prfEncryptThenMAC`, `Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.authenticatedEncryption_prfEncryptThenMAC`, and `Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.indcca_prfEncryptThenMAC`: concrete non-vacuous composition of `prfCipher` (`2 * n`-bit ciphertexts) with `(prfMAC family hpoly).reindex (fun n => 2 * n) (.of_tidy (by polytime))`, discharging `hctLen`, `INDCPA`, and `SUFCMA` simultaneously from a single `hprf : PseudorandomFunction family` hypothesis.
3. **Tests (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/EncryptThenMAC.lean`)**:
   - Concrete `echoPrfCipher` and `echoPrfEtM` checks verifying `prfCipher` randomization (two distinct ciphertexts of the same plaintext under the same key lie in `encrypt` support), `prfCipher` and `encryptThenMAC` decryption completeness, wrong-length rejection, tampered-tag rejection, and non-canonical framing rejection, plus smoke checks for all reduction `IsOraclePPT` certificates, quantitative bounds, and asymptotic/non-vacuity theorems.

### Verbatim Source Quotes (Boneh–Shoup v0.6)

Extracted mechanically from `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-samuel-Code-complexitylib/c4b0c164-d16c-427e-bb85-8d58900dabca/scratchpad/bs-text/book.txt` via `sed -n 'START,ENDp'`:

- **Section 5.4.1, Example 5.2 (printed pp. 183–184; `sed -n '9364,9379p' .../book.txt`, lines 9364–9379)**:
  > **Example 5.2.** Before proving CPA security of $\mathcal{E}'$ let us first see the construction in action. Suppose $\mathcal{E}$ is the one-time pad, namely $E(k, m) := k \oplus m$ where $\mathcal{K} = \mathcal{M} = \mathcal{C} = \{0, 1\}^L$. Applying the generic hybrid construction above to the one-time pad results in the following popular cipher $\mathcal{E}_0 = (E_0, D_0)$:
  > - for $k' \in \mathcal{K}'$ and $m \in \mathcal{M}$, define
  >   $$E_0(k', m) := x \stackrel{R}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{X}, \text{ output } (x, F(k', x) \oplus m)$$
  > - for $k' \in \mathcal{K}'$ and $c' = (x, c) \in \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{C}$, define
  >   $$D_0(k', c') := \text{output } F(k', x) \oplus c$$
  >
  > CPA security of this cipher follows from the CPA security of the generic hybrid construction $\mathcal{E}'$ which is proved in Theorem 5.2 below. $\blacksquare$

- **Section 5.4.1, Theorem 5.2 (printed p. 184; `sed -n '9380,9390p' .../book.txt`, lines 9380–9390)**:
  > **Theorem 5.2.** If $F$ is a secure PRF, $\mathcal{E}$ is a semantically secure cipher, and $N := |\mathcal{X}|$ is super-poly, then the cipher $\mathcal{E}'$ described above is a CPA secure cipher.
  >
  > In particular, for every CPA adversary $\mathcal{A}$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}'$ as in the bit-guessing version of Attack Game 5.2, and which makes at most $Q$ queries to its challenger, there exists a PRF adversary $\mathcal{B}_F$ that attacks $F$ as in Attack Game 4.2, and an SS adversary $\mathcal{B}_E$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}$ as in the bit-guessing version of Attack Game 2.1, where both $\mathcal{B}_F$ and $\mathcal{B}_E$ are elementary wrappers around $\mathcal{A}$, such that
  > $$\text{CPAadv}[\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{E}'] \le \frac{Q^2}{N} + 2 \cdot \text{PRFadv}[\mathcal{B}_F, F] + Q \cdot \text{SSadv}[\mathcal{B}_E, \mathcal{E}]. \qquad (5.5)$$

- **Section 9.4.1, Encrypt-then-MAC (printed p. 367; `sed -n '18303,18316p' .../book.txt`, lines 18303–18316)**:
  > **9.4.1 Encrypt-then-MAC**
  > Let $\mathcal{E} = (E, D)$ be a cipher defined over $(\mathcal{K}_e, \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{C})$ and let $I = (S, V)$ be a MAC defined over $(\mathcal{K}_m, \mathcal{C}, \mathcal{T})$. The encrypt-then-MAC system $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}} = (E_{\text{EtM}}, D_{\text{EtM}})$, or EtM for short, is defined as follows:
  > $$\begin{aligned}
  > E_{\text{EtM}}((k_e, k_m), m) &:= c \stackrel{R}{\leftarrow} E(k_e, m), \ t \stackrel{R}{\leftarrow} S(k_m, c) \\
  > &\phantom{:=}\ \text{Output } (c, t) \\
  > D_{\text{EtM}}((k_e, k_m), (c, t)) &:= \text{if } V(k_m, c, t) = \text{reject then output reject} \\
  > &\phantom{:=}\ \text{otherwise, output } D(k_e, c)
  > \end{aligned}$$
  > The EtM system is defined over $(\mathcal{K}_e \times \mathcal{K}_m, \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{C} \times \mathcal{T})$. The following theorem shows that $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}$ provides authenticated encryption.

- **Section 9.4.1, Theorem 9.2 (printed p. 367; `sed -n '18317,18332p' .../book.txt`, lines 18317–18332)**:
  > **Theorem 9.2.** Let $\mathcal{E} = (E, D)$ be a cipher and let $I = (S, V)$ be a MAC system. Then $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}$ is AE-secure assuming $\mathcal{E}$ is CPA-secure and $I$ is a secure MAC system. Also, $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}$ is 1AE-secure assuming $\mathcal{E}$ is semantically secure and $I$ is a one-time secure MAC system.
  >
  > In particular, for every ciphertext integrity adversary $\mathcal{A}_{\text{ci}}$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}$ as in Attack Game 9.1 there exists a MAC adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\text{mac}}$ that attacks $I$ as in Attack Game 6.1, where $\mathcal{B}_{\text{mac}}$ is an elementary wrapper around $\mathcal{A}_{\text{ci}}$, and which makes no more signing queries than $\mathcal{A}_{\text{ci}}$ makes encryption queries, such that
  > $$\text{CIadv}[\mathcal{A}_{\text{ci}}, \mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}] = \text{MACadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\text{mac}}, I].$$
  > For every CPA adversary $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cpa}}$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}$ as in Attack Game 5.2 there exists a CPA adversary $\mathcal{B}_{\text{cpa}}$ that attacks $\mathcal{E}$ as in Attack Game 5.2, where $\mathcal{B}_{\text{cpa}}$ is an elementary wrapper around $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cpa}}$, and which makes no more encryption queries than does $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cpa}}$, such that
  > $$\text{CPAadv}[\mathcal{A}_{\text{cpa}}, \mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}] = \text{CPAadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\text{cpa}}, \mathcal{E}].$$

### Specializations and Omissions Relative to Boneh–Shoup

- **Ciphertext-length compatibility (`c.length = M.msgLen n`)**: In Section 9.4.1 (printed p. 367), $\mathcal{E}$ has message space $\mathcal{M}$ and ciphertext space $\mathcal{C}$, and $I$ has message space $\mathcal{C}$. Here plaintexts at security parameter $n$ have length $n$ and ciphertexts under supported keys have length `M.msgLen n`. Because `(M.reindex ctLen hctLen).msgLen n = M.msgLen (ctLen n)`, reindexing `M` by `ctLen` supplies message length `ctLen n` when the base MAC has `M.msgLen = id` (as holds for `prfMAC`), while transferring `M.SUFCMA` to `(M.reindex ctLen hctLen).SUFCMA` via `MACScheme.SUFCMA.reindex` additionally requires `StrictMono ctLen` (both hold for `prfEncryptThenMAC` with `ctLen := fun n => 2 * n`).
- **Omitted `1AE` half and query-count preservation in Theorem 9.2**: Theorem 9.2 also states that $\mathcal{E}_{\text{EtM}}$ is `1AE`-secure assuming $\mathcal{E}$ is semantically secure and $I$ is a one-time secure MAC system, and that $\mathcal{B}_{\text{mac}}$ (resp. $\mathcal{B}_{\text{cpa}}$) makes no more queries than $\mathcal{A}_{\text{ci}}$ (resp. $\mathcal{A}_{\text{cpa}}$). This module formalizes the multi-query adaptive `AuthenticatedEncryption` and `INDCCA` statements; the one-time `1AE` half and separate query-count preservation theorems are omitted.
- **Specialization of Theorem 5.2 to the Example 5.2 one-time-pad instantiation (`prfCipher`) and two-world CPA bound with a factor-`2` collision term**: Theorem 5.2 (printed p. 184; proof on printed pp. 184–189) is stated for the general hybrid construction $\mathcal{E}'$ combining a PRF $F$ with a semantically secure cipher $\mathcal{E}$ ($\text{CPAadv}[\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{E}'] \le Q^2 / N + 2 \cdot \text{PRFadv}[\mathcal{B}_F, F] + Q \cdot \text{SSadv}[\mathcal{B}_E, \mathcal{E}]$, where $Q^2 / N$ comes from the birthday bound $\Pr[Z] \le Q^2 / (2N)$ in equation (5.11) on printed p. 187). Here `prfCipher` formalizes the Example 5.2 instantiation (printed pp. 183–184) where $\mathcal{E}$ is the one-time pad $k \oplus m$ on $\{0, 1\}^n$ ($\text{SSadv} = 0$, $N = 2^n$), and `advantage_cpaGame_prfCipher_le` bounds two-world `cpaGame` distinguishing advantage by $\text{PRFadv}[\text{cpaToPrfDistinguisher adversary false}, F] + \text{PRFadv}[\text{cpaToPrfDistinguisher adversary true}, F] + 2 \cdot Q^2 / 2^n$: it uses two fixed-bit PRF distinguishers instead of one coin-flipping distinguisher $\mathcal{B}_F$ with factor $2$, and its collision term $2 \cdot Q^2 / 2^n$ is $2\times$ the source's $Q^2 / N = Q^2 / 2^n$ because `bad_prfCipherForgetfulWithBadOracle_le` uses a per-step union bound $Q \cdot Q / 2^n$ per challenge bit rather than the birthday sum $\sum_{i < Q} i / 2^n \le Q^2 / 2^{n+1}$.

### Framework friction

- Plain `@[program_certificate]` field-composition lemmas (`MACScheme.computableInPolyTime_msgLen_comp`, `MACScheme.isPPTOn_keyGen_comp`, `SymmetricCipher.isPPTOn_encrypt_comp`, etc.) are not directly usable by `polytime` / `ppt` (`fun_prop`), so clients must introduce local tidy/PPT hypotheses inside proofs to bridge them (logged on #733).

### Abstract impact

None (does not affect `docs/abstract.tex`).

Refs #1000

issue.title: refactor(probabilistic): build clean oracle phases from plain deterministic certificates (#862)
issue.body:
The clean-phase calculus `IsTidyOraclePPTOn` now takes plain deterministic certificates, `ComputableInPolyTime`, in place of `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`. A clean deterministic phase is the tidy normal form of the plain machine (`ComputesInTimeAndSpace.computesTidily_tidy`), run with its coin bits ignored (`ComputesTidily.of_deterministic`). That machine-level step lives in one rule, `IsTidyOraclePPTOn.of_computableInPolyTime`, and every other rule builds on it.

This is step 3 of #862. Probabilistic machines already have a normal form at the level the public notions need: `isOraclePPTOn_iff_isTidyOraclePPTOn` says every strict oracle PPT certificate has a clean realization ([plan and correction](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/862#issuecomment-6389062916)). What tied the probabilistic layer to the deterministic tidy calculus was the clean-phase rules' deterministic premises. After this PR, `Normalization` is re-proved with plain automation, and deleting `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime` (#862 step 5) no longer has to touch the clean-phase calculus.

**Changes**
- `Probabilistic/Oracle/Tidy.lean`: `of_computableInPolyTime` replaces `of_computableTidilyInPolyTime`. `pair`, `bind_with`, `preprocess`, `map`, `map_with`, `cond`, `ite` and `finite_cases` take plain premises.
- `Probabilistic/Oracle/Iteration.lean`: `iterate_spec`, `iterateWith_spec` and `iterateWith_of_bounded_growth` take plain counters and initial states. The preparation machine is now a clean phase from `of_computableInPolyTime`.
- `Probabilistic/Oracle/Normalization.lean`: the interpreter's deterministic steps use plain certificates and plain `fun_prop`.
- `Probabilistic/Oracle/Composition.lean`: statements are unchanged. Proofs pass `.of_tidy` premises to the clean rules.
- `ComplexityTests/PlainCleanPhase.lean`, new, with four examples and axiom guards:
  - a clean phase from the plain certificate of upstream's copy machine, which does not clear its tapes;
  - plain postprocessing of a fair bit;
  - a branch on a plain condition;
  - a loop with a plain counter.

**Breaking change.** `IsTidyOraclePPTOn.of_computableTidilyInPolyTime` is now `of_computableInPolyTime` with a plain premise, and the rules above take plain premises. There are no aliases, per #862, and all clients are updated.

**Limits.**
- The public plain rules in `Oracle/Composition` keep their tidy premises, a transitional state. Their clients include Crypto files that #852 is editing (`Signature`, `OneWay/MCSP`), so restating them waits. A prepared continuation is on `wip/plain-oracle-composition-862`: those statements made plain, with the Classes/IP/MIP/Oracle clients partly updated and round trips removed. It is to be finished after #852 and the Crypto sweep.
- `IsTidyOraclePPTOn` itself stays public until the internal boundary exists (#862 step 5).
- The ratchet counts are unchanged: these statements still mention `IsTidyOraclePPTOn`.

**Validation.** All six gates pass locally (`scripts/check.sh`) on the change before a rebase onto doc-only main commits; after the rebase (head `6ef24846`) `mk_all --check` passes and the touched modules were rebuilt. `scripts/check_tidy_surface.py` reports 1302 statements in 225 modules, matching the baseline. Hosted CI covers the head.

**Abstracts.** No impact. No selected headline, definition or catalogue entry mentions the clean-phase calculus.

**Review.** Requested from `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`.

issue.title: design(reduction): uniform many-one reduction core and ordered first-order reductions
issue.body:
## Status

**Design proposal, awaiting maintainer/coordinator decision before implementation.** Opened by worker `claude-opus-5-5-48cb80c1`. No branch yet; no code written.

## Motivation

Most reduction notions in the library are instances of one shape, `∃ f, Good f ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B`, but each is defined and developed separately:

| Notion | `Good f` | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `PolyTimeReducible` | `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f encA encB` | `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Reduction.lean:80` |
| `LogSpaceReducible` | `ComputableInLogSpace f enc encB` | `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/LogSpace.lean:158` |
| `MappingReducible` | `IsComputable f encA encB` | `Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Halting/Reduction.lean:53` |
| `FPTReducible` | FPT time + parameter bound `κB (f a) ≤ h (κA a)` | `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Parameterized.lean:456` |
| promise `PolyTimeReducible` | polytime, membership on the promise | `Complexity/Computability/PCP/Approximation.lean:88` |
| `FO.Reduces` / `FO.QFReduces` | `f = I.Model` for a (QF) interpretation | `Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Reduction.lean:166`, `Reduction/QuantifierFree.lean:73` |
| `FO.ReducesNontrivial` | as above, correctness on ≥ 2 elements | `Complexity/Logics/FirstOrder/Reduction/Nontrivial.lean:73` |
| `ParsimoniousReducible` | polytime, count-preserving (`f a = g (r a)`) | `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/SharpP/Completeness.lean:53` |

Consequences: `refl`/`trans`/`comp` are re-proved for at least six notions; `Hard`/`Complete` are re-defined for PolyTime, LogSpace, #P and Search (plus `NPHard`/`coNPHard` abbreviations); `compl` lemmas are repeated (`PolyTimeReducible.compl`, `LogSpaceReducible.compl`, `FPTReducible.compl`, `NPHard.compl`, …); and every bridge between notions is a bespoke proof (`LogSpaceReducible.polyTimeReducible`, `FO.Reduces.logSpaceReducible`, `FullTupleInterpretation.logSpaceReducible_onSentence`). cslib has no generic reduction framework.

The immediate trigger is the roadmap item "first-order reductions are logspace reductions" (`ROADMAP.md`, ordered first-order complexity milestone). Defining ordered `≤_fo` as yet another bespoke notion would repeat the pattern.

## Proposed core

A small, machine-free module (placement is an open question below):

```lean
/-- A many-one reduction of `A` to `B` by a map satisfying `Good`. -/
structure ManyOneReduction {α β : Type*} (Good : (α → β) → Prop) (A : Set α) (B : Set β) where
  toFun : α → β
  good : Good toFun
  mem_iff : ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ toFun a ∈ B

def ManyOneReducible {α β : Type*} (Good : (α → β) → Prop) (A : Set α) (B : Set β) : Prop :=
  ∃ f, Good f ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a ∈ B
```

with, at minimum:

* `ManyOneReducible.of_reduction`, `.exists_reduction` (witness ↔ `Prop`); `ManyOneReducible` is stated as the bare `∃` so existing notions can be redefined to unfold to **exactly** their current form.
* `refl` from `Good id`; `trans` from closure under composition (a family `Good : ∀ {α β}, … → (α → β) → Prop` with `id`/`comp` fields, or hypotheses). Reflexivity and transitivity are **not** assumed for every map class (see the FO question below).
* `mono` (`Good ≤ Good'`), `compl` (free), and a **lift** lemma: if every `Good` map has a `Good'` map on representations commuting with decoding, reductions transfer. Logspace ⇒ polytime is `mono`; order-free FO ⇒ logspace and ordered FO ⇒ logspace are `lift`.
* Generic `Hard`, `Complete`, `ClosedUnder` over classes indexed like the current `∀ {α : Type}, (α ↪ List Bool) → Set (Set α)`, with `Hard.trans`, `Complete.compl`-style lemmas and "complete `B ∈ D`, `D` closed ⇒ `C ⊆ D`" stated once.
* Named witnesses (`ManyOneReduction`) are where quantitative facts (output size, explicit degree) attach, e.g. Cook–Levin's `reduce` could carry a `length_reduce_le` without changing `PolyTimeReducible`.

Non-goals: truth-table, Levin search (backward solution maps), oracle/Turing and cryptographic security reductions have different shapes and stay as they are.

## Ordered first-order reductions on the core

Define an ordered interpretation with a domain formula φ₀ from the start (full-tuple = `φ₀ = ⊤`), so milestone 2 does not change a merged definition. Target universe: the φ₀-tuples, lexicographically ordered, renumbered by rank onto `Fin m`; input relations transported; canonical numerics on `Fin m`. `Ordered.Reduces K K'` is `ManyOneReducible` for the FO-interpretable maps `Ordered.Structure L → Ordered.Structure L'`.

Decisions to confirm:

1. **Size proviso.** `Ordered.Structure` requires `2 ≤ size`, so the definition requires φ₀ to select at least two tuples on every source. Automatic for full-tuple with `k > 0`.
2. **Transitivity is not free.** Composing restricted-domain interpretations needs `BIT` on rank-numbered domains, which need not be FO-definable (`ROADMAP.md`, citing the paragraph after Immerman's Exercise 1.33). Either `≤_fo` is not a preorder in general, or interpretations carry numeric-definability certificates (full-tuple ones already do). To be checked against Immerman before fixing the definition; the core deliberately derives `trans` only from composition closure.
3. **Placement.** The core is machine-free; `Complexity/Foundations/...` avoids `Logics` importing `Computability`. Alternatively `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Reduction/ManyOne.lean` next to `TruthTable.lean`.

## Transducer unification (milestone 2)

The order-free transducer (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/LogSpace/FirstOrder/Reduction.lean`, 892 lines) already counts domain tuples and reconstructs tuples of requested ranks — the restricted-domain mechanism. The ordered full-tuple transducer (`…/LogSpace/FirstOrder/Ordered/Reduction.lean`, 522 lines) is a separate program adding compiled numeric atoms. Proposal: one domain-counting transducer parametrized by the formula compiler (order-free, or ordered with native ≤/BIT/0/1/max), with both existing transducers as instances and existing public theorems kept (deprecated aliases where names move).

## Milestones

1. **Core + two clients + ordered `≤_fo`.** Core module; `PolyTimeReducible` and `LogSpaceReducible` redefined to unfold to their current statements (no downstream breakage expected), `LogSpaceReducible.polyTimeReducible` via `mono`; ordered interpretations with φ₀ and `Ordered.Reduces`; `Ordered.Reduces ⇒ LogSpaceReducible` of `Query.encodedLanguage` for full-domain reductions, via `lift` on the existing #137 transducer. Nonvacuous client (e.g. an existing full-tuple reduction).
2. **Restricted domains.** Unified transducer; general `Ordered.Reduces ⇒ LogSpaceReducible`; order-free and full-tuple transducers become instances.
3. **Migrations**, each a small PR: `MappingReducible`, `FPTReducible`, promise reductions, `FO.Reduces`/`QFReduces`/`ReducesNontrivial`, `Hard`/`Complete` families.

## Size estimate (unverified)

Measured over `Complexity/`: `refl`/`trans`/`comp`/`mono` 24 decls / 93 lines; `Hard`/`Complete` 152 decls / 941 lines, but most are problem-specific theorems (`TSP_npHard`, …) that remain; `mem_*` closure lemmas 47 / 520 lines, mostly real proofs (median 6 lines; `mem_AM` 66, `mem_MA` 60, `mem_BPP` 39). The core itself is roughly net-neutral (≈300–400 boilerplate lines removed, ≈200 added). The larger deletion is milestone 2: ≈1,414 existing transducer lines plus ≈700 new versus ≈900–1,100 unified — an estimate made without reading the transducer internals.

## Index impact

Milestone 1 adds a theorem-index entry for ordered `≤_fo ⇒ ≤_log` (full domain); redefinitions that unfold to current statements need only a no-impact assessment.

feat(ThreeSAT): prove 3SAT-3 completeness
issue.body:
Proves 3SAT-3 NP-complete under binary `encCNF`: clauses have width at most three (binary clauses permitted), and each variable has at most three literal occurrences, counting repetitions within a clause. Only the variable-occurrence restriction of Papadimitriou94, Proposition 9.3 is formalized; the additional bound of two occurrences per signed literal is not part of the language or completeness statement. `toThreeSATThree` is a total native-machine polynomial-time reduction from `ThreeSAT`, rejecting non-width-three inputs with `[[]]`. Its verifier is certified using the existing SAT verifier. This implements #1081; planarity, orthogonal drawings, and the quantitative planar endpoint remain open in #1079.

The reusable CNF construction gives every occurrence a copy `(original variable, clause index, literal index)`, then adds binary implication cycles. It proves equisatisfiability, generic cycle constancy, width preservation, the occurrence bound, and exact counts: `m + ℓ` clauses, `3ℓ` literals, and `ℓ` distinct variables. Original labels retain their supplied encoding; binary pairing numbers the copies without expanding arbitrary labels to unary. Tests cover yes/no instances, repeated literals, singleton cycles, empty formulas/clauses, rejected wide inputs, and a label `2^100`. The guide explains the endpoint and counts.

Textbook source: [Papadimitriou94, Proposition 9.3, pp. 183–184](https://djvu.online/file/ugtJZIrmGbFU7), verified against the book text. The statement restricts “each variable” to “appear at most three times” and also bounds each signed literal by two; this PR formalizes the variable restriction only. The proof on p. 184 gives the fresh-copy implication cycle and explicitly permits binary clauses. Repeated literals are allowed, and each syntactic occurrence counts separately here, as in the book's preceding convention. All four new modules and the main theorem now cite the existing bibliography key.

Source: adapted from [lean-trominoes at 6d5b36c](https://github.com/edemaine/lean-trominoes/tree/6d5b36c15cec6cb18d30137b7f1c7fb92ea24332), preserving Erik Demaine, Stefan Langerman, and GPT 5.6 credit. Exact locators: `SAT/ThreeSAT/PeriodicThreeSATThree.lean`, definitions `occurrenceClauses`, `cycleFrom`, `cycleClauses`, and `formula`; `PeriodicThreeSATThreeExactSize.lean`, `formula_clauses_length` and literal/variable counts; `FiniteThreeSATThree.lean`, theorem `satisfiable_iff`, whose statement is `FiniteCNF.Satisfiable (formula source) ↔ FiniteCNF.Satisfiable source`. Here formulas and clauses are existing ordinary `CNF`/`Clause` lists, offsets are absent, assignments are total Boolean functions on the variable type of an ordinary formula, and source presentation-literal count is `φ.vars.length`. The periodic framework is not imported.

Existing APIs reused: `CNF`, `Clause`, `Literal`, `vars`, `distinctVars`, `relabel`, `Satisfiable`, `SAT.verifier`, `ThreeSAT`, and plain `ComputableInPolyTime`/NP reductions. `Cslib.Logic.PL.occurrences` lists the indexed literal occurrences flat; `occurrenceClauses` retains the clause boundaries. `ClauseSet.occurrences` counts mentioning clauses, so the required literal-occurrence restriction uses `vars.count`. The only new problem definition is this missing width/occurrence restriction; the construction remains over the existing CNF representation.

Validation at `cf3b1ddca85453eff32ae54bfc277d9cbb59f320` (tree `efda37543642f375c5ac14e985a61cbde4dca9b6`): all six required gates pass on this committed revision via `COMPLEXITYLIB_CACHE_AUTO=0 LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2 scripts/check.sh` using the existing isolated caches: strict build, import aggregate, strict tests including the global axiom audit, environment lint, style lint, and init-import check. Lean MCP reports clean diagnostics for `ThreeSATThree.lean`, including the revised entirely plain numeric composition. Hygiene (including `--check-simp`), changed-file checks, documentation configuration, and the catalogue check pass. The extra local guide check at the prior revision had the documented Windows MD4Lean FFI export blocker; the guide is unchanged by this review delta, and the reviewer recorded passing guide CI at the prior revision.

Review delta: citations and scope/API wording, removal of redundant “finite” qualifiers and doubled blank lines, plus the numeric proof refactor. Every public statement and definition is unchanged; lean-trominoes source credit is preserved.

Curated abstracts: no impact. Existing public statements, definitions, selected headline semantics and rendering are unchanged; no new headline is proposed. `build_abstracts.py --check` passes. No ROADMAP direction is closed by this milestone.

AI assistance: implemented and self-reviewed with Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol`), worker session `t3-96187517-three`, delegated by `t3-96187517-root`. Independent API/correctness review is requested from the parent; this is not human editorial approval.

issue.title: chore(circuit): audit API, structure and checked documentation
issue.body:
Circuit quality-program tracker for #587. Task claims and active implementation leads are recorded in the comments; there is no reserved owner fleet or final reviewer. issue.title: feat(mac): strong unforgeability with pair freshness

issue.title: doc(start): make public declarations findable and ordinary claims easy to state
issue.body:
Samuel asked coordinators to make existing results easy to reach. The user's path is: recognize the result → understand its assumptions → find the public declaration → import it → apply it. Two steps of that path are awkward today.

1. **Finding a declaration.** README "Start here" sends users looking for "a computational model or mathematical tool" to `Complexity.lean`, a flat list of about 1,870 imports. Searchable doc-gen4 docs already build (`docs.yml`, manual dispatch, about 1 h, 52 MiB artifact), but they aren't published anywhere. Proposal: publish them to GitHub Pages on a nightly schedule plus manual dispatch, with concurrency so only the latest build deploys, and point "Start here" at the site. **This needs Samuel's OK**, because it enables Pages and creates a public site, although every page comes from public sources.
2. **Stating an ordinary claim.** No "Start here" row covers the most common task: showing a problem is in `P`/`NP`, or giving a polynomial-time reduction. Once #559 lands (plain `P`, `NP`, `PolyTimeReducible`), add a short checked example showing that with plain `ComputableInPolyTime` and `fun_prop`/`polytime`, plus a "Start here" row linking it. No tidy-machine knowledge should be needed.

**Done when:** "Start here" links a usable API search, and a checked example covers stating P/NP membership and reductions without tidy-machine knowledge.

Available; item 2 waits for #559, item 1 for Samuel's decision. Recorded by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

issue.title: feat(crypto): construct native shallow GSW decryption circuits
issue.body:
Construct the actual selected-row GSW decryption circuit on the complete serialized secret followed by the complete square-matrix ciphertext. Evaluation agrees with total `decryptSerialized` for every well-sized raw pair, without key-generation, encryption-support or noise hypotheses. Shifted partial products, the exact half-split carry-save tree and carry-lookahead finishing compute the phase modulo `2^w`; the decoder covers widths zero and one and both half-open boundary ties.

The proved depth is at most `28 + 18 clog₂(w+1) + 12 clog₂(n)` and gate count at most `131(n+1)(w+1)²`. A native polynomial-time generator charges the full code, matrix selectors and wiring, and also constructs the complete layered NAND augmentation. Its actual compiled layer count fits the existing `DepthParameters.depthBudget` at every security parameter. Public generator statements are plain; construction helpers are private, with narrow companion `import all` access. Checked clients exercise decoder ties, negative wraparound, boundary widths, empty arrays, the uniform parameter family, compiler semantics/encoded-size overhead and audited axioms.

Rebased onto main `7122d105`; #594 is already present and its duplicate cherry-pick is removed. All eight original #528 commits are retained, including the two that preceded that cherry-pick. The independent mathematical/API review at `ee20f997` remains [review 5635643747](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/607#pullrequestreview-5635643747). The rebase preserves that source, and the subsequent [plain API delta](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/compare/71aa74e9...93e2da84) replaces six public tidy constructor certificates with plain hypotheses and conclusions, updates their clients, and keeps tidy inside proofs/private construction helpers. The circuit definitions, evaluation, depth/size bounds and budget proofs are unchanged. Prior unavailable private-machine checkpoints and earlier contributions remain credited in #528; this implementation does not claim to recover those files.

Closes #528. The broader #486 objective remains open: this proves the actual decryption circuit, native construction and budget fit, not bootstrappability, a transfer of a decision-LWE premise, circular security or the concrete FHE endpoint. Existing selected abstract statements and catalogue entries are unchanged; no new headline is proposed and no PDF rendering changes.

Validation: all six required gates passed at `93e2da84c0f36ff7e86e20a135de83e05f7efac2` (strict build, generated imports, tests, lint, style and init imports). Focused plain-client and ordinary-import API checks, hygiene including changed-source `--check-simp`, and the abstract catalogue check passed. The six old public tidy certificate names are removed without aliases; no global private `fun_prop` registration is added. The earlier six-gate result at `ee20f997` remains valid for the independently reviewed mathematical checkpoint. Final independent delta review is requested before integration; the authors do not approve or merge this work.

issue.title: quality(logics): area checklist
issue.body:
Area checklist for #587, owned by `lead-claude-logics-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Snapshot: `main` at d52fd12c. Scope: `Complexity/Logics/**` (98 modules: 57 FirstOrder, 35 Propositional, 6 SecondOrder) and their test, abstract and client callers.

This is the audit; no edits yet. Edits start after #559, #560, #568 and the deprecation sweep merge, one bounded, single-theme PR at a time, each cross-reviewed by `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`. Cross-area changes (marked below) are announced on #587 first.

**Summary.** The area is in comparatively good shape. First-order logic is built on Mathlib's `ModelTheory` throughout. CNF reuses `Std.Sat.Literal` and documents why `Std.Sat.CNF` (array-based) and `Cslib.Logic.PL.Proposition` are not reused. Ordered first-order reductions are `ManyOneReducibleBy` instances, and every interpretation variant compiles to `FO.Interpretation`. Hygiene passes, there are no heartbeat overrides, and proof lengths match the library (p99 74 lines vs 66; max 116). The gaps are:

- a large public surface;
- a few misplaced or duplicated APIs, mostly in client modules outside the area;
- tidy predicates in the Cook–Reckhow statements;
- module-doc drift;
- two small automation gaps;
- a handful of untested modules.

**Baseline.** These numbers come from a local run of #584's `QualityReport.lean` over the cached build at d52fd12c, plus `.ilean` references. They will be reconciled with the shared report when it is posted.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Public declarations (excluding constructors and recursors) | 1,635 (plus 152 private) |
| Referenced by other library modules / only by tests / by no other module | 817 / 197 / 621 |
| Of the 621: unattributed theorems not named in a module doc | ~270 (~175 in 29 Propositional files, ~95 in 31 FirstOrder/SecondOrder files) |
| Exposed definitions | 515 (95 of 98 modules use `@[expose] public section`) |
| Public definitions without a docstring | 28, all instances or derived |
| "Main results" theorems without a docstring | 46 |
| Tidy predicates in public statements, outside certificate lemmas | 2 (`ProofSystem.ofVerifier`, `ProofSystem.pSimulates_iff_tidy`) |
| Alpha-equivalent duplicates | 2 (in `ValiantVazirani`, outside the area) |
| `grind` annotations | 0 (`simp`, `fo_realize`, `aesop (FirstOrder)` and `fun_prop` sets exist) |

### 1. `refactor(logics): make propositional proof helpers private` (surface; about 29 files) — #601, #667

- [x] Make a theorem private when it is referenced nowhere outside its module, is not named in a module doc, abstract or test, and belongs to no `simp`/`fun_prop`/`aesop` set. The main groups are:
  - the `CNF.Sparsification` list lemmas (29 in `ClauseSet/Sparsification/List`);
  - the `ClauseSet.Sparsification.Path` and `BranchingRule` helpers;
  - the intermediate `computableTidilyInPolyTime_{reduce,flower,heavy,candidates,choice}`;
  - the `Pigeonhole` bottleneck lemmas (23);
  - the `ArithQBF` degree lemmas;
  - the `splitAux`, `exclude` and Tseitin parity helpers;
  - the coding-lemma helpers.

  API-like lemmas stay public: `Derives.mono`, `RefutableInSize.mono`, `QBF.closed_*`, `ProofSystem.{mem, exists_eq, nonempty}`, `Simulates`/`PSimulates` `refl`/`trans`, `Derivation.{derives, size_pos}` and `CNF.{eval, length}_compact`.

  *Benefit:* about 175 fewer public names, and editing a proof internal no longer invalidates downstream builds. *Risk:* low. A helper that an exposed body uses fails to build and stays public, or goes with item 9's `@[expose]` narrowing. No aliases (D1).

### 2. `refactor(logics): make first-order proof helpers private` (surface; about 31 files) — #606

- [x] Apply the same rule to:
  - the `TaggedInterpretation` internals (`coords_*`, `realize_domainAt*`, `realize_toInterpretation_*_of_{subsingleton,nontrivial}`, `ofCopies_bijective`);
  - the `cnf.relMap_*Sym`, `realize_satMatrix` and `*_copies_iff` helpers;
  - the coloring gadget lemmas;
  - the `Encoding/Layout` helpers;
  - the `DomainInterpretation` rank helpers;
  - the ESO `*_isExpansionOn` and `realize_onSentence_sum*` lemmas.

  The closure API stays public: `QFReduces.{isoClosed, compl}`, `ReducesNontrivial.compl` and `Interpretation.ext_iff`.

  *Benefit and risk:* as in item 1. The Fagin abstract and bridge use none of these declarations.

### 3. `refactor(proof-systems): state the verifier proof system with plain computability` (statements) — #611

- ~~Rename the `isPolyTime_*` certificates.~~ Superseded: Samuel's direction on #456 (T1–T3) removes tidy from every public statement, and the library-wide sweep will restate all 25 tidy certificates in this area as plain `computableInPolyTime_*`. They are in `CNF/PolyTime`, `CNF/ThreeCNF/PolyTime` and `Sparsification/PolyTime`. The sweep runs once Machines lands the auto-mirroring attribute, so this item no longer renames them by hand.
- [ ] `ProofSystem.ofVerifier` and `ofVerifier_frame_append` take a tidy verifier certificate. Once #559 states `NP` with plain `ComputableInPolyTime` verifiers, they take the plain hypothesis (#456). `pSimulates_iff_tidy` becomes private; its only client is one example in `ComplexityTests/ProofComplexity.lean`.
- With this item, only the 25 certificates left for that sweep mention tidy in a public statement in this area.

*Benefit:* the Cook–Reckhow statements contain no proof machinery, and certificate names say what they state. *Risk:* low.

### 4. `refactor(logics): collect QBF and CNF API from client modules` (placement and duplicates; cross-area, announce first) — #688

- [ ] Move the general QBF combinators `QBF.{exs, alls, conj, imp, iff, lit, ofClause, ofCNF}`, with their `eval_*` and `freeVars_*` lemmas, from `Classes/Space/TQBF/Formula.lean` into `Logics/Propositional/QBF`. The `tokens_*` lemmas stay with the TQBF encoding.
- [ ] Move `CNF.numVars` (94 uses, already in `Cslib.Logic.PL`) and its two lemmas from `Complexity/FineGrained.lean` into `Propositional/CNF.lean`.
- [x] (Removed by #631; they were deprecated aliases.) Delete `ValiantVazirani.mem_vars_iff` and `ValiantVazirani.vars_relabel`, which are alpha-equivalent to `CNF.mem_vars` and `CNF.vars_relabel`, and update their callers.

*Benefit:* QBF and CNF API lives with its type, and client modules stop owning general logic. *Risk:* low, since everything moves within existing import chains. Coordinate with the classes-area lead.

### 5. `refactor: place Cook–Reckhow proof systems with the complexity classes` (placement; cross-area, needs the classes lead's agreement)

- [ ] `Propositional/ProofSystem.lean` is in namespace `Cslib.Complexity`, treats proof systems for any language and imports Cook–Levin, so its path does not mirror its namespace. Move it to `Computability/Complexity/ProofSystem.lean`, move `NP_eq_coNP_iff_coNP_subset_NP` next to `coNP`, and update the `ROADMAP.md` links.

*Benefit:* the path mirrors the namespace, as the upstream rule requires, and Logics no longer imports Cook–Levin. *Risk:* low; ownership moves to the classes area. If the classes lead declines, the file stays and the decision is recorded.

### 6. `feat(logics): automate CNF evaluation` (automation) — #625

- [ ] Add `fun_prop` certificates in `CNF/PolyTime.lean` for evaluating a literal, a clause or a formula under a polynomial-time assignment. They replace the `fun_prop [CNF.eval, Clause.eval, Literal.eval]` unfoldings in `Problems/SAT/PolyTime.lean` and `FineGrained/Assignment.lean`.
- [ ] Add a `simp` lemma `l.eval σ = true ↔ σ l.1 = l.2` for an arbitrary literal (the current one needs a pair), and `Literal.eval_negate`. They replace about 25 `simp [… Literal.eval …]` unfoldings across `DNF`, `ThreeCNF`, `Resolution`, `DecisionTree/NormalForm`, `TQBF/Formula`, `CircuitSAT` and `ValiantVazirani`.
- [ ] Assess a small `grind` set for CNF semantics, following CSLib's convention for logics, and add it only if it shortens real clients.

*Benefit:* routine facts follow without unfolding. *Risk:* low; simp-set changes can alter normal forms in clients, which the build checks.

### 7. `doc(logics): align module docs with the public API` (documentation) — #617, #644

- [ ] Qualify the names in the module docs of `FirstOrder/Projection.lean`, `ProjectionFormula.lean` and `Projection/Graph.lean`, which list `Projection.…` and `InputLiteral` unqualified. Expand the shorthand in `Problems/SizedGraph.lean`.
- [ ] Write docstrings for the 46 "Main results" theorems that lack one, mostly `realize_*` lemmas in `FirstOrder/Basic`, `Ordered/*` and `Subformula`. Alternatively, trim those lists to the headline results.
- [ ] Add `## References` to `ClauseSet/Basic`, `ClauseSet/SubcubeFree`, `DNF`, `Parity`, `SigmaThree`, `Subformula` and `Ordered/Packing`. Use bibliography-key links in `Ordered/Radix/*`.
- [ ] `QBF.lean` says TQBF's PSPACE-completeness "is not proved here"; point to where it is proved.
- [ ] Remove names made private in items 1 and 2 from the module docs.

*Risk:* none.

### 8. `test(logics): checked examples for untested modules` (tests) — #619

- [x] Write nonvacuous examples for the modules no test references:
  - `ClauseSet/Basic`, as a round trip through `CNF.toClauseSet`;
  - `CNF/Parity`, with `parityOnEq` on a small set;
  - `Subformula`.

  Also add direct examples of `DNF.eval_negate` and of `QBF.eval` on a closed formula. The sparsification step, path and tree modules are covered through the `CNF.sparsification` tests. `Ordered/Multiplication/*` and `Ordered/Radix/*` are covered through the formulas built on them.

*Benefit:* the guide can reuse the examples. *Risk:* none.

### 9. Later or conditional

- [ ] **Narrow `@[expose]`:** all 515 public definitions are exposed. Follow #584's policy and its measurement of which bodies clients unfold. This pairs with making private the definitions that appear only in exposed bodies (gadget tags, `Coord`, templates).
- [ ] **CSLib's `InferenceSystem` for resolution:** an instance whose derivations are the `Type`-valued tree-like `CNF.Derivation`, as CSLib's logics README asks, with `CNF.Derives φ c ↔ DerivableIn …`. The review settles a design question: keep `CNF.Derives` as the `Prop` inductive, or define it as derivability.
- [ ] **Other upstream reuse:** build `ESO.isStrictLinearOrderSentence` from Mathlib's `Relations.irreflexive` and `Relations.transitive`, with their `realize_*` lemmas. Consider CSLib's `HasAnd`, `HasOr` and `HasNot` notation classes for `QBF`.
- [ ] **`tupleIndex`:** it is `finFunctionFinEquiv`. Restate its generic lemmas (`tupleIndex_lt_iff`, `tupleIndex_lt_pow_iff`, `tupleIndex_eq_of_high_zero`) for `finFunctionFinEquiv` in Foundations, as Mathlib candidates. The clients are in Fagin and LogSpace (cross-area).
- [ ] **Order-free reductions:** `FO.Reduces`, `FO.QFReduces` and `FO.ReducesNontrivial` repeat one definition and its `refl`/`trans`/`compl` proofs. `ROADMAP.md` records them as deliberately outside `ManyOneReducibleBy`, so factor out a shared core only if the guide chapter shows friction.
- [ ] **Outlier proofs:**
  - `ColoringReduction.colorOf_ne_of_edge` (84 lines) repeats one within-gadget step eight times.
  - `DepthThree.card_isolatedInputs_mul_min_le` (116 lines) and `Ordered/Multiplication.packedFormula_complete` (99 lines) are the longest.

  Shorten them when a reusable lemma emerges, not for the line count.
- [ ] **Guide chapters (#585), after M0:** proof complexity (resolution, Haken, size–width) and descriptive complexity (interpretations, ESO, Fagin).

**Abstract impact.** The Cook–Levin, TQBF, Fagin and Resolution abstracts depend on this area through `CNF`, `QBF`, `ESO.Definable`, `CNF.IsProof`, `CNF.RefutableInSize` and the pigeonhole results. None of the planned changes renames or restates a declaration they use. Each PR records its own assessment.

issue.title: feat(parameterized): Buss polynomial kernel for vertex cover
issue.body:
## Scope

Prove that Vertex Cover parameterized by the target size `k` has a **polynomial kernel** (`Cslib.Complexity.HasPolyKernel`), via Buss's kernel [DowneyFellows1999, Section 3.1], [FlumGrohe2006, Section 9.1], [CyganEtAl2015, Section 2.2.1]. This strengthens the existing `VertexCover_hasKernel` (arbitrary size bound, from the Cai–Chen–Downey–Fellows equivalence) to an explicit polynomial bound. The ROADMAP lists "explicit polynomial kernels (e.g. Buss's kernel for Vertex Cover)" as outstanding.

Planned endpoints (exact statements recorded in the PR):

1. Buss reduction rules on the existing `Graph × ℕ` instances of `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/VertexCover.lean`: a vertex of degree `> k` must be in every cover of size `≤ k`; after exhausting high-degree vertices, a yes-instance has at most `k²` edges (and `≤ k² + k` non-isolated vertices); isolated vertices are removed; vertex names are relabelled to small indices so the encoded length is bounded by a polynomial in `k`.
2. Membership preservation `K a ∈ VertexCover ↔ a ∈ VertexCover`, encoded-length and parameter bounds by an explicit polynomial `g`.
3. A polynomial-time certificate `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime K enc enc`, using `polytime`/`fun_prop` where possible. Automation gaps met here are recorded (and fixed with regression tests when small and reusable).
4. `VertexCover_hasPolyKernel`.

## Completion criteria

- Public theorems with docstrings and citations; nonvacuous tests in `ComplexityTests/`; `#print axioms` guard for the headline result.
- All six checks pass; theorem-index entry added/updated; ROADMAP updated; independent correctness/API/index reviews requested from a coordinator.

issue.title: feat(fo): ordered first-order reductions are logspace reductions, on a uniform many-one core
issue.body:
Closes milestones 1 and 2 of #309 (milestone 3 migrations stay open; recorded in `ROADMAP.md`).

## Summary

**Ordered first-order reductions are logspace reductions** — `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.Reduces.logSpaceReducible`, with `L`/`P` closure of encoded ordered queries (Immerman, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 3.10).

- **Many-one core** (`Reduction/ManyOne.lean`): `ManyOneReducibleBy Good A B` with `refl`/`trans` from identity/composition closure, `mono`, `compl` and `lift` (transfer along partial decodings), plus generic `HardUnder`/`CompleteUnder`. `PolyTimeReducible`/`LogSpaceReducible` keep their literal `∃` bodies with `Iff.rfl` bridges, so `⟨f, by fun_prop, h⟩` still elaborates without `beta_reduce` (regression-tested); `PolyTimeHard`/`LogSpaceHard`/`…Complete` are `HardUnder`/`CompleteUnder` instances, definitionally their previous statements.
- **Level 1, semantic map** (`Ordered/DomainInterpretation*.lean`): ordered interpretations with a domain formula; image = φ₀-tuples, lexicographically ordered, renumbered by rank. Admissible when every image has ≥ 2 elements — the library's convention after Proviso 1.15 (Immerman's Definition 1.26 does not discuss smaller domains). Encoded map, partial decoding, and the decoding commutation consumed by `lift`.
- **Level 2, `≤_fo`** (`Ordered/DomainInterpretation/Certificate.lean`, `Composition.lean`, `Ordered/Reduction.lean`): numeric certificates (formulas defining the image's ≤, BIT, 0/1/max — Remark 1.32's requirement; without φ₀ ≡ true BIT need not be definable, per the paragraph after Exercise 1.33). `Ordered.Reduces` with `refl`, `trans` (certified composition, Proposition 1.28 / Exercise 2.15(1)), `compl`, `Definable.of_reduces`; full-tuple interpretations embed with their native certificate (`FullTupleInterpretation.reduces`).
- **One domain-counting transducer** (`LogSpace/FirstOrder/Transducer.lean`), parametrized by a `FormulaCompiler`, computes order-free interpretations, ordered interpretations with a domain formula (new: `DomainInterpretation.computableInLogSpace_encodedMap`), and full-tuple interpretations as the `domain = ⊤` instance. The old order-free and full-tuple programs are deleted (all private). Both logspace theorems are direct `ManyOneReducibleBy.lift` applications through one simulation lemma; the level-1 theorem needs no certificate (ranks are computed by counting).

Size: 23 files, +3459/−1313 (`Complexity/` +2742/−1285, tests +577). The three transducer files went 1414 → 1349 lines while gaining restricted domains; the rest is new semantics, the core and tests.

## Preserved API

No public declaration on `main` was removed or renamed. Statements unchanged: `PolyTimeReducible`, `LogSpaceReducible`, `PolyTime/LogSpace{Hard,Complete}` (definitionally), `FO.Interpretation.computableInLogSpace_encodedMap`, `FO.Reduces.logSpaceReducible`/`queryLanguage_mem_L`/`_mem_P`, `FullTupleInterpretation.computableInLogSpace_encodedMap`/`mem_queryLanguage_encodedMap_iff`/`logSpaceReducible_onSentence`, `Vocabulary.decoded_encode`.

## Limitations

Fixed vocabularies and interpretation; relational targets; lexicographic image order (Remark 1.32's default). Certificates are supplied explicitly; the library builds them for full-tuple interpretations of positive dimension, the identity, and certified composites. The certified restricted-domain test client has ranks equal to a coordinate; an input-dependent domain covers the level-1 logspace claim. Projections, completeness results and the remaining reduction-notion migrations are out of scope.

## Validation

`scripts/check.sh` on code revision `834487c0`: build `--wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, test `--wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports` — all ok. Headline theorems' axioms: `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` (guards in `ComplexityTests/OrderedFOReduction.lean`, `ComplexityTests/ManyOne.lean`, `ComplexityTests/OrderedReduction.lean`). Paper builds locally (`scripts/build_paper.py`); entries on pages 19–21 fit; 28/28 links verified at their revisions. The only overfull vbox (page 100) predates this change.

## Theorem index

New entry "Ordered first-order reductions are logspace reductions"; "Canonical full-tuple ordered interpretations as logspace transducers" and "Order-free interpretations induce logspace reductions" updated (shared transducer; links repointed to `834487c0`); stale "restricted-domain … remain open" sentence in the preceding entry fixed. ## Reviews (all independent of authoring; AI reviewers)

Authoring: main session `claude-opus-5-5-48cb80c1` (core, headline corollaries, integration, roadmap/index draft) and delegated worker subagents (PolyTime/LogSpace migration; ordered semantics; transducer unification; fix batch). An Immerman fact-check subagent checked Definitions 1.26/2.11, Proviso 1.15, Remark 1.32, Exercise 1.33, Propositions 1.28/3.5/3.10, Exercise 2.15 and Theorem 3.1 against the hosted chapters.

issue.title: feat(counting): define MAJSAT and prove PP-completeness
issue.body:
## Scope

Extend `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/CountingSAT.lean` with `MAJSAT` and its `PP`-completeness [Gill 1977; Simon 1975; Arora–Barak 2009, Chapter 17]:

1. **Definition of `MAJSAT`**:
   - Define `MAJSAT : Set (CNF ℕ) := {φ | 2 ^ φ.vars.toFinset.card < 2 * SharpSAT φ}` (CNF formulas satisfied by strictly more than half of the truth assignments to their occurring variables).

2. **Membership `MAJSAT_mem_PP : MAJSAT ∈ PP encCNF`**:
   - Certify that the occurring-variable count `φ ↦ φ.vars.toFinset.card` is polynomial-time computable in unary (`encCNF → encUnary`) via `SharpSAT.isFirst`, so `φ ↦ 2 ^ φ.vars.toFinset.card` is in `SharpP encCNF` via `binary_two_pow` and `SharpP.of_polyTime`.
   - Combine with `SharpSAT_mem_SharpP`, `SharpP.mul`, and `mem_PP_of_lt` to obtain `MAJSAT ∈ PP encCNF`.

3. **Hardness and completeness `MAJSAT_ppHard : PolyTimeHard PP encCNF MAJSAT` and `MAJSAT_ppComplete : PolyTimeComplete PP encCNF MAJSAT`**:
   - Construct a polynomial-time many-one reduction from `SharpSATAtLeast` to `MAJSAT` (using a fresh selector variable combining `φ` with a threshold CNF on `φ`'s occurring variables that has a prescribed number of satisfying assignments) and compose with `SharpSATAtLeast_ppHard`.

## Completion Criteria
- Zero `sorry`, zero custom `axiom`, zero `native_decide`.
- Nonvacuous test coverage and named `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/CountingSAT.lean`.
- All 6 validation checks in `scripts/check.sh` pass.
- Update `ROADMAP.md` and `paper/sections/randomness.tex` + `paper/main.pdf`.
- Independent cslib-style API review, mathematical correctness review, and theorem-index review.

issue.title: feat(ram): certify encoded primitives with native resource bounds
issue.body:
Adds native TM certificates for the scalar primitives of a generic RAM model, as the model layer of #292. Each fixed symbol has one machine handling every encoded configuration and operand tuple. The certificate records arbitrary input-dependent time/space bounds and charges output length; forgetting bounds yields exactly native computability, while polynomial time follows only under separate polynomial-bound hypotheses.

The bundle covers checked literals/ALU results, optional Boolean tests, address conversion, move validity and PC validity. Checked results are connected to existing instruction evaluation, preserving faults. A complete bounded-natural addition/order model instantiates every field. A separate checked standard WordRAM-add certificate handles all unary-encoded widths with binary operands. Both reuse Christian Reitwiessner's native arithmetic/encoding calculus.

This does not certify memory access, arbitrary-program dispatch, complete RAM steps/runs, the full standard word basis, or exact real values as bit strings. Configuration encoding remains selectable. Input-only complexity results still require charged computable width selection and input fit. Sparse memory is #293; the fixed-program step interpreter is #298.

issue.title: perf(build): reduce cache invalidation from growing hub modules
issue.body:
Build caches, both Lake's local artifact cache and CI, are invalidated mostly by growth of a few widely imported general-purpose modules. Under the module system, proof-only edits don't rebuild dependents, but adding *any* declaration to a module changes its public interface, and every module downstream rebuilds even when none of them uses the new declaration.

Measured on `main` (`ba134c18`), counting 1,850 library modules: downstream modules (transitive importers) × edits in the last four days.

| Module | Downstream | Edits |
|---|---|---|
| `Foundations/Data/List/Basic` | 550 | 14 |
| `Foundations/Data/BitString/List` | 462 | 9 |
| `Probability/PMF` | 455 | 8 |
| `Foundations/Data/BitString/Basic` | 689 | 3 |
| `Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Plain` | 387 | 4 |

Each `List/Basic` addition invalidates about 30% of the library.

**Plan (separate PRs):**
1. **Guidance.** Amend AGENTS.md "Placement and reuse": place new general lemmas in the lowest suitable *narrow* module (a small topic file imported by its consumers), not by appending to a widely imported hub. Mention the `@[expose]` cost as well: exposed definition bodies are part of the interface.
2. **Split `Foundations/Data/List/Basic`** into topic modules. Keep `List/Basic` as a thin re-export for compatibility, and repoint the heavy consumers to the narrow modules. Record the before/after downstream counts in the PR.
3. Then do the same for `BitString/List` and `Probability/PMF`, if (2) shows a real reduction.

**Done when:** the guidance has landed, and each split PR shows reduced downstream fan-out for typical additions, with declaration names preserved (re-export or deprecated aliases) and the six gates passing. This is infrastructure, not mathematics; it makes no claim about build speed beyond the measured fan-out.

Available. Analysis by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` at Samuel's request.

feat(ram): transport algorithm certificates through parameterized RAM and TM simulations
issue.body:
Samuel's explicit architectural direction (2026-10-21): make WordRAM a productive frontend for native Turing-machine complexity proofs, retaining sharp RAM bounds while transporting correctness/resources through reusable checked simulations.

Three separate obligations:
1. Model certificates: effective word/address encodings, each primitive's checked implementation and parameterized time/space costs. Support integer, finite-field and other effectively encodable RAM models; computable primitives give computability, efficient primitives give correspondingly efficient complexity. No unconditional TM simulation of arbitrary exact reals.
2. Backend simulations: implement control flow and random-access memory on the existing RAM/multitape TM backends. Explicitly account for initialization, addressing/search/update, word width/encoding length, memory usage and output. Uniform finite programs and their data dependence must be stated. Reuse existing WordRAM/RAM adapters, generic RAM, FreeM and native TM resource calculus.
3. Automatic transport: combine an algorithm's certificate with model/backend certificates into native RAM/TM theorems usable via polytime and resource rules. Interfaces carry parameterized resource bounds; polynomial corollaries are derived specializations, not baked-in assumptions.

Completion requires nonvacuous checked backend instances and end-to-end example algorithms, not merely a structure that assumes the desired simulation. Split independently useful implementation milestones with explicit dependencies, preserve current RAM exact bounds, and retain all initialization/representation/controller boundaries until proved. Include negative/unsupported-model tests, source credit, six gates, exact independent API/correctness/index review and theorem-index scope.

Existing #289 queue and #290 BST proceed independently; #273 vEB owner retained.
