issue.title: ci(docs): publish the API documentation to GitHub Pages
issue.body:
Publishes the doc-gen4 API documentation to GitHub Pages at https://www.cslib.io/complexitylib/ and points README "Start here" at its search. The organisation's Pages domain applies, so `cslib-community.github.io/complexitylib/` redirects there. Until now, users looking for a definition or tool were sent to `Complexity.lean`, a flat list of about 1,870 imports; `Complexity.lean` stays linked for the full module list. This is item 1 of #578, which Samuel approved there. Infrastructure and documentation only: no Lean changes, no mathematical progress, and no effect on the abstracts catalogue.

**Workflow.** `docs.yml` keeps its build and the `check_docs.py` gate. It then checks the site size and uploads the Pages artifact. A separate `deploy` job runs `configure-pages` and `deploy-pages` into the `github-pages` environment, only for builds of `main`. That job alone has `pages: write` and `id-token: write`; the build job keeps `contents: read`. The three Pages actions are pinned to full commit SHAs (configure-pages v6.0.0, upload-pages-artifact v5.0.0, deploy-pages v5.0.1). A manual run on another branch builds and checks the docs, uploads `api-docs` as before, and skips the deploy job. Pull requests don't trigger the workflow, so they can't deploy.

**Triggers.** Nightly (03:17 UTC) and `workflow_dispatch`, without `push`. `main` received 64 pushes in the 24 hours before this PR and a build takes about an hour, so nearly every push-triggered build would be cancelled by the next merge after spending most of a runner-hour. Nightly keeps the site at most a day behind; a dispatch on `main` refreshes it at once. A per-ref `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: true` lets a newer build supersede an older one, so only the latest build of `main` deploys.

**Size: the main limitation.** Pages caps a published site at 1 GB, and the docs are close to it. The 22 October build (1,647 modules, run 39794423110) is 55 MB compressed but 962,395,848 bytes uncompressed in 8,260 files: Mathlib pages 570 MB, `Complexity` 106 MB, Std 94 MB, Init 74 MB, the search index 48 MB and Lean 46 MB. The 18 October build (703 modules) was 807 MB. The validation run below (current `main`, 1,874 modules) measured 973,243,475 bytes: 90.6 % of 1 GiB, about 100 MB of headroom. `main` gained about 135 modules a day over the past three days, roughly 6.5 MB a day at the recent per-module cost, so at that pace the limit is about two weeks away, sooner if new modules pull in more of Mathlib. The workflow fails before deploying if the site exceeds 1 GiB (the value `deploy-pages` uses for "1 GB"), warns above 90 %, and writes the size to the job summary; after a failed run Pages keeps serving the previous deployment. Keeping the site under the limit needs a follow-up. Measured options: `DISABLE_EQUATIONS=1` removes about 48 MB (equation blocks), and dropping the 829 Lean/Std/Lake modules outside the library's import closure (doc-gen4 always documents them) about 37 MB. Together they would add about two more weeks at that pace. A lasting fix would link Mathlib declarations to an external Mathlib docs site instead of hosting its 570 MB of pages, or host the docs somewhere without the 1 GB cap.

**Subpath and search.** No base-path setting is needed. Every page sets a relative `SITE_ROOT`, the search index stores relative `docLink`s (all 320,004 entries), and a scan of the 3.9 million `href`/`src` attributes found no root-relative links. The leanprover-community `mathlib4_docs` site runs the same doc-gen4 `search.js` and `declaration-data.js` (byte-identical) from a Pages subpath, and its `.//declarations/declaration-data.bmp` request resolves there. Two small caveats are unrelated to the subpath. `404.html` uses relative asset paths, so it is unstyled when GitHub serves it for a missing deep URL. And 404 links on 323 library pages already point at pages that don't exist, wherever the site is hosted, for example `Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime.html` → `Cslib/Tactic/PolyTime.html`.

**Pages enablement.** Enabled at 23:28 UTC on 23 October with `POST /pages build_type=workflow`, after the validation run passed; nothing blocked it. That also created the `github-pages` environment with a deployment branch policy allowing only `main`, so a branch run could not deploy even without the job condition. I also turned on "Enforce HTTPS", matching the organisation's other Pages sites (AlgoLib, CSwL, fad, bignum). The site returns 404 until the first deployment, from the first nightly run or a dispatch on `main` after merge.

**Validation.** [Run 40033874751](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033874751) (`workflow_dispatch` on e95f28b3) passed in 59 minutes. It covered the docs build, `check_docs.py` (1,874 modules), the size check with the expected 90 % warning, the `api-docs` artifact (56.5 MB) and the `github-pages` artifact (49.3 MB). The deploy job was skipped, as intended for a branch. The later commit e1787207 changes only the URL in the README and a workflow comment. `actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0 reports no findings for `docs.yml`. `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only` and the script unit tests pass. The deploy path (`configure-pages`, `deploy-pages`) can only run from `main`, so it will first run on the first nightly or `main` dispatch after merge.

Refs #578; its other items remain open.

issue.title: refactor(machines): spike, plain closure rules without a tidy calculus (#862)
issue.body:
**Spike — not for merge.** Evidence for #862: can the tidy computability *calculus* be deleted, with each plain closure rule proved directly and tidiness used only as a machine-level construction inside proofs? Verdict and analysis are in the #862 report; this PR holds the prototype so CI checks it.

The new modules prove plain closure rules from plain hypotheses. Each proof unpacks the plain machines, makes them tidy with the tidy normal form (`ComputesInTimeAndSpace.computesTidily_tidy`), combines them with the existing machine combinators, and concludes plain computability. None of these modules imports a tidy asymptotic predicate: `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, `…InO`, `…InDegree` and the rest are not in their environment. They add no public tidy statement, and the tidy-statement ratchet still matches its baseline.

- `…/Complexity/PlainDirect/PolyTime.lean`: `ComputableInPolyTime` composition, pairing for any `PairEncoding`, `if` on a plain Boolean test in any encoding, left folds, and pair projections. Composition is entirely machine-level (`ComputesTidilyInTimeAndSpace.comp`). Pairing, `if` and folds call the explicit-bound combinators `PairEncoding.pair_mono`, `ComputableTidilyInTimeAndSpace.ite` and `.foldl` with anonymous machine constructors.
- `…/PlainDirect/BigO.lean`: `ComputableInO` composition and `if`, with exactly the bounds of the tidy rules. The `3 s` that the normal form adds to time is absorbed by applying it with space `min s (k t + k)`.
- `…/PlainDirect/Degree.lean`: `ComputableInDegree` composition, with the tidy rule's degrees `max d₁ (e₁ d₂)` and `e₁ e₂`.
- `ComplexityTests/PlainDirect.lean`:
  - checks that no tidy predicate is in scope;
  - registers the direct rules with `attribute [local fun_prop]` and closes goals borrowed from `PolyTimePlain.lean`, including that test's negative control;
  - proves the parity of a word with the direct fold rule;
  - composes upstream's untidy copy machine with itself under the `O` and degree rules.

Validation: all six gates passed locally (`scripts/check.sh`, as a full check because `Complexity.lean` changed) on the first commit before a rebase. `scripts/check_tidy_surface.py` reports 1887 statements, matching the baseline. After rebasing onto main `7f8c7d06` (head `e3df3ca7`), `mk_all --check` passes and the prototype and test modules were rebuilt; hosted CI covers the full gates. Every new declaration depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The **PR title** check fails by design: `spike` is not an allowed type, and the title marks this as not for merge.

Abstracts: no impact (new local-only spike modules; no selected statement changes).

issue.title: refactor(classes): state the Classes area plainly (#456 S2)
issue.body:
Plain-first sweep (#456), **Classes** area. Every public statement under `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/**` and the PCP, Communication, DecisionTree, QueryComplexity, TreeEval, Kolmogorov, MCSP, USTCON, Languages and MachineLearning trees now states plain computability. This S2 stage retains tidy computability inside proofs under the in-progress sweep guidance in #862; S4 tracks its later removal outside the internal machine library. The only exceptions are the 5 case-1 originals that the design leaves for S1/S3.

**Queue note.** The tool output here was regenerated on `main` `e863ee37`, which includes #855 (plain captured-map callbacks), and the hand commits were replayed. One replay conflict needed resolving: `mem_BPP_iff_exists_mem_BPTIME` now passes the plain verifier straight to #855's `map_with`. The branch was then rebased over #853 and #856. Those touch no file the sweep changes apart from `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean`, which merges cleanly, so the tool output would be the same.

## Counts

| | Before (`main`) | After |
|---|--:|--:|
| `check_tidy_surface`, modules in the area | 589 statements in 179 modules | 5 in 3 modules |
| `tidy_sweep.py report --area Classes` | 588 | 5 (all case 1, plain twin exists) |

`scripts/tidy_surface_baseline.json` is lowered with `--update`: 179 entries, 584 statements (1886 → 1302 in total). No other area's entries change. The remaining 5 are `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_compl`, `computableTidilyInPolyTime_{and,or,select}Verifier` (SharpP/Combinators) and `Toda.computableTidilyInPolyTime_sharpTest`. Each has a committed plain twin that `fun_prop` uses. The originals are left for S1/S3 to internalize, as the tool's case 1 says, and module docs now list the twins.

## Tool plan (fresh base)

| Area | Total | (1) Plain twin | (2) Rename and restate | (3) Definition or field | Unclassifiable |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Classes | 588 | 5 | 548 | 0 | 35 |

Unclassifiable: 32 bridges, 2 unsupported notion (`ComputableTidilyInBigO`) and 1 tidy notion definition (`ComputableTidilyInFPTTime`). These are the 35 boundary obligations below.

**How it was run.** `rewrite --area Classes --verify --rounds 8` was run through a thin wrapper around `tidy_sweep.py`. The wrapper retains the tool's normal collision and binding checks. It renames mechanical-conversion gaps and reports them for manual repair instead of deferring whole declarations; the field fallback requires a unique target suffix among existing constants. Its bridge-planning adjustment creates local transitions only for the recognized polynomial-time and polynomial-space properties. Run strictly, the tool would leave 100 declarations tidy only because of how they are called. The wrapper's result: 548 case-2 declarations, of which 16 were deferred, 205 translated and 327 wrapped. The frozen `run10.json` records 72 imports, 147 round trips removed, 88 local transitions, and 221 sites for hand fixes. Intermediate tool verification stopped after round 8; the manual repairs and final-head checks below complete validation:

| Lenient site (primary category) | Count |
|---|--:|
| conclusion that is not a bare predicate | 102 |
| partial application | 84 |
| dot notation on a tidy receiver | 24 |
| field notation whose binding the tool cannot establish | 6 |
| tactic lemma list | 3 |
| tidy hypothesis under binders | 2 |

## Commits

1. `refactor: state PCP verifier component efficiency plainly` and `refactor: simplify PCP abstract bridge over plain verifier components`. These are **Codex's prepared PCP slice** (`refactor/pcp-plain-verifier-field-456`, `f4e24754` and `440a91c5`), cherry-picked with `-x`. They keep the PCP definition's three plain predicates and its binary coin and query encodings.
2. `restate the Classes certificates plainly (tool output)`: the rewrite, unchanged. It does not build on its own.
3. `hand-complete the Classes restatement`: the manual fixes below, the FPT and BigO boundary, and the ESO layout declarations.
4. `restate the remaining deferred Classes certificates`.
5. `retire the class and reduction tidy bridges`.
6. `reflow, review docs and lower the tidy surface baseline`.
7. `follow main's CNF and graph refactors, review module docs`: adapts to #826 and #828 after regenerating.
8. `test(classes): plain fun_prop over restated Classes certificates`.
9. `follow the Wave 5 names and MINKT after regenerating`: adapts to #835 and #817.
10. `follow #843, #844 and #848 after regenerating`. `SharpPWithOracle.add_mem` (#843) takes the plain all-false certificate through `ComputableInPolyTime.computableInPolyTimeWithOracle`. The ETH lower bounds of #844 use plain certificates. The TreeEval instantiation tests of #848 instantiate the plain `ComputableInBigO` endpoints, with plain `ComputesInTimeAndSpace`.

## Samples of statement changes

```lean
-- Classes/Space/Closure.lean (acceptance criteria of #580)
theorem mem_PSPACE_iff_computableInPolySpace : A ∈ PSPACE enc ↔
    ∃ f : α → Bool, ComputableInPolySpace f enc encBool ∧ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a = true
theorem setOf_exists_mem_PSPACE … (hℓ : ComputableInPolyTime ℓ encB encUnary) …

-- Parameterized.lean (was ComputableTidilyInFPTTime.comp)
theorem ComputableInFPTTime.comp {f : α → β} {g : β → γ}
    (hg : ComputableInFPTTime g encB encC κB) (hf : ComputableInFPTTime f encA encB κA)
    {h : ℕ → ℕ} (hκ : ∀ a, κB (f a) ≤ h (κA a)) : ComputableInFPTTime (g ∘ f) encA encC κA

-- USTCON/Space.lean (was computableTidilyInBigO_decide; same bounds, output still uncharged)
theorem computableInBigO_decide : ∃ t, ComputableInBigO
    (fun I : USTCONInstance ↦ decide (I ∈ USTCON)) encUSTCON encBool t
    fun I ↦ Nat.log2 (encUSTCON I).length + 1

-- Classes/SharpP/Space.lean (deferred by the tool, restated by hand)
theorem SharpP.computableInPolySpace (hf : f ∈ SharpP enc) : ComputableInPolySpace f enc encNat

-- Classes/Space/Closure.lean (was …computableTidilyInO…)
theorem mem_PSPACE_iff_computableInO : A ∈ PSPACE enc ↔ ∃ (f : α → Bool) (T S : α → ℕ),
    ComputableInO f enc encBool T S ∧ PolyBounded (fun a => (enc a).length) S ∧
      ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ f a = true
```

## The 35 boundary obligations: 8 FPT, 3 uncharged BigO, 24 bridges

**FPT (8).** The raw tidy definition `ComputableTidilyInFPTTime` is removed, with its seven bridges: `ComputableInFPTTime.tidy`, `.of_tidy`, `ComputableTidilyInFPTTime.computableInFPTTime`, `computableInFPTTime_iff_computableTidilyInFPTTime`, `computableInFPTWithParam_iff_tidy`, `fptReducible_iff_tidy` and `isKernelization_iff_tidy`. As Codex asked, the canonical Type*-generic `ComputableInFPTTime` and its time-only constructor `ComputableInTimeAndSpace.computableInFPTTime` are reused unchanged, not renamed. They keep one uniform machine, arbitrary parameter-growth functions and a fixed input-length exponent. The closure rules become plain and stay over `Type`, as the closure theorems are:

- `ComputableInFPTTime.ite` and `ComputableInFPTTime.comp`
- `ComputableInPolyTime.computableInFPTTime`
- `ComputableInO.computableInFPTTime`
- `mem_FPT_iff_computableInFPTTime`

The tidy normal form survives only in two private helpers. `IsKernelization` is unchanged and keeps both its encoded-length and its parameter bounds. `IsKernelization.mem_FPT` now goes through the plain `ComputableInO.computableInFPTTime`.

**Uncharged BigO (3).** `TreeEval.computableInSpace_eval`, `TreeEval.computableInSpace_eval_log_mul_log_log` and `USTCON.computableInBigO_decide` stated `ComputableTidilyInBigO`. They now state plain `ComputableInBigO` with the same bounds. Time and workspace stay independent, and the output is still not charged.

- *Bound-sensitive classification:* migrated to plain. The bounds are about the algorithms (Cook–Mertz, Reingold), not about the tidy machinery.
- *Overhead:* none, since tidy implies plain at the same bound (`ComputableTidilyInBigO.computableInBigO`).
- The TreeEval subtype and zero cases are unchanged, and `computableInLogSpace_decide` keeps USTCON's `2 * c` logspace conversion.

**Bridges (24).** All are removed, with no aliases and no private escape:

- `mem_X_iff_tidy` for twenty classes: `P`, `NP`, `BPP`, `RP`, `ZPP`, `PP`, `SBP`, `MA`, `AM`, `SharpP`, `WPP`, `LWPP`, `SigmaP`, `PiP`, `FNP`, `FPSearch`, `PLS`, `PPP`, `PPAD`, `PPA`
- `polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy`, `parsimoniousReducible_iff_tidy`, `polyTimeTruthTableReducible_iff_tidy` and `searchReducible_iff_tidy`

The classes and reductions are already stated plainly. Their clients end tidy constructions with `.of_tidy`, or take `.tidy` of a plain component after destructuring. Module docs no longer list the bridges.

## Other bound-sensitive and machine-level statements

No other public statement in the area changes its bound. The `ComputableInO`, `ComputableInSpace` and `ComputableInPolySpace` restatements keep their bounds, through the same-bound equivalences.

Seven statements remain about a given tidy machine's run, so they are genuinely about the tidy machinery. They are kept and are candidates for the machine layer, which this PR does not touch. They are outside `check_tidy_surface`'s count:

- on `ComputesFunTidilyInTimeAndSpace`: `CookLevin.reduce_mem_SAT_iff_of_computesTidily`, the two `Fagin` strict-verifier tableau lemmas, `Alternation.gameReduce_mem_TQBF_iff` and `TQBF.reduce_mem_TQBF_iff`
- `TreeEval.Reader.tidy_machine` and `USTCON.Reader.tidy_machine`

## Manual fixes, and why

- **The 221 lenient sites.** Fixed at the argument with `.tidy` or `.of_tidy`, a mechanical pass driven by the `Application type mismatch` diagnostics. Where `(lemma …).tidy` blocked elaboration of the expected type, the explicit form `ComputableInPolyTime.tidy (lemma (.of_tidy h))` is used.
- **Tidy `fun_prop` that relied on a rule the sweep made plain.** Tidy `fun_prop` cannot use plain composition rules, and the local transition `ComputableInPolyTime.tidy` can send it into an exponential search. There are three fixes:
  - explicit `have h := X.tidy` certificates;
  - 48 private `@[local fun_prop]` *tidy views* proved from the plain rules, in 10 files: IP/TQBF/Verifier, GeneralizedGeography/Reduction, HardnessEncoding/PolyTime, Ladner, BussKernel, Toda/Hierarchy, ArthurMerlin/GraphNonIsomorphism, Alternation/TQBF and Crypto GMW PolyTime/Simulator;
  - where a rule's own module still composes it tidily, the tidy statement stays a private lemma with `attribute [local fun_prop]`, and the public rule is derived from it by `.of_tidy`.

  The Crypto GMW files change only by proof-local views, with no statement change.
- **A private global `@[fun_prop]`.** `bool_or'` in `Problems/Graph.lean` is now `attribute [local fun_prop]`. A private declaration with a global `fun_prop` attribute breaks `fun_prop` in importing modules ("Unknown constant `_private…`") once their goals reach it.
- **`fun_prop` timeouts.** These were in Space/TQBF/Prenex, AffineDisperser and the PCP preprocess and Cook–Levin tests. `trace.Meta.Tactic.fun_prop` traced each to a missing rule, which is now supplied explicitly, for example `CookLevin.computableInPolyTime_cert`.
- **The 16 tool-deferred declarations are restated by hand.** These are the three FPT ones, the three ESO layout rules, `ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle.computableInPolyTime` and `.exists_computableInO`, `DecidableInTimeO.exists_computableInO`, `{Time,Space}Constructible.computableInO`, `Interaction.computableInPolySpace_evaluate`, `{SharpP,GapP}.computableInPolySpace`, `ComputableInO.computableInPolyTime_take` and `ComputableInPolyTime.bitsEnumList_of_polyBounded`.
- **Name resolution.** Inside `PolyTimeReducible.mem_NP` and its siblings, a bare `mem_NP` resolves to the declaration being defined, so these are qualified as `Complexity.mem_NP`. `bitsEnumList` is also qualified.
- **Imports.** `BigO.Plain` and `PolySpace.Plain` are added where the new conversions need them, in addition to the tool-recorded imports.
- **`SAT.polyTimeReducible_CircuitSAT`.** Its private certificate is now plain, so the reduction has no `.of_tidy`.
- **Tests.**
  - 160 test lines are restated plainly with unchanged proofs.
  - Axiom guards follow the renames. Where a shorter name now fits on one line, the guard is `whitespace := lax`.
  - The `mem_PPAD` bridge test is removed.
- **Docs and line length.** The 30 docstrings the tool flagged are reworded, module "Main results" sections list plain certificates, and the tool-flagged long lines are reflowed.

## Deferred

Nothing in the area is deferred, and no statement is weakened. The 5 case-1 originals remain by design.

## Framework friction (#733)

- **Tidy `fun_prop` cannot consume plain rules.** Every restated `@[fun_prop]` rule that tidy proofs elsewhere still compose needs a local view or a `.tidy` certificate, which accounts for the 48 views and the additional local transitions. Adding `ComputableInPolyTime.tidy` as a `fun_prop` transition can loop or time out. Suggested fix: the checked plain calculus mirror (#671), so these proofs can move to plain `fun_prop` and the views can go.
- **Private `@[fun_prop]` breaks importers.** This is worth a lint or a note in the guide.
- **Plain-rule integration follow-ups for the existing proof-local workarounds:**
  - `ComputableInPolyTime.isPPTOn` is now available on main from #813 (Promise/Reduction).
  - #864 supplies `ComputableInPolyTime.intBin_mul'` (Int/Binary; WPP products) and `MultiTapePTM.exists_computableInO_run` (Oracle/Space); its source is independently approved with green CI, and its test-import conflict refresh is pending.
  - These existing sweep wrappers are permitted by #862's current guidance; later collapse work can consume the shared plain providers.
- **Tool gaps.** The tool's conversion gaps (221 lenient sites) and its `(lemma …).tidy` form, which can block expected-type elaboration.

## Automation parity

- 160 test-statement lines in 90 test files moved from tidy to plain goals, and the same `fun_prop`, `polytime` or term proofs close them.
- New client examples: plain `fun_prop` composes the restated Buss-kernel (`high`, `degree`), Sipser–Lautemann (`verifier`) and `Clique.verifier` certificates with plain hypotheses (`ComplexityTests/{VertexCoverKernel,SipserLautemann,NPCompleteness}.lean`).

## Acceptance criteria of the superseded #580 and #626

- **#580 (met).** In `Classes/Space/Closure.lean`, `mem_PSPACE_iff_computableInPolySpace` and `mem_PSPACE_of_computableInPolySpace` are plain, and `setOf_exists_mem_PSPACE` takes a plain `hℓ`.
- **#626 (met).** No `mem_NP` proof or reduction in `Problems/` contains `.of_tidy`. No public statement in the area mentions `.of_tidy` or a tidy predicate outside the case-1 originals and the machine-level statements above. Every "Main results" section lists plain certificates.
- **Outside the rule.** `mem_NP` proofs and reductions outside `Problems/` (Classes, Parameterized, TFNP, Promise, …) still end some tidy constructions with `.of_tidy` inside their proofs, for example `PolyTimeReducible.mem_BPP`. These are proof terms, not statements. Removing them needs plain rules for the tidy combinators they use, which is S1's work.

## Abstract impact

`build_abstracts.py --check` passes (14 abstracts, 19 headline theorems). No headline theorem changes meaning. The only abstract change is Codex's PCP bridge simplification, which removes four `CookLevinBridge.computableInPolyTime_iff_tidy` round trips now that the PCP fields are plain.

## Validation at the head

At `ab874236`, on `main` `68c331e9`:

- `scripts/check.sh`, all six gates: `build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style` and `checkInitImports`.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: all hygiene checks passed.
- `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: passes.
- `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`: 1302 statements in 225 modules, matching the lowered baseline.
- `python3 scripts/tidy_sweep.py report --area Classes`: 5, all case 1.

## Overlap with open PRs (file-overlap check at this head)

- **#852**: `Classes/Promise/Reduction.lean` and the S3 baseline.
- **#866**: `USTCON/Reader/Cert.lean`.
- **#846**: `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean`.
- **#671**: `ComplexityTests/PolyTimePlain.lean`.

Whichever lands first, the other rebases.

Credit: the PCP slice and the inventory of the 35 boundary obligations are Codex's preparation (`codex-audit-prerequisites-provider-608`, coordinated by `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`), handed over on #456 ([comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/456#issuecomment-6386287353)). issue.title: refactor(problems): state per-problem polynomial-time certificates plainly
issue.body:
Found while writing #585's NP-completeness chapter. Each problem's public polynomial-time facts are stated with the tidy proof device rather than plain `ComputableInPolyTime`, for example `Clique.computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifier`, `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_compl` and `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_adjBool`. #587's standard asks for plain computability in user-facing statements, with tidy machines confined to proofs and the combinator layer.

**Evidence (`main` after #559 and #603).** `Problems/` has 96 public theorems named `…computableTidilyInPolyTime_…` across 27 modules, and 38 `.of_tidy` bridges. 19 of the bridges are the same line in `mem_NP`: `⟨Polynomial.X, verifier, .of_tidy computableTidilyInPolyTime_verifier, isVerifier⟩`. A newcomer reading a problem module sees tidy names in its "Main results" and copies the bridge. The guide shows instead that plain `by fun_prop` proves these goals through the tidy-to-plain transition (#612 does this for `Clique.mem_NP`).

**Proposal**, per module in `Computability/Complexity/Problems`:
1. `mem_NP` and reductions prove their cost obligations with `by fun_prop` (or `polytime`), with no `.of_tidy`.
2. Where a problem's verifier or reduction map is API, state a plain certificate (`computableInPolyTime_verifier`, …) and list that in "Main results".
3. Keep the tidy `@[fun_prop]` rules that other tidy proofs compose, such as `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_adjBool`, which `VertexCover`, `Coloring`, `Hamiltonian` and `TSP` use. Drop them from "Main results", and make them `private` where no other module uses them (#584's measurement says which).
4. With #612, definitions written around the missing membership certificate can use `∈` again. For example, `VertexCover.verifier` tests `y.2.any (fun w => decide (w = u))`.

**Done when** no `mem_NP` or reduction in `Problems/` contains `.of_tidy`, and each module's "Main results" lists plain certificates only. This is part of the complexity area's #587 pass; it changes proofs and module docs, not theorem statements of results.

Refs #585, #587. Recorded by `worker-claude-585-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

issue.title: feat(stateful): certify resource bounds across interface refinements
issue.body:
Stateful clients already had separate semantic Hoare rules and per-operation resource bounds, but no client contract that carried a budget through interface implementations. This adds `Spec.CostHoare`, separate `Module.ChargeBound` certificates, and compositional transport through adaptive linking and native realizations.

The `stateful` Aesop rule set supports pure/call contracts and named routine reuse. Intermediate assertions, budgets and implementations are explicit proof inputs. An adaptive counter client is implemented through a mutable cell and paired storage: the zero branch costs seven, the nonzero branch two, and budget six is refuted. A parametric test charges the continuation at its updated state.

This first milestone of #274 follows #160 and supports the architecture intended for #273. Total controller-time certificates, `polytime` integration, argument delivery/decoding and vEB remain subsequent work. The native example is a primitive evidence interpretation, not a newly implemented RAM backend. Existing `WordRAM/Dynamic` realization contracts can supply native-operation bounds separately.

issue.title: feat(crypto): certify native GSW key generation and encryption
issue.body:
Follow-up to #495 and the concrete GSW correctness core in #496; part of #486.

The finite random-input samplers have native certificates, but the modular matrix algorithms that turn those samples into public keys and ciphertexts do not. This task closes that specific efficiency gap and supplies the executable encryption needed by the decision-LWE reduction.

Scope and acceptance:

- Define total serialized public-key, secret-key and ciphertext algorithms with explicit dimension and binary operand encodings. Prove exact bridges to `GSW.publicMatrix` and `GSW.encryptWithCoins`, including bit order, padding/normalization and output framing. Malformed input words must have specified total behavior.
- Certify signed modular reduction for errors and subtraction. Reuse existing binary arithmetic, remainder, bit extraction, range/map and list-index APIs; avoid enumeration of the modulus and fixed-size finite-type certificates as evidence of uniform efficiency.
- Certify the actual public-matrix and encryption computations uniformly over growing unary dimensions and the complete binary inputs. Compose with #495's samplers and exact distribution bridges to certify full probabilistic key generation and encryption.
- Account for complete output lengths, including `N^2` ciphertext bits, where `N=(n+1)*w`. Every input and saved value used in a computation must be charged.
- Exercise negative wraparound, ragged/malformed inputs, zero dimensions, width zero and little-endian bit order. Supply growing-parameter clients and headline axiom guards.
- Pass the six repository checks, obtain independent exact-revision API/correctness review, and assess the formal abstract catalogue. Update the roadmap without claiming decryption, NAND runtime, security or bootstrappability complete.

Source inspection by `/root/maintenance_audit` found existing native arithmetic/list routines sufficient in principle; this is a design assessment, not a completed certificate. Decryption and NAND certification are a following independently reviewable extension using the same routines.

State: available. No implementation owner is claimed by this issue creation. AI-assisted scope recorded by `worker-codex-lwe-design-20261023`.

issue.title: refactor(parameterized): define FPT reductions, kernels and proof systems with plain computability
issue.body:
Milestone M2e of #456. Fpt-reductions, kernelizations and proof systems are now defined with plain computability: `ComputableInFPTTime` from #555 and `ComputableInPolyTime` from #554. Tidy computability is a proof device, so it no longer appears in these definitions. All names are kept, and each definition still unfolds definitionally (`fptReducible_iff_manyOneReducibleBy` is still `Iff.rfl`).

**Public declarations whose shape changed**
- `Cslib.Complexity.ComputableInFPTWithParam` and `Cslib.Complexity.FPTReducible` use `ComputableInFPTTime` instead of `ComputableTidilyInFPTTime`.
- The `IsKernelization.polyTime` field, and so `IsKernelization.mk`, has type `ComputableInPolyTime K enc enc`.
- The `ProofSystem.computable` field, and so `ProofSystem.mk`, has type `ComputableInPolyTime toFun encBits enc`.
- `Cslib.Complexity.ProofSystem.PSimulates` uses `ComputableInPolyTime`.

No other public statement changes.

**Migration lemmas.** `computableInFPTWithParam_iff_tidy`, `fptReducible_iff_tidy`, `isKernelization_iff_tidy` and `ProofSystem.pSimulates_iff_tidy` restate each definition with the tidy notion, so a proof switches with one rewrite. `ProofSystem` holds data, so it gets no iff: proofs use `P.computable.tidy`, and constructions use `h.computableInPolyTime`. The proof fixes are one-step uses of `.tidy`, `.of_tidy` and `.computableInPolyTime`/`.computableInFPTTime`. `hasPolyKernel_of_mem_P` now uses `by fun_prop`, which works whether the `P` decider is tidy or plain.

**Limitations and overlaps**
- Some hypotheses stay tidy and are left for M3: `FPTReducible.of_computableTidilyInPolyTime`, and the verifier hypothesis of `ProofSystem.ofVerifier`, `ofVerifier_frame_append` and `polynomiallyBounded_ofVerifier`. The verifier hypothesis matches `NP`'s current definition.
- #559 (plain `P`/`NP`) edits the same line of `hasPolyKernel_of_mem_P`. Whichever PR lands second keeps this PR's `by fun_prop`. #559's other edits to `ProofSystem.lean`, `Parameterized.lean` and `Kernelization.lean` touch different lines.

**Tests.** Two tests adapted to the new definitions: the Narrow kernel in `ComplexityTests/Parameterized.lean`, and the `FPTReducible` unfolding in `ComplexityTests/ManyOne.lean`, which is now the plain form by `Iff.rfl` plus the tidy form through `fptReducible_iff_tidy`. New clients cover each migration lemma: the identity in fpt time with a parameter bound, Buss's kernelization made tidy, and a p-simulation from a tidy translation.

**Validation.** At `80b1870d`, rebased linearly on `main` @ `ba134c18`: `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates. `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` (89 tests), `scripts/check_hygiene.py` and `scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` also pass. `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` reports one heuristic hit, at `Circuit/Boolean/CarryLookahead.lean:127`. That file is already on `main` (`42412a60`) and outside this diff.

**Abstract impact.** None. No selected abstract or bridge uses these definitions, and `build_abstracts.py --check` passes.

**AI disclosure.** Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5), worker `worker-claude-549-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Not yet independently reviewed.

Closes #549

issue.title: quality(classes): area checklist
issue.body:
Area checklist for #587, owned by `lead-claude-classes-c4b0c164` (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Snapshot: `main` at d52fd12c, with tidy counts rechecked at 014cd572 (after #559).

**Scope (474 modules):**
- `Computability/Complexity/**`, `PCP/**`, `Communication/**`, `DecisionTree/**`, `QueryComplexity/**`, `TreeEval/**`
- `Kolmogorov/**`, `MCSP/**`, `USTCON/**`, `Languages/**`, `MachineLearning/**`
- their tests, abstracts and clients
- `Logics/Propositional/ProofSystem.lean`, which joins the area by agreement on #596 (item 1)

**How the work runs:**
- One bounded, single-theme PR at a time, about 40 files at most.
- No PR edits a file touched by an open PR or by the deprecation sweep.
- Each PR is cross-reviewed by `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`.
- Cross-area changes (marked ↔) are announced on #587 first.
- Renames, moves and privatizations update every in-repo client, with no aliases (#588).
- The area's 131 deprecated declarations are left to the sweep.

Tidy machines leave public statements through #456's mechanical S1–S3 plan, not through hand edits here; see "Statements" below.

## Summary

Hygiene is already good:
- no heartbeat overrides, no bare non-terminal `simp`, and no large terminal `simpa`;
- one tactic-mode definition, plus one tactic-built `Prop` instance;
- every public definition has a docstring;
- every name in a module doc's main lists exists.

Tests are plentiful and mostly nonvacuous.

The gaps:
- **Surface.** 42% of public declarations are referenced by no other module.
- **Tidy statements.** 770 public statements mention a tidy notion, including the definition of `PCP`.
- **Plumbing.** Certificates for problems and reductions are assembled by hand.
- **Parallel developments:**
  - the graph toolkit lives inside `IndependentSet.lean`;
  - there are four "distinct variables" lists;
  - IP and MIP each have their own replay;
  - there are two gap-amplification pipelines;
  - binary and fan-in Tree Evaluation are separate;
  - there is a second sensitivity API.
- **Placement.** Machine, logic and general lemmas sit in class files, and `Inclusions.lean` is a hub.
- **Names.** Certificates and problem lemmas follow several naming schemes.
- **Citations.** Problem and class definitions and headline theorems rarely cite a source.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Public declarations (excluding constructors, recursors and auxiliary declarations) | 6,972 |
| Used by other library modules | 2,500 |
| Used only by tests | 1,366 |
| Used by no other module | 2,900 |
| Automation attribute (`simp`, `fun_prop`, instance), so uses can't be counted | 206 |
| Of the 2,900 unused, not named in any module doc, README, ROADMAP or UPSTREAM | 2,064 (1,716 theorems) |
| Public statements mentioning a tidy notion (at 014cd572) | 770 |
| … with `Tidily` in the name | 432 |
| … referenced by no other module | 437 |
| Public definitions without a docstring | 0 |
| Public theorems without a docstring | 964 (about 80 of them listed as main results) |
| Theorem length: median, 99th percentile, maximum | 8, 80, 246 lines (`realize_layoutESOSentence`) |
| Theorems of at least 100 lines | 28 |
| In Problems: `fun_prop` calls / `polytime` calls / `.comp` and `.prod` steps | 264 / 5 / 219 and 88 |

The counts come from `.ilean` references of the cached build. They will be reconciled with `scripts/quality_report.py` (#604) when it lands.

## Statements: the tidy sweep (#456 S1–S3)

No certificate or result is restated by hand. The scripted S2 rename does that after Machines' plain mirror (S1) lands, and S3 keeps tidy out of public statements afterwards. This area's part:

- [ ] **Before S2:** make private the tidy helpers no other module uses (437 of the 770), so that S2 renames less. This is part of the surface PRs below.
- [ ] **Log on #456, as S1 input:**
  - every proof here that opens a certificate to reach the machine (Cook–Levin, Ladner, the time hierarchy, circuit-value completeness, the PCP table verifier, Tree Evaluation, USTCON);
  - every plain-`fun_prop` failure met along the way.
- [ ] **After S2, the non-mechanical remainder:**
  - Give `PCPVerifier.PolyTime` and `IsPCPVerifier` named fields; proofs destructure them by position (`hV.2.1`).
  - State the Tree Evaluation headlines with `Nat.size` rather than `encNat` lengths.
  - Delete the now-redundant `mem_X_iff_tidy` bridges once nothing outside Machines needs them.
- **#580** (plain PSPACE boundary): S2's rename covers its statements and clients. Its placement part is item 8. I propose closing it with S2.

## Wave 1: ready now

### 1. `refactor(proof-systems): place Cook–Reckhow proof systems with the classes` (#596 item 5; placement; 5 files) ↔ agreed on #596
- [x] Move `Logics/Propositional/ProofSystem.lean` to `Computability/Complexity/ProofSystem.lean`. (#620)
- [x] Move `NP_eq_coNP_iff_coNP_subset_NP` into `Classes/NP.lean`. (#620)

The plain `ofVerifier` hypothesis comes with S2.

### 2. `refactor: make proof helpers private` (surface; one PR per subtree)

**Rule**, as in #601:
- A theorem becomes private when nothing outside its module (no library module, module doc, abstract, test or guide) names it and it carries no automation attribute.
- A definition becomes private only when no public statement or exposed body mentions it.
- A private `@[fun_prop]` rule uses `attribute [local fun_prop]` (#609).
- Declarations referenced nowhere, not even in their own file, are deleted. Examples: `Graph.selectVertices` and its family, `HamCycle.cities`, `Buss.computableTidilyInPolyTime_distinctVertices`, the dead `Ary.Tree` length lemmas and 13 dead `SensitivitySeparation.Internal` declarations.

**PRs:**
- [x] 2a: `QueryComplexity/SensitivitySeparation/Internal` (43 files). Only 6 of its 301 public declarations are used outside it. (#634; second pass in progress)
- [x] 2b: the Tree Evaluation and USTCON readers (about 15 files, about 250 declarations), including the 34 hypothesis-named `h*` theorems in `Reader/Cert/Step`. (#634; second pass in progress)
- [x] 2c: PCP (about 25 files). (#634; second pass in progress)
- [x] 2d: Classes IP, MIP, Space and Alternation (about 40 files). (#634; second pass in progress)
- [x] 2e: Classes ValiantVazirani, ArthurMerlin, PH, Ladner, TFNP, Oracle, Toda, LogSpace and Hierarchy (about 40 files). (#634; second pass in progress)
- [x] 2f: Problems, Parameterized, FineGrained, Fagin, AffineDisperser and HardnessEncoding (about 35 files). (#634; second pass in progress)
- [x] 2g: Communication, DecisionTree, the rest of QueryComplexity, Kolmogorov, MCSP and MachineLearning (about 35 files). (#634; second pass in progress)

*Benefit:* about 2,000 fewer public names, and editing a proof step no longer changes the interface that downstream builds depend on. *Risk:* low. A use from an exposed body or another module fails the build, and that declaration stays public.

### 3. `doc(classes): fix stale module docs` (about 15 files)
- [x] `ValiantVazirani.lean` and `Oracle.lean` still call RP, P and NP tidy. (#635)
- [x] `Fagin/Converse.lean` lists a nonexistent `definable_iff_queryLanguage_mem_NP`. (#635)
- [x] `PCP/GapTheorem`, `Amplification` and `Amplifier` say polynomial time is "not addressed". Link `Encoded.gapGraph` and `NP_eq_PCP_log`. (#635, #623)

issue.title: feat(SAT): prove orthogonal planar 3SAT-3 NP-hardness
issue.body:
This proves NP-hardness of planar 3SAT with clause width and literal-occurrence count at most three, both for formulas whose incidence graph admits an integer orthogonal drawing and for formulas with that drawing supplied. Binary clauses are allowed; repeated literals count separately. Every generated route is simple, avoids nonincident vertices, and meets other routes only at common graph endpoints on their full real supports. Parallel incidence occurrences retain distinct routes.

The total native polynomial-time compiler starts from ordinary binary-encoded 3SAT. For original size `S = clauses + literal occurrences + 1`, it emits grid sides at most `13440*S`, at most `29400*S²` clauses and `59290*S²` literal occurrences/routes, `1127000*S²` segments, and Manhattan wire length at most `14700000*S²`. These are bounds on the actual emitted formula and drawing, including empty and syntactically rejected inputs. Source labels and emitted coordinates use binary encodings. The supplied-drawing and existential-drawing languages are proved NP-hard; no membership theorem for these target languages is claimed.

The implementation reuses CNF, listed Graph, the ordered incidence graph, first-occurrence selection, compaction, real segment support, and plain computability. The new drawing encoding combines existing binary point/route encodings; the syntax guard isolates the width/count tests from the assignment verifier. The global finite tiling and quantitative proof are original. Source credit for the occurrence splitter and fixed crossover adapted from lean-trominoes is preserved in their modules.

This completes the mathematical scope of #1079 and stacks on #1111. The earlier stack layers retain their own validation and reviews. [Final wrapper/hardness delta review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1122#pullrequestreview-5645449436) found no blocking findings in the unchanged endpoint semantics. Maintainer integration and outside-fleet coordinator approval remain required.

Validation: [b971639d](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/commit/b971639d52273e397a7f5b9365536ab132b4eb39), tree `af3e4ebf`: all six required gates pass, including the global axiom audit, plus focused regressions, hygiene and documentation configuration. Each updated parent PR also records all six gates at its final restacked head. The additional guide build retains the existing Windows Verso `lean_md4c_markdown_parse` linker limitation before chapter elaboration; no dependency source was edited.

[Compiler/semantics/count/time/bounds review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1122#pullrequestreview-5645238698), [actual geometry closure review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1122#pullrequestreview-5645391233), and the wrapper/hardness review above cover the mathematical development. The later citation, Batteries/CNF reuse, shared-tail and encoding APIs, module-placement and targeted-import fixes have a clean [independent technical delta review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1122#issuecomment-6404981483). Final merge ancestry preserves that reviewed tree exactly. No statement meaning, emitted data, encoding or resource bound changed. All stale module imports are removed and the aggregate is regenerated. The nonblocking checker-speed suggestion is tracked in #1125. These records do not claim execution of the certified native machines. Fresh outside-fleet coordinator verdicts remain required for the updated stack.

issue.title: feat(crypto): prove correct and efficient layered Gentry evaluation
issue.body:
Next bounded recovery milestone under #322, depending on #446. Status: available; no worker claim yet. Preserve the full Gentry objective and do not close #322 when this milestone is complete.

Construct a real evaluator for layered circuits with constant, copy, and NAND nodes. Every node reads only the preceding layer. Use L + 1 key pairs and L encrypted-key links for L layers; key-chain length must depend on depth, not gate count. Constants use fresh encryption, copy nodes use identity refresh, and NAND nodes use the concrete NAND refresh from #446.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define explicit layered syntax, ordinary plaintext semantics, encodings, and the actual probabilistic evaluator; do not bundle evaluation correctness or runtime into its input interface.
- Prove the supported-state invariant: after layer i, the ciphertext-list length equals that layer's width, every ciphertext has the base fixed width, and decryption under sk_i equals the plaintext semantics. Intermediate ciphertexts need no freshness assumption. Encrypted-key links must actually encrypt the preceding secret key under the next public key.
- Handle depth zero, zero inputs, constants, empty layers, identity/wiring, and shared/repeated wire references. Include instances exposing these cases and repeated evaluated ciphertexts.
- Derive a uniform strict-PPT certificate charging the complete encoded circuit, key chain, links, inputs, and outputs. Certify total computation on malformed encoded inputs as well as valid chains. One useful construction truncates each produced ciphertext to the decryption circuit's input arity A(n) = secretWidth(n) + ciphertextWidth(n): the existing circuit generator computes A in unary, this cap is polynomial, and truncation is identity on every valid ciphertext. This avoids assuming a new efficient width function or relying on valid-key bounds for malformed paths.
- Complete the six project gates, named axiom guards, and independent API/correctness reviews of the final revision; assess curated abstracts without promoting this partial result to the full theorem.

Suggested existing APIs: IsPPTOn.mapMWith and the bounded probabilistic iteration rules; Boolean circuit encodings and the native augmentation generator from #446. Keep shared wires as indexed list entries rather than expanding a computation tree.

Still outside this milestone: a certified translation from arbitrary shared DAG circuits to the layered syntax; the acyclic key-chain IND-CPA hybrid reduction; and the separate circular-security fixed-key theorem. No general DAG-to-layering transformer was found in current local/pinned circuit modules. The later compiler must respect Circuit.depth (designated-output depth); Program.depth can be larger because of dead gates. A depth-preserving De Morgan-to-NAND translation may use a constant number of microlevels and polynomially many shared scratch slots, not one key per topological gate.

Source: Craig Gentry, Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices, STOC 2009, §§1–2 (Gentry2009 in references.bib). Proposal based on read-only API inspection by author worker `/root/maintenance_audit`; no proof of this follow-up is claimed.

## Summary

Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

### Deliverables

1. **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/ReadOnce.lean`**:
   - `LitFormula` and `PosFormula`: inductive binary AND/OR formula trees over positive/negated literals and positive variables, with `size` (binary AND/OR gate count), `leafSize`, `leafSupport`, `eval`, `IsReadOnce`, `IsSubformula`, `numOr`, `flipSensitive`, and direct compilation `PosFormula.toCircuit` (`size_toCircuit : F.toCircuit.size = F.size` and `cost_binaryCost_toCircuit : F.toCircuit.program.cost binaryCost = F.size`, using only binary `AND`/`OR` gates and no `NOT` gates).
   - **Tree unfolding from minimum-size De Morgan circuits**:
     - `Program.exists_litFormula_of_card_biUnion_wireSupport_ge`: by DAG rigidity (#844), a De Morgan circuit on $n \ge 1$ essential inputs with at most $n - 1$ binary AND/OR gates (`c.program.cost binaryCost + 1 ≤ n`) has every binary gate feed at most one downstream binary gate, so unfolding along wires yields a read-once `LitFormula` of size $n - 1$ and leaf size $n$.
     - `Circuit.exists_litFormula_of_cost_binaryCost_le` and `Circuit.exists_posFormula_of_cost_binaryCost_le`: if in addition every variable is positively essential (cannot appear strictly negated in a read-once De Morgan formula), the circuit is computed by a read-once `PosFormula` of size $n - 1$ and leaf size $n$.
   - **Structural properties of read-once positive formulas**:
     - `PosFormula.flipSensitive` and `PosFormula.card_flipSensitive_le_numOr_add_one`: for any baseline assignment $w_0$, `flipSensitive w₀ F` is the set of variables in `F.leafSupport` where flipping the input bit to `true` (`1`) flips `F.eval` from `false` (`0`) to `true` (`1`), and a read-once positive formula with $k$ OR gates satisfies `|flipSensitive w₀ F| ≤ k + 1` (supplying Ilango's Claim 14 at `w₀ = packXYZ zeros2n zeros2n ones2n`, all-zero on the $4n$ $x, y$ variables with $z$ fixed to ones).
     - `PosFormula.eval_eq_of_isSubformula_of_eval_eq`: if $G$ is a subformula of $F$ (`G.IsSubformula F`), two assignments $w_1, w_2$ agree outside $G$'s leaf support (`∀ i ∉ G.leafSupport, w₁ i = w₂ i`), and $G.eval\,w_1 = G.eval\,w_2$, then $F.eval\,w_1 = F.eval\,w_2$.

2. **`Complexity/Computability/MCSP/PartialETH.lean`**:
   - `PartialMCSP.MonotoneReadOnce`: the monotone read-once formula variant of `PartialMCSP`, asking for a `PosFormula x.arity` with `F.IsReadOnce`, `F.size ≤ x.threshold`, and `x.AgreesWith F.eval`.
   - `PartialMCSP.ilangoGamma` and `PartialMCSP.ilangoInstance`: Ilango's $6n$-variable partial Boolean function $\gamma_G : \{0,1\}^{2n} \times \{0,1\}^{2n} \times \{0,1\}^{2n} \to \mathrm{Option\ Bool}$ with threshold $6n - 1$, constructed from a $2n \times 2n$ bipartite permutation graph $G = (n, E)$ using seven clauses:
     - **Formula Structure Clauses (1)–(4)**:
       - (1) $x = 0^{2n} \mapsto \bigvee_{i < 2n} (y_i \wedge z_i)$
       - (2) $x = 1^{2n} \mapsto \bigvee_{i < 2n} z_i$
       - (3) $z = 1^{2n} \mapsto \bigvee_{i < 2n} (x_i \vee y_i)$
       - (4) $z = 0^{2n} \mapsto 0$ (`false`)
     - **Half-Block Preservation Clauses (5)–(6)**:
       - (5) $z = 1^n 0^n,\; y = 0^{2n} \mapsto \bigvee_{i < n} x_i$
       - (6) $z = 0^n 1^n,\; y = 0^{2n} \mapsto \bigvee_{n \le i < 2n} x_i$
     - **Graph Conflict Clause (7)**:
       - (7) If $\exists ((j, k), (j', k')) \in E$ with $x = \overline{e_k}\,\overline{e_{k'}}$ (`antiUnitPair k k'`), $y = 0^{2n}$ (`zeros2n`), and $z = e_j\,e_{j'}$ (`unitPair j j'`), then $1$ (`true`).
     - Otherwise: $?$ (`none`).
   - **Ilango's Claim 13 (`ilangoInstance_posEssential`)**: every total extension $f$ agreeing with `ilangoInstance G` ($n > 0$) depends positively on all $6n$ input variables, proved directly from the existing slabs of $\gamma_G$:
     - $x_i$: comparing $(0^{2n}, 0^{2n}, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 0$ (Clause 1) vs $(e_i, 0^{2n}, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 1$ (Clause 3).
     - $y_i$: comparing $(0^{2n}, 0^{2n}, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 0$ (Clause 1) vs $(0^{2n}, e_i, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 1$ (Clause 1 / Clause 3).
     - $z_i$: comparing $(1^{2n}, 0^{2n}, 0^{2n}) \mapsto 0$ (Clause 2 / Clause 4) vs $(1^{2n}, 0^{2n}, e_i) \mapsto 1$ (Clause 2).
   - **Ilango's Lemma 12 (`PosFormula.exists_perm_of_agreesWith_ilango`, via Claims 14–17)**: every read-once monotone formula $F$ of leaf size $6n$ ($n \ge 1$) satisfying Clauses (1)–(4) has the exact canonical form
     $$F(x, y, z) = \bigvee_{i < 2n} \bigl((x_{\pi(i)} \vee y_i) \wedge z_i\bigr)$$
     for some permutation $\pi \in S_{2n}$ (with Claim 14 proved via `card_flipSensitive_le_numOr_add_one` at baseline `w₀ = packXYZ zeros2n zeros2n ones2n` in `numAnd_le_two_mul_of_clause3`, and Claim 16 proved via `not_mem_leafSupport_zVar_of_isSubformula_and_left` and `not_mem_leafSupport_zVar_of_isSubformula_and_right` using `PosFormula.eval_eq_of_isSubformula_of_eval_eq` and Clause 1).
   - **Ilango's Theorem 11 (`mem_BipartitePermutationIndependentSet_iff_ilangoInstance_mem_monotoneReadOnce`, `_binaryGate`, `_mem`)**: for $n \ge 2$, the three target problems collapse at threshold $6n - 1$ via `PosFormula.toCircuit` (`mem_of_mem_monotoneReadOnce`), `mem_binaryGate_of_mem`, and `Circuit.exists_posFormula_of_cost_binaryCost_le`:
     $$G \in \text{BPIS} \iff \text{ilangoInstance}(G) \in \text{PartialMCSP.MonotoneReadOnce} \iff \text{ilangoInstance}(G) \in \text{PartialMCSP.BinaryGate} \iff \text{ilangoInstance}(G) \in \text{PartialMCSP}.$$
   - **Total $2^{O(n)}$-time reduction (`ilangoReduction`)**: handles $n < 2$ directly via polynomial-time search (`decideSmallBPIS`) and outputs `ilangoInstance G` for $n \ge 2$, with plain computability certificates `exists_computableInO_ilangoReduction` and `exists_computableInO_ilangoReduction_encBinary`.
   - **Subexponential-time transfer and ETH lower bounds**:
     - `decidableInSubexpTime_bpis_of_ilangoReduction` and `_encBinary`: transfers $2^{o(m \log m)}$ decidability along `ilangoReduction` to $2^{o(n \log n)}$ decidability of `BipartitePermutationIndependentSet`.
     - `ETH.not_decidableInSubexpTime_PartialMCSP` (and `_encBinary`, `_binaryGate`, `_binaryGate_encBinary`, `_PartialMonotoneReadOnceMCSP`, `_PartialMonotoneReadOnceMCSP_encBinary`, `_tableSize`, `_tableSize_encBinary`): under `ETH`, `PartialMCSP` rejects the subexponential decider family `DecidableInSubexpTime` at $m \log_2 m = \log_2 N \cdot \log_2 \log_2 N$.

3. **Shared `ComputableInPolyTime` frontends (`PolyTime/List.lean`, `PolyTime/Nat.lean`, `PolyTime/Nat/Binary.lean`)**:
   - Added plain `@[fun_prop]` frontends `range` and `unary_range'` (`List.lean`), `unary_le`, `unary_lt`, `unary_le'`, `unary_lt'`, and `unary_to_binary` (`Nat.lean`), and `binary_testBit` and `unary_testBit'` (`Nat/Binary.lean`).

4. **`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/FineGrained/PermutationIndependentSet.lean`**:
   - 1-line fix removing `@[fun_prop]` from `private theorem computableTidilyInPolyTime_toBinary` (an `id` transition lemma whose private constant name caused `fun_prop` transition search in downstream modules to fail).

---

## Faithfulness

| Formal declaration | Source locator | Comparison & notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PosFormula.exists_perm_of_agreesWith_ilango` | **Ilango (FOCS 2020)**, Section III.B, Lemma III.4, p. 428; **ECCC TR20-183**, Section 3, Lemma 12 (p. 22) & Claims 14–17 (pp. 22–26) | **Exact match.** Any read-once monotone formula of leaf size $6n$ ($n \ge 1$) satisfying Clauses (1)–(4) computes $\bigvee_{i < 2n} ((x_{\pi(i)} \vee y_i) \wedge z_i)$ for some permutation $\pi \in S_{2n}$. Claim 14 (sensitivity at `w₀ = packXYZ zeros2n zeros2n ones2n` under Clause 3) uses `PosFormula.card_flipSensitive_le_numOr_add_one` in `numAnd_le_two_mul_of_clause3`; Claim 16 (no two `z`-leaves share an `AND` gate under Clause 1) uses `not_mem_leafSupport_zVar_of_isSubformula_and_left` and `not_mem_leafSupport_zVar_of_isSubformula_and_right` via `PosFormula.eval_eq_of_isSubformula_of_eval_eq`. |
| `PartialMCSP.ilangoInstance_posEssential` | **Ilango (ECCC TR20-183)**, Section 3, Claim 13, p. 22 | **Exact match.** Proved directly from Clauses (1)–(4) of $\gamma_G$: flipping $x_i$ on $(0^{2n}, 0^{2n}, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 0$ vs $(e_i, 0^{2n}, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 1$, flipping $y_i$ on $(0^{2n}, 0^{2n}, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 0$ vs $(0^{2n}, e_i, 1^{2n}) \mapsto 1$, and flipping $z_i$ on $(1^{2n}, 0^{2n}, 0^{2n}) \mapsto 0$ vs $(1^{2n}, 0^{2n}, e_i) \mapsto 1$. |
| `PartialMCSP.mem_BipartitePermutationIndependentSet_iff_ilangoInstance_mem_monotoneReadOnce`, `_binaryGate`, `_mem` | **Ilango (FOCS 2020)**, Section III.B, pp. 427–428; **ECCC TR20-183**, Section 3, Theorem 11, p. 20, construction and proof pp. 21–24 | **Exact match with proved size-measure bridges (Decision D5).** Theorem 11 in ECCC TR20-183 reduces $2n \times 2n$ BPIS to $\text{MCSP}^*$ at threshold $6n - 1$. In the forward direction, `PosFormula.toCircuit` (`size_toCircuit` and `cost_binaryCost_toCircuit`) compiles the canonical read-once positive formula into a NOT-free De Morgan circuit of all-gates and binary-gate cost $6n - 1$ (`mem_of_mem_monotoneReadOnce`), and `mem_binaryGate_of_mem` passes from `unitCost` to `binaryCost`. In the reverse direction, for $n \ge 2$, `ilangoInstance_posEssential` and `Circuit.exists_posFormula_of_cost_binaryCost_le` unfold any circuit of `binaryCost` at most $6n - 1$ into a read-once positive formula of size $6n - 1$, where Clauses (5)–(6) enforce block-preservation of $\pi$ and Clause (7) enforces edge-avoidance on $(\overline{e_k}\,\overline{e_{k'}}, 0^{2n}, e_j\,e_{j'})$. |
| `PartialMCSP.exists_computableInO_ilangoReduction`, `_encBinary` | **Ilango (FOCS 2020)**, Section III.B, p. 428; **ECCC TR20-183**, Section 3, Theorem 11, pp. 20–21 | **Exact match.** Constructs the $2^{6n}$-entry partial truth table and threshold in time $2^{O(n)} \cdot \text{poly}(|G|)$ for both unary (`PartialMCSP.enc`) and binary (`PartialMCSP.encBinary`) threshold encodings. |
| `Complexity.ETH.not_decidableInSubexpTime_PartialMCSP`, `_tableSize`, `_binaryGate`, `_PartialMonotoneReadOnceMCSP` (+ `_encBinary` variants) | **Ilango (FOCS 2020)**, Section I.A, Theorem I.3, p. 424; **ECCC TR20-183**, Section 1.2.2, Theorem 3, p. 6 | **Exact match.** Rejects the subexponential decider family `DecidableInSubexpTime` under `ETH` both in terms of arity $m$ (measure $m \log_2 m$, i.e., time $2^{o(m \log m)}$) and in terms of truth-table size $N = 2^m = I.\text{tableSize}$ (measure $\log_2 N \cdot \log_2 \log_2 N$, i.e., time $2^{o(\log N \log \log N)} = N^{o(\log \log N)}$). |

issue.title: feat(Kolmogorov,Crypto): prove OWF implies K^t is mildly hard on average (Liu-Pass FOCS'20 M2a, #798)
issue.body:
Refs #798 (Milestone M2a: `OWF => K^t is mildly hard on average`), #733.

Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

### Summary

Implements Milestone M2a of #798: the forward direction of Liu and Pass (*On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*, 2020 IEEE 61st Annual Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS), pp. 1243–1254, `LiuPass2020`), consuming the shared probability/entropy (#985, `Complexity/Probability/Entropy/BitString.lean`) and average-case hardness (#986, `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/AverageCase.lean`) modules tracked in #733:

> If one-way functions exist, then there exists a polynomial $p$ such that for every time bound $t(n) \ge p(n)$, the time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity $K^t$ is mildly hard on average (and mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate for $g(n) = d \cdot (\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$, $d \cdot \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$, $d \cdot \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, and the real-valued $d \log_2 n$ window).

### Mathematical Scope & Paper Attribution

- **Source:** Yanyi Liu and Rafael Pass, *On One-Way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*, FOCS 2020 (`LiuPass2020`, pp. 1243–1254; full version `arXiv:2009.11514v1`):
  - **Definitions 2.4 & 2.5 ([Liu and Pass, §2.3, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]) and library companions (from #986):**
    - Exact average-case hardness against uniform strict PPT (`MildlyHardOnAverage`), with `ENat`-valued library companion `MildlyHardOnAverageENat`; deterministic polynomial-time specialization `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`; and infinitely-often deterministic library companions `MildlyHardOnAverageIO` and `MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat`, over `BitString.uniformList n`.
    - Symmetric $g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`) formalized via `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g x.length`.
    - One-sided underestimation helper (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO`) replacing $|H(x) - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$ with $f(x) - g(|x|) \le H(x) \le f(x)$, together with the certified uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling transfer theorem `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` deriving symmetric $g$-approximation hardness from one-sided $(2g)$-approximation hardness via $H'(x) = H(x) - g(|x|)$ when $x \mapsto g(|x|)$ is polynomial-time computable (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat`).
  - **Section 3.2 (pp. 1247–1248, PDF pp. 5–6):** *Warm-up: Hard-on-Average from Regular PRGs*. Constructs a length-doubling PRG $G : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^{2n}$ from any OWF (via HILL99) and uses the $K^t$ sparsity bound vs. generator output upper bound to distinguish $G(U_n)$ from $U_{2n}$.
  - **Theorem 3.1 (§3, p. 10 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`; FOCS pp. 1246–1247) & Theorem 5.2 (§5.2, p. 11 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`):** *OWFs Imply Mildly Hard-on-Average of $K^t$ (Full Proof from Conditionally Entropy-Preserving PRGs)*. Given any OWF, Theorem 5.5 (`OneWay.exists_condEPPRG` in `CondEPPRG.lean`) yields a conditionally entropy-preserving PRG $G : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^{n + \gamma \log n}$. Proving `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => d * (Nat.log 2 x.length + 1)) encBits encNat`, `LiuPass.lean:175`) via `polytime` and `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) instantiates the one-sided theorem at gap $2d$ under stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$ and applies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`. Monotonicity (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mono`) and rounded-log bridges then yield the ceiling ($d \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$), floor ($d \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$), and real-valued ($|v - K^t(x)| \le d \log_2 n$) approximation hardness endpoints.
- **M2a Polynomial-Overhead Scope vs. Source Rate-1 Universal Simulation:**
  - The source theorem (Theorem 3.1) states $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon)n$ for all $\varepsilon > 0$ via a rate-$1$ universal Turing machine simulation of the polynomial-time PRG prefix evaluator (`LiuPass2020`, p. 1248, PDF p. 6).
  - Because `Kolmogorov.timeBounded` (`K^t`) in `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/TimeBounded.lean` is defined on the fixed multi-tape `Turing.TuringMachine` model whose evaluator `TimeBounded.computableInPolyTime_eval` incurs polynomial step overhead $p(n)$, M2a proves the **M2a polynomial-overhead form** (`∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, n + 1 ≤ p.eval n) ∧ ∀ t : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, p.eval n ≤ t n) → ...`). All polynomial-threshold declarations and module docstrings are explicitly labeled as the M2a polynomial-overhead form.

### Architecture & Module Changes

1. **Shared Supplier Modules (#985 & #986, #733 items 6 & 7):**
   - `Complexity/Probability/Entropy/BitString.lean` (#985): reusable Shannon entropy and statistical distance lemmas on `BitString m` in `namespace Cslib.Probability.PMF`.
   - `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/AverageCase.lean` (#986): general average-case hardness definitions, monotonicity, the uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling bridge (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`), rounded-logarithm comparisons, and negative-side nonvacuity lemmas on `fun _ => 0`.
2. **`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/AverageCase.lean` ($K^t$-specific bridges):**
   - Contains the $K^t$-specific bridges (`mildlyHardOnAverageENat_timeBounded_iff`, `mildlyHardOnAverageIOENat_timeBounded_iff`), generator description bounds (`exists_timeBounded_generator_le`, `timeBoundedNat_generator_le`, `exists_timeBounded_of_computableInPolyTime`), and uniform counting / threshold acceptance bounds (`card_filter_timeBoundedNat_lt`, `sum_uniform_timeBoundedNat_lt_le`, `uniformList_threshold_accept_ge`, `generator_threshold_accept_le`).
3. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/CondEPPRG.lean`:**
   - Imports `Complexity.Probability.Entropy.BitString` (#985).
4. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/LiuPass.lean`:**
   - Proves both one-sided (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`) and symmetric (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`) uniform-PPT and deterministic approximation hardness for `d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`, `d * Nat.clog 2 n`, `d * Nat.log 2 n`, and the direct real-valued $|v - K^t(x)| \le d \log_2 n$ corollary `OneWay.exists_eventually_real_abs_sub_le_timeBoundedNat`, as well as the exact Theorem 3.1 endpoints (`OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverage_timeBoundedNat`, `OneWay.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageENat_timeBounded`, and `InhabitedOneWay` / deterministic / IO variants).
5. **`ComplexityTests/LiuPass.lean` & `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean`:**
   - Signature, non-vacuity, and `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` coverage.

### Framework friction

- **Uniform-PPT shift bridge and logarithmic-gap certificate:** The uniform-PPT shift bridge `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` (#986) reuses the existing binary subtraction certificate (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_sub`, through a proof-local `.of_tidy` conversion) and `IsPPTOn.map_with`, taking an explicit `ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat` premise for the gap computation. In `LiuPass.lean:175`, `computableInPolyTime_mul_log_two_succ` proves this certificate for $g(n) = d(\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1)$ via `polytime` on unary output composed with `ComputableInPolyTime.unary_to_binary`, and `CondEPPRG.exists_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_timeBoundedNat_log_succ` (`LiuPass.lean:549–563`) applies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` at gap $2d$ under stretch $\gamma \ge 4d + 3$.
- **Rate-1 universal simulation vs. fixed TM evaluator polynomial overhead:** As documented on #798 and in `LiuPass.lean`, closing the gap from $t(n) \ge p(n)$ to $t(n) \ge (1 + \varepsilon)n$ requires a linear-time universal simulation theorem for the machine model underlying `Kolmogorov.timeBounded`, which is orthogonal to the cryptographic COND-EP-PRG reduction and tracked separately from M2a.

### Verification

- `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 ./scripts/check.sh` (all 6 gates: `build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`) passed with zero `sorry` and zero warnings.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp` passed.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_tidy_surface.py` passed (`1289 public tidy statement(s) in 225 module(s), matching the baseline`).
- `python3 -B scripts/check_changed_files.py` passed.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_docs.py --config-only` and `./scripts/guide.sh --check` passed.

### Abstract impact

No selected abstract statement, definition, scope, or catalogue entry changes in `ComplexityAbstracts/`.

issue.title: feat(crypto): construct fixed-key FHE under explicit circular security
issue.body:
Next bounded milestone under #322, following #478 / #472. Construct and certify the fixed-key scheme whose public evaluation key encrypts its own secret key. The key generator takes only the security parameter; there is no depth budget. Keep #322 open until the complete recovery criteria are audited, and retain the separate concrete-LWE obligation.

Acceptance criteria:

- Define the actual sampler: one supported base key pair (pk, sk), bitwise encryption of sk under pk, serialized public artifact (pk, encrypted-sk), and sk as the private artifact. No secret plaintext is exposed publicly. Reuse this single encrypted-key sample across every refresh.
- Reuse the existing ordinary-circuit compiler and refresh evaluator to evaluate every finite shared Boolean circuit. All circuits are permitted. Prove correctness for arbitrary pointwise decrypting, well-sized inputs, including outputs of previous evaluations, with the same key and ciphertext width. Do not replace correlated self-link reuse by independently sampled links.
- Prove perfect correctness of the actual Scheme, exact secret/ciphertext widths independent of circuit size/depth, and polynomial compactness/decryption cost from the native decryption-circuit generator. Key generation has no supplied circuit or depth bound.
- Give native uniform certificates for key generation, encryption, decryption and evaluation on their complete encoded inputs, including malformed public artifacts and references. Reuse semantic/circuit/list automation; do not add theorem-specific TM implementations.
- Define a precise one-key, bitwise circular/KDM assumption comparing (pk, Enc_pk(sk)) and (pk, Enc_pk(0^|sk|)) against uniform native PPT tests. Keep ordinary base IND-CPA separate. The assumption must not simply assert IND-CPA of the output scheme, and no circular security is claimed from ordinary IND-CPA.
- Prove actual output-scheme adaptive two-stage IND-CPA through the public-artifact hybrids and an explicit base adversary for the zero-link world. Charge saved state and complete public encoding. A supported independent key sample can supply the zero-word length under fixed supported secret width; do not assume an efficiently computable width merely for security.
- Instantiate construction/correctness/runtime premises in concrete finite regressions, explicitly label insecure examples, test repeated evaluation with the same public artifact, and include a leaking example rejected by the security notions. Do not claim a concrete secure LWE instantiation from these tests.
- Assemble the fixed-key all-circuit correctness, native efficiency, compactness and conditional security results for the same algorithms. Add axiom guards, update ROADMAP, assess the curated abstract catalogue, pass all six gates and independent exact-revision API/correctness review.

Planned reusable files: Encryption/Circular.lean for the explicit self-encryption experiment; Homomorphic/FixedKey/{Encoding,Basic,Correctness,PolyTime,Security,Bootstrapping}.lean for the construction. Adjust placement if concrete reuse or review warrants it. Existing encryptedWires_evaluateLayers already permits pointwise valid repeated keys/links and old evaluated ciphertexts.

Source: Craig Gentry, [Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf), Section 2, especially the self-loop paragraph following Theorem 5. The proof plan and precise experiment above require implementation and independent review; they are not completed results.

Owner/session: worker-codex-gentry-fixedkey-20261023. Planned branch: feat/gentry-fixedkey-20261023 in an independent checkout initially stacked on #478. Root authors the circular experiment, security reduction, assembly and regressions; /root/maintenance_audit will author construction/correctness/native certificates in a separate checkout. /root/refactor_plan_review provides read-only source/model reconnaissance; /root/library_map remains independent of authoring.

issue.body:
Makes 57 declarations in Computability/Complexity (classes, problems, Fagin, Cook-Levin), PCP, TreeEval, Kolmogorov and MachineLearning public again (36 API, 21 general mathematics), across 38 files. Earlier passes made them `private` because nothing outside their module used them (#634 (39), #691 (13), 07880a58 (3), #898 (1), 08b0f8d8 (1)). Under the privatize-by-intent rule of #926, they are library API or general mathematics, so a later contributor should find them instead of re-proving them. Part of the audit tracked on #587.

Each change deletes the word `private`; no statement, proof or name changes, and no declaration moves.

**Classification rule** (#926, CONTRIBUTING "Public surface under the module system"):
- **PLUMBING** stays private: a step meaningful only inside one proof, or a fact about a module-local construction, encoding or intermediate quantity.
- **API** becomes public: a fact stated only in terms of public definitions that a user would expect, such as characterizations, bounds, monotonicity and closure, simp and equation lemmas, invariance lemmas and named results.
- **GENERAL** becomes public: general mathematics (lists, finsets, arithmetic, probability, linear algebra). These belong in `Complexity/Foundations` and are listed below as follow-ups, not moved here.

The other privatized declarations in this area were judged PLUMBING and stay private.

issue.title: ci(scripts): lint module-doc names and restatement-only tests in changed files
issue.body:
Part of #949 (consolidation tooling). Two narrow, diagnostic lints that run in CI only on the files a pull request adds or changes, plus a sorted `references.bib`.

## Lints (`scripts/check_changed_files.py`)

- **Module-doc names.** In a changed module under `Complexity/`, each backquoted name that heads a bullet of a "Main …" section of the module docstring (the names before the bullet's first colon) must name a declaration. A name resolves when some library, test or abstract module defines or refers to it, according to the build's `.ilean` files, matched exactly or as a suffix on a component boundary. Tactic, attribute and rule-set names that the library declares (`syntax`, `macro`, `elab`, `declare_aesop_rule_sets`, `register_simp_attr`) also resolve, such as `polytime`, `ppt` and `program_certificate`. So does a commented allowlist of nine upstream tactic names (`fun_prop`, `simp`, …). Backquoted text that isn't an identifier, such as `Qᶜ` or `foo_*`, isn't checked.
- **Restatement-only tests.** A *new* file under `ComplexityTests/` fails when it has examples and every one is `example … := name` (or `:= by exact name`), unless it imports or names `ComplexityAbstracts`. The rule doesn't count `rfl`, `trivial` and similar terms as restatements, because they check a statement by evaluation. It doesn't police test quality beyond that.

The CI step "Changed-file lints" runs after the build on `pull_request` and `merge_group` events. It fetches the event's base commit and compares against it directly, because the checkout is shallow. Run locally, the script compares against the merge base with `origin/main`, including uncommitted and untracked files.

**Over all of current `main`** (not only changed files): the doc-name lint finds no unresolved names in 2,011 modules (14,624 listed names). Two existing test files consist only of restatements: `ComplexityTests/Smoke.lean` and `ComplexityTests/ListBasicImports.lean`, both import smoke tests. The lint applies only to new files, so they aren't flagged. This PR changes no Lean file, so nothing needed fixing or allowlisting.

## Sorted bibliography (separate commit)

`references.bib` is sorted by key, case-insensitively as BibTeX compares keys, with one blank line between entries. The multiset of the 379 entries is unchanged, including `Schoening1999` from #908, which landed after the first sort. The check compared entry texts before and after, and only one missing and one doubled blank line between entries changed. `scripts/check_hygiene.py`, which runs on every PR, now checks that keys are unique and sorted. It takes over the duplicate-key check that `scripts/check_docs.py` ran only in the nightly docs build. With entries placed by key, two PRs adding citations conflict only when their keys are adjacent.

**Once this lands, any open PR that appends a `references.bib` entry needs one re-sort:** a rebase that moves each new entry to its place in key order.

## Validation

- Hosted CI at `bfa72cfa`, rebased onto `main` `c89dd48c`: [Lean Action CI run 40154272379](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40154272379), success. Every step ran, including the new "Changed-file lints" step against base `c89dd48c`. The earlier run at `62b4c224` failed: the merge with `main` contained #908's `Schoening1999` out of order. The rebase re-sorts it.
- Unit tests in `scripts/test_check_changed_files.py` and new cases in `scripts/test_check_hygiene.py`.

issue.body:
Place deterministic exponential padding with the exponential-time classes and narrow the imports used by the actual hardness-encoding client. Full declaration names, statements, binder order and complete proof bodies are preserved byte-for-byte.

The first focused commit relocates only `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInO.lengthUnary` from `Classes/Constructible` to the lower quantitative machine API, beside `unary_two_pow`, retaining old-import visibility through a public import. This prerequisite avoids duplicating the streaming length adapter or importing constructibility back into EXP; it leaves `lengthNat` and the other constructibility helpers in place. A Quantitative-only client checks unary length and its composition with exponential padding.

The second commit moves `Cslib.Complexity.setOf_mem_E_of_computableTidilyInPolyTime_pad` from Padding to EXP. EXP publicly imports `Classes.Hierarchy` and `Classes.Time` and uses quantitative rules privately; HardnessEncoding/PolyTime now publicly imports EXP directly. Static local source import closures, excluding each root, drop from 195 to 185 modules for EXP and 288 to 278 for HardnessEncoding; neither retains `Classes.Padding`, `Classes.Constructible` or `Classes.Hierarchy.Time`. An EXP-only client checks the moved theorem and an inhabited polynomial-time premise. Existing hardness-encoding clients compile through the narrower boundary. The hierarchy test now explicitly imports `Classes.Hierarchy.Time` for the constructibility and hierarchy declarations it exercises, rather than receiving them through EXP.

Closes #411.
