issue.title: feat(Crypto): keyed collision-resistant hash families and the Merkle-Damgard transform
issue.body:
Closes #669 (part of #640 Track D).

## Summary

This PR formalizes keyed collision-resistant hash families and compression functions (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CollisionResistant.lean`) and the Merkle–Damgård iterated-compression transform and deterministic collision-extraction reduction (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MerkleDamgard.lean`, Boneh–Shoup Section 8.4, Figure 8.5 and Theorem 8.3).

### Mathematical Progress

1. **Keyed Collision-Resistant Hash Families (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CollisionResistant.lean`)**:
   * `isCollision H valid n k m₁ m₂`, `collisionGame H valid adversary n` (`isPPTOn_collisionGame`, `isPPT_collisionGame`), and `CollisionResistantOn H valid` / `CollisionResistant H`.
   * `succProbability_collisionGame_le_of_extract`, `CollisionResistantOn.of_extract`, and `CollisionResistantOn.mono`: deterministic polynomial-time collision extraction transfers collision resistance between hash families.
   * `not_collisionResistantOn_of_le_succProbability`: general nonvacuity lemma showing that any strict PPT collision finder with success probability bounded away from zero refutes `CollisionResistantOn`.
   * `CompressionFamily` (`2n → n` collision-resistant compression families) and `HashFamily` (unrestricted collision-resistant hash families on arbitrary-length bit strings `List Bool`).

2. **The Merkle–Damgård Transform and Collision Reduction (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MerkleDamgard.lean`)**:
   * **Block-chain level**: `merkleDamgardChain`, `chainTraceStep`, `chainTrace`, and `extractChainCollision` (polynomial-time backward trace scan, `computableInPolyTime_extractChainCollision`), together with:
     * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_not_suffix`: fundamental suffix-free chain collision lemma;
     * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_getLast?_ne`: Boneh–Shoup Theorem 8.3 Case 1 (distinct final blocks);
     * `isCollision_extractChainCollision_of_length_eq`: Boneh–Shoup Theorem 8.3 Case 2 (equal block counts);
     * `CompressionFamily.collisionResistantOn_merkleDamgardChain`: any polynomial-time suffix-free block encoding turns a `CompressionFamily` into a collision-resistant hash family.
   * **Unrestricted bit-string level**: `mdEndBlock`, `mdDataBlock`, `mdBlocks` (suffix-free `n`-bit block encoding of arbitrary bit strings for `n ≥ 2`, `mdBlocks_suffix_iff`), `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`, `isCollision_extractMerkleDamgardCollision`, and `CompressionFamily.collisionResistant_merkleDamgard` / `CompressionFamily.hashFamily_merkleDamgard`.

### Tests and Nonvacuity (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleDamgard.lean`)
* Concrete `2n → n` XOR compression function (`xorCompress`) and checked examples of `mdBlocks`, `merkleDamgard`, `extractMerkleDamgardCollision`, and both cases of `extractChainCollision` (Theorem 8.3 Cases 1 and 2).
* Client checks verifying that ordinary importing clients retain the public plain `ComputableInPolyTime` API without globally registering private tidy helpers.
* Nonvacuity refutation (`not_collisionResistant_constHash`) via an explicit zero-coin PPT collision finder.
* `#print axioms` guards for all 12 headline declarations.

### Formal Abstract Assessment
* No impact on existing selected headline abstracts in `abstracts/catalogue.json` (`python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes).

## Validation & Review
* Built and checked `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.CollisionResistant`, `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MerkleDamgard`, and `ComplexityTests.Crypto.MerkleDamgard` (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, 6496 jobs), `lake exe mk_all --check`, `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`, and `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.
* Pre-PR independent review conducted by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-md669` on `ec5de574`; all 3 items (module docstring coverage, `private` internal helpers / plain `@[program_certificate]` attributes, and Boneh–Shoup section locators) addressed in `483287ce`.
* Addressed coordinator review (`pullrequestreview-5636180774`) in `da71993b` by removing global `program_certificate` attributes from the private tidy helpers in `CollisionResistant.lean` and `MerkleDamgard.lean`, updating "Construction 8.1" citations to Section 8.4 / Figure 8.5 / Theorem 8.3, and adding plain-API client examples in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleDamgard.lean`.

*AI disclosure: Authored by `worker-jetski-5950b838` and subagent `1a2b8286-7df4-4f01-af32-7c3474556ff0` (Gemini), with independent pre-PR review by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-md669`.*

issue.title: feat(Crypto): indexed signatures and Merkle signatures from one-time signatures
issue.body:
Milestone M1 of #1001: Merkle's tree signature from any one-time signature scheme and a collision-resistant hash family. It comes with an explicit-loss security reduction whose two reductions are certified efficient. The design is in [the M0 comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/1001#issuecomment-6398003266).

**Stacked on #1024** (Kilian's Merkle verifier and binding game), which is in turn stacked on #1023 (Merkle trees). The signature verifier checks the tree opening with #1024's `merkleVerify`. The collision case uses #1024's `isCollision_of_merkleVerify`.

## What is proved

**`IndexedSignature.lean`.** This module adds indexed signature schemes (Boneh–Shoup Definition 14.6). The signer takes an index `u < q(n)` as an explicit input, and the security game refuses to sign twice under one index. This is how the stateful use of Merkle's scheme is modelled: the state is the leaf counter, and the signer's obligation never to repeat it is what the game enforces. It differs from the source in four ways, each labelled in the module doc:

- **Signing** may be randomized.
- **Messages** are arbitrary bit strings.
- **Refusal instead of restriction.** The oracle refuses a repeated or out-of-range index, so every oracle adversary is admissible.
- **Forgeries** may name any index; the scheme's verifier must reject indices outside its capacity.

**`MerkleSignature.lean`.** `MerkleSignature.scheme S H depth hH hlen hcap` is an indexed scheme of capacity `2 ^ depth n`.

- **Keys.** The public key is a uniform `n`-bit hash key and the Merkle root of `2 ^ depth n` one-time verification keys.
- **Signature.** A signature at leaf `u` consists of the one-time key, the one-time signature on the digest `H k msg`, and the authentication path.
- **Verification.** It uses `merkleVerify` (path length `depth n`, `u < 2 ^ depth n`, root) and then the one-time check.
- **Lemmas.** Completeness is `verify_sign`; the strict PPT and polynomial-time certificates are `isPPTOn_keyGen`, `isPPTOn_sign` and `computableInPolyTime_verify`.

**`MerkleSignature/Security.lean`.**

- **The bound**, `succProbability_indexedEufCmaGame_le`. For every forger `A` and every `n`:

  `Pr[A forges] ≤ 2 ^ depth n · Pr[oneTimeForger A wins the one-time game of S] + Pr[collisionFinder A finds a collision of H]`.

  - `collisionFinder` generates all keys and answers honestly. If the forged verification key differs from the one at the named leaf, it extracts a tree collision. Otherwise it returns the forged message together with a signed message at that leaf with the same digest.
  - `oneTimeForger` plants its challenge at a uniform leaf (`leafIndex`, exactly uniform on `2 ^ depth n` values). It answers that leaf through its one-time oracle, truncating to a polynomial bound. Its simulation is proved exact (`eval_run_plantedHandler`), so the loss is exactly `2 ^ depth n`.
- **Efficiency:** `isPPT_collisionFinder` and `isOraclePPT_oneTimeForger`.
- **Security:** `SignatureScheme.OneTimeEUFCMA.indexedEUFCMA_merkle`, and `OneWay.exists_indexedEUFCMA`. The latter combines it with Lamport (`OneWay.exists_oneTimeSignature`): a one-way function and a `HashFamily` give indexed EUF-CMA signatures of every polynomial capacity.

## Sources and notation

- **Merkle**, *A Certified Digital Signature*, CRYPTO '89, LNCS 435, pp. 218–238, §6 "Tree Authentication". I checked it against the author's posted 1979 manuscript of the same text:
  > The use of tree authentication to create tree signatures is now fairly clear, A transmits Yi to B, A then transmits the authentication path for Yi, B knows R, the root of the authentication tree, by prior arrangement.
- **Boneh–Shoup** `[BonehShoup2023]`, v0.6. I checked §14.6.1, p. 597:
  > Definition 14.6. A q-indexed signature system is a signature system S = (G, S, V) where the message space is M0 = {1, . . . , q} × M and the signing algorithm S is deterministic. We say that S is a secure q-indexed signature if for all efficient q-query signature adversaries A, the quantity iSIGadv[A, S] is negligible.

  > Security of this construction follows immediately from the security of the underlying one-time signature. The proof of security uses the same "plug-and-pray" argument as in Exercise 13.2.

  > Place the q one-time public keys at the leaves of a Merkle tree and compute the corresponding hash at the root. This single hash value at the root is the public key for the q-indexed scheme. […] A signature on a message (u, m) contains the Merkle proof needed to authenticate the one-time public key pk_u, along with the one-time signature on m using sk_u.

  And §13.2, p. 533, Theorem 13.1, with `SIGadv[A, S'] ≤ SIGadv[B_S, S] + CRadv[B_H, H]`.

How the sources' notation maps to the Lean:

| Source | Lean |
|---|---|
| `q` | `capacity n = 2 ^ depth n` |
| `(u, m)` | index `u : ℕ`, message `msg : List Bool` |
| `pk_u`, `sk_u` | `(keys.getD u ([], [])).1`, `.2` |
| Merkle proof | `merklePath` (#1023) |
| `iSIGadv` | `Game.succProbability` of `indexedEufCmaGame` |
| one-time security | the existing `SignatureScheme.eufOneTimeGame` / `OneTimeEUFCMA` |
| `CRadv` | `collisionGame H (fun _ _ => true)` |

The explicit bound composes the sourced pieces: plug-and-pray, the Merkle-tree collision extraction behind Boneh–Shoup Theorem 8.8, and hash-and-sign (Theorem 13.1). The composition is original to this library, and the docstrings say so.

## Not in this PR

- **Counter layer.** The design proposed a counter-stateful layer, `CounterEUFCMA`, derived from `IndexedEUFCMA`. It is not included and stays open on #1001.
- **Later milestones.** M2 (stateless, via GGM and Boneh–Shoup Theorem 14.6) through M4 (Rompel) are untouched.

## Other changes

- **List lemmas.** `List.getD_append_cons_length` and `List.getD_append_cons_of_ne` are now in `Foundations/Data/List/Lookup.lean`. `OneWayToSignature` had a private copy of the second; that copy is replaced.
- **`fun_prop` locality.** In `OneWayToSignature`, three `@[fun_prop] private` rules become `attribute [local fun_prop]`. As CONTRIBUTING warns, the private rules were exported and broke `polytime` in importers (found here). Statements are unchanged.

## Validation

- Hosted CI: [Lean Action CI run 40202104986](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40202104986) on `13778adc`.
- **Local runs:**
  - `scripts/check.sh` (all six gates)
  - `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
  - `python3 scripts/check_changed_files.py --base pr/1024`
  - `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py` (no new tidy statements)
  - `lake exe mk_all --check`
- **No Lean MCP server** was available in this session, so I iterated with `lake env lean`.
- **Tests** (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleSignature.lean`) run concrete instances: Lamport on the identity, a toy truncating hash, two leaves at `n = 4`.
  - Honest signatures at both leaves verify, and the signer produces exactly the checked signature.
  - A message with another digest is rejected, while a toy-hash collision is accepted: that is the case the collision reduction handles.
  - The signature of leaf 0 is rejected at leaf 1. At index `0 + 2` the opening recomputes the root, and only the range check rejects it.
  - The capacity hypothesis holds for constant depth and for depth `Nat.clog 2 (n + 1)`.

**Size.** The PR is about 1.8k lines, above the usual 1.5k target. Most of it is the security file (about 1.1k lines). Each oracle-PPT certificate of the one-time forger needs a manual reply-size bound (`plantedHandler_bound`).

**Abstracts:** no impact; no catalogue or abstract changes. A headline for signatures belongs with M2 or M4 and is Samuel's call.

**Framework friction (#733):**
- **Leaked `fun_prop` rules.** Private `@[fun_prop]` rules in `OneWayToSignature` leaked into importers and broke `polytime`. Fixed here.
- **Continuation inference.** In `IsPPTOn.bind_with` / `IsOraclePPTOn.bind_with` / `map_with`, continuations whose arguments are projections are not higher-order patterns, so Lean cannot infer them. Elaborating them unannotated also timed out in `whnf`, unfolding `collisionOf`/`decodeSignature`. The fix was explicit `(second := fun (c : T) (x : U) => …)` with binder types. A `bind_with` variant taking the continuation explicitly, or a note in the guide, would help.
- **Reply-size bounds.** `run_interpret_preprocess_open` needs a reply-size bound that does not depend on the handler's state. No lemma derives it from per-branch certificates, so `plantedHandler_bound` does the size accounting by hand.

issue.title: feat(Computability/Kolmogorov): formalize MKtP ∈ EXP and MINcKT ∈ NP (#798)
issue.body:
## Summary

Completes **Milestone M1.2** of [#798](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/798) (`MKtP ∈ EXP`, conditional Kolmogorov complexity `condTimeBounded`, and `MINcKT ∈ NP`):

### Mathematical Progress

1. **`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/EXP.lean`**:
   - **`Cslib.Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.mem_EXP`**: Downward closure of `EXP` under polynomial-time many-one reductions.

2. **`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/MKtP.lean`**:
   - **Optimal $\mathrm{Kt}$-witnesses and [Liu and Pass, Section 3.1, Fact 3.1, p. 10][LiuPass2021Crypto]**:
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_length_add_clog_eq_levinKt` and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_length_add_clog_eq_levinKtNat`: every string $x$ has a non-zero step count $s > 0$ and program $p$ achieving $|p| + \lceil \log_2 s \rceil = \mathrm{Kt}(x)$.
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain_lt_of_levinKtNat_witness_two_pow_lt` and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.encard_setOf_forall_optimal_levinKt_two_pow_lt`: if any witness $(p, s)$ with $|p| + \lceil \log_2 s \rceil \le \mathrm{Kt}(x)$ runs for more than $2^{\mathrm{copyOverhead} + \lceil \log_2(|x| + 1) \rceil + m}$ steps, then $K(x) < |x| - m$ (accounting for the extra $\lceil \log_2(|x| + 1) \rceil$ term from `levinKt_le_length_add`).
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.two_pow_lt_ncard_setOf_exists_optimal_levinKt_le_two_pow`: all but fewer than $2^{n - m}$ strings of length $n$ have an optimal $\mathrm{Kt}$-witness running in at most $2^{\mathrm{copyOverhead} + \lceil \log_2(n + 1) \rceil + m}$ steps.
   - **`MKtP ∈ E ⊆ EXP` and `MKtPAt ∈ EXP`**:
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP : Set (List Bool × ℕ)` (paired with unary threshold encoding `encPair encBits encUnary` so that $k + 1 \le |(x, 1^k)|$ holds unconditionally for arbitrary $k \in \mathbb{N}$; noted in the module docstring alongside Liu–Pass §2.2's $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$-bit binary threshold convention) and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtPAt (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (List Bool)`.
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP.boundedSearch`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP.boundedSearch_eq_true_iff_of_two_pow_le`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP.computableInPolyTime_boundedSearch`: bounded search over candidate programs `p = Ladner.word j` for $j < N$ running `universalTMRunFor p (Ladner.capPow 2 (k - p.length) N)`, certified in polynomial time when $k$ and $N$ are encoded in unary, with `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP.mem_E` padding $N$ to $2^{|\mathrm{enc}(x, k)|} \ge 2^{k + 1}$ via `setOf_mem_E_of_computableInPolyTime_pad`.
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP.mem_E : MKtP ∈ E (encPair encBits encUnary)`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtP.mem_EXP : MKtP ∈ EXP (encPair encBits encUnary)`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtPAt.polyTimeReducible_MKtP`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtPAt.mem_EXP`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MKtPAt.mem_EXP_polynomial`.
   - **Promise problem `GapMKtP`**:
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMKtP`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMKtP.yesSet`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMKtP.noSet`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMKtP.disjoint_yesSet_noSet`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMKtP.id_eq` ([Oliveira and Santhanam, Appendix A, Definition 44, p. 34][OliveiraSanthanam2018]).

3. **`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/Conditional.lean`**:
   - **Conditional Universal Multi-Tape Reference Machine (`condUniversalTM`)**:
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.condUniversalTMProgram`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.condUniversalTMRunFor`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.condUniversalTM`: runs self-delimiting binary program `p` on pair input `encPair encBits encBits (w, y)`, certified in polynomial time (`Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.computableInPolyTime_condUniversalTMRunFor`) and forming a conditional description method `List Bool → DescriptionMethod (List Bool) (List Bool)` in the sense of `Complexity.Computability.Kolmogorov.ChainRule`.
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.exists_etimeBoundedComplexity_condUniversalTM_le_ofMultiTapeTM`: clock-preserving conditional simulation of any finite-state binary `MultiTapeTM` operating on `encPair encBits encBits (w, y)` with additive code prefix overhead `2 * code.length + 2`.
   - **Conditional Kolmogorov Complexity Measures ($K(x \mid y)$, $K^t(x \mid y)$, $\mathrm{Kt}(x \mid y)$)**:
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condPlain`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condPlainNat`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condTimeBoundedAt`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condTimeBounded`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condTimeBoundedNat` (conditional analogue of [Hirahara, Definition 7][Hirahara2018]), `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condLevinKt`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.condLevinKtNat` (conditional analogue of [Allender et al., Definition 1][AllenderBuhrmanKouckyVanMelkebeekRonneburger2006]).
     - Polynomial-time upper bounds: `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_condTimeBoundedAt_le_of_computableInPolyTime` ($K^t(F(w, y) \mid y) \le |w| + c$), `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_condTimeBoundedAt_apply_le` ($K^t(f(y) \mid y) \le c$), `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_condTimeBoundedAt_self_le` ($K^t(y \mid y) \le c$), and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_condTimeBoundedAt_le_length_add` ($K^t(x \mid y) \le |x| + c$).
     - Counting and incompressibility for every condition $y$: `Cslib.Kolmogorov.encard_setOf_condTimeBoundedAt_lt`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.exists_length_eq_forall_le_condTimeBoundedAt`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.two_pow_lt_ncard_setOf_length_eq_le_condTimeBounded_add`.

4. **`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/MINcKT.lean`**:
   - **`MINcKT ∈ NP`, `MINcKTAt ∈ NP`, and `GapMINcKT`**:
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKT.Instance`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKT`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKT.enc`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKT.check`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKT.computableInPolyTime_check`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKT.mem_NP : MINcKT ∈ NP MINcKT.enc` (conditional analogue of [Hirahara, Definition 9][Hirahara2018]).
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKTAt`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKTAt.toInstance`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKTAt.computableInPolyTime_toInstance`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKTAt.polyTimeReducible_MINcKT`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKTAt.mem_NP`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINcKTAt.mem_NP_polynomial₂`.
     - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMINcKT`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMINcKT.yesSet`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMINcKT.noSet`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMINcKT.disjoint_yesSet_noSet`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMINcKT.id_eq` (conditional analogue of [Hirahara, Definition 11][Hirahara2018], parameterized by gap functions `σ, τ : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ`).

### Documentation & Catalogue Assessment
- Updated `ROADMAP.md`, `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/MINKT.lean`, and `references.bib` (recording `definition numbers follow ECCC TR18-138` on [Hirahara][Hirahara2018] and `section and theorem numbers follow ECCC TR21-056` on [Liu and Pass][LiuPass2021Crypto]).
- Assessed `abstracts/catalogue.json`: `MKtP ∈ EXP` and `MINcKT ∈ NP` are foundational complexity class memberships supporting the metacomplexity track (#798) rather than standalone headline theorems in the curated abstract catalogue, so no new abstract entry is needed.

### Validation
- `./scripts/check.sh` passed (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`).
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`, `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only`, and `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passed.
- Non-vacuity tests in `ComplexityTests/MINcKT.lean` verify concrete `MKtP` yes-instances, [Liu and Pass][LiuPass2021Crypto] Fact 3.1 witness step bounds, `MINcKT` 0-step non-membership, self-conditioning yes-instances, and conditional incompressibility no-instances.

issue.title: feat(crypto): add joint (security, d) polynomial runtime for leveled FHE
issue.body:
## Summary

Addresses Item 4 of #1104 ("A runtime polynomial in `(λ, d)` jointly"):

- **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Homomorphic/Leveled/Bootstrapping.lean`**:
  - Adds plain-first `Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.schemeFamily_spec`, packaging Gentry's depth-indexed leveled FHE family `fun d => Leveled.scheme D (fun _ => d)` with:
    - Polynomial secret-key and ciphertext width bounds (`Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded`),
    - Joint uniform strict PPT runtime certificates in `(security, d)` for `keyGen` (`Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encUnary) (encPair encBits encBits) (fun p => (Leveled.scheme D (fun _ => p.2)).keyGen p.1)`), `encrypt`, and `evaluate` (`Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn` on `(1^security, 1^d, pk, C, inputs)`), and
    - Joint deterministic polynomial runtime in `(security, d)` for `decrypt` (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime`).
- **`abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/GSWFHEAbstract.lean` & `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/GSWFHEBridge.lean`**:
  - Defines `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEAbstract.NativeInDepth` (and `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEBridge.NativeInDepth` / `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEBridge.nativeInDepth_of`), asserting that for a depth-indexed scheme family `E : ℕ → Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme`, key generation, encryption, decryption, and evaluation each run on a single uniform machine taking `(1^security, 1^d, …)` with one runtime polynomial in `(security, d)` jointly ([Gentry2009] Definition 3).
  - Strengthens `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEAbstract.leveled`, `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEBridge.leveled`, and `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEBridge.leveled_witness` so that `leveled` provides both the depth-indexed family `E` satisfying `NativeInDepth E` (and all correctness, width, decryption-circuit, and IND-CPA properties at each `d : ℕ`) and, for every unary-polynomial depth budget `budget`, a scheme `S` obtained by substituting `d = budget security` into `E` (`S.keyGen security = (E (budget security)).keyGen security` and `S.evaluate security = (E (budget security)).evaluate security`).
- **`ComplexityTests/Abstracts/GSWFHETests.lean` & `abstracts/catalogue.json`**:
  - Adds a client test unpacking `E` and `NativeInDepth E` from `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEAbstract.leveled` and updates the `gsw-fhe` scope summary in `abstracts/catalogue.json`.

## Source Statement & Notation Mapping

- **Source & exact locator:** Craig Gentry, *Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices*, STOC 2009, Section 2, Definition 3 & Theorem 3, pp. 170–171.
- **Source statement (paraphrase of [Gentry2009, Definition 3, p. 170] + verbatim complexity clause as cited in #1104):**
  Paraphrase of Definition 3: a family of homomorphic encryption schemes $\{\mathcal{E}^{(d)} : d \in \mathbb{Z}^+\}$ is leveled fully homomorphic if each $\mathcal{E}^{(d)}$ compactly evaluates all circuits of depth at most $d$ using a common decryption circuit shared across all $d$, and verbatim: *"the computational complexity of $\mathcal{E}^{(d)}$'s algorithms is polynomial in $\lambda$, $d$, and (in the case of $\mathsf{Evaluate}_{\mathcal{E}^{(d)}}$) the size of $C$"*.
- **Notation & convention mapping:**

| Source (`[Gentry2009]`, Definition 3 & Theorem 3, pp. 170–171) | Lean statement (`Leveled.schemeFamily_spec` / `GSWFHEAbstract.NativeInDepth` / `GSWFHEAbstract.leveled`) |
|---|---|
| Security parameter $\lambda$ and depth index $d \in \mathbb{N}$ | `(security, d) : ℕ × ℕ` encoded in unary (`Encoding.encPair Encoding.encUnary Encoding.encUnary`) |
| Depth-indexed scheme family $\{\mathcal{E}^{(d)}\}_{d \in \mathbb{N}}$ | `E : ℕ → Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme`, witnessed by `fun d => Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.scheme D (fun _ => d)` |
| Single decryption circuit shared across all depths $d$ | `circuit : ∀ security, Cslib.Circuits.Circuit Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.signature ((3 * secretWidth security + 1) + (ciphertextWidth security + 1)) 1` chosen before `d` and `budget` |
| Joint polynomial runtime in $(\lambda, d)$ for $\mathsf{KeyGen}_{\mathcal{E}^{(d)}}$, $\mathsf{Encrypt}_{\mathcal{E}^{(d)}}$, $\mathsf{Decrypt}_{\mathcal{E}^{(d)}}$ | First three conjuncts of `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEAbstract.NativeInDepth E` taking `(1^security, 1^d, …)` |
| Joint polynomial runtime in $(\lambda, d, |C|)$ for $\mathsf{Evaluate}_{\mathcal{E}^{(d)}}$ | Fourth conjunct of `ComplexityTests.Abstracts.GSWFHEAbstract.NativeInDepth E`: `Randomized.StrictPPT` on `(1^security, 1^d, pk, C, inputs)` with `C` encoded via `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.encCircuit 1` |
| Substitution $d = \text{budget}(\lambda)$ for unary-polytime depth budgets | `S.keyGen security = (E (budget security)).keyGen security ∧ S.evaluate security = (E (budget security)).evaluate security` |

Refs #1104

- `taskset -c 0-7 ./scripts/check.sh`
- `taskset -c 0-7 lake build ComplexityAbstracts`
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`
- `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`
- `python3 scripts/check_changed_files.py`
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`
- `python3 scripts/check_pr_names.py --strict`

issue.title: feat(ppt): lift plain deterministic certificates to pure programs
issue.body:
Expose `ComputableInPolyTime.isPPTOn`: a deterministic function with a plain polynomial-time certificate gives a strict fair-coin program returning that function's value. The machine ignores its sampled bits. Types, encodings, uniform input scope and result distribution match the existing raw theorem; its construction is reused with proof-local `h.tidy`.

Bounded support for #750. Payload-only rebase onto actual main `60440a792ceac91ab7f524bcd197b044ecc56d62` after #811 and #823 squash-merged. The provider and test files are byte-identical to approved `11b13eea`; the aggregate adds only the original test import. Both original global registrations and the raw proof remain unchanged. No tactic-index change, callback batch, model change, alias or raw fallback is added.

The old queue prefix failed fresh GMWPointwise and OraclePPT proofs because the new plain route exposed missing encoding-conversion/projection support. [The corrected causal record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/813#issuecomment-6386870517) isolates the registration interaction and establishes the library-only #811+#823 context as sufficient; removing the raw rule alone was not a fix, and BEq is not a prerequisite for these regressions.

At exact `6b2fe277e4bbe7827a10a821d7efc1cc4a28312d`, strict provider/original-client targets pass (7318 jobs). Both original failure files were then executed directly in fresh Lean processes: GMWPointwise passes in 4.944s and OraclePPT in 6.796s, with unchanged source blobs and their original 200,000-heartbeat limits. No diagnostic preamble, attribute filter, budget increase or fixture change was used. These are fresh proof executions, not inferred from cached gate success.

All six local gates at four threads, fresh-output S3 (1899 statements/402 modules, matching the inherited baseline), hygiene with --check-simp, catalogue selection (14 abstracts/19 headlines) and whitespace checks pass. Ordinary-import named/automatic/missing-premise regressions remain intact. The earlier scoped [652 review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/608#issuecomment-6382530362) and provider source approval are reused; exact-new-head integration review and hosted CI remain required. This does not claim the separately owned final per-search backend or global S1 parity.

Abstract assessment: no selected headline statement, model, encoding, bound or renderer changes; no new PDF inspection is needed.

issue.title: Kilian's succinct arguments: PCP + collision-resistant hashing ⇒ succinct arguments for NP
issue.body:
Posted by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` at Samuel's direction (2026-10-25). Part of the crypto program (#640, #643).

## Goal
**Kilian's succinct arguments:** if collision-resistant hash families exist, every language in NP has an interactive argument with polylogarithmic communication (Kilian 1992). The library already has the PCP theorem (a curated headline) and keyed collision-resistant hash families (#678), so the main missing piece is the commitment layer. A second endpoint is the random-oracle version: Micali's CS proofs, or the BCS transform for IOPs. It ties this track to #643's sumcheck and GKR work.

## Milestones
- **M0, design** (a comment here before any Lean): exact statements and source locators. Candidates are Kilian STOC 1992; Barak–Goldreich, *Universal arguments*, for the careful analysis; Micali 2000; Ben-Sasson–Chiesa–Spooner, TCC 2016. M0 also fixes the argument model (computational soundness against PPT provers, with explicit communication and verifier time) and the reuse plan.
- **M1, Merkle-tree vector commitments** from a collision-resistant family: position binding with a certified reduction, and opening size `O(log n)` hash values.
- **M2, Kilian's protocol:** composing a PCP with M1, with completeness and computational soundness by extraction or rewinding, and an exact soundness loss.
- **M3, the succinctness accounting:** communication and verifier time, kept separate from the PCP's query and randomness complexity.
- **M4 (optional), the random-oracle version:** Micali or BCS, reusing the Fiat–Shamir random-oracle API.

## Rules
The #897 shared rules apply. Security statements need certified efficient reductions (#733), plain-first statements (#456), and reuse of the existing PCP, hash and interactive APIs.

issue.title: refactor(classes): define P, NP, FNP and polynomial-time reductions with plain computability
issue.body:
Milestone M2a of #456. This is a refactor of definitional presentation, not new mathematics: `P`, `NP`, `FNP`, `FPSearch`, `SearchReducible`, `PolyTimeReducible` (and `PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`), `PolyTimeTruthTableReducible` and `ParsimoniousReducible` now ask for plain `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime` instead of `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`. The two notions are equivalent (`computableInPolyTime_iff_computableTidilyInPolyTime`), so no class changes. Names are unchanged, `mem_X` is still the definitional unfolding, and each definition gets a one-rewrite tidy form for proofs:

- `mem_P_iff_tidy`, `mem_NP_iff_tidy`, `mem_FNP_iff_tidy`, `mem_FPSearch_iff_tidy`
- `polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy`, `PromiseProblem.polyTimeReducible_iff_tidy`, `searchReducible_iff_tidy`, `polyTimeTruthTableReducible_iff_tidy`, `parsimoniousReducible_iff_tidy`

`mem_P_iff_exists_decidableInTimeAndSpace` and `mem_NP_iff_exists_computableInTimeAndSpaceOfLength` keep their statements and are now short term proofs from the definitions. `Classes/P.lean` and `Classes/NP.lean` publicly import `PolyTime/Plain.lean` (which re-exports the tidy module they imported before), so the bridges are available wherever `P` or `NP` is.

**Public statements whose shape changed**
- The nine definitions above.
- `mem_P`, `mem_NP`, `mem_FNP`, `mem_FPSearch`: plain instead of tidy.
- `polyTimeReducible_iff_manyOneReducibleBy`: now `ManyOneReducibleBy (ComputableInPolyTime · encA encB)`.

No other statement text changed. Statements that mention these classes now refer to the plain definitions, which are equivalent to the old ones.

**Proof migration.** About 105 library files and 20 test files needed edits, almost all one token: `.of_tidy h` where a tidy certificate fills a plain slot, `h.tidy` where a plain hypothesis feeds a tidy-only lemma, or `mem_X_iff_tidy.mp/mpr` where a proof destructures or builds a whole membership. No proof got materially longer.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- Lemmas with tidy hypotheses or conclusions keep their statements and are left for M3, e.g. `mem_FNP_iff_exists_bounded`, `mem_FPSearch_of_total`, `exists_total_of_mem_FPSearch`, `verifierSearch_mem_FNP`, `SearchReducible.of_isTotalSearch`, `truthTable_mem_P`, `mem_NP_of_witness`, `mem_PromiseP_iff`, `mem_PromiseNP_iff`, `ofSlices_mem_P_iff`.
- Proofs that open a `P` or `NP` certificate to reach the machine (Cook–Levin, Ladner, the time hierarchy, circuit-value completeness) go through `mem_P_iff_tidy`/`mem_NP_iff_tidy` because they use tidy run lemmas.
- Rebased onto `main` after #557 (#547): where both sides are now plain the boundary conversions are gone; the ones that remain feed tidy-stated helper lemmas. The delta is listed in the rebase comment.
- Plain `fun_prop` did not reach three goals that tidy `fun_prop` proves (two tests and `TQBFCNF_mem_PSPACE`); they use `.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`. Reported on #545, which has since added plain `trans`/`fst'`/`snd'` rules.

**Abstract impact.** No abstract statement or catalogue entry changes. Two bridge proofs change, by one line each: `CookLevinBridge.polyTimeReducible_iff` is now `Iff.rfl`, since the bridge's local plain reducibility is definitionally the library's, and `TQBFBridge.tqbf_pspaceHard` destructures the plain certificate directly. `FaginBridge` and `SubsetSumBridge` are unchanged. #497 moves these files; the integrator should carry the two one-line edits across. `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes.

**Docs.** Module docstrings of the changed definitions; one word in `UPSTREAM.md` (the `P`/`NP` definitions are plain-machine, not tidy-machine); the #456 entry in `ROADMAP.md`.

**Validation.** `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates (build, `mk_all --check`, test, lint, lint-style, `checkInitImports`) at `c9c869e8` (linear on `main` `ba134c18`), together with the Python unit tests, `check_hygiene.py` and `build_abstracts.py --check`. The reviewed revision was `37d41d36`.

Closes #546

issue.title: feat(crypto): efficient DDH self-reduction, group-element ElGamal, and hashed ElGamal (#1047)
issue.body:
Refs #1047
Refs #640

## Summary

This PR adds four pieces of the Diffie–Hellman and ElGamal milestone of #1047, following Boneh–Shoup v0.6:
- word- and game-level consequences of DDH rerandomization;
- an original single-invocation worst-case-to-average-case DDH reduction;
- group-element ElGamal;
- Hashed ElGamal with a one-time-pad cipher.

It also moves the chosen-plaintext and one-time DEM games to the admissibility convention decided on #1120, which landed #1096 also uses for 1CCA.

### Already on `main` (not new here)

- **Rerandomization API.** `ddhRerandomize`, `ddhRerandomize_smul_generator`, `ddhRerandomizeLaw`, `ddhRerandomizeLaw_real` and `ddhRerandomizeLaw_ideal`. The target laws are `ddhRealTupleLaw` and `ddhIdealTupleLaw`.
- **Bit ElGamal.** `elGamalCPAGame`, `elGamalINDCPA` and `DDH.elGamalINDCPA`.
- **KEM–DEM hybrid for `Bool` messages.** `hybridEncrypt`, `advantage_hybridGame_le`, `advantage_hybridGame_le_two_mul`, `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa` and the bit one-time pad `otpEncrypt`.
- **Chosen-message adversaries.** `AdversaryOf`, `WordAdversary` and the always-unrestricted `INDCPAOf`, from #1043.
- **Bit-string lemmas.** `uniformList_map_listXor` and `uniformList_map_zipWith_xor`, the latter from #1067.

### New in this PR

1. **Admissibility convention (#1120)**, in `Encryption/Basic.lean` and `Encryption/PolyTime.lean`.
   - `gameOn valid` takes `valid : ℕ → List Bool → Msg → Msg → Bool`, which sees the security parameter, the public key and the challenge pair. An invalid pair makes the game return `false` in both experiments. `INDCPAOn` is the notion.
   - `game` and `INDCPAOf` become the always-true `abbrev`s, and `INDCPA` is unchanged.
   - `WordINDCPA` is `INDCPAOn (fun _ _ m₀ m₁ => m₀.length == m₁.length) encBits`.
   - `AdversaryOf.restrict` plays `gameOn valid` inside `game` by recording validity in its saved state (`eval_game_restrict`, `AdversaryOf.IsPPT.restrict`). This gives `INDCPAOf.indcpaOn` and `INDCPAOf.wordINDCPA`.
   - Supporting results: `eval_gameOn`, `INDCPAOn.congr` and `isPPTOn_gameOn`. The statement of `isPPTOn_game` is unchanged, and it is now derived from `isPPTOn_gameOn`.
   - The DEM side has the same shape: `demGameOn` and `DEMOneTimeINDCPAOn`, with `demGame`, `DEMOneTimeINDCPAOf`, `DEMOneTimeINDCPA` and `DEMOneTimeWordINDCPA` as `abbrev`s. Supporting results: `eval_demGame_restrict`, `isPPTOn_demGameOn` and `DEMOneTimeINDCPAOf.demOneTimeINDCPAOn`.
   - This replaces the previous head's clamp-based mechanism, which is removed: gameWith, INDCPAWith, selectChallenge, sameLength, AdversaryOf.clamp, wordGame, demGameWith and DEMOneTimeINDCPAWith.
2. **KEM–DEM hybrid over any message type**, in `Encryption/Hybrid.lean`.
   - The `main` development is generalized from `Bool` to `Msg` with an encoding `encMsg`. The definitions keep their names (`hybridEncrypt`, `hybridDecrypt`, `hybridIdealGame`, `hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, `hybridToDEMAdversary`), and `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa` now concludes `INDCPAOf encMsg`.
   - `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpaOn` proves Exercise 11.9(b) under an admissibility predicate that ignores the public key, through `eval_demGame_hybridToDEMAdversary_restrict`.
   - The `n`-bit word one-time pad: `otpWordEncrypt`, `otpWordDecrypt`, `otpWordDecrypt_otpWordEncrypt`, `isPPTOn_otpWordEncrypt` and `computableInPolyTime_otpWordDecrypt`. Its security: `demOneTimeINDCPA_otpWordEncrypt` (unrestricted) and `demOneTimeWordINDCPA_otpWordEncrypt`. Its PKE corollary is `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_otpWordEncrypt_indcpa`, which concludes `WordINDCPA`.
3. **DDH**, in `DiffieHellman.lean`.
   - Word-level rerandomization `encodeDDHRerandomize`, with `encodeDDHRerandomize_encode`, `encodeDDHRerandomize_val` and `computableInPolyTime_encodeDDHRerandomize`.
   - The game-level consequences of `ddhRerandomizeLaw_real` and `ddhRerandomizeLaw_ideal`: `ddhRerandomizeGame`, `ddhRerandomizeGame_real`, `ddhRerandomizeGame_ideal`, `advantage_ddhRerandomizeGame_eq` and `DDH.ddhRerandomizeGame`.
   - An original, single-invocation reduction with explicit sampling losses:
     - `ddhSampleModExponents` and `isPPTOn_ddhSampleModExponents`;
     - `sampleModZModLaw` and `dist_sampleModZModLaw_le`, with loss `1 / 2 ^ n` per exponent;
     - `ddhSelfReduceDistinguisher` and `isPPTOn_ddhSelfReduceDistinguisher`;
     - `ddhWorstCaseGame`;
     - `advantage_ddhRerandomizeGame_ddhWorstCaseGame_le`, with loss `3 / 2 ^ n`;
     - `advantage_ddhRealGame_le_ddhWorstCaseGame`, with loss `6 / 2 ^ n`;
     - `ddh_of_worstCase`.
4. **ElGamal**, in `ElGamal.lean`.
   - **Word-level operations:** `encodeElGamalPublicKey`, `encodeElGamalEncrypt`, `decodeElGamal_encodeElGamalEncrypt` and their polynomial-time certificates.
   - **Shared typed-message reduction:**
     - `elGamalMsgCPAGameOn`, `elGamalMsgToDDHDistinguisher` and `ddhRealGame_elGamalMsgToDDHDistinguisher`;
     - `AdmitsGroupElements`, `ddhIdealGame_elGamalMsgToDDHDistinguisher_false_eq_true` and `advantage_elGamalMsgCPAGameOn_le`;
     - `isPPTOn_elGamalMsgToDDHDistinguisher` and `DDH.negligible_elGamalMsgCPAGameOn`.

     The game uses the same `valid` shape as `Encryption.gameOn`.
   - **Bit ElGamal** is re-derived through the shared reduction, via `admitsGroupElements_encodeBit` and `elGamalCPAGame_eq_elGamalMsgCPAGameOn`, and the statement of `DDH.elGamalINDCPA` is unchanged. `elGamalToDDHDistinguisher` is now an `abbrev` of the shared distinguisher.
   - **Group-element ElGamal:** `elGamalGroupCPAGameOn`, `elGamalGroupToDDHDistinguisher`, `advantage_elGamalGroupCPAGameOn_le` and `DDH.negligible_elGamalGroupCPAGameOn`. The previous head's adversary-side hypothesis (ValidGroupMessages, removed) is now the predicate `valid`. The reduction needs `valid` to be polynomial time and to satisfy `AdmitsGroupElements`.
   - **Hashed ElGamal:**
     - the scheme: `hashedElGamalEncrypt`, `hashedElGamalDecrypt`, `hashedElGamalDecrypt_hashedElGamalEncrypt`, `encodeHashedElGamalEncrypt` and `decodeHashedElGamal`, with certificates;
     - the KDF game and assumption: `kdfRealGame`, `kdfIdealGame` and `SecureKDF`;
     - the three-hop `PMF` chain: `hashedElGamalCPAGame`, `hashedElGamalIdealDDHGame` and `hashedElGamalUniformPadGame`;
     - the reductions: `hashedElGamalToDDHDistinguisher` and `hashedElGamalToKDFDistinguisher`;
     - the results: `hashedElGamalUniformPadGame_false_eq_true`, `advantage_hashedElGamalCPAGame_le` and `DDH.negligible_hashedElGamalCPAGame`.

     The proof does **not** go through `KEMINDCPA` (see Limitations).
5. **Shared bit-string supplier, already landed via #1170:**
   - `listXor_pair_self_left` and `listXor_pair_self_left_of_length` in `Foundations/Data/BitString/List/Operations.lean`;
   - `uniformList_map_listXor_length` in `Probability/BitString/List.lean`.
6. **Proof-only client updates.** Because `game` is now an `abbrev`, proofs that unfold `Encryption.game` also unfold `Encryption.gameOn`. This affects:
   - four `Homomorphic` modules: FixedKey `Reduction` and `Security`, and the KeyChain and Leveled `Reduction/Game` files;
   - two abstract bridges: `GSWSecurityBridge` and `GSWFHEBridge`;
   - two tests: `FixedKeySecurity` and `LeveledSecurity`.

   No statement changes.

## Source quotes and mapping (Boneh–Shoup v0.6)

Quotations are copied from the v0.6 text, with the math retyped: subscripts and superscripts inline, and calligraphic and blackboard letters plain. Page numbers are the printed page footers. "…" marks an elision. Each mapping to Lean comes after its quote and is not part of the quotation.

**Attack Game 11.1, Section 11.2, p. 436.**
> Attack Game 11.1 (semantic security). For a given public-key encryption scheme E = (G, E, D), defined over (M, C), and for a given adversary A, we define two experiments.
> Experiment b (b = 0, 1):
> • The challenger computes (pk, sk) ←R G(), and sends pk to the adversary.
> • The adversary computes m₀, m₁ ∈ M, of the same length, and sends them to the challenger.
> • The challenger computes c ←R E(pk, m_b), and sends c to the adversary.
> • The adversary outputs a bit b̂ ∈ {0, 1}.

Mapping: `gameOn valid keyGen encrypt adversary bit n`.
- `adversary.choose` receives the public key and returns the pair.
- "of the same length" becomes the predicate `valid`. A pair that fails it is inadmissible, and the experiment then returns `false` whatever `bit` is, so the pair contributes no advantage.
- `WordINDCPA` takes `valid := fun _ _ m₀ m₁ => m₀.length == m₁.length`. For `Bool` messages (`INDCPA`), every pair is admissible.

**Attack Game 2.1, Section 2.2, p. 16.**
> Attack Game 2.1 (semantic security). For a given cipher E = (E, D), defined over (K, M, C), and for a given adversary A, we define two experiments, Experiment 0 and Experiment 1. For b = 0, 1, we define
> Experiment b:
> • The adversary computes m₀, m₁ ∈ M, of the same length, and sends them to the challenger.
> • The challenger computes k ←R K, c ←R E(k, m_b), and sends c to the adversary.
> • The adversary outputs a bit b̂ ∈ {0, 1}.

Mapping: `demGameOn valid encryptSym adversary bit n`.
- K is the set of `n`-bit keys (`BitString.sampleList n`).
- The adversary receives the empty public key `[]`, and `valid` is evaluated at it.
- `DEMOneTimeWordINDCPA` uses the equal-length predicate.

**Exercise 11.9(b), p. 461.**
> (b) Prove that E is semantically secure, assuming that E_kem and E_s are semantically secure. You should prove a concrete security bound that says that for every adversary A attacking E, there are adversaries B_kem and B_s (which are elementary wrappers around A) such that
> SSadv[A, E] ≤ 2 · SSadv[B_kem, E_kem] + SSadv[B_s, E_s].

Mapping:
- `advantage_hybridGame_le_two_mul` is the bound, and `advantage_hybridGame_le` is its two-distinguisher form. Both were on `main` for `Bool` and are generalized here to `Msg`.
- `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa` is the asymptotic statement, with every pair admissible.
- `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpaOn` is the same statement with both games restricted by a polynomial-time `valid` that ignores the public key.

**Exercise 10.8, Section 10.11, p. 425.**
> 10.8 (Random self-reduction for DDH (I)). Consider a specific cyclic group G of prime order q generated by g ∈ G. Let DH be the set of all DH-triples, i.e.,
> DH := {(g^α, g^β, g^{αβ}) ∈ G³ : α, β ∈ Z_q}.
> For fixed u ∈ G, and let T_u be the subset of G³ whose first coordinate is u. Consider the randomized mapping from G³ to G³ that sends (u, v, w) to (u, v*, w*), where
> σ ←R Z_q, τ ←R Z_q, v* ← g^σ v^τ, w* ← u^σ w^τ.
> Prove the following:
> (a) if (u, v, w) ∈ DH, then (u, v*, w*) is uniformly distributed over DH ∩ T_u;
> (b) if (u, v, w) ∉ DH, then (u, v*, w*) is uniformly distributed over T_u.

**Exercise 10.9, Section 10.11, pp. 425–426.**
> 10.9 (Random self-reduction for DDH (II)). Continuing with the previous exercise, consider the randomized mapping from G³ to G³ that sends (u, v, w) to (ũ, v, w̃), where
> ρ ←R Z_q, ũ ← g^ρ u, w̃ ← v^ρ w.
> Prove the following:
> (a) ũ is uniformly distributed over G;
> (b) (u, v, w) ∈ DH ⟺ (ũ, v, w̃) ∈ DH;
> (c) if we apply the randomized mapping from the previous exercise to (ũ, v, w̃), obtaining the triple (ũ, v*, w̃*), then we have
> • if (u, v, w) ∈ DH, then (ũ, v*, w̃*) is uniformly distributed over DH;
> • if (u, v, w) ∉ DH, then (ũ, v*, w̃*) is uniformly distributed over G³.

Mapping: the group is written additively. `ddhRerandomize d u v w r s₁ s₂`, already on `main`, is
`(r • u + s₁ • g, v + s₂ • g, r • w + (r * s₂) • u + s₁ • v + (s₁ * s₂) • g)`. In multiplicative notation that is `(g^{s₁} u^r, g^{s₂} v, g^{s₁s₂} v^{s₁} u^{r s₂} w^r)`.

This is Exercise 10.9's map followed by Exercise 10.8's map, with the roles of `u` and `v` swapped in both:
- Exercise 10.9's map with ρ = s₂ gives `(u, g^{s₂} v, u^{s₂} w)`.
- Exercise 10.8's map, fixing the second coordinate, with σ = s₁ and τ = r then gives the triple above.

Exercise 10.9(c) is `ddhRerandomizeLaw_real` (the image is uniform over DH, `ddhRealTupleLaw`) and `ddhRerandomizeLaw_ideal` (the image is uniform over G³, `ddhIdealTupleLaw`). Both are on `main`. This PR adds:
- the word-level evaluator `encodeDDHRerandomize`;
- the game-level statements `ddhRerandomizeGame_real`, `ddhRerandomizeGame_ideal`, `advantage_ddhRerandomizeGame_eq` and `DDH.ddhRerandomizeGame`.

**Exercise 10.10, Section 10.11, p. 426 (not formalized; it stays open in #1047).**
> 10.10 (Random self-reduction for DDH (III)). Continuing with the previous exercise, prove the following. Suppose A is an efficient algorithm that takes as input three group elements and outputs a bit, and which satisfies the following property: if α, β, γ ∈ Z_q are chosen at random, then
> |Pr[A(g^α, g^β, g^{αβ}) = 1] − Pr[A(g^α, g^β, g^γ) = 1]| = ε,
> where the probability is over the random choice of α, β, γ, as well as any random choices made by A. Assuming that 1/ε is poly-bounded, show how to use A to build an efficient algorithm B that for all inputs (u, v, w) correctly decides whether or not (u, v, w) ∈ DH with negligible error probability. That is, adversary B may output an incorrect answer, but for all inputs, the probability that its answer is incorrect should be negligible.
> Hint: Use a Chernoff bound.

Mapping: not formalized. Exercise 10.10 starts from an average-case distinguisher and builds a worst-case decider with negligible error, by amplification with a Chernoff bound. This PR proves only the single-invocation step, without amplification, and labels it original:
- `ddhSelfReduceDistinguisher` runs the given distinguisher once, on a tuple rerandomized with `ProbComp.sampleModNat` exponents.
- `advantage_ddhRealGame_le_ddhWorstCaseGame` bounds the average-case DDH advantage by its advantage on any fixed DH tuple family against any fixed non-DH family, plus `6 / 2 ^ n`.
- `ddh_of_worstCase` is the asymptotic form.

**Exercise 11.5(a), p. 459.**
> 11.5 (Multiplicative ElGamal). Let G be a cyclic group of prime order q generated by g ∈ G. Consider a simple variant of the ElGamal encryption system E_MEG = (G, E, D) that is defined over (G, G²). The key generation algorithm G is the same as in E_EG, but encryption and decryption work as follows:
> • for a given public key pk = u ∈ G and message m ∈ G:
> E(pk, m) := β ←R Z_q, v ← g^β, e ← u^β · m, output (v, e)
> • for a given secret key sk = α ∈ Z_q and a ciphertext (v, e) ∈ G²:
> D(sk, (v, e)) := e/v^α
> (a) Show that E_MEG is semantically secure assuming the DDH assumption holds in G. In particular, you should show that the advantage of any adversary A in breaking the semantic security of E_MEG is bounded by 2ε, where ε is the advantage of an adversary B (which is an elementary wrapper around A) in the DDH attack game.

Mapping:
- **The scheme.** The group is additive, so the ciphertext is `(β • g, (α * β) • g + m)`. At word level it is `encodeElGamalEncrypt`, decrypted by `decodeElGamal`.
- **The game.** `elGamalMsgCPAGameOn valid encodeMsg setup` plays Attack Game 11.1 with exact uniform exponents at the `PMF` level.
- **The message space.** M = G is a word-level predicate: `valid` must admit only words that encode group elements (`AdmitsGroupElements`). Group-element messages (`elGamalGroupCPAGameOn`) use the identity encoding. Bit messages (`elGamalCPAGame`) use the always-true predicate with `encodeBit`.
- **The bound.** `advantage_elGamalMsgCPAGameOn_le` bounds the advantage by the sum of the DDH advantages of two wrappers, `elGamalMsgToDDHDistinguisher … false` and `… true`. This is the 2ε of the source, with one wrapper per challenge bit.
- **The asymptotic statements** are `DDH.negligible_elGamalGroupCPAGameOn` and `DDH.elGamalINDCPA`.

**Section 11.5, p. 445, and Remark 11.1, p. 446.**
> It is built out of several components:
> • a cyclic group G of prime order q with generator g ∈ G,
> • a symmetric cipher E_s = (E_s, D_s), defined over (K, M, C),
> • a hash function H : G² → K.
> …
> E(pk, m) := β ←R Z_q, v ← g^β, w ← u^β, k ← H(v, w), c ← E_s(k, m)
> output (v, c);

> Remark 11.1 (Hashing (v, w) vs hashing only w). In E_EG, we derive the key k by hashing both v and w. In a variant, which we call E′_EG, we could derive the key k by hashing just w.

Mapping: `hashedElGamalEncrypt H d u m β` is the E′_EG variant. It hashes only w = β • u, together with the group description `d`, which the source treats as a system parameter. The symmetric cipher E_s is fixed to the one-time pad `listXor pad.length [pad, m]`. That specialization is this PR's choice, not Remark 11.1's.

**Attack Game 11.3, pp. 448–449, and Definition 11.5, p. 449.**
> Attack Game 11.3 (secure key derivation). For a given hash function F : X × Y → Z, and for a given adversary A, we define two experiments.
> Experiment b (b = 0, 1):
> • The challenger computes x ←R X, y ←R Y, z₀ ← F(x, y), z₁ ←R Z, and sends (x, z_b) to the adversary.
> • The adversary outputs a bit b̂ ∈ {0, 1}.
> If W_b is the event that A outputs 1 in Experiment b, then we define A’s advantage with respect to F as
> KDFadv[A, F] := |Pr[W₀] − Pr[W₁]|.

> Definition 11.5 (secure key derivation). A hash function F : X × Y → Z is a secure KDF if for every efficient adversary A, the value KDFadv[A, F] is negligible.

Mapping:
- `kdfRealGame` and `kdfIdealGame` are Experiments 0 and 1, and `SecureKDF` is Definition 11.5, with:
  - x the group description `d`, drawn from `setup n`;
  - y = γ, with F(x, y) = `H (d, encode (γ • g))`;
  - Z the set of `msgLen n`-bit words.
- The distinguisher also receives independent uniform `α • g` and `β • g`. A strict PPT machine cannot sample them, because exact uniform exponents modulo an odd prime are not samplable in bounded time. They are independent of `(x, z_b)`.

**Theorem 11.5, p. 449.**
> Theorem 11.5. If the DDH assumption holds for G, H : G² → K is a secure KDF, and E_s is semantically secure, then E_EG is semantically secure.
> In particular, for every SS adversary A that plays Attack Game 11.1 with respect to E_EG, there exist a DDH adversary B_ddh that plays Attack Game 10.6 with respect to G, a KDF adversary B_kdf that plays Attack Game 11.3 with respect to H, and an SS adversary B_s that plays Attack Game 2.1 with respect to E_s, where B_ddh, B_kdf, and B_s are elementary wrappers around A, such that
> SSadv[A, E_EG] ≤ 2 · DDHadv[B_ddh, G] + 2 · KDFadv[B_kdf, H] + SSadv[B_s, E_s]. (11.14)

Mapping:
- **The game.** `hashedElGamalCPAGame` plays the role of Attack Game 11.1 for E′_EG with the one-time pad. It admits every challenge pair, which is stronger than the equal-length rule; the ciphertext length does not depend on the message.
- **The bound.** `advantage_hashedElGamalCPAGame_le` bounds the advantage by two DDH terms (`hashedElGamalToDDHDistinguisher … false` / `… true`) plus two KDF terms (`hashedElGamalToKDFDistinguisher … false` / `… true`). For the one-time pad SSadv[B_s, E_s] = 0, because `hashedElGamalUniformPadGame_false_eq_true` shows the uniform-pad hybrids are equal.
- **The asymptotic statement** is `DDH.negligible_hashedElGamalCPAGame`.
- **Not covered.** Theorem 11.5 for a general E_s, and E_EG hashing (v, w), are not covered.

## Existing notions considered

- **`gameOn` and `INDCPAOn`.** These generalize `main`'s `game` and `INDCPAOf` rather than sitting beside them: both are now the always-true `abbrev`s. They follow cca2GameOn and INDCCA2On from landed #1096: same predicate type, same false-on-invalid shape, same `…On` naming. The previous head's clamp-based gameWith and INDCPAWith, which replaced invalid pairs by `(m₀, m₀)`, are removed, so one admissibility mechanism remains.
- **`AdversaryOf.restrict`.** The previous head's AdversaryOf.clamp, now removed, cannot express "return `false` on an invalid pair". `restrict` records the validity bit in the saved state instead, and it is the only device used to pass from unrestricted to restricted notions.
- **`demGameOn` and `DEMOneTimeINDCPAOn`.** These generalize `main`'s `Bool`-only `demGame` and `DEMOneTimeINDCPA`, which are now `abbrev`s.
  - `Encryption.gameOn` cannot be reused: its `encrypt` sees only the public key, while a DEM encrypts under the secret key.
  - `SymmetricCipher.INDCPA` in `Encryption/Authenticated.lean` cannot be reused either. It is multi-query adaptive CPA on `n`-bit messages, while Exercise 11.9 needs the one-time notion of Attack Game 2.1.
- **`AdmitsGroupElements`.** `PrimeOrderGroupFamily` has no membership test, so validity of a word is stated as membership in `Set.range (F.encode d)`. This replaces the previous head's adversary-side ValidMessages and ValidGroupMessages, which are removed.
- **`elGamalMsgCPAGameOn`, `hashedElGamalCPAGame` and the hashed hybrids.** These cannot be `Encryption.gameOn`, whose key generator is a `ProbComp`, because ElGamal samples exact uniform exponents at the `PMF` level. They use the same `valid` shape where a predicate is needed. `main`'s `elGamalCPAGame` is kept, and `elGamalCPAGame_eq_elGamalMsgCPAGameOn` proves it equal to the bit instance.
- **`kdfRealGame`, `kdfIdealGame` and `SecureKDF`.** The library has no key-derivation notion.
- **`ddhRerandomizeGame` and `ddhWorstCaseGame`.** These are built on `main`'s `ddhRerandomize` and `ddhRerandomizeLaw`, and on `ddhRealGame` and `ddhIdealGame`.
- **`ddhSampleModExponents` and `sampleModZModLaw`.** These reuse `ProbComp.sampleModNat` and its distance bound.
- **`otpWordEncrypt` and `otpWordDecrypt`.** These reuse `BitString.listXor`. `main` had only the bit pad `otpEncrypt`.

## Limitations

- **Exact exponent sampling.** Key generation and challenge encryption in the ElGamal and Hashed ElGamal games sample exact uniform exponents in `ZMod (F.order d)` at the `PMF` level. Efficient key generation and encryption remain open (ROADMAP).
- **Hashed ElGamal does not go through `KEMINDCPA`.** For the same sampling reason, its security is a direct three-hop `PMF` chain rather than an instance of `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_otpWordEncrypt_indcpa` (module docstring, "Limitations").
- **`SecureKDF` is assumed.** The only instance is the degenerate `msgLen = 0` smoke test `secureKDF_nil` in the tests. A nondegenerate instance and Theorem 11.5 for a general E_s stay open in #1047.
- **Exercise 10.10 is open**, as described above.
- **Group-element ElGamal takes `valid` as a parameter**, because the family has no membership test. The tests instantiate it on Schnorr groups with `twoElements`, which admits the encoded identity and generator.
- **`KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpaOn` requires `valid` to ignore the public key.** The DEM adversary receives `[]`. The equal-length rule satisfies this.
- **Integration with #1096.** The current-main refresh retains its landed CCA development and uses the shared `gameOn` definition in the required proof simplifications.

## Tests

- **Equal-length rule.** `ComplexityTests/Crypto/HybridEncryption.lean` shows that the rule has force:
  - the length-only scheme `lengthOnlyEncrypt` satisfies `WordINDCPA` (`wordINDCPA_lengthOnly`);
  - it fails the unrestricted `INDCPAOf encBits`, because `lengthAdversary` wins with advantage `1` (`not_indcpaOf_lengthOnly`).
- **Hybrid instances.** `indcpa_hybridEncrypt_idealEncaps_otpWordEncrypt` instantiates `KEMINDCPA.hybrid_otpWordEncrypt_indcpa`, and the word pad is checked by a concrete round trip.
- **DDH and ElGamal**, in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/DiffieHellman.lean`:
  - concrete `decide` checks of the word-level ElGamal, Hashed ElGamal and rerandomization operations on the Schnorr group `d23`;
  - the group ElGamal theorem with predicate `twoElements` (`admitsGroupElements_twoElements`, `computableInPolyTime_twoElements`) and an adversary whose pair is admissible;
  - the degenerate Hashed ElGamal smoke test;
  - a concrete instance of `advantage_ddhRealGame_le_ddhWorstCaseGame` on `d23` at `n = 4`.

  The three signature-restatement examples are removed.

## Abstract impact

No statement or catalogue entry changes. The proofs in `GSWSecurityBridge` and `GSWFHEBridge` add `Crypto.Encryption.gameOn` to a `simpa only` set.

## Framework friction

The three reusable word-XOR facts were extracted verbatim into the existing BitString and probability homes by #1170, now actually merged as `b8be084b`. This consumer reuses that shared source, the existing `Game`/advantage machinery, strict PPT certificates, sampling APIs and shared hybrid games. The parallel game notions and their differing message/admissibility/sampling scopes are explained above; no new compatibility API or global automation fallback was introduced. This addresses the shared-machinery split requested under #733.

## Validation

Current-main candidate: `610ca8ee5758d500cb601825f7e6e27a3b03b48f`, an ordinary history-preserving merge of reviewed `c2fb6d5a` with actual main `b8be084b` (including #1170, #1168, #1161 and #1096).

- Strict affected five-source check: PASS (6814 jobs).
- Original DiffieHellman, HybridEncryption, FixedKeySecurity and LeveledSecurity targets: PASS (7074 jobs).
- DiffieHellman.lean and ElGamal.lean are byte-identical to the reviewed c2 source. The current-main plain APIs are retained; proof transports made obsolete by those APIs were removed.
- All six required local gates pass on this exact source: strict library build, mk_all, strict tests (including the formal abstract audits), lint, lint-style and checkInitImports. Changed-file lints pass (11 library modules). The only newly required downstream repair adds `gameOn` to the existing CCA proof simplification set; its statement and experiment are unchanged. Fresh native update/check confirms the unchanged 896 statements / 132 modules baseline, with no increases or allowlist changes. Hygiene/check-simp passes. Exact-head hosted checks are running: [Lean Action CI 40310701297](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40310701297) and [Formal abstract PDFs 40310701290](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40310701290); no hosted success is claimed yet. Earlier c2 hosted CI is historical evidence only: [Lean Action CI 40233981961](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40233981961) and [formal abstracts 40233981911](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40233981911).

- **Takeover.** After three review rounds, the coordinator took the PR over (comment 6402929856). `worker-claude-takeover-1053-c4b0c164`, a Claude Code worker delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`, made these changes:

issue.title: refactor(classes): make proof helpers private across the classes area
issue.body:
Makes 734 proof helpers private, in 129 modules of the classes area. This is item 2 of #610, sized as one mechanical PR following Samuel's rule change on #587. Statements and proofs are unchanged. The only edits are the `private` modifier, line breaks in signatures that it pushed past 100 columns, and five `@[expose]` attributes removed from definitions that became private (they are redundant there, and `--wfail` rejects them).

**Rule.** A declaration becomes private when all of the following hold:
- `scripts/quality_report.py` (#604, run at d52fd12c) lists it as a privatization candidate. That means:
  - no other library module, test or abstract references it;
  - no module doc or README names it;
  - it has no implicit-use attribute (`simp`, `fun_prop`, `aesop`, instance, …);
  - no statement or exposed body that stays public mentions it.
- Its own module uses it, so it is a step of a proof there. Unused candidates stay public for a separate review.
- Its name is not API-shaped.

The following stay public even when they meet the rule:
- names ending in `_iff`, `mono`, `anti`, `nonneg`, `pos`, `apply`, `ext`, `comm`, `congr`, `symm`, `trans`, `refl`, `def`, `injective` and the like;
- names that contain a class or problem name (`mem_BPP`, `UP_subset_ModP`, `inter_mem_ParityP`, `SATH_notMem_P`) or are `isVerifier`;
- the definitional modules of communication, decision-tree and query complexity, Kolmogorov complexity and learning, except their proof developments (`DecisionTree/Switching`, `DecisionTree/CanonicalTree`, `SensitivitySeparation/Internal`) and nine Huang and sensitivity proof steps;
- a few modules whose lemmas are the basic API of their definitions (`TFNP`, `PH`, `ZPP`, `RP`, `BooleanHierarchy`, `Alternation`, `Constructible`, `Parameterized`, `FineGrained`, `FineGrained/Exponents`, `Reduction/TruthTable`, `Classes/PCP`, `MIP/Defs`, `TFNP/Subclasses/Principles`, `TreeEval/Instance`), and the PCP modules whose fate #610 leaves open (`ConstraintGraph`, `RegularConstraintGraph`, `LocalTest`, `Amplification`, `Amplifier`, `GapTheorem`, `Approximation`).

**Build exceptions.** Nine more declarations stay public because the build needs them public:
- seven are reached through dot notation or namespace resolution, which does not find private names: `iffTokens`, `Graph.vertexEquiv`, `mod_lt_of_lt_mul`, `Interaction.pushStep`, `natDegree_minpoly_of_aeval_eq_zero`, `ModelChecker.tupleExpr` and `Encoded.Graph.readLabel`;
- two are used by an exposed public body: `USTCON.Reader.card_label_eq_numLabels` and `walkFrom`.

**Scope.** Files touched by an open PR or by the deprecation sweep (#631) are left out, for example `Hierarchy`, `Ladner/PolyTime`, `MIP/NEXP`, `ValiantVazirani/Reduction` and `TreeEval/Reader/Cert/Weight`. That covers 201 candidates, plus the 12 modules that #632 and #621 also edit (124 declarations, dropped in 8bca8c48). These files follow in a second pass once those PRs land.

| Subtree | Declarations made private |
|---|---|
| Classes | 285 |
| TreeEval | 108 |
| PCP | 70 |
| QueryComplexity | 47 |
| Problems | 44 |
| Parameterized | 38 |
| FineGrained | 34 |
| Fagin | 28 |
| DecisionTree | 26 |
| AffineDisperser | 21 |
| CookLevin | 14 |
| HardnessEncoding | 10 |
| USTCON | 5 |
| Communication, MCSP | 2 each |

105 of them have tidy statements, so #456's S2 sweep has 105 fewer public statements to rename.

**Why.** Users and agents get about 730 fewer public names to navigate. Editing these proof steps also no longer changes the exported module interfaces that downstream builds depend on (#609).

**Review.** Check against the rule above, with spot checks. Proof steps such as `Reader.hTup`, `IP.PSPACE.pushStep` and the `Switching` encode/decode lemmas illustrate the rule, while a result that a module's doc should list would be an exception.

**Risk.** Low. The build rejects any private name that another module, a test, an abstract or an exposed body uses; that check found the nine exceptions above. No aliases are needed (#588).

**Validation** at 8bca8c48 (on 375ea689):
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates;
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`;
- the Python unit tests;
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.

**Abstract impact.** None. Abstracts and bridges reference no changed declaration, which the report confirms (zero abstract references) and the build of `ComplexityAbstracts` checks.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/OneWay): formalize Yao's weak-to-strong OWF hardness amplification
issue.body:
Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

Refs #733, #798. Restacked onto `main` after #998 squash-merged at 17e656d875374bb21f69f225da0d02e99866fa91; #992 is also consumed from main.

### Summary

This supplier PR (M2b-2) formalizes Yao's weak-to-strong one-way function hardness amplification ([Yao1982]; [Goldreich, Vol. 1, §2.3, Theorem 2.3.2][Goldreich2001]; [Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]) in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/OneWay/Amplification.lean`:

> **Theorem 2.3 ([Yao82], p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`).** *Assume there exists a weak one-way function. Then there exists a one-way function.*

1. **Construction (`OneWayAmplification.parallelCore`, `OneWayAmplification.plantedImage`):**
   - Given `hf : WeakOneWay f`, apply `WeakOneWay.exists_fixedOutputLength` (#992) to obtain a weak one-way function $g$ with a polynomial-time unary output-length schedule `outLen : ℕ → ℕ` (`∀ x, (g x).length = outLen x.length`) and a positive polynomial $q \in \mathbb{N}[X]$ ($\forall N,\, 0 < q(N)$) such that `WeakOneWayAt g (fun N => 1 / (q.eval N : ℝ))`.
   - At parameter $n \in \mathbb{N}$, set block width $w(n) := n + 1$, block count $k(n) := 2 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot w(n)$, and input schedule $m(n) := k(n) \cdot w(n)$.
   - `parallelCore k w g n X` splits $X$ into $k(n)$ blocks of width $w(n)$ via `BitString.listRow` and concatenates $g(x_0) \mathbin{\Vert} \dots \mathbin{\Vert} g(x_{k(n)-1})$.

2. **Direct reduction and probability bound (`OneWayAmplification.familyInversionGame_parallelCore_negligible`):**
   - For any uniform strict PPT inverter $\mathcal{A}$ (`IsPPT encBits A`) and any target polynomial degree $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $p_d(n) := (n + 1)^{d + 1}$ and $t_d(n) := 4 \cdot q(w(n)) \cdot k(n) \cdot p_d(n)$.
   - Using `IsPPT.exists_total_seeded_evaluator`, the internal inverter $B_d(1^N, y)$ runs $t_d(N-1)$ independent mega-trials over `BitString.sampleList`, planting $y$ in each slot $j < k(N-1)$ via `plantedImage` and picking a valid preimage if one is found.
   - Using `BitString.uniformList_all_listRow_true` twice—once across the $k(n)$ input blocks of $X$ and once across the $t_d(n)$ independent seed blocks of $B_d$—together with the exact single-slot planting law `BitString.uniformList_replaceRow` (#998), the weak one-wayness bound on $g$ forces $\mathcal{A}$'s inversion probability at parameter $n$ to be at most $(1/2)^{n+1} + \frac{1}{2 p_d(n)} \le \frac{1}{p_d(n)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

3. **Headline theorems (`WeakOneWay.exists_oneWay`, `exists_oneWay_of_exists_weakOneWay`, `exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay`):**
   - Applying `OneWayReindex.oneWay` (#992) to the schedule $m(n)$ ($m(n) \ge n + 1$) extends `parallelCore k w g` to a single strong one-way function on all binary strings.
   - `exists_oneWay_iff_exists_weakOneWay` ([Goldreich, Vol. 1, §2.3, Theorem 2.3.2][Goldreich2001]) combines `exists_oneWay_of_exists_weakOneWay` ([Liu and Pass, Theorem 2.3, §2.1, p. 8 of `arXiv:2009.11514v1`][LiuPass2020]; [Yao1982]) with `OneWay.weakOneWay` (#992).

### Framework friction

- All shared mathematical prerequisites requested in review `5642226904` reuse existing library declarations (`one_sub_pow_le_half` in `Complexity/Foundations/Data/Finset/Sampling.lean`, `Real.one_sub_pow_mul_one_add_mul_le_one` in `Complexity/Foundations/Analysis/BernoulliInequality.lean`) or have been extracted into the preceding shared-support supplier PR #998 (`Real.one_sub_pow_le_one_div_one_add_mul`, `BitString.replaceRow`, `BitString.listRow_replaceRow`, `BitString.uniformList_replaceRow`, `PMF.bind_apply_le_on_support`, `PMF.map_true_mono`, `PMF.map_true_le_add`, `PMF.map_any_range_true_le_sum`, `PMF.map_not_true`).
- The reduction $B_d$ uses `IsPPTOn.map_with` on `BitString.sampleList` composed with a deterministic multi-tape certificate (`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.mapWithInput`, `flatMapToBitsWithInput`, `bitsRowWithInput`, `filterWithInput`), avoiding any custom probabilistic loop combinators.

issue.title: feat(crypto): prove a pointwise GMW view-to-PRG advantage reduction
issue.body:
Prove a pointwise finite security reduction for the existing masked-3SAT GMW simulator, making the current efficient-family restriction explicit at its actual proof boundary. This is a bounded mathematical milestone toward ROADMAP priority1, not completion of the broader auxiliary-input GMW objective deferred in #324. The integrated deterministic polynomial-time-family result remains credited to #357.

Current baseline: main e98c1b256ba3fe0c97fd6b3d5d7b6444c1ad4bc9. `GMW/Simulator.lean:626–659` replaces PRG pads directly and currently requires efficiently generated instance/witness/auxiliary families. It does not consume `BitCommitmentScheme.computational_hiding`; stateful Naor hiding is useful separately but is not a prerequisite on this proof path. `Hybrid/Sequence.lean:128–148` already proves a finite sequence-gap identity. The simulator in `GMW/PolyTime.lean:571–622` is witness-free and certified PPT.

Scope and acceptance criteria:

1. Define one uniform reduction with explicit ordinary input/advice encoding of security parameter, instance, valid witness, auxiliary string, and PRG challenge. Prove a finite view-advantage bound for every valid tuple, with no efficient-generation assumptions and without assuming a hiding/ZK field.
2. Derive and prove the exact hybrid loss and guessing-error term, including the existing generator parameter shift. A scouting candidate is the product of two dyadic-range losses with an exponential guessing-failure term; those constants and indexes are NOT yet checked and must not be advertised as a result.
3. Certify the complete reduction clock polynomial in its full encoded input, including hybrid selection, sampling, adaptive replies and retained verifier coins/state. Keep the simulator witness-free. Recover the existing uniform-family security theorem as a corollary, preserving public contracts or deprecated aliases.
4. Use a concrete satisfiable formula/witness and a randomized verifier whose challenge depends on the first commitment and whose output retains its coins/state. Cover zero/empty hybrid boundaries. Finite toy-generator identities may test the model but cannot certify cryptographic security.
5. Record the exact remaining auxiliary/nonuniform PRG premise separately. Do not claim current uniform `OneWay`/HILL implies it. Preserve completeness/soundness and document remaining witness-level Levin reductions and sequential amplification.
6. Run all six gates, axiom guards, independent exact-revision API/style and correctness reviews, and the reader-facing statement/index assessment required by the final repository policy.

Convention boundary: the finite theorem quantifies over every auxiliary word, but its algorithmic certificate is polynomial in total encoded input length. A security corollary for arbitrary polynomially bounded auxiliary strings must state each polynomial budget and the stronger PRG security premise. Unbounded auxiliary input with runtime bounded only by common-input/security size is a different convention and remains outside this milestone; current `IsPPT` uses parameter plus input length.

Source credit: Goldreich–Micali–Wigderson; Naor for the related commitment construction; existing Complexitylib formalizations and its three-copy masked-3SAT adaptation. Goldreich's author-hosted [Chapter4 draft, printed pp151–153 and173](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/PSBookFrag/part4N.pdf) explains the auxiliary-input clock convention and nonuniform-secrecy use; [AppendixC, TheoremC.10, printed p546](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/CC/r6.pdf) explicitly assumes nonuniform hardness. This is a missing formal assumption/bridge, not an impossibility claim.

Queue state: available, unclaimed. Coordinator-codex-01a1658b-20261022 created this after read-only scouting by worker_time408 and live open/closed issue searches. No implementation or theorem is claimed. Completing this issue must not mark the full original GMW endpoint complete.
