issue.title: feat(crypto): certified PPT reductions and probabilistic operations for Cramer-Shoup (#1000)
issue.body:
## Summary

Constructs the uniform strict-PPT (`IsPPTOn`) operations and security reductions for the **Multiplicative Cramer–Shoup public-key encryption scheme** ($\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$, [Boneh and Shoup, Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 521–522](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf), specialized to associated data $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$) over a `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, following the Games 0–4 reduction structure of [Boneh and Shoup, Section 12.5.3, Theorem 12.9, printed pp. 488–493](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf). Stacked on merged #1096, #1193, #1169, and #1207 (`UntilBad` witness-finding oracle supplier PR):

1. **Approximate exponent sampling via `ProbComp.sampleModNat` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CramerShoup/Reductions.lean`)**:
   - `sampleCramerShoupExp`, `sampleCramerShoupPair`, `sampleCramerShoupTripleExponents`, and `sampleCramerShoupSK`, sampling exponents modulo `F.order d` with `n + (encNat (F.order d)).length` random bits.
   - `Game.advantage` bounds relative to exact uniform draws on `ZMod (F.order d)`: `advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupExp_le` (`1 / 2 ^ n`), `advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupPair_le` (`2 / 2 ^ n`), `advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupTripleExponents_le` (`3 / 2 ^ n`), and `advantage_bind_sampleCramerShoupSK_le` (`6 / 2 ^ n`).
2. **Phase 1/2 and collision-tracking decryption oracle handlers**:
   - `cramerShoupPhase1Oracle`, `cramerShoupPhase2Reply`, `cramerShoupPhase2Oracle`, and `cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Oracle` (built on `finderPhase2Oracle`).
   - Modulo-order secret-key invariance and challenge consistency: `encodeCramerShoupPublicKey_eq_skNatOfZMod`, `encodeCramerShoupChallenge_eq_skNatOfZMod`, `decodeCramerShoup_eq_skNatOfZMod`, `cramerShoupPhase1Oracle_eq_skNatOfZMod`, `cramerShoupPhase2Oracle_eq_skNatOfZMod`, `cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Oracle_eq_skNatOfZMod`, and `encodeCramerShoupEncrypt_publicKey_eq_challenge` (Game 0 $\to$ Game 1, eq. (12.21), printed p. 490).
3. **Certified strict-PPT DDH distinguishers (`Game 1 → Game 2`, eq. (12.22), printed p. 492)**:
   - `cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher` and `cramerShoupToDDHDistinguisher`, with uniform strict-PPT certificates `isPPTOn_cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher` and `isPPTOn_cramerShoupToDDHDistinguisher`.
4. **Certified strict-PPT CRHF collision finders (`Game 3 → Game 4`, eqs. (12.24)–(12.25), printed p. 492)**:
   - `cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder` and `cramerShoupToCollisionFinder`, with uniform strict-PPT certificates `isPPTOn_cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder` and `isPPTOn_cramerShoupToCollisionFinder`.
5. **Certified strict-PPT `Encryption.cca2GameOn` operations**:
   - `decodeCramerShoupSK` (`decodeCramerShoupSK_encCramerShoupSK`), `cramerShoupValid` (`computableInPolyTime_cramerShoupValid`), `cramerShoupKeyGenProb` (`isPPTOn_cramerShoupKeyGenProb`), `cramerShoupEncryptProb` (`isPPTOn_cramerShoupEncryptProb`), and `cramerShoupDecryptOpt` (`computableInPolyTime_cramerShoupDecryptOpt`, `cca2Phase1Oracle_cramerShoupDecryptOpt`, `cca2Phase2Oracle_cramerShoupDecryptOpt`, `decodeBits4_dropFrame_encodeCramerShoupPublicKey`, `encodeCramerShoupEncrypt_skNatOfZMod`).

## Source Statements ([Boneh and Shoup, v0.6](https://toc.cryptobook.us/book.pdf), Section 12.5.3 & Exercise 12.27)

Verbatim from Boneh and Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography* (Version 0.6, Section 12.5.3, printed pp. 490, 492):

> **Game 2.** We next modify the Challenger in Game 1, replacing line (1) with
> $$(1) \qquad \alpha, \beta, \gamma \xleftarrow{R} \mathbb{Z}_q,\; u \leftarrow g^\alpha,\; v \leftarrow g^\beta,\; w \leftarrow g^\gamma$$
> It is clear that any 1CCA adversary that can distinguish between Games 1 and 2 can be converted into a DDH adversary. More precisely, we can easily construct an elementary wrapper $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}$ around $\mathcal{A}$, such that
> $$|\Pr[W_1] - \Pr[W_2]| \le \text{DDHadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{ddh}}, \mathbb{G}]. \quad (12.22)$$
> …
> **Game 4.** Now we widen the rejection rule in the decryption oracle (line (5)), replacing it with:
> $$(5) \qquad \text{if } (\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{z}', \hat{c}) = (v, w, z', c) \text{ or } \mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v}) \text{ or } z' \ne f'(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{\rho})$$
> where $\mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v})$ is the condition:
> $$(\hat{v}, \hat{w}, \hat{c}) \ne (v, w, c) \quad \text{and} \quad \hat{\rho} = \rho$$
> Let $Z_4$ be the event that in Game 4, the adversary submits a decryption query that would not have been rejected in Game 3, and yet triggers the condition $\mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v})$ in Game 4. Actually, we may as well define $Z_4$ to be the event that $\mathit{Coll}_{u,v}(\hat{u}, \hat{v})$ holds in Game 4 (which could only happen after line (2) is executed), since if this happens at all, then it happens before the two games diverge. Clearly, Games 3 and 4 proceed identically unless $Z_4$ occurs, and so by the Difference Lemma, we have
> $$|\Pr[W_3] - \Pr[W_4]| \le \Pr[Z_4]. \quad (12.24)$$
> Moreover, if event $Z_4$ does occur, this immediately gives us a collision for $H'$. Therefore, we can construct an elementary wrapper $\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}$ around $\mathcal{A}$ that outputs the colliding inputs when $Z_4$ occurs, and so
> $$\Pr[Z_4] \le \text{CRadv}[\mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{cr}}, H']. \quad (12.25)$$

Verbatim from Boneh and Shoup (Version 0.6, Exercise 12.27, printed pp. 521–522):
> Show that $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{MCS}}$ is CCA secure, provided $H'$ is collision resistant and the DDH assumption holds for $\mathbb{G}$.

**Scope and Adaptation Note**:
- Specialized to associated data $\mathcal{D} = \mathrm{Unit}$ and single-challenge 1CCA (`Definition 12.2`, printed p. 468).
- In the uniform strict-PPT (`IsPPTOn`) model over dyadic coin tosses, `sampleCramerShoupExp` draws `n + (encNat (F.order d)).length` random bits via `ProbComp.sampleModNat`, incurring at most `1 / 2 ^ n` statistical distance per exponent draw (`6 / 2 ^ n` for the 6-tuple secret key in `cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher` and `9 / 2 ^ n` for the 3 challenge exponents plus 6-tuple secret key in `cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder`).

## Existing Notions Considered

| New Declaration | Existing Notion Checked | Why Reused or Added |
|---|---|---|
| `sampleCramerShoupExp`, `sampleCramerShoupPair`, `sampleCramerShoupTripleExponents`, `sampleCramerShoupSK` | `ProbComp.sampleModNat` (`Complexity/Languages/Probabilistic/UniformNat.lean`) | Reuses `ProbComp.sampleModNat (n + (encNat (F.order d)).length) (F.order d)` so each exponent draw is uniform strict PPT (`IsPPTOn`) and within statistical distance `1 / 2 ^ n` of `PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod (F.order d))`. |
| `cramerShoupPhase1Oracle`, `cramerShoupPhase2Reply`, `cramerShoupPhase2Oracle`, `cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Oracle` | `cca2Phase1Oracle`, `cca2Phase2Oracle` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/CCA2.lean`), `cramerShoupPhase1Reply`, `cramerShoupCollisionPhase2Reply` (#1169), `finderPhase2Oracle` (`Complexity/Crypto/Game/UntilBad.lean`) | Wraps the pure decryption replies from #1169 into `StateT` handlers for `CCA2AdversaryOf` and connects them to `cca2Phase1Oracle` / `cca2Phase2Oracle` via `cca2Phase1Oracle_cramerShoupDecryptOpt` and `cca2Phase2Oracle_cramerShoupDecryptOpt`. |
| `cramerShoupMsgToDDHDistinguisher`, `cramerShoupToDDHDistinguisher`, `cramerShoupMsgToCollisionFinder`, `cramerShoupToCollisionFinder` | `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DDH` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/DiffieHellman.lean`), `CollisionFinderFor` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/CollisionResistant.lean`) | Certified strict-PPT reductions (`IsPPTOn`) from a `CCA2AdversaryOf Msg` to the library's `PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DDH` distinguisher and `CollisionFinderFor F.Desc`. |
| `decodeCramerShoupSK`, `cramerShoupValid`, `cramerShoupKeyGenProb`, `cramerShoupEncryptProb`, `cramerShoupDecryptOpt` | `Encryption.cca2GameOn`, `Encryption.INDCCA2On` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/CCA2.lean`, #1096) | Provides the `ProbComp` key generation, encryption, deterministic decryption, and group-membership challenge admissibility predicate (`cramerShoupValid`) together with their plain-first `ComputableInPolyTime` and `IsPPTOn` certificates (#456). |

## Framework friction and abstract-impact assessment

- **Framework friction**:

issue.title: feat(crypto): separate restricted and general auxiliary-input zero knowledge (#698)
issue.body:
Closes #698 (item 1 of #680).

### Summary

This PR separates restricted polynomial-time-generable computational zero knowledge (`GenerableZeroKnowledge`) from general auxiliary-input computational zero knowledge over arbitrary polynomially bounded valid families (`AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge`) in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/ZeroKnowledge.lean`, and connects the existing 3-copy masked-3SAT truth-table commitment GMW protocol (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/GMW`) to both notions:

- **Explicit advice-PRG premise and GMW view consequence (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/GMW/Simulator.lean`)**:
  - `GMW.AdvicePRG enc generator length`: packages plain polynomial-time computability (`ComputableInPolyTime generator encBits encBits`), stretch `∀ s, (generator s).length = length s.length`, and negligible PRG distinguishing advantage against every full-input uniform strict PPT test `test : (ℕ × (α × (List Bool × List Bool))) × List Bool → ProbComp Bool` (charged for `((1^n, (a n, (w n, z n))), challenge)`) across all arbitrary polynomially length-bounded families `a : ℕ → α`, `w z : ℕ → List Bool`. This stronger advice-supplied premise is stated explicitly and is not derived from uniform `PseudorandomGenerator` or `OneWay` security.
  - `GMW.AdvicePRG.gmwView_negligible`: wraps `gmwView_negligible_of_advice_prg` under plain `ComputableInPolyTime f enc encCNF` and `GMW.AdvicePRG enc generator length`, showing that for the 3-copy masked-3SAT protocol (`gmwProver` vs. the witness-free simulator `gmwSimulator`), every full-input uniform strict PPT distinguisher `adversary` (charged for `((1^n, (a n, z n)), view)`) has negligible advantage across all polynomially length-bounded valid families `a, w, z` (`∀ n, ThreeSAT.verifier (f (a n), w n) = true`).
- **Restricted vs. general auxiliary-input zero knowledge (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/ZeroKnowledge.lean`)**:
  - `GenerableZeroKnowledge enc prover isWitness`: for every uniform strict oracle PPT malicious verifier `Vstar` (charged for `(1^n, (a, z))`), there exists a single uniform strict PPT witness-free simulator `S` (chosen before the families and charged for `(1^n, (a, z))`) whose output ensemble is `ComputationallyIndistinguishable` from the real interaction output across all deterministic polynomial-time-generable families `a : ℕ → α`, `w z : ℕ → List Bool` (`ComputableInPolyTime · encUnary _`) satisfying `∀ n, isWitness (a n) (w n) = true`.
  - `AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge enc prover isWitness` and `ZeroKnowledgeProof.AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge`: for every uniform strict oracle PPT malicious verifier `Vstar`, there exists a single uniform strict PPT witness-free simulator `S` (chosen before the families and distinguisher, and charged for `(1^n, (a, z))`) such that for all arbitrary polynomially length-bounded families `a : ℕ → α`, `w z : ℕ → List Bool` (`PolynomiallyBounded`) satisfying `∀ n, isWitness (a n) (w n) = true` and every full-input uniform strict PPT distinguisher `adversary` (charged for `((1^n, (a, z)), view)`), the distinguishing advantage between real and simulated views is `Negligible`.
  - `AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge.generableZeroKnowledge` and `ZeroKnowledgeProof.AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge.generableZeroKnowledge`: general auxiliary-input zero knowledge implies restricted polynomial-time-generable zero knowledge by deriving polynomial encoded-length bounds `((encoding_length _).comp h.tidy).polynomiallyBounded` from deterministic polynomial-time generation and lifting any unary-indexed `ComputationallyIndistinguishable` distinguisher via `hadversary.preprocess` to ignore the extra `(a, z)` input.
  - `GenerableZeroKnowledge.advantage_negligible`: under `GenerableZeroKnowledge`, any full-input distinguisher `adversary n (a n) (z n)` also has negligible advantage on deterministic polynomial-time-generable families by recomputing `(a n, z n)` from `1^n` in preprocessing.

issue.title: feat(crypto): formalize Gentry's bootstrapping theorem for leveled and fixed-key FHE
issue.body:
Closes #322

## Summary

Formalizes **Gentry's bootstrapping theorem** for both **compact leveled fully homomorphic encryption (`leveledFHE_of_bootstrappable`)** and **fixed-key fully homomorphic encryption under circular security (`fixedKeyFHE_of_circularSecure`)** ([Gentry 2009][Gentry2009]) in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Bootstrapping.lean` (namespace `Cslib.Crypto`).

### Main Definitions & Results
- **Public-Key Bit Encryption, Semantic Security, & Multi-Bit Key Encryption (`EncryptionScheme`, `SemanticSecure`, `encryptKey`, `isPPTOn_encryptKey`, `encryptKeyTest_gap`)**:
  - Uniform public-key bit-encryption scheme with uniform strict PPT `keyGen` and `encrypt` (`IsPPTOn`), deterministic polynomial-time `decrypt` and `skLength`, fixed secret-key length `skLength n` on `(keyGen n).support`, and support correctness `decrypt_encrypt`.
  - Bit-by-bit key encryption `encryptKey` with uniform strict PPT certificate `isPPTOn_encryptKey` and signed hybrid advantage bound `encryptKeyTest_gap`.
- **Acyclic Key Chain & Leveled Semantic Security (`leveledKeyGen`, `isPPTOn_leveledKeyGen`, `LeveledSemanticSecure`, `leveledSemanticSecure_of_semanticSecure`)**:
  - Iterates key generation to build an acyclic evaluation key chain `[(pk_1, ek_0), …, (pk_L, ek_{L-1})]` where `ek_ℓ ← encryptKey pk_{ℓ+1} sk_ℓ`.
  - Proves `leveledSemanticSecure_of_semanticSecure` (`S.SemanticSecure → ComputableTidilyInPolyTime D encUnary encUnary → S.LeveledSemanticSecure D`) via a uniform strict PPT two-tier hybrid reduction across the `D n` levels (from top level `D n - 1` down to `0`) and across the `skLength n` secret-key bits within each level, with total loss `dyadicSize (D n) * dyadicSize (S.skLength n)`.
- **Bootstrappability & Fixed-Key FHE under Circular Security (`Bootstrappable`, `homInterpretation`, `decryptHomomorphism`, `evalHomCode`, `evalHomOutput`, `computableTidilyInPolyTime_evalHomOutput`, `decrypt_evalHomOutput_circuit`, `decrypt_evalHomOutput_formula`, `length_evalHomOutput_le`, `CircularSecure`, `fixedKeyFHE_of_circularSecure`)**:
  - `Bootstrappable S` equips `S` with deterministic polynomial-time augmented decryption `evalAugDecrypt` for the De Morgan operations (`Boolean.Op`: `.const b`, `.not`, `.and`, `.or`) composed with decryption and unary polynomial-time compactness bound `cipherBound`.
  - Under circular evaluation key `ek ← encryptKey pk sk`, `decryptHomomorphism` is a `Circuits.Homomorphism` into `Boolean.interpretation`, and `fixedKeyFHE_of_circularSecure` certifies uniform strict PPT key generation, deterministic polynomial-time circuit evaluation, circular security, polynomial compactness (`≤ S.cipherBound n` independent of circuit size and depth), and arbitrary-depth circuit and formula correctness.
- **Leveled FHE without Circular Security (`evalLevelStep`, `evalLeveledCode`, `evalLeveledOutput`, `computableTidilyInPolyTime_evalLeveledOutput`, `decrypt_evalLeveledCode_wire`, `decrypt_evalLeveledOutput_circuit`, `decrypt_evalLeveledOutput_formula`, `length_evalLeveledOutput_le`, `leveledFHE_of_bootstrappable`)**:
  - Evaluates all wire levels synchronously across the evaluation key chain `chain : EvalChain`, refreshing the `m` input ciphertexts at each level via `.and` self-recryption (`b && b = b`).
  - Proves by induction on level `L` that every wire `w` with `wireDepths w ≤ L` decrypts under `sk_L` to its true circuit trace value (`decrypt_evalLeveledCode_wire`), yielding `leveledFHE_of_bootstrappable` (uniform strict PPT key generation, deterministic polynomial-time evaluation, `LeveledSemanticSecure D` from base `SemanticSecure` alone, output length `≤ S.cipherBound n`, and correctness on all circuits and formulas of depth `≤ D n`).

### Scope & Limitations
- `Bootstrappable S` axiomatizes polynomial-time augmented-decryption gate evaluation (`evalAugDecrypt`) and its compactness bound (`cipherBound`) directly as a primitive typeclass interface on `S` (witnessed non-vacuously by `trivialScheme` in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/Bootstrapping.lean`), rather than compiling `S.decrypt` into a circuit and evaluating that circuit inside a concrete bounded-depth somewhat homomorphic encryption scheme. Constructing a concrete lattice/ideal-lattice or LWE-based bootstrappable scheme remains future work recorded in `ROADMAP.md`.

## Validation
All 6 checks in `./scripts/check.sh` passed cleanly:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`

issue.title: feat(crypto): exact security of Schnorr signatures with δ = 1/q (#581 3b-ii, part 1)
issue.body:
Refs #581. Stacked on #708, which is stacked on #702. This is the first part of milestone 3b-ii: the exact Schnorr corollary with `δ = 1/q`.

## What is proved

- `schnorr_commit_map_fst_le`: in a vector space of prime order `q` with a nonzero base `g`, the Schnorr commitment `r • g` of a uniform `r` takes each value with probability at most `1/q`. These are the unpredictable commitments of Boneh–Shoup Definition 19.7.
- `schnorr_succProbability_eufCmaGame_le` (Boneh–Shoup Theorem 19.7 with Equation 19.21, exact form): a forger making at most `Qs` signing and `Qro` hash calls against Schnorr signatures succeeds with probability at most

  `Qs · (Qs + Qro) / q + (Qro + 1) / N + √((Qro + 1) · ε')`,

  where `ε'` is the probability that the forking reduction computes a discrete logarithm of the public key.

The `ZMod 11` test now goes through this corollary. A forger that knows the witness still forces `ε' ≥ 81/242`.

## Scope and remaining work

This PR is exact and typed. The computational statement for strict PPT forgers under the discrete-log assumption is the rest of 3b-ii and comes next. It needs:

- the word-level random-oracle game;
- coin presampling near `Replay`;
- a reduction and extractor certified PPT with plain statements;
- an explicit statistical-distance term, because PPT simulation samples `ZMod q` only approximately.

## Validation

- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates pass.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: passes.
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: passes.

  - Symmetric $g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`) formalized with `Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g x.length`.
  - One-sided underestimation helper (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO`) formalized with `f x - g x.length ≤ v ∧ v ≤ f x`.
- **Monotonicity and Transfer Bridges:**
  - Gap monotonicity (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mono`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet.mono`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mono`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet.mono`) and specialization to exact hardness (`g = 0`).
  - Certified uniform-PPT shift + gap-scaling bridge (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`): converts a symmetric $g$-approximator $H$ into a one-sided $(2g)$-underestimator $H'(x) = H(x) - g(|x|)$ when $x \mapsto g(|x|)$ is polynomial-time computable (`ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat`).
  - Rounded-logarithm comparisons (`nat_clog_two_le_log_two_succ`, `real_logb_two_le_nat_log_two_succ`, `nat_dist_le_mul_log_two_succ_of_abs_sub_le_mul_logb`) and the real-valued $|(v : \mathbb{R}) - (f(x) : \mathbb{R})| \le d \log_2 |x|$ bridge `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.eventually_real_abs_sub_le`.
- **Negative-Side Nonvacuity:**
  - `not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero`, `not_mildlyHardOnAverageDet_zero`, `not_mildlyHardOnAverage_zero`, `not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO_zero`, `not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet_zero`, `not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_zero`, `not_mildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox_zero`.

`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/AverageCase.lean` is byte-for-byte identical to the module reviewed in #975 at `df768b5c`.

### Framework friction

- The uniform-PPT shift bridge reuses the existing binary subtraction certificate (through a proof-local tidy conversion) and `IsPPTOn.map_with`. Its explicit `ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat` premise supplies the captured gap computation. This PR adds no subtraction implementation or parallel runtime model.

issue.title: Track D: Uniform MACs, EUF-CMA, and PRF-to-MAC security (Boneh–Shoup Ch. 6)
issue.body:
Parent: #640 (Track D, item 2).

### Scope

Formalize uniform symmetric Message Authentication Codes (`MACScheme`), existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (`EUFCMA` and `OneTimeEUFCMA`), and the canonical PRF-based MAC construction and security reduction following [Boneh–Shoup, Chapter 6, §6.1–6.4][BonehShoup2023]:

1. **Definitions (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean`)**:
   - `MACForger`, `MACScheme` (with strict-PPT `keyGen` and `tag`, plain polynomial-time `verify : ComputableInPolyTime ...`, and completeness `verify_tag`), and deterministic constructor `MACScheme.ofDeterministic`.
   - Adaptive chosen-message experiments `eufCmaGame`, `EUFCMA`, `eufOneTimeGame`, `OneTimeEUFCMA`, their strict-PPT certificates (`isPPTOn_eufCmaGame`, `isPPT_eufCmaGame`, `isPPTOn_eufOneTimeGame`, `isPPT_eufOneTimeGame`), and `EUFCMA.oneTimeEUFCMA`.
2. **PRF-to-MAC construction and security (`prfMAC`, Boneh–Shoup Theorem 6.1)**:
   - Construct `prfMAC family : MACScheme` from any length-preserving keyed family `family : List Bool → List Bool → List Bool` with plain polynomial-time evaluation.
   - Define the oracle-PPT reduction `macToPrfDistinguisher : MACForger → OracleDistinguisher` and prove `isOraclePPT_macToPrfDistinguisher`.
   - Prove the exact quantitative bound (Boneh–Shoup Theorem 6.1):
     `Game.succProbability (ProbComp.eval ((prfMAC family).eufCmaGame adversary n)) ≤ Game.advantage (ProbComp.eval (prfRealGame family (macToPrfDistinguisher adversary) n)) (ProbComp.eval (prfIdealGame (macToPrfDistinguisher adversary) n)) + 1 / 2 ^ n`
     via the lazy random-oracle equivalence (`prfIdealGame_eq_lazy`), showing that any unqueried `n`-bit forgery message draws a fresh uniform `BitString n` tag hit with probability at most `1 / 2 ^ n`.
   - Deduce `PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC : PseudorandomFunction family → (prfMAC family).EUFCMA`.
3. **Validation and tests (`ComplexityTests/MAC.lean`)**:
   - Concrete nonvacuous `MACScheme` instance, evaluation checks, and `#print axioms` guards for the headline theorems.

*Note on Carter–Wegman MACs*: The universal-hash-based Carter–Wegman MAC construction from ε-AXU hashing plus a PRF is a separate follow-up milestone once #663 (the unified universal-hashing abstraction) lands.

issue.title: feat(probability): approximately uniform residues modulo a binary q in strict PPT
issue.body:
Refs #581. This is part C of the 3b-ii plan: approximately uniform `ZMod q` samples in strict PPT, for a **binary** modulus `q`.

The sampler is a separate primitive from #713's bounded integer boxes. #725’s box certificate charges its radius in unary; it also provides a binary-bound interval certificate, with an explicit attempt budget and failure law. Here the sampler always returns a residue and bounds its statistical bias, running in time polynomial in `log q` by reducing sampled bits without rejection. The shape was agreed on #713: option 1, backed by both coordinators.

There are two contracts:
- **This sampler** always returns a residue, with a bias bounded in statistical distance.
- **#713's bounded-rejection interval sampler** (#725) has an explicit failure branch and is exactly uniform conditional on success; its box-law client needs that.

Both reuse the existing `sampleBinaryNat` fair-bit primitive, and #713 and #725 remain the home for bounded boxes. Clients: the Schnorr simulator in the forking reduction (#581 3b-ii), and possibly #660 and LWE samplers whenever they need a binary modulus.

## What is proved

The distribution facts are in Probability, and the certificate is in plain computability:

- `Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le` (new module `Complexity/Probability/StatisticalDistance/UniformMod.lean`): a uniform value below `N`, read in `ZMod q`, is within statistical distance `(N mod q) / N` of uniform on `ZMod q`.
  - Each residue has `⌊N/q⌋` or `⌊N/q⌋ + 1` preimages, counted with Mathlib's `Nat.count_modEq_card`.
  - `dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le_div` gives `q / N`.
- `Cslib.Probability.sampleModNat width modulus` reduces `width` fair bits modulo `modulus` (in `Languages/Probabilistic/UniformNat.lean`):
  - its law is `eval_sampleModNat`;
  - `dist_map_natCast_eval_sampleModNat_le` bounds its distance from uniform on `ZMod q` by `q / 2^width`.
- `Cslib.Probability.isPPTOn_sampleModNat` (in `Computability/Probabilistic/UniformNat.lean`): the sampler is uniformly strict PPT for a computed unary width and a computed **binary** modulus (`encNat`). The public hypotheses are plain `ComputableInPolyTime`; tidy appears only in the proof.

## Tests

`ComplexityTests/UniformNat.lean` gets three checks:
- when `q ∣ N` the residues are exactly uniform (here 6 values mod 3);
- the leftover bound `1/4` holds for 4 values mod 3;
- a computed-width, computed-modulus PPT instance.

## Validation

All of the following were run locally:

- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates pass.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: passes.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 172 tests, OK.
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: passes.

## Abstract assessment

No abstract.

Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5) as `worker-claude-581-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Not yet independently reviewed. Review is requested from `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Dvi6MU29zU9t8zYfeU51sB


## Framework friction

This shared primitive reuses sampleBinaryNat. It deliberately has a total-return/statistical-bias contract, distinct from #725’s explicit failure and exact conditional uniformity; #725 also supplies a binary-bound interval certificate. Computational client/game lifting remains tracked in #581, #733 and #744.

issue.title: feat(crypto): formalize uniform MAC schemes and PRF-to-MAC EUF-CMA reduction (#668)
issue.body:
Closes #668 (part of #640 Track D item 2a).

## Summary

This PR formalizes uniform symmetric Message Authentication Codes (`MACScheme`) on `n`-bit messages at security parameter `n`, fresh-message existential unforgeability under adaptive chosen-message attack (`EUFCMA`) and one-time adaptive chosen-message attack (`OneTimeEUFCMA`), the canonical PRF-based deterministic MAC construction (`prfMAC`), and the quantitative security reduction of Boneh and Shoup (*A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, Section 6.3, Theorem 6.2).

### Mathematical Progress (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean`)
* **`MACScheme` and Fresh-Message EUF-CMA / One-Time EUF-CMA Security**:
  * `MACScheme` bundles strict PPT `keyGen`, strict PPT `sign`, deterministic polynomial-time `verify` (`ComputableInPolyTime`), and perfect completeness on supported keys, `n`-bit messages, and tags.
  * `MACScheme.signingOracle`, `MACScheme.eufCmaGame`, `MACScheme.EUFCMA` (`isPPTOn_eufCmaGame`, `isPPT_eufCmaGame`). As in `SignatureScheme.eufCmaGame`, `eufCmaGame` enforces fresh-message unforgeability (`!queried.contains msg`), whereas Boneh–Shoup Attack Game 6.1 / Definition 6.2 forbids only previously returned `(message, tag)` pairs (fresh-pair / strong unforgeability). For general randomized `sign` algorithms the two notions differ; for deterministic canonical MACs with a unique valid tag per message (such as `prfMAC`), fresh-message and fresh-pair unforgeability coincide.
  * `MACScheme.oneTimeSigningOracle`, `MACScheme.eufOneTimeGame`, `MACScheme.OneTimeEUFCMA` (`isPPTOn_eufOneTimeGame`, `isPPT_eufOneTimeGame`).
  * `MACScheme.EUFCMA.oneTimeEUFCMA`: full EUF-CMA security implies one-time EUF-CMA security via `SignatureScheme.limitToOneQuery`.
* **Canonical PRF-based MAC (`prfMAC`) and Quantitative Forgery Reduction (Boneh–Shoup Section 6.3, Theorem 6.2)**:
  * `prfMAC family hpoly`: constructs a deterministic `MACScheme` from any polynomial-time keyed family `family`, sampling an `n`-bit key uniformly via `BitString.sampleList n`, tagging via `prfOracle family sk.length sk msg`, and verifying via `(msg.length == sk.length) && (family sk msg == tag)`.
  * `macLogHandler` and `macToPrfDistinguisher`: strict oracle-PPT reduction (`isOraclePPT_macToPrfDistinguisher`) that simulates the MAC tagging oracle using the external PRF/random-function oracle, logs queried messages, and uses one additional oracle query to test a candidate unqueried `n`-bit forgery.
  * `eval_prfRealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher`: exact distributional equivalence between `prfRealGame family (macToPrfDistinguisher adversary) n` and `(prfMAC family hpoly).eufCmaGame adversary n`.
  * `succProbability_prfIdealGame_macToPrfDistinguisher_le`: in the ideal random-function game, any unqueried `n`-bit forgery message misses the lazy random-oracle cache and draws a fresh uniform `n`-bit tag, succeeding with probability at most $1 / 2^n$.
  * `succProbability_eufCmaGame_prfMAC_le`: quantitative security bound
    $$\Pr[\text{Forge}] \le \mathrm{Adv}_{\mathrm{PRF}}(\text{macToPrfDistinguisher}(\mathcal{A}), n) + 2^{-n}.$$
  * `PseudorandomFunction.eufCma_prfMAC` and `PseudorandomFunction.oneTimeEUFCMA_prfMAC`: any uniform `PseudorandomFunction` yields an `EUFCMA`-secure (and `OneTimeEUFCMA`-secure) `MACScheme`.

### Tests and Nonvacuity (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/MAC.lean`)
* Concrete witnesses (`trivialMACScheme` and `echoPrfMAC`), evaluation tests for valid/invalid tags and one-time query slot consumption, nonvacuity refutation (`not_oneTimeEUFCMA_trivialMACScheme`, `not_eufCMA_trivialMACScheme`), and `#print axioms` guards for all 7 headline declarations.

### Formal Abstract Assessment
* No impact on existing selected headline abstracts in `abstracts/catalogue.json` (`python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes).

## Validation & Review
* Built and checked `Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MAC` and `ComplexityTests.Crypto.MAC` (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, 6508 jobs), `lake exe mk_all --check`, `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`, and `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.
* Pre-PR independent review conducted by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-mac668` on `e874e9a2`; all 3 documentation/example items addressed in `b677a7db`.
* Addressed coordinator review (`pullrequestreview-5636168295`) in `d5776322` by explicitly documenting fresh-message vs. fresh-pair EUF-CMA for randomized MAC signing and updating the Boneh–Shoup PRF-to-MAC references to Section 6.3 and Theorem 6.2.

*AI disclosure: Authored by `worker-jetski-5950b838` (Gemini) with independent pre-PR review by `reviewer-jetski-5950b838-mac668`.*

issue.title: feat(Crypto): formalize KEM-DEM hybrid public-key encryption (Boneh-Shoup Exercise 11.9)
issue.body:
Parent: #640 (Track C, Item 3: Hybrid encryption) and #1000 (Step 1).

## Scope

Formalize Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs), one-time symmetric Data Encapsulation Mechanisms (DEMs), and the KEM–DEM hybrid public-key encryption paradigm following [Boneh and Shoup, Version 0.6, Section 2.2 (Attack Game 2.1, Definition 2.2) and Exercise 11.9][BonehShoup2023] in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/Hybrid.lean`:

1. **Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (`kemRealGame`, `kemIdealGame`, `KEMINDCPA`)**:
   - Real and ideal KEM IND-CPA experiments (`kemRealGame`, `kemIdealGame`, Exercise 11.9) where `kemIdealGame` replaces the encapsulated key with an independent uniform `n`-bit key `BitString.sampleList n`.
   - Strict PPT certificates (`isPPTOn_kemRealGame`, `isPPTOn_kemIdealGame`) and asymptotic security predicate `KEMINDCPA`.
2. **One-Time Symmetric Bit Encryption (`demGame`, `DEMOneTimeINDCPA`)**:
   - One-time symmetric chosen-plaintext experiment (`demGame`, Section 2.2, Attack Game 2.1 and Definition 2.2) keyed by `BitString.sampleList n` against uniform two-stage `Encryption.Adversary` distinguishers.
   - Strict PPT certificate (`isPPTOn_demGame`) and asymptotic security predicate `DEMOneTimeINDCPA`.
3. **Hybrid Encryption Construction and Correctness (`hybridEncrypt`, `hybridDecrypt`)**:
   - `hybridEncrypt encaps encryptSym` and deterministic `hybridDecrypt decaps decryptSym` encoding `(ctKem, ctDem)` via `encPair encBits encBits` (Exercise 11.9(a)).
   - Polynomial-time certificates (`isPPTOn_hybridEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_hybridDecrypt`) and exact decryption correctness (`hybridDecrypt_encPair`, `hybridDecrypt_hybridEncrypt`).
4. **Boneh–Shoup Exercise 11.9(b) Reductions and Asymptotic Security**:
   - Direct per-bit KEM distinguisher `hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, single hidden-bit KEM distinguisher `hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, and two-stage DEM adversary `hybridToDEMAdversary`, with strict PPT certificates (`isPPT_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `isPPT_hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, `isPPT_hybridToDEMAdversary`).
   - Exact distributional bridges (`eval_kemRealGame_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `eval_kemIdealGame_hybridToKEMDistinguisher`, `eval_demGame_hybridToDEMAdversary`) via the intermediate game `hybridIdealGame`.
   - Quantitative per-`n` advantage bounds `advantage_hybridGame_le_two_mul` (Exercise 11.9(b) single hidden-bit distinguisher bound `2 * Adv_KEM + Adv_DEM`) and `advantage_hybridGame_le` (two-distinguisher triangle-inequality variant).
   - Asymptotic Boneh–Shoup Exercise 11.9(b) (`KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa`): `KEMINDCPA` and `DEMOneTimeINDCPA` imply `Encryption.INDCPA` for `hybridEncrypt`.
5. **Non-vacuous One-Time Pad DEM (`otpEncrypt`, `otpDecrypt`)**:
   - Exact correctness (`otpDecrypt_otpEncrypt`), polynomial-time certificates (`isPPTOn_otpEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_otpDecrypt`), exact zero advantage for `n ≥ 1` (`eval_demGame_otpEncrypt_false_eq_true`, `advantage_demGame_otpEncrypt_eq_zero`), unconditional security (`demOneTimeINDCPA_otpEncrypt`), and the KEM-to-PKE corollary (`KEMINDCPA.hybrid_otpEncrypt_indcpa`).
6. **Tests & Validation (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/HybridEncryption.lean`)**:
   - Non-vacuous runtime/distributional checks (`not_kemINDCPA_leaking`, `kemINDCPA_idealEncaps`, `indcpa_hybridEncrypt_idealEncaps_otpEncrypt`).

issue.title: Zero-knowledge architecture: one interactive-protocol core, then sumcheck, IOPs, Ligero, toward libzk
issue.body:
Samuel wants zero-knowledge and proof-system abstractions that are modular and meet the #587 standard as they grow. The long-term goal is to formally verify succinct proof schemes such as **libzk**, the Ligero- and sumcheck-based system by Matteo Frigo and Abhi Shelat that is being standardized through an IETF draft, starting from the draft standards.

**Current state:**
- Interaction is modeled several separate ways:
  - IP (`Classes/IP.lean`: provers as oracles to a `WordOracleComp` verifier);
  - GMW zero knowledge (`Crypto/Computational/ZeroKnowledge.lean`, `GMW/*`: a two-round runner in `ProbComp`);
  - Sigma protocols (`Crypto/Protocols/SigmaProtocol/*`: a three-move structure over `PMF`);
  - MIP (`DetProver`) and PCP verifiers.

  Each states completeness, soundness and zero knowledge locally.
- Sumcheck exists only inside the IP = PSPACE protocol (`Classes/IP/TQBF/Protocol.lean`).
- Reed–Solomon codes, Berlekamp–Welch and Sudan decoding exist (`Foundations/Data/Code`).
- There are no IOPs, Ligero, Merkle commitments, Fiat–Shamir/BCS compilers or polynomial commitments.

**Prior art:** ArkLib (Verified-zkEVM; Lean 4, on VCVio's oracle computations) formalizes IOPs and sumcheck. We can't depend on it, because modules must stay upstreamable into cslib, but its design must be studied before ours.

**Milestones:**
1. **Design (cross-area; reviewed before code).**
   - Survey the existing models here and ArkLib's.
   - Propose one interactive-protocol core: protocol syntax and transcripts; prover and verifier execution in `ProbComp`/`OracleComp`; oracle access to prover messages (IOPs); and the random-oracle model.
   - Propose a single property library: completeness; soundness, statistical and computational; knowledge soundness, including special soundness and round-by-round; zero knowledge, honest-verifier and malicious, in perfect, statistical and computational versions.
   - Cover composition (sequential, parallel, AND/OR) and a migration or bridging plan for IP, Sigma, GMW-ZK, MIP and PCP.
   - Cross-reviewed by the Codex fleet (Crypto and Machines areas) and the Classes area.
2. **Standalone sumcheck,** extracted from TQBF: exact completeness, Schwartz–Zippel soundness and round-by-round soundness. IP = PSPACE becomes a client.
3. **IOPs and Ligero:** Reed–Solomon proximity testing, linear and quadratic constraint checks, Merkle-tree commitments, and BCS/Fiat–Shamir compilation (reusing #640 track A's random-oracle Fiat–Shamir).
4. **libzk, theory only:** formalize the protocols underlying the draft (sumcheck-based proofs, the Ligero commitment and IOP, Fiat–Shamir/BCS compilation) and their completeness, soundness and zero-knowledge theorems at the level of the mathematical construction.

**Out of scope (Samuel, 2026-10-23):** specific circuits such as ECDSA verification, concrete ciphersuites and parameter sets, field and hash instantiations, and wire formats. The aim is the relevant theory, not a particular deployment.

Coordinated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Milestone 1 is staffed as soon as capacity frees, and nothing in 2–4 starts before the core design is agreed.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/MAC): complete Carter-Wegman PRF-pad admissibility and multi-query fresh-nonce security (#736)
issue.body:
Part of #736
Part of #640 (Track D)

### Summary

Completes the uniform `IsOraclePPT` admissibility, word-level one-time pad-test family, asymptotic `PseudorandomFunction` corollaries, and multi-query issued-counter PRF-masked Carter–Wegman MAC security milestone in `Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MAC/CarterWegman.lean`:

- **Mathematical progress**:
  - **One-query `IsOraclePPT` admissibility and word-level families**:
    - `isOraclePPT_prfPadDistinguisher`: proves that `prfPadDistinguisher test` is uniformly strict oracle-PPT (`IsOraclePPT encBool`) whenever `(n, r) ↦ test n (BitString.ofList n r)` is `IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits) encBool`.
    - `wordProbPadTest`, `eval_wordProbPadTest`, `isPPTOn_wordProbPadTest`, `isOraclePPT_prfPadDistinguisher_wordProbPadTest`: uniform word-level constructor for the induced one-time Carter–Wegman pad test from PPT word-level `seed`, `hash`, `query`, and `forge` families.
    - `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfOneTimeGame`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfOneTimeStrongGame`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfOneTimeGame_wordProbPadTest`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfOneTimeStrongGame_wordProbPadTest`: asymptotic security corollaries under `PseudorandomFunction family` and `Negligible ε`.
  - **Multi-query issued-counter PRF-masked Carter–Wegman MAC** (after [BonehShoup2023], Section 7.5, Theorem 7.10):
    - `counterSeqHandler`, `maskedCounterSlotGame`, `maskedCounterGame`, `maskedCounterStrongGame`, `counterPadSeqDistinguisher`: arbitrary-pad-sequence multi-query Carter–Wegman signing handler and games.
    - `uniform_bind_run_interpret_counterSeqHandler` and `uniform_bind_counterPadSeqDistinguisher`: proves that evaluating a random function `table ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (ι → Y)` at pairwise distinct nonces `nonce 0, ..., nonce (Q - 1)` is identically distributed to the independent-pad handler `counterRealHandler`.
    - `prfPadSeqDist`, `prfCounterSlotGame`, `prfCounterGame`, `prfCounterStrongGame`, `prfMultiPadDistinguisher`, `prfCounterSlotGame_le`, `prfCounterGame_le`, `prfCounterStrongGame_le`: concrete multi-query PRF-pad reduction.
    - `isOraclePPT_prfMultiPadDistinguisher`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfCounterSlotGame`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfCounterGame`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfCounterStrongGame`: uniform `IsOraclePPT encBool` certificate (via `IsOraclePPTOn.iterateWith_of_bounded_growth`) and asymptotic security corollaries with `hforger`, `hnonce_len`, and `hnonce_inj` required only eventually (`∀ᶠ n in Filter.atTop`).
- **Scope and remaining gap on #736 / `ROADMAP.md`**:
  - The counter construction here models Boneh–Shoup Section 7.5, Theorem 7.10 under two restrictions compared to Attack Game 7.4: (a) the signer's counter schedule `nonce n i` fixes the nonces rather than letting the adversary choose distinct nonces, and (b) `checkCounterSlot` / `checkCounterGlobal` / `checkCounterStrong` accept forgeries only at issued counter slots (`pads[idx]? = some r`) and reject unissued `idx` (which removes the `1 / |T|` unissued-nonce guessing term).
  - Full nonce-based Carter–Wegman security with adversary-chosen distinct nonces and forgeries at arbitrary nonces (Boneh–Shoup Attack Game 7.4 / Theorem 7.10) and randomized Carter–Wegman security (Theorem 7.9) remain open in `ROADMAP.md` under #736.
- **Design note (`MACScheme` vs `prfCounter*Game`)**:
  - `MACScheme` in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean` has randomized stateless signing `sign : List Bool → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)` with no nonce input or signer state, so stateful counter signing (`CounterForger`, `prfCounterSlotGame`, `prfCounterGame`, `prfCounterStrongGame`) cannot instantiate `MACScheme.EUFCMA` / `MACScheme.SUFCMA` directly (whereas randomized Carter–Wegman, Theorem 7.9, can be stated against `MACScheme.EUFCMA`).

### Framework friction

- **`MACScheme` lacks signer state or a nonce input (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MAC.lean`)**: `MACScheme.sign : List Bool → List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)` is randomized (`ProbComp`) and can express randomized Carter–Wegman (Theorem 7.9), but is stateless and takes no nonce parameter, so stateful counter-based and nonce-based Carter–Wegman (`CounterForger`, `prfCounter*Game`) must define their own multi-query games rather than instantiating `MACScheme.EUFCMA` / `MACScheme.SUFCMA`. Logged on #733 (`https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/733#issuecomment-6399067289`).

### Abstract impact assessment

No change to `abstracts/catalogue.json`: this milestone completes the Carter–Wegman PRF-pad admissibility and issued-counter multi-query reduction on the cryptography roadmap rather than adding a new headline complexity separation.

issue.title: Restricted versus general auxiliary-input zero knowledge (#680 item 1)
issue.body:
Parent tracker: #680 (Item 1), under #593 and #643.

### Scope & Acceptance Criteria
1. **Explicit public API identities for restricted vs. general auxiliary-input zero knowledge** in `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/ZeroKnowledge.lean`:
   - `GenerableZeroKnowledge enc prover isWitness`: uniform computational zero-knowledge against uniform strict oracle PPT malicious verifiers `Vstar` quantified over deterministic polynomial-time-generable instance, valid-witness, and auxiliary-input families (`ComputableInPolyTime · encUnary _`), with one efficient witness-free simulator `S` chosen per `Vstar` before the choice of `(a, w, z)`.
   - `AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge enc prover isWitness` (and `ZeroKnowledgeProof.AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge`): general auxiliary-input computational zero-knowledge for arbitrary polynomially bounded valid families `a : ℕ → α`, `w z : ℕ → List Bool` (`PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => (enc (a n)).length)`, `PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => (w n).length)`, `PolynomiallyBounded (fun n => (z n).length)`, and `∀ n, isWitness (a n) (w n) = true`), against full-input uniform strict PPT distinguishers `adversary : ℕ → α → List Bool → List Bool → ProbComp Bool` charged for the complete encoded input `((1^n, (a n, z n)), view)`, with one efficient witness-free simulator `S` per `Vstar` chosen before the families and distinguisher.
2. **Stronger-to-restricted bridge:**
   - Prove `AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge.generableZeroKnowledge` (and `ZeroKnowledgeProof.AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge.generableZeroKnowledge`): general auxiliary-input zero knowledge implies restricted poly-time-generable zero knowledge (`GenerableZeroKnowledge`), using the fact that deterministic polynomial-time-generable families have polynomially bounded encoded lengths and any unary-indexed `ComputationallyIndistinguishable` distinguisher lifts to a full-input distinguisher.
3. **Advice-PRG consequence for GMW:**
   - Package the explicit advice-PRG premise of `GMW.gmwView_negligible_of_advice_prg` as a named predicate (`GMW.AdvicePRG`) and prove that `PseudorandomGenerator.zeroKnowledgeProofOfReduction` and `PseudorandomGenerator.zeroKnowledgeProofThreeSAT` satisfy `ZeroKnowledgeProof.AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge` under `GMW.AdvicePRG`, without inferring that stronger premise from uniform OWF/PRG security.
4. **Tests & Documentation:**
   - Preserve all existing `ZeroKnowledgeProof` fields and theorems; update docstrings and `ROADMAP.md` to clearly distinguish `GenerableZeroKnowledge` from `AuxiliaryInputZeroKnowledge`; add nonvacuous checks and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/ZeroKnowledge.lean`.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/OneWay): add WeakOneWay, output normalization, and schedule reindexing
issue.body:
Refs #733 and #798. This is supplier M2b-1; Yao amplification (M2b-2) and the Liu–Pass converse (M2b-3) remain separate work.

Authored by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Antigravity/Gemini) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.

### What this supplies

- `WeakOneWayAt f α` uses the existing unrestricted-preimage `inversionGame`, polynomial-time evaluation of f, and eventual strict success `< 1 - α(n)` for every uniform strict PPT inverter. `WeakOneWay f` chooses one positive natural-coefficient polynomial q before the inverter, with gap `1/q(n)`, following Liu–Pass Definition 2.2, §2.1, p. 7 of arXiv:2009.11514v1. The parameterized helper does not impose additional range hypotheses on α.
- Strict/non-strict equivalence uses polynomial slack: `WeakOneWay.of_le` replaces q by `2*q`; `exists_monotone_poly` uses `q + X + 1`. Strong one-wayness implies weak one-wayness; efficient inverse and constant-function examples refute it.
- Weak normalization reuses `OneWayNormalization.normalize` and its self-delimiting `BitString.padWord`, with the existing `inversion_le` reduction. Under an honest polynomial image bound B, the output length is exactly `2*B(n)+1`, with a uniform polynomial-time unary length certificate. This adds no new padding implementation or claim of exact equality between inversion games.
- `OneWayReindex.reindex m core` wraps the greatest fitting parameter n together with `core n` of the input's `m(n)`-bit prefix. Its transfer theorems require unary polynomial-time m, `m(n) ≥ n+1`, and a joint polynomial-time core; monotonicity of m is not required. The finite initial lengths below `m(0)` are excluded from the reduction bound and do not affect eventual security.
- The reduction builds one uniform family inverter per global inverter. For each sampled shared coin tape it searches all auxiliary lengths `M ≤ m(n+1)` and checks candidate preimages, rather than choosing an optimal length by advice or success probabilities. Its success dominates every relevant M without a probability loss. Weak transfer uses polynomial monotonicity; strong transfer uses the polynomial bound relating M to its selected parameter.

### Framework friction

The implementation reuses the existing OneWay game, uniform PPT seeded evaluator, bounded search, GeneratorReindex parameter lemmas and negligible-function composition. `familyInversionGame` is the supporting parameter-indexed experiment: it samples an `m(n)`-bit input and checks `core n (candidate.take (m n)) = core n input`. Candidates may be shorter than `m(n)`; longer candidates are truncated. This explicit family contract is the premise for the shared reduction, while the final WeakOneWay/OneWay conclusions use the existing global inversion model.

### Validation and abstract impact

The author reports all six `scripts/check.sh` gates plus hygiene, tidy-surface, changed-file, docs and guide checks passing. The PR adds focused constant/identity negatives, a strong-to-weak/normalization client, a concrete schedule evaluation and eight axiom guards. Hosted validation is linked in the review.

No selected abstract statement, definition, scope, or catalogue entry changes. This is shared infrastructure for later M2b results, not completion of amplification or the converse.

issue.title: feat(crypto): construct and certify homomorphic refresh
issue.body:
Construct Gentry's identity and NAND refresh from bit encryption, evaluation, and actual decryption circuits. Correctness covers every well-sized old ciphertext, including outputs of earlier evaluations, and permits the same encrypted secret key in both NAND input blocks. The refreshed ciphertext keeps the base scheme's fixed width.

This is the first bounded recovery milestone for #322. `Bootstrappable` requires only that the concrete decryption and NAND-augmented circuits belong to the base evaluator's permitted family. Uniform strict-PPT refresh is derived from certificates for the base encryption/evaluation algorithms and uniform decryption-circuit generation. The NAND augmentation itself is constructed in native polynomial time, with exact gate count `2 * size(D) + 2`.

Reusable additions include strict-PPT list traversal with captured inputs, native sequential composition of circuit codes, typed Boolean circuit evaluation with explicit input padding/truncation, and a generic NAND circuit. The three commits separate these prerequisites, the refresh development, and source credit/roadmap updates.

The regression scheme is explicitly insecure. Its fresh ciphertexts have tag false and evaluated ciphertexts have tag true; direct base evaluation on an evaluated encryption of true produces false. Tests prove different-key switching, shared encrypted-key inputs, two successful refreshes, fixed widths, and an actual instance of every refresh-efficiency hypothesis.

The full objective remains open: depth-layered DAG evaluation without tree expansion, its uniform resource bounds, the acyclic key-chain IND-CPA reduction, and the separately assumed circular-security fixed-key result. This milestone uses perfect correctness and fixed-width padded representations; it establishes no concrete LWE scheme or encryption-security theorem. Mathematical source: [Craig Gentry, STOC 2009, §§1–2](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf), credited in `references.bib`.

Validation on the exact source tree `363aba871001940aac385acb03a1fc558929d80a` of head `16ca0631a9ae7caf1ade7685a3a937a42d1e812e`:

issue.title: feat(crypto): shared witness-finding oracle support in Game/UntilBad (#1000)
issue.body:
## Summary

Shared `#733` supplier PR for the Cramer–Shoup CRHF collision-finding reduction (#1000 Step 3), extending `Complexity/Crypto/Game/UntilBad.lean` (`namespace Cslib.Crypto.Game`) with a generic witness-finding stateful oracle runner (+138 lines, plus +36 lines of concrete two-sided tests in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/UntilBad.lean`):

1. **Witness-finding oracle handler and runner (`Complexity/Crypto/Game/UntilBad.lean`)**:
   - `finderPhase2Oracle`: stateful oracle handler over `Option (List Bool)` that replies with `o₂ request.2` and records `some (extract request.2)` whenever `isBad request.2 = true`.
   - `runFinderOracle`: evaluates a `WordOracleComp Unit α` program under `finderPhase2Oracle` starting from state `s : Option (List Bool)` and tests whether the final recorded witness satisfies `isGood`.
   - Structural and absorption lemmas: `runFinderOracle_pure`, `runFinderOracle_query_inl`, `runFinderOracle_query_inr`, and `runFinderOracle_true_of_good` (once a state `some w` with `isGood w = true` is recorded, `runFinderOracle` evaluates to `PMF.pure true`).
   - Difference bound (`runStatelessOracle_le_runFinderOracle`): for any two stateless oracle reply functions `o₁, o₂ : List Bool → List Bool` that agree whenever `isBad req = false`, if every query with `isBad req = true` yields a valid witness `isGood (extract req) = true`, then for every `prog : WordOracleComp Unit α`, continuation `next : α → Game`, and `b : Bool`,
     `runStatelessOracle o₁ prog next b ≤ runStatelessOracle o₂ prog next b + runFinderOracle o₂ isBad extract prog none isGood true` (and symmetrically with `o₁` and `o₂` swapped).

## Existing Notions Considered

| New Declaration | Existing Notion Checked | Why Reused or Added |
|---|---|---|
| `finderPhase2Oracle`, `runFinderOracle`, `runFinderOracle_pure`, `runFinderOracle_query_inl`, `runFinderOracle_query_inr`, `runFinderOracle_true_of_good`, `runStatelessOracle_le_runFinderOracle` | `IdenticalUntilBad` (`Complexity/Crypto/Game/UntilBad.lean`), `runStatelessOracle` (#1193) | `runStatelessOracle_bind_le` (#1193) bounds `runStatelessOracle` divergence by a union-bound sum over queries `(Q / q)`, whereas reductions that extract an explicit witness from a bad oracle query (such as a hash collision in Game 3 $\to$ Game 4 of Cramer–Shoup, Boneh–Shoup §12.5.3 eqs. (12.24)–(12.25)) bound the divergence between two stateless oracle handlers by the probability that a witness-recording `StateT (Option (List Bool)) ProbComp` simulation outputs a valid witness. Placed in `Complexity/Crypto/Game/UntilBad.lean` per #733. |

## Framework friction and abstract-impact assessment

- **Framework friction**: None. Induction on `prog : WordOracleComp Unit α` aligns directly with `runStatelessOracle_pure`, `runStatelessOracle_query_inl`, and `runStatelessOracle_query_inr` from #1193.
- **Abstract-impact assessment**: None. Purely additive declarations in `Complexity/Crypto/Game/UntilBad.lean` (`namespace Cslib.Crypto.Game`).

issue.title: Commitment hiding against a randomized stateful receiver (#680 item 2)
issue.body:
Part of #680 (Item 2) and #593 / #643.

## Objective & Scope

`BitCommitmentScheme.computational_hiding` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Commitment.lean`) currently formulates hiding over deterministic polynomial-time receiver-string and committed-bit families (`r : ℕ → List Bool`, `b₀ b₁ : ℕ → Bool`).

This task adds the two-stage uniform efficient stateful-receiver hiding experiment and proves the corresponding strengthening of Naor's bit commitment hiding theorem without dropping the existing deterministic-family result:

1. **Two-stage stateful commitment receiver (`CommitmentReceiver`, `CommitmentReceiver.IsPPT`)**:
   * `choose : ℕ → List Bool → ProbComp ((List Bool × (Bool × Bool)) × List Bool)` receives the unary security parameter `n` and auxiliary input `aux : List Bool`, and outputs a receiver challenge string `r : List Bool`, a pair of chosen bits `(b₀, b₁) : Bool × Bool`, and a private saved state `state : List Bool`.
   * `guess : ℕ → List Bool → List Bool → ProbComp Bool` receives `n`, the saved `state`, and the commitment `c`, and outputs a distinguishing bit.
   * `CommitmentReceiver.IsPPT` certifies both stages as uniform strict PPT algorithms charging the complete encoded input (including the saved state), aligned with `Encryption.Adversary` (`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Encryption/Basic.lean`) and #643.
2. **Hiding experiment (`commitmentHidingGame`, `StatefulHiding`, `BitCommitmentScheme.StatefulHiding`)**:
   * `commitmentHidingGame commit receiver aux bit n`: runs `choice ← receiver.choose n aux`, samples `seed ← BitString.sampleList n`, computes `c := commit choice.1.1 (if bit then choice.1.2.2 else choice.1.2.1) seed`, and runs `receiver.guess n choice.2 c`.
   * Full strict PPT certificate (`isPPTOn_commitmentHidingGame`, `isPPT_commitmentHidingGame`) when `commit` is polynomial-time and `receiver.IsPPT` holds.
   * Bridge showing `StatefulHiding` implies the existing deterministic-family `computational_hiding` (preserving all existing callers and theorems).
3. **Naor's stateful-receiver hiding theorem (`PseudorandomGenerator.naorReceiverDistinguisher`, `PseudorandomGenerator.naorStatefulHiding`)**:
   * Explicit reduction `naorReceiverDistinguisher` (certified `IsPPT`) with quantitative advantage bound and exact ideal-world distributional equality (`commitmentHidingGame (naorCommit id)` has identical distributions for `bit = false` and `bit = true` for arbitrary, possibly malformed receiver challenge strings `r` and correlated states `state`).
   * Proof that `PseudorandomGenerator.naorBitCommitment` satisfies `BitCommitmentScheme.StatefulHiding`.
4. **Tests & Nonvacuity (`ComplexityTests/Crypto/Commitment.lean`)**:
   * Concrete genuinely randomized receiver whose output retains correlated private state (e.g., sampling a random mask bit in `state` and choosing `(b₀, b₁) = (mask, !mask)`), verification that `StatefulHiding` rejects a trivial non-hiding commitment scheme, and `#print axioms` guards.

issue.title: feat(probability): statistical distance of independent draws

issue.body:

Stronger constructions/reductions follow as focused tasks after the current critical plain-API migration; this tracker does not displace that work. No implementation is claimed or assigned yet.

Keep the quantifier order: one efficient witness-free simulator for each malicious verifier, before the choice of those families; charge the complete encoded input. Reuse #427's completed pointwise `GMW.gmwView_advantage_le` and `gmwView_negligible_of_advice_prg` ([existing explicit advice-PRG premise](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/c8096188dbc2908a5c9c570a4d410931475ffa78/Complexity/Crypto/Computational/GMW/Simulator.lean#L958)). 2. **Commitment hiding against a randomized stateful receiver.** [`BitCommitmentScheme.computational_hiding`](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/c8096188dbc2908a5c9c570a4d410931475ffa78/Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Commitment.lean#L847) currently uses deterministic polynomial-time receiver-string and committed-bit families. Add a two-stage uniform efficient receiver experiment: generation produces a challenge, the chosen bits and private state; the final distinguisher receives the commitment and the same correlated state. Make challenge encodings, auxiliary-input assumptions and malformed-input behavior explicit. Prove the corresponding strengthening of Naor's theorem without dropping the existing result or assuming a hiding field in its own proof. Reuse existing probabilistic programs, encodings and saved-state game APIs, with #643 alignment rather than a new interaction model. Acceptance includes a genuinely randomized receiver whose output retains correlated private state and a reduction certifying its complete execution. This is the next bounded strengthening, not a prerequisite retroactively imposed on the existing GMW pointwise theorem.

3. **Efficient simulation and extraction for Sigma protocols.** [`SpecialSoundness` and `SpecialHVZK`](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/blob/c8096188dbc2908a5c9c570a4d410931475ffa78/Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/SigmaProtocol/Basic.lean#L107) express exact extraction correctness and distributional simulation without computational certificates. Keep that algebraic layer, name/document its scope clearly, and have #643 provide separate efficiency-certified properties for named simulators/extractors before using them for full cryptographic security. Use the existing plain deterministic/PPT/OraclePPT contracts uniformly across security parameters and charge all encodings, transcript data and oracle effects. State realization/sampling assumptions explicitly; if approximation is necessary, carry its error rather than silently identifying an arbitrary exact PMF with an efficient sampler. Reuse #636's concrete certified Schnorr reduction/extraction; #660's Lyubashevsky result remains an exact algebraic milestone until its efficiency obligations are proved. Coordinate with #581 and #645. Acceptance: checked efficient wrappers/bridges, representative concrete instances and explicit remaining assumptions; an exact algebraic theorem alone must not discharge an efficiency obligation.

These are related tracking items, not one implementation PR. Each implementation needs a fresh overlap check, a bounded theme, real clients, appropriate checks and independent current-head review. D1 applies to any renaming: update in-repository clients without deprecated aliases. issue.title: feat(crypto): prove IND-CPA for acyclic bootstrapping
issue.body:
Next security milestone under #322, following the construction in #469 / #463. Status: available; no implementation claim. Prove security of the actual acyclic public artifact and then the actual `Leveled.scheme`, against uniform strict-PPT adversaries. Correctness and runtime certificates alone do not establish this result.

Acceptance criteria:

- Add a standard two-stage bit-message IND-CPA experiment: after seeing the generated public key, the adversary chooses two bits and a saved bit-string state; after receiving encryption of the selected bit, it produces its guess. Require native `IsPPTOn` certificates for both stages, charging complete encoded inputs and saved state. Quantify one uniform adversary before the security parameter, and express negligible distinguishing advantage through the existing game API. Keep the generic game reusable, with a thin wrapper for `Homomorphic.Scheme`.
- Define the actual public-key/link sampler and a zero-link sampler using the same independent keys, replacing each encrypted secret with an equal-length zero word. Prove computational indistinguishability of their serialized public outputs from base IND-CPA, actual native key generation/encryption and fixed supported secret-key length.
- Construct the reductions and prove exact adjacent-game identities. Zero links from the final key backwards. At link i, embed the base challenge public key at i+1, generate every other key pair, and challenge successive bits of the known predecessor secret. The outgoing link carrying the unknown challenge secret must already be zeroed. Do not replace this correlated key-chain argument with the independent-source sequence-hybrid lemma or assume distinct sampled keys.
- Build one uniform reduction over polynomially many link/bit hops, using the existing signed random-hop/dyadic machinery with an explicit polynomial loss. Fixed-hop negligibility alone is insufficient. Derive a polynomial bit capacity from native key-generation output bounds; use the known predecessor secret's actual length and fixed-width equality to simulate zero links. Do not add computability of `secretWidth` or a decryption-generator premise merely to simplify the security proof.
- Prove native certificates for both reduction stages, including key sampling, encryption traversal, indexing, serialization, total saved-state decoding and inactive-hop handling. Cover zero budget, empty secret words and padded dyadic coordinates. The reduction must not access the challenge secret or use external advice.
- After zeroing links, embed the base challenge at the initial key, simulate the remaining zero-link public artifact, run the target adversary's adaptive message selection and add the existing fresh-ciphertext tag. Transfer across the public-artifact hybrids to prove IND-CPA of `Leveled.scheme D budget` for every efficiently computed unary budget. State exactly which assumptions are needed for security; combine with the existing correctness/compactness results without assuming either conclusion.
- Test the game and simulation identities on concrete finite examples, including a deliberately insecure scheme/adversary rejected by the security definition. Audit headline axioms; run all six gates and independent API/correctness reviews. Update the roadmap and assess the curated formal abstracts against the final result.

Reuse candidates from read-only reconnaissance: `Crypto/Game.lean` (`Indistinguishable`), `Crypto/Computational/Basic.lean` (computational indistinguishability and postprocessing), `Crypto/Game/Hybrid.lean` (signed random-hop composition), `UniformNat.lean` (strict-PPT dyadic sampling), `PPT/Capture.lean`, and the actual key-chain and captured traversal certificates. Missing mathematical ingredients include key-sampling splice equalities, contextual bit-encryption splice equalities, and the adjacent-game simulations. `Hybrid/Sequence.lean` assumes independent repeated sources and does not by itself discharge these obligations.

The target protects fresh challenge ciphertexts with the entire public artifact visible. Circuit privacy, arbitrary reuse of evaluated wrapper ciphertexts, fixed-key circular-security bootstrapping and a concrete LWE instantiation remain outside this milestone and open under #322. Keep that parent objective open.

Sources: Craig Gentry, [Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/hits09/gentry-homomorphic-encryption.pdf), Section 2; Dan Boneh and Victor Shoup, [public-key encryption, Attack Game 11.1](https://theory.stanford.edu/~dfreeman/cs259c-f11/lectures/boneh-shoup-pke.pdf), for the chosen-message experiment. The proposed simulation plan above still requires Lean proofs. Planning by `worker-codex-gentry-budget-20261023` with read-only API/source reconnaissance by `/root/maintenance_audit`.

issue.title: doc(LiuPass,ROADMAP,tests): correct the Liu–Pass time-bound note; add a same-length leaking KEM test
issue.body:
Fixes four issues found by an external agent review shared by Samuel. The PR changes documentation and tests only: no library statement or definition changes.

1. **`LiuPass.lean` time-bound note.** The note credited the polynomial threshold `∃ p, ∀ t ≥ p` to "polynomial-overhead universal simulation" (`DescriptionMethod.exists_etimeBoundedComplexity_universalTM_le_ofMultiTapeTM`). That theorem is clock-preserving: it uses the same `t` on both sides and adds only a description-length constant. The rewritten note says where the threshold actually comes from. `exists_timeBounded_of_computableInPolyTime` takes the generator's own `ComputableInPolyTime` running-time certificate, gets constants `c', d'`, and sets `p₀(n) = (c'+1)(n+1)^(d'+1)`. Theorem 5.2 then shifts this to `p_G(m) = p₀(m + 2γ + 3)` to cover the encoded truncation count. The note keeps the explicit statement that only the polynomial-threshold form is proved, and keeps the convention that `K^t` counts steps of the described machine. The module's label "M2a polynomial-overhead form" carried the same misattribution, so every remaining occurrence now reads "M2a polynomial-threshold form".
2. **`ROADMAP.md`.** The Liu–Pass converse (`exists_oneWay_of_mildlyHardOnAverage_timeBoundedNat` and the equivalences) landed in #1005, so this PR drops it from the open directions. In its place, the roadmap now lists the near-linear regime of Theorem 3.1 (c).
3. **`ComplexityTests/Crypto/HybridEncryption.lean`.** The existing `leakingEncaps` fixture stays as the length-boundary case: its leaked key has `n + 1` bits, so a length mismatch alone detects it. The new fixture `sameLengthLeakingEncaps n pk := pure (pk, pk)` leaks a uniform `n`-bit key under `toyKeyGen`. The tests prove:
   - the real game accepts with probability 1 (`eval_kemRealGame_sameLengthLeaking`);
   - the ideal game accepts with probability `2⁻ⁿ` (`eval_kemIdealGame_sameLengthLeaking_true`);
   - the advantage is exactly `1 - 2⁻ⁿ` for every `n` (`advantage_kem_sameLengthLeaking`), with instances at `n = 1` (`1/2`) and `n = 2` (`3/4`);
   - the fixture is not IND-CPA secure (`not_kemINDCPA_sameLengthLeaking`);
   - the fixture has a PPT certificate (`sameLengthLeakingEncaps_ppt`).
4. **`ComplexityTests/GKRProtocol.lean`.** The module doc now gives the correct breakdown of `5/101`: two sumcheck challenges of at most `2/101` each and one line challenge of at most `1/101`. The output step adds nothing, because the output layer has width 0.

**Source check (arXiv:2009.11514v1, checked against the PDF).** Theorem 3.1 (c), §3, p. 9: "For all constants d > 0, ε > 0, and every polynomial t(n) ≥ (1 + ε)n, K^t is mildly hard-on-average to (d log n)-approximate." §5.1, p. 11: "We say that G has rate-1 efficiency if its running time on inputs of length n is bounded by n + O(n^ε) for some constant ε < 1." Theorem 5.2 (§5.2, p. 11) assumes a rate-1 efficient condEP-PRG, and Theorem 5.6 (§5.3, p. 17) builds one from OWFs by padding. The near-linear range therefore rests on the generator's rate-1 running time, not on rate-1 universal simulation. The old note's phrase "rate-1 universal simulation" was corrected to match, and the ROADMAP direction uses the same wording.

**Review classification.** Documentation- and test-only. The new declarations are test fixtures and test theorems in `ComplexityTests`; no library statement, definition, abstract or security claim changes.

**Abstracts.** No impact: no abstract or catalogue entry refers to the changed text.

**Validation.** Local: all six `scripts/check.sh` gates, `check_hygiene.py`, `check_changed_files.py --base origin/main` and `lake exe mk_all --check` pass. The touched modules were rebuilt after rebasing onto #1027. CI: [ci-checks run 40202414571](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40202414571).
