issue.title: feat(promise): define RPReducible and probabilistic promise classes (#798)
issue.body:
## Summary Implements prerequisite **P1** of the metacomplexity program (#798, design comment 4 decision **D6**): randomized polynomial-time many-one reductions with one-sided error on promise problems (`PromiseProblem.RPReducible` and the threshold-indexed library generalization `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError`), the semantic probabilistic promise classes `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP` and `PromiseCoRP`, basic closure lemmas (reflexivity, deterministic lift, composition with both multiplicative and additive soundness accounting), faithfulness/convention bridges, and promise-class closure properties. ### Main Definitions & Theorems (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/Promise/Reduction.lean` and `Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean`) 1. **Shared Event-Probability Composition Bound (`Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean`):** - `Cslib.Probability.PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul`: if a first stage `p` lands in `pre` with probability at least `s₁` and for every supported `a ∈ pre` the continuation `kernel a` lands in `event` with probability at least `s₂` ($0 \le s_2$), then `p.bind kernel` lands in `event` with probability at least `s₁ * s₂`. 2. **Probabilistic Promise Classes (`PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP`, `PromiseCoRP`) [Goldreich, July 2005 author version, Definition 1.2, p. 4 and Section 6.2, p. 18][Goldreich2006]:** - `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError` and `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithOneSidedError`: Goldreich's bounded-error ($\ge 2/3$ on `Q.yes` and $\ge 2/3$ rejection on `Q.no`) and one-sided-error ($\ge 1/2$ on `Q.yes` and zero acceptance on `Q.no`) conditions restricted to instances in the promise `Q.yes ∪ Q.no`. - `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP`, and `PromiseCoRP`: promise problems solvable by a polynomial-time verifier (`ComputableInPolyTime`) with bounded or one-sided error on the promise. - Decision-problem agreement and `promiseClass` inclusions: - `ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP`, `ofSet_mem_PromiseRP`, `ofSet_mem_PromiseCoRP` (`PromiseProblem.ofSet A ∈ PromiseBPP enc ↔ A ∈ BPP enc`, etc.) - `promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP`, `promiseClass_RP_subset_PromiseRP`, `promiseClass_coRP_subset_PromiseCoRP` - Structural inclusions and complementation: - `compl_mem_PromiseBPP`, `compl_mem_PromiseRP_iff`, `compl_mem_PromiseCoRP_iff` - `PromiseP_subset_PromiseRP`, `PromiseP_subset_PromiseCoRP`, `PromiseP_subset_PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseNP`, `PromiseRP_subset_PromiseBPP`, `PromiseCoRP_subset_PromiseBPP` - Uniform strict PPT `ProbComp Bool` characterizations: - `mem_PromiseBPP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`, `mem_PromiseRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn`, `mem_PromiseCoRP_iff_exists_isPPTOn` - Closure under deterministic promise reductions (`PromiseProblem.PolyTimeReducible`, preserving `{α β γ : Type*}` universe polymorphism on existing deterministic declarations): - `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseNP`, `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`, `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseRP`, `PolyTimeReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP` 3. **Randomized One-Sided Promise Reductions (`RPReducibleWithError` and `RPReducible`):** - `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y`: a uniform strict PPT program `R : α → ProbComp β` (`IsPPTOn encA encB R`) that maps every `a ∈ X.yes` strictly into `Y.yes` (`∀ b ∈ (ProbComp.eval (R a)).support, b ∈ Y.yes`) and maps every `a ∈ X.no` into `Y.no` with probability at least `s a` (`s a ≤ ((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.no).toReal`). - `PromiseProblem.RPReducible encA encB X Y`: `RPReducibleWithError encA encB (fun _ => 2 / 3) X Y`. - Relation to deterministic reductions and reflexivity: - `PolyTimeReducible.rpReducibleWithError`, `PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible`, `Complexity.PolyTimeReducible.rpReducible_ofSet` - `RPReducibleWithError.refl`, `RPReducible.refl`, `RPReducibleWithError.of_subset`, `RPReducible.of_subset` - Composition with explicit error accounting (library lemmas): - `RPReducibleWithError.trans`: composing a reduction with soundness `s₁ : α → ℝ` and a reduction with uniform soundness `s₂ : ℝ` ($0 \le s_2$) yields a reduction with multiplicative soundness `fun a => s₁ a * s₂` via `PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_ge_mul`. - `RPReducibleWithError.trans_add`: union-bound / additive soundness `fun a => s₁ a + s₂ - 1` when $s_2 \le 1$. - Composition with deterministic promise reductions on either side: `PolyTimeReducible.trans_rpReducibleWithError`, `RPReducibleWithError.trans_polyTimeReducible`, `PolyTimeReducible.trans_rpReducible`, `RPReducible.trans_polyTimeReducible`. - Class closure and collapse consequences (library lemmas): - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`, `RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP_of_mem_PromiseP`, `RPReducible.mem_coRP_of_ofSet` - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP`, `RPReducible.mem_BPP_of_ofSet`: applies two nested 3-vote majority layers `M = maj3 (maj3 M₀)` to the target `PromiseBPP` solver `M₀` (amplifying per-query acceptance on `Y.yes` from $\ge 2/3$ to $\ge 20/27$ then $\ge 16400/19683 \ge 9/11$, and bounding per-query acceptance on `Y.no` by $\le 1/3$ then $\le 7/27$ then $\le 3283/19683 \le 2/11$), forms the composite experiment `T a = R a >>= M` (which accepts `a ∈ X.yes` with probability $\ge 9/11$ since every supported output of `R a` lies in `Y.yes`, and accepts `a ∈ X.no` with probability at most $1/3 + 2/11 = 17/33$ by `PMF.toOuterMeasure_bind_failure_toReal_le`), and runs `and2 T` (`T a` twice with `&&`) to obtain YES acceptance $\ge (9/11)^2 = 81/121 \ge 2/3$ and NO acceptance $\le (17/33)^2 = 289/1089 \le 1/3$ (hence NO rejection $\ge 800/1089 \ge 2/3$). - `RPReducible.mem_PromiseRP_of_compl`, `RPReducible.mem_PromiseBPP_of_compl`, `RPReducible.mem_RP_of_compl_ofSet` - `NP_subset_coRP_of_forall_rpReducible`, `NP_subset_BPP_of_forall_rpReducible` --- ## Faithfulness to the Literature (#798 Standing Rule) | Source | Source Definition / Convention | Formal Statement & Bridge Lemmas | |---|---|---| | **Ilango (ITCS 2020)**, Section 2 (*Preliminaries*, "randomized reduction", p. 34:11) | A randomized polynomial-time reduction $R$ from $L$ to a problem $\Pi$ satisfies: (1) if $x \in L$, $\Pr_R[R(x) \in \Pi_{\mathrm{YES}}] = 1$; (2) if $x \notin L$, $\Pr_R[R(x) \in \Pi_{\mathrm{NO}}] \ge 2/3$. (Note: Corollary 3.4, p. 34:16 is a specific randomized reduction to $\mathrm{MOCSP}$; the generic class-pullback and collapse consequences here are labelled as library lemmas.) | **Exact match:** `PromiseProblem.RPReducible` uses completeness on every support element and soundness threshold $2/3$ on `X.no`.
• **Probability-1 completeness bridge:** `PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_toOuterMeasure_eq_one` (via Mathlib's `ENNReal.toReal_eq_one_iff` and `PMF.toOuterMeasure_apply_eq_one_iff`) proves equivalence between support-based completeness and `((ProbComp.eval (R a)).toOuterMeasure Y.yes).toReal = 1`.
• **`Pr[...]` notation bridge:** `PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_probability` connects `RPReducible` to `2 / 3 ≤ Pr[(fun b => decide (b ∈ Y.no)) <$> R a]`.
• **Seeded polynomial-time function bridge:** `PromiseProblem.rpReducible_iff_exists_seeded` proves equivalence between uniform strict PPT `R : α → ProbComp β` (`IsPPTOn`) and an explicit plain `ComputableInPolyTime` function `f : α × List Bool → β` with a coin-length polynomial `p : Polynomial ℕ`.
• **Library collapse lemmas:** `PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseCoRP`, `PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_coRP_of_ofSet`, `NP_subset_coRP_of_forall_rpReducible`, and `NP_subset_BPP_of_forall_rpReducible`. | | **Ilango, Loff & Oliveira (CCC 2020)**, Section 4.2, Lemmas 15–16, pp. 22:20–22:23 | Randomized polynomial-time reduction for $\mathrm{Multi\text{-}MCSP}$ from gap/approximate bounded Set Cover with deterministic YES completeness and high-probability NO soundness (Section 3.2 is $\mathrm{MDCP}$). | **Library parametric generalization:** `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y` parameterizes the NO soundness threshold by `s : α → ℝ` (including weakened constant bounds such as `fun _ => 1 / 2`). `PromiseProblem.RPReducible.rpReducibleWithError_half` is a library weakening lemma (`2 / 3 ⇒ 1 / 2`, not reverse amplification). | | **Hirahara (FOCS 2022 / ECCC TR22-119)**, Lemma 8.3, p. 26 & Theorem 8.5, pp. 30–31 | Polynomial-time randomized reduction from the gap problem $\alpha\text{-}\mathrm{CMMSA}$ to $\mathrm{MCSP}^*$ (and $\mathrm{MINKT}^*$) in the same one-sided orientation: YES instances map to YES instances for every random choice; NO instances map to NO instances with probability $1 - o(1)$. | **Library parametric generalization & composition accounting:** `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError encA encB s X Y` accommodates instance-dependent soundness `s : α → ℝ` (such as $1 - o(1)$), and the library composition lemmas `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError.trans` (soundness `fun a => s₁ a * s₂`) and `PromiseProblem.RPReducibleWithError.trans_add` (soundness `fun a => s₁ a + s₂ - 1`) provide explicit multiplicative and additive error accounting. | | **Goldreich (2006)**, *On promise problems: a survey* (July 2005 author version), Definition 1.2, p. 4 & Section 6.2, p. 18; **Valiant & Vazirani (1986)**, Section 1, Theorem 1.1, pp. 86–87 | Semantic definitions of $\mathrm{PromiseBPP}$ (Definition 1.2, p. 4), $\mathrm{PromiseRP}$ and $\mathrm{PromiseCoRP}$ (Section 6.2, p. 18), where error bounds hold on `Q.yes` and `Q.no` and are unconstrained outside `Q.promise`. Valiant & Vazirani (§1, Theorem 1.1, pp. 86–87) use the dual one-sided orientation (NO instances map exclusively to `Y.no`, YES instances map to `Y.yes` with inverse-polynomial probability $\ge 1/(4n)$). | **Exact class match + library complement-duality identities:**
• `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError`, `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithOneSidedError`, `PromiseBPP`, `PromiseRP`, and `PromiseCoRP` match Goldreich's July 2005 author version verbatim, with decision-problem bridges `ofSet_mem_PromiseBPP`, `ofSet_mem_PromiseRP`, `ofSet_mem_PromiseCoRP` and one-way `promiseClass` inclusions `promiseClass_BPP_subset_PromiseBPP`, etc.
• **Complement-duality identities (library identities):** `PromiseProblem.rpReducibleWithError_compl_iff` expresses the dual one-sided orientation with general threshold `s : α → ℝ` (directly representing inverse-polynomial bounds such as Valiant–Vazirani's $1/(4n)$) as `RPReducibleWithError encA encB s Xᶜ Yᶜ`; `PromiseProblem.rpReducible_compl_iff` is the specialization to the constant threshold `2 / 3` (distinct from Valiant–Vazirani's unamplified $1/(4n)$ bound), and `PromiseProblem.RPReducible.mem_PromiseRP_of_compl` proves the corresponding `PromiseRP` pullback. | --- ## Abstract-Impact Assessment No existing selected abstract or headline theorem in `scripts/build_abstracts.py` is modified or affected by this PR. This PR adds foundational promise-reduction and promise-class definitions and closure lemmas in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/Promise/Reduction.lean` (plus a shared PMF event lemma in `Complexity/Probability/PMF/Event.lean`). `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` confirms the 14 selected abstracts and 19 headline theorems remain intact. ## AI Disclosure Implemented by `worker-antigravity-20261024` (Google DeepMind Antigravity agent, Gemini model) under delegation from `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. issue.title: feat(crypto): formalize Gentry's bootstrapping theorem for leveled and fixed-key fully homomorphic encryption
issue.body:
## Scope

Implement Target 3 of the highest-priority roadmap items (Gentry's bootstrapping theorem):

1. `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/Bootstrapping.lean`:
   - Formalize homomorphic encryption schemes, semantic security (IND-CPA against uniform PPT adversaries), ciphertext compactness, and bootstrappability via homomorphic evaluation of augmented decryption circuits (`Decrypt ∘ Aug`).
   - Prove Gentry's leveled bootstrapping theorem: any semantically secure, bootstrappable encryption scheme yields a compact leveled fully homomorphic encryption scheme for every polynomially bounded circuit depth `D`, with semantic security proved via a hybrid argument over the acyclic leveled key chain.
   - Prove Gentry's fixed-key FHE theorem: under an explicit circular-security assumption (`CircularSecure`), the construction with a self-encrypted evaluation key yields a compact fixed-key fully homomorphic encryption scheme without a predetermined depth bound.
2. Tests with a non-vacuous concrete instance and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/Bootstrapping.lean`, plus updates to `paper/main.tex` and `ROADMAP.md`.

## Completion Criteria
- Zero `sorry`, zero custom `axiom`, zero `native_decide`.
- Passes `./scripts/check.sh` and independent API, correctness, and theorem-index reviews.

issue.title: feat(Crypto): Merkle-tree verification and position binding (#999)
issue.body:
Milestone M1 of #999 (Kilian's succinct arguments): the verifier and the security notion of Merkle trees as an authenticated data structure. It adds verification of openings and position binding, reduced to collision resistance with no loss. The design is in the [M0 comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/999#issuecomment-6397996791).

**Stacked on #1023.** That PR is the shared Merkle-tree supplier from #1001: the tree, authentication paths, root recomputation and collision extraction. This PR is a thin layer over it, at #1023's head `512188fa`, and adds no second tree. It is meant to be the single shared verifier for #999 and #1001, as #1023's pre-check (finding 3) asked. Once #1023 lands, the base becomes `main` and the branch is restacked. (The first revision, `211f0400`, built its own tree; it is replaced.)

### What's added

New module `Complexity/Crypto/Computational/MerkleTree/Binding.lean`:

- **The verifier.** `merkleVerify H k d root i leaf path` accepts when `path` has `d` labels, `i < 2 ^ d`, and `merkleRootOfPath` recomputes `root`. These are the checks #1023's module docs require of a verifier ("What a verifier must check"); a test shows each one rejecting an opening the others accept.
  - **Completeness.** `merkleVerify_merklePath` and `merkleVerify_merklePath_of_clog_eq`: honest openings are accepted, the latter at any depth `d = Nat.clog 2 leaves.length`.
  - **Short openings.** Openings have one label per level, of at most `k.length` bits (`length_le_of_mem_merklePath`). Tree nodes have `k.length` bits (`length_of_mem_merkleLevel`, public).
  - **Efficiency.** `computableInPolyTime_merkleVerify` is a plain certificate.
  - **Binding.** `isCollision_of_merkleVerify`: two openings of one position to different leaves, both accepted at the same depth, give a collision through `extractMerkleCollision`.
- **The game.** `merkleBindingGame` and `MerklePositionBinding` are stated against uniform strict PPT adversaries, using `Game.Indistinguishable` against `false`, as `CollisionResistantOn` does.
- **The reduction.** `merkleCollisionFinder` runs the adversary and applies #1023's `extractMerkleCollision`.
  - `succProbability_merkleBindingGame_le` bounds the binding advantage by the collision advantage at every parameter: loss 1, no additive error.
  - `isPPT_merkleCollisionFinder` certifies the reduction.
  - `HashFamily.merklePositionBinding`: every `HashFamily` gives position binding.

New tests in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/MerkleBinding.lean`:
- **Under a hash that returns its message:** honest openings of a three-leaf tree are accepted. A wrong leaf, a truncated path and an out-of-range position (`4`, whose path recomputes the root) are rejected. A pair of child labels posing as a leaf recomputes the root and is rejected only by the length check.
- **Under a toy XOR hash:** an honest path also opens a position to a wrong leaf, and the reduction extracts the collision one level below the root.
- **Under a hash that ignores its message:** `¬ MerklePositionBinding`, so the notion is not vacuous. The test also checks a concrete PPT reduction and that compression families give binding trees through Merkle–Damgård.

### Sources and notation

**Boneh–Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*, v0.6 (Jan. 2023), §8.9.1.** I checked it against the v0.6 PDF.
- **Definition 8.3 (p. 323).** An authenticated data structure scheme is `D = (H, P, V)`, where "V is an algorithm that is invoked as V(i, x, y, π) and outputs accept or reject", with the requirement "V(i, x_i, H(T), P(i, x_i, T)) = accept".
- **Attack Game 8.2 (p. 324).** "The adversary A outputs a y ∈ Y, a position i ∈ {1, . . . , n}, and two pairs (x, π) and (x′, π′) where x, x′ ∈ X. We say that A wins the game if x ≠ x′ and V(i, x, y, π) = V(i, x′, y, π′) = accept."
- **Definition 8.4 (p. 324).** "We say that an authenticated data structure scheme D is secure if for all efficient adversaries A, the value ADSadv[A, D] is negligible."
- **Theorem 8.8 (p. 324).** "The Merkle hash tree scheme is a secure authenticated data structure scheme, assuming the underlying hash function h is collision resistant."

How the source's notation maps to the Lean:

| Boneh–Shoup | Lean |
|---|---|
| `H(T)`, `P(i, x, T)` (Fig. 8.12) | #1023's `merkleRoot H k leaves`, `merklePath H k leaves i` |
| `V(i, x, y, π)` | `merkleVerify H k d y i x π`, with the depth `d` explicit |
| correctness in Definition 8.3 | `merkleVerify_merklePath` |
| Attack Game 8.2, `ADSadv[A, D]` | `merkleBindingGame`, its success probability |
| Definition 8.4 | `MerklePositionBinding` |
| Theorem 8.8 | `HashFamily.merklePositionBinding` |

Labelled differences:
- **Hash.** The hash is a keyed family with a uniform `n`-bit key, and adversaries are uniform strict PPT programs, as in `CollisionResistant`.
- **Depth.** The adversary chooses the depth (its first path's length) and must open both leaves at it, which makes the game stronger than one at a fixed `n`.
- **Positions.** Positions are `0 ≤ i < 2 ^ d`, padding included, rather than `1 ≤ i ≤ n`.
- **Unary positions.** The adversary writes its position in unary (`encMerkleBindingOutput`), so the game covers polynomially bounded positions. That is enough for #999, where PCP proofs have polynomial length, and for #1001's polynomial capacity. It is not enough for trees with superpolynomially many positions, such as universal arguments; those would need binary-position certificates in #1023 (#1023 pre-check, finding 4).

**Kilian context.** Barak–Goldreich, *Universal Arguments and their Applications*, ECCC TR01-093, Construction 3.4, steps P1.3 (printed p. 9) and V3.2 (p. 10); I checked it against the ECCC PDF. Their tree differs from Boneh–Shoup's, which #1023 builds:

> The label of a leaf associated with γ ∈ {0,1}^d, denoted ℓ_γ, is the value of π_y at position γ; that is this oracle answer to the query γ. The label of an internal node associated with γ ∈ ∪_{i=0}^{d−1}{0,1}^i is the value obtained by applying h_α to the string ℓ_γ0ℓ_γ1.

So their leaves are raw proof bits, and nodes hash the plain concatenation. Their prover sends both child labels at each level, and V3.2 checks `ℓ'_γ = h_α(ℓ'_γ0ℓ'_γ1)` along the path. Their `h_α` resists non-uniform circuits. M2 uses the Boneh–Shoup tree for Kilian's commitments.

### Validation

- CI: [Lean Action CI at `d9909af1`](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40199020645)
- Locally: all six gates (`scripts/check.sh`), `check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `check_changed_files.py --base pr/1023`, `mk_all --check` and `check_tidy_surface.py` (no new tidy statements) pass.
- **Range-diff.** The restack onto `512188fa` was clean: the two earlier commits are unchanged (`git range-diff`, `=`), and `d9909af1` adds the pre-check fixes.

**Abstracts:** no impact. No curated abstract or catalogue entry changes. A Kilian headline may be proposed after M2/M3, as Samuel's call.

**Framework friction (#733):**
- **Missing plain comparison.** There is no plain `ComputableInPolyTime.binary_lt'`, only the tidy one, so the range check in `merkleVerify` goes through `.tidy`/`.of_tidy`.
- **Duplicate supplier.** #999 and #1001 designed Merkle trees at the same time. #1001's supplier was opened first, and this PR now builds on it.

### Review

Pre-check findings 1–7 at `e2cc9041` ([comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1024#issuecomment-6398372274)) are addressed in `d9909af1`. Approval by `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023` is requested: this PR adds public definitions and a security claim.

issue.title: feat(crypto): Fiat–Shamir signatures in the random-oracle model, exact security (#581 3b-i)
issue.body:
Refs #581 (milestone 3b-i of the Boneh–Shoup Chapter 19 plan; see #640 Track A).

## What is proved

**Mathematical progress**

- `SigmaProtocol.fiatShamir` is the Fiat–Shamir signature scheme of a Sigma protocol in the random-oracle model (Boneh–Shoup §19.6.1).
- `fiatShamir_correct`: with a complete protocol and keys in the relation, honest signatures verify.
- `succProbability_eufCmaGame_le` (Boneh–Shoup Theorem 19.16 with Equation 19.21, via Bellare–Neven Lemma 1) has these hypotheses:
  - the protocol is special sound on the generated keys and special HVZK;
  - its commitments are `δ`-unpredictable;
  - the keys are in the relation.

  Then every forger with explicit coins that makes at most `Q` signing and hash calls in total wins the random-oracle EUF-CMA game with probability at most

  `C(Q, 2) · δ + (Q + 1) / N + √((Q + 1) · ε')`,

  where `ε'` is the one-way success probability of the explicit reduction `FiatShamir.reduction`. The book has `Q_s (Q_s + Q_ro + 1) · δ` and `Q_ro` in place of `C(Q, 2) · δ` and `Q`; the module docstring records this difference.

  The proof has four hops:
  1. The difference lemma replaces the real signer by one that programs the oracle at `(m, t)`. The bad event, a commitment that hits the table, has probability at most `C(Q, 2) · δ`.
  2. Special HVZK replaces the programming signer by the simulator.
  3. The simulated transcripts are presampled.
  4. The result is a program over the hash oracle alone. The oracle forking lemma of #658 and special soundness extract a witness from it.

**Supporting infrastructure** (general, reusable)

- `OracleComp.IsQueryBounded` is a structural call budget. It is preserved by sequencing and by running through a handler, and it implies `HasQueryBounds`. It also justifies `IsQueryBounded.run_interpret_withSampleList`, which presamples a handler's per-call draws for PMF handlers.
- `OracleComp.IdenticalUntilBad` gives:
  - the difference lemma `bind_apply_le` for stateful handlers (Boneh–Shoup Theorem 4.7);
  - the growing-union bound `toOuterMeasure_bad_le`, of the form `n · budget + C(n, 2) · δ`.
- `runWithAnswers_bind`, `IsQueryBounded.length_runWithAnswers_le` and `runWithAnswers_run_interpret_invariant` give deterministic reasoning about a handler's run on fixed answers.
- `ROMSignature`, a typed signature scheme with `OracleComp` access to `H`:
  - the lazily sampled oracle `oracle`;
  - a generic `eufCmaGame`;
  - `Scheme.Correct`.

  The interface is deliberately small (a scheme, a forger with explicit coins, and a memoized uniform oracle), so it can be re-expressed in the #643 interactive-protocol core. It does not overlap the word-level MAC game of #677 or the hash families of #678.

## Scope and remaining milestones

- This PR is exact and typed: it makes no efficiency claim. Following the #643 security-interface scan, the simulator and extractor used in a computational theorem must be certified efficient. That certification belongs to **3b-ii**: computational Schnorr signatures under the discrete-log assumption for strict PPT forgers, with coin presampling near `Replay` and a reduction certified plainly as in #636 (plain public statements, tidy only inside proofs).
- Follow-up noted, not addressed here: #660's Lyubashevsky protocol has the same gap. Its simulator and extractor would need certificates before they are used in a full security theorem.
- Still open for #581 after this PR: 3b-ii; 2c (eavesdropping in the strict PPT model with an explicit statistical-distance term); and the Chapter 20 items on Track A.
- `SpecialSoundOn` and `oneWayGame` are used unchanged (not generalized to an implicit `W`), so this PR does not conflict with #660.

## Tests

`ComplexityTests/Crypto/FiatShamir.lean` instantiates everything for Schnorr signatures in `ZMod 11` with base `2`:

- correctness;
- `1/11`-unpredictable commitments;
- a forger that knows the witness and always wins, which proves that the theorem's bound is non-vacuous: the reduction extracts discrete logarithms with probability at least `81/242`;
- axiom guards.

## Validation

All of the following were run locally on the rebased head:

- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates pass (`build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`).
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`: passes.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 171 tests, OK.
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`: passes.

After a final rebase onto newer `main`, the changed modules and tests were rebuilt with `--wfail`, and `mk_all --check` and hygiene were rerun.

## Abstract assessment

No new abstract. The headline candidate is the computational Schnorr-signature theorem of 3b-ii, which is better assessed when it lands.

issue.title: feat(crypto): sample GSW keys with supported correctness
issue.body:
Constructs the actual finite GSW key-generation and encryption programs using uniform `w`-bit residues, independent binary coins, and errors given by the difference of two independent `η`-bit counts. Proves correctness for every supported generated key and fresh ciphertext under `w > 0` and `4*m*η < 2^w`, and for NAND of two fresh ciphertexts under `4*(1+N)*m*η < 2^w`, where `N=(n+1)*w`.

One flat tape of `n*w + m*n*w + 2*m*η + N*m` fair bits realizes the complete joint public-key, secret-key and ciphertext distribution. Serialized random-input samplers have uniform native PPT certificates, including all list framing, with unary dimensions and binary residues/errors. Exact distribution bridges and total decoder round trips connect those programs to the typed mathematical samplers. Reusable vector, finite-seed and uniform-support lemmas keep the client proofs compositional.

Tests cover exact nontrivial noise masses, signed endpoints, excluded errors, actual generated keys, both message bits and NAND, zero dimensions and widths, decoder normalization, growing native inputs and headline axiom guards. Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013) and NIST FIPS 203 Algorithm 8 are credited; the latter supplies the scalar noise construction, without a Gaussian-equivalence or hardness claim.

Closes #495. The full generated-key decision-LWE security reduction and admissible parameter families are tracked in #501; native certificates for modular matrix algorithms are tracked in #500. Full bootstrappability remains open in #486. This milestone certifies random-input generation, not complete encryption runtime. The selected formal abstract catalogue and existing headline statements are unaffected; the final FHE endpoint will receive its own checked abstract.

All six `scripts/check.sh` gates and `git diff --check` pass on the final integration source tree `b0508ed95ee0d7f676037414c7f4bbb633824cff`, published at `14f944215584f80090b89e45fc23b888675bc9b0`. Implement a reusable bounded fair-bit sampler for a positive finite interval, using existing dyadic/capped sampling and a fixed attempt budget. Prove the joint output/failure law, conditional uniformity and an explicit failure/statistical-error bound; then apply it coordinatewise to integer boxes. State resource assumptions on the input encodings explicitly, including radius, dimension, attempt budget and output length, and certify the whole program with a uniform plain public PPT contract. Unary polynomially bounded radius is an acceptable first stated scope; do not claim logarithmic-radius complexity from it. Keep zero dimension, radius zero, no attempts and malformed bounds visible in meaningful checks.

issue.title: feat(crypto): construct a depth-budgeted homomorphic scheme
issue.body:
Next construction milestone under #322, depending on compiler #462 / #455. The full secure leveled and fixed-key FHE objectives remain open.

Construct an actual depth-budgeted instance of the existing Homomorphic.Scheme, using the acyclic key-chain sampler, ordinary-circuit compiler and refresh evaluator. The permitted circuits must be exactly those with designated-output Circuit.depth at most the chosen budget.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add reusable identity-layer padding at the ordinary Layered API. Preserve plaintext evaluation and output width, prove well-formedness, and normalize a schedule of length at most L to exactly L layers. Certify the actual padding operation uniformly in unary L and the complete encoded schedule.
- For depth budget D, generate exactly 2D + 1 independent base key pairs with adjacent encrypted links. The public serialized artifact contains only public keys and encrypted links; private witnesses cannot appear in the public evaluator.
- Compile the actual shared circuit, pad with identity refresh layers to 2D, and retain ordered output wiring. Every allowed depth d <= D must finish under the same endpoint key, including d = 0 and D = 0.
- Package actual key generation, fresh encryption, decryption and single-output evaluation in the existing bit-string Scheme interface. Fresh inputs and evaluated outputs use different endpoint keys; explicitly represent that distinction. Proposed adaptation: one ciphertext tag bit and private initial/final keys. Gentry2009 Section2's displayed decryption expects the final key, whereas Scheme.Correct also requires decrypting fresh ciphertexts. Do not claim this tag adaptation is verbatim source text, and do not add a final-to-initial encrypted link.
- Prove Scheme.Correct from base correctness, fixed widths and actual augmented-decryption bootstrappability. This must concern support of the actual derived algorithms, not a certificate assumed to contain the desired result.
- Prove exact ciphertext width independent of circuit size, depth and budget, including fresh and evaluated ciphertexts. The derived secret representation and decryption algorithm must likewise not grow with the depth budget. State polynomial compactness/efficiency premises explicitly and derive bounds from the existing native certificates where available.
- Give strict native PPT certificates for the actual derived key generation/encryption/evaluation and a native deterministic certificate for decryption. Include all serialization, total decoding, unary budget computation, padding and output selection. Runtime must cover malformed public/private keys and ciphertexts. Reuse Decoder.pair/list/bits, existing tidy composition, and current PPT rules; no supplied depth table or runtime certificate.
- Test a concrete nonvacuous base fixture at positive budget with circuits of different actual depths that decrypt under the same final key, fresh decryption under a different initial key, depth-zero wiring, budget zero, constants with no input, malformed serialized inputs, and every runtime premise. Include named guarded axiom audits.
- Run all six project gates and independent exact-revision API and correctness reviews. Assess the curated abstract catalogue; a construction milestone is not a secure-FHE headline.

Before implementation, compare existing APIs and review the tag/final-key design. Keep reusable padding and codec helpers in their lowest appropriate modules. Preserve public interfaces.

Out of scope for this bounded milestone: acyclic-chain IND-CPA hybrid reduction, fixed-key circular-security theorem, and concrete LWE instantiation. They remain required under #322. Sources: Craig Gentry, Fully Homomorphic Encryption Using Ideal Lattices (STOC2009), Section2; existing cslib/Mathlib circuit and runtime calculus.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/Computational): formalize CDH, DDH, and ElGamal encryption (#873)
issue.body:
Closes #873 (part of Track C #640, Items 1 and 2).

### Summary
Formalizes the Computational Diffie–Hellman (`CDH`) and Decisional Diffie–Hellman (`DDH`) assumptions over `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, proves the hierarchy `DiscreteLog ≤ CDH ≤ DDH` and worst-case-to-average-case random self-reducibility of DDH, and formalizes ElGamal public-key encryption and its IND-CPA security reduction to DDH ([BonehShoup2023], Sections 10.4–10.6 and 11.4, Theorem 11.1):

1. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/DiffieHellman.lean`**:
   - **Computational Diffie–Hellman (`cdhGame`, `CDH`)**: Attack Game 10.5 over `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, plus the reduction `dlToCDHAdversary` (`succProbability_discreteLogGame_le_cdhGame`, `isPPTOn_dlToCDHAdversary`, `CDH.discreteLog : F.CDH setup → F.DiscreteLog setup`).
   - **Decisional Diffie–Hellman (`ddhRealGame`, `ddhIdealGame`, `DDH`)**: Attack Game 10.6 over `PrimeOrderGroupFamily`, plus the reduction `cdhToDDHDistinguisher` (`ddhRealGame_cdhToDDHDistinguisher`, `ddhIdealGame_cdhToDDHDistinguisher_true_le`, `succProbability_cdhGame_le_advantage_ddh_add`, `isPPTOn_cdhToDDHDistinguisher`, `DDH.cdh`, `DDH.discreteLog`).
   - **Random self-reducibility of DDH (`ddhRerandomize`, `ddhRerandomizeLaw`)**: `ddhRerandomizeLaw_real` proves that re-randomizing any fixed real DDH tuple `(α • g, β • g, (α * β) • g)` produces the exact uniform real DDH distribution `ddhRealTupleLaw`, and `ddhRerandomizeLaw_ideal` proves that re-randomizing any fixed non-DDH tuple `(α • g, β • g, γ • g)` with `γ ≠ α * β` produces the exact uniform ideal DDH distribution `ddhIdealTupleLaw`.

2. **`Complexity/Crypto/Computational/ElGamal.lean`**:
   - **Group-element ElGamal (`elGamalEncrypt`, `elGamalDecrypt`, `decodeElGamal`)**: algebraic encryption/decryption (`elGamalDecrypt_elGamalEncrypt`) and polynomial-time encoded decryption (`decodeElGamal_encode`, `decodeElGamal_elGamalEncrypt`, `computableInPolyTime_decodeElGamal`).
   - **One-time group mask (`smul_generator_surjective`, `uniform_smul_generator_add`)**: proves `α ↦ α • g` is surjective on `F.Carrier d` and `γ • g + m` is uniformly distributed over `F.Carrier d` for uniform `γ : ZMod (F.order d)`.
   - **ElGamal bit encryption and IND-CPA security (`bitElement`, `encodeBit`, `elGamalCPAGame`, `elGamalINDCPA`)**: reuses `Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.Adversary` and `Adversary.IsPPT`, defines `elGamalToDDHDistinguisher`, and proves `ddhRealGame_elGamalToDDHDistinguisher`, `ddhIdealGame_elGamalToDDHDistinguisher_false_eq_true`, `advantage_elGamalCPAGame_le`, `isPPTOn_elGamalToDDHDistinguisher`, and `DDH.elGamalINDCPA : F.DDH setup → F.elGamalINDCPA setup` ([BonehShoup2023], Theorem 11.1).

3. **`ComplexityTests/Crypto/DiffieHellman.lean`**:
   - Concrete `decide` checks on the order-11 Schnorr subgroup of `(ZMod 23)ˣ`, non-vacuity instantiations of `DDH.cdh`, `DDH.discreteLog`, and `DDH.elGamalINDCPA`, and 14 `#guard_msgs in #print axioms` guards.

issue.body:
Refs #640. This is milestone #645: the track B foundations, which don't depend on Fiat–Shamir. The design was agreed in https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/645#issuecomment-6377172784.

### What is proved

Everything is an exact `PMF` statement. No efficiency is claimed, and no hardness assumption is used in the protocol theorems.

- **SIS** (`Crypto/Computational/SIS/Basic.lean`, beside `DecisionLWE`).
  - `SIS.IsSolution A β z`: `z ≠ 0`, `|z i| ≤ β` for every `i`, and `A z ≡ 0 (mod q)`, for any modulus and any index types.
  - `SIS n m w β : Prop` (`q = 2 ^ w`): every uniform strict-PPT program (`IsPPT encBits`) that gets `1^λ` and `Matrix.toBinary A` of a uniform `A` finds a solution with negligible probability. Its output is read as `m` centered residues.
  - `SIS.decode_toBinary` shows the centered reading loses no solution when `2β < q`.
  - It is a hypothesis against classical adversaries, as the docstring says. The tests refute it for degenerate parameters (no rows), so it is not vacuous.
- **Exact rejection sampling** (`Probability/RejectionSampling.lean`).
  - `y` is uniform on a finite set `B` in an additive group, and the sampler outputs `some (y + v)` if `y + v ∈ S`, else `none`.
  - If `S - v ⊆ B`, then `Pr[some z] = |S|/|B| · uniform_S(z)` and `Pr[none] = 1 - |S|/|B|` (`shiftReject_apply_some_eq_mul`, `shiftReject_apply_none`). So the law is independent of `v` (`shiftReject_eq`).
  - The box instance `boxReject ι γ β v` takes `‖v‖∞ ≤ β ≤ γ`. Acceptance is exactly `((2(γ-β)+1)/(2γ+1))^|ι|`, accepted values are uniform on `[-(γ-β), γ-β]^ι`, and the abort probability is at most `2|ι|β/(2γ+1)` (`boxReject_apply_none_le`, by Bernoulli's inequality).
- **Sigma protocols with aborts** (`SigmaProtocol/Abort.lean`).
  - `SigmaProtocol` is unchanged. An aborting protocol has responses `Option Z`.
  - `acceptedTranscript` and `acceptedConversation` erase aborted runs.
  - `NonAbortComplete R` is completeness up to aborts.
  - `NonAbortSpecialHVZK R simulate` is exact per-challenge zero knowledge of the accepted view, aborts included. `acceptedConversation_eq` is its uniform-challenge form.
- **Lyubashevsky identification** (`SigmaProtocol/Lyubashevsky.lean`). The statement is `(A, T)`, the witness is `S` with `A S = T`, and challenges are `BitString k`. The prover commits to `A y` with `y ← [-γ, γ]^m`, answers `y + S ĉ` only inside `[-(γ-β), γ-β]^m`, and otherwise aborts. With `|S_ij| ≤ η` and `kη ≤ β ≤ γ`:
  - `lyubashevsky_nonAbortComplete`: every answer is accepted.
  - `lyubashevsky_acceptedTranscript_none`, `lyubashevsky_acceptedTranscript_none_le`: at every challenge the abort probability is exactly `1 - ((2(γ-β)+1)/(2γ+1))^m`, which is at most `2mβ/(2γ+1)`.
  - `lyubashevsky_specialSoundness`: two accepting conversations with distinct challenges give `(z - z', ĉ' - ĉ)`, an SIS solution for `[A | T]` with bound `max (2(γ-β)) 1`.
  - `lyubashevsky_nonAbortSpecialHVZK`: the simulator (rejection with no shift, then `w = A z - T ĉ`) has exactly the honest accepted view.

### API change

`SigmaProtocol.SpecialSoundness` (and its `mono` and `exists_witness`) now takes the extracted witness's type `W` as an implicit argument: relaxed special soundness. Lyubashevsky extracts a kernel vector of `[A | T]`, not a secret matrix. Existing uses infer `W = X` and are unchanged, and nothing else in the library is affected. #605's `SpecialSoundOn` and `oneWayGame` still take the prover's witness type, so the lattice extractor will need the same generalization there before the rewinding bound applies to it.

Under #643's planned core, an abort is a prover message `⊥`. `acceptedTranscript` is the transcript seen through a view that erases aborted runs, so the core can absorb it as a view parameter.

### Remaining for track B (#640)

- Fiat–Shamir with aborts and the signatures, after track A's random-oracle Fiat–Shamir.
- Identification security under SIS, which needs #605's rewinding with relaxed extraction.
- Strict-PPT samplers for integer boxes.
- SIS for general (prime) moduli.
- Module SIS and module lattices toward Dilithium.

### Validation

At `7dfa10ab`:
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six gates pass.
- `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp` passes.
- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 127 tests pass.
- `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passes.
- `scripts/check_docs.py --config-only` passes.

`ComplexityTests/Crypto/Lyubashevsky.lean` uses `ZMod 7`, `n = 1`, `m = 2`, `k = 1`, `γ = 2`, `β = 1`. It checks:
- honest answers, an abort, and accepting and rejected conversations, by `decide`;
- an extractor run, whose output `(-1, 1, 1)` is checked as an SIS solution both by `decide` and through the theorem;
- the abort probability `1 - (3/5)^2`;
- a simulator-law point, `1/25`, transferred to the honest prover by the HVZK theorem;
- the box-sampler law, and the non-vacuity of `SIS`;
- `#print axioms` guards.

### Abstract assessment

The headline catalogue is unaffected. These are foundations, and the natural headline candidate is the later lattice signature theorem, not identification.

### AI disclosure

Written by Claude Code (Opus 5.5), agent `worker-claude-lattice-c4b0c164`, delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Boneh–Shoup v0.6 Chapter 17 is only a stub, so the definitions follow Lyubashevsky (2009, 2012) and the Dilithium paper. New bib entries: `Ajtai1996`, `Lyubashevsky2009`, `Lyubashevsky2012`, `DucasEtAl2018`. No human or independent review yet; Codex cross-review is requested.

issue.title: feat(Crypto/Protocols/MAC/CarterWegman): nonce-based and randomized Carter-Wegman MACs (#736)
issue.body:
Refs #736

### Summary

Extends `Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MAC/CarterWegman.lean` and `ComplexityTests/Crypto/CarterWegman.lean` with two mathematical developments from Boneh–Shoup [BonehShoup2023]:

1. **Full nonce-based Carter–Wegman MAC security (Attack Game 7.4 & Theorem 7.10, Section 7.5.1, p. 274)**:
   - Defines `NonceForger M N Y` (an adaptive multi-query oracle adversary that chooses its own `(m, x) : M × N` pairs on each signing query and outputs a candidate forgery `((m', x'), t') : (M × N) × Y`), the pad-function signing handler `nonceFnHandler`, the key-independent simulated handler `nonceSimHandler`, the transcript-reconstruction map `reconstructPadFn`, and the Attack Game 7.4 verification predicate `checkNonceSUF` (requiring `(tr.map (fun e => e.1.2)).Nodup`, `!tr.contains out`, and `verify hash k (padFn x') m' t' = true`), together with its message-freshness specialization `checkNonceEUF`.
   - Proves the multi-query lazy-pad simulation equivalence `uniform_bind_run_interpret_nonceFnHandler` by induction on `OracleComp`: under a uniform random function `rf ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (N → Y)`, running `nonceFnHandler` has the exact same joint `(output, transcript, padFn)` distribution as running `nonceSimHandler` (which returns independent uniform tags without touching `k`) and reconstructing `padFn` at the end via `reconstructPadFn` on distinct-nonce transcripts.
   - Proves `seed_uniform_checkNonceSUF_le` and the ideal-pad bounds `nonceStrongGame_le_max` (`≤ max ε (Fintype.card Y)⁻¹`), `nonceStrongGame_le` (`≤ (Fintype.card Y)⁻¹ + ε`), and `nonceGame_le` without any query-count restriction on the adversary, handling both fresh-nonce forgeries (`(Fintype.card Y)⁻¹` by uniform unqueried pad evaluation) and reused-nonce forgeries with a fresh message (`ε` by `IsDeltaUniversalHash`).
   - Proves the concrete PRF-pad reduction `maskedNonceStrongGame_toReal_le_add_advantage` / `prfNonceStrongGame_le_of_distinguisher` / `prfNonceGame_le_of_distinguisher`, the asymptotic `PseudorandomFunction` corollaries `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfNonceStrongGame` and `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfNonceGame`, and concrete instantiations for `xpolyHash`, `BitString.LinearHash.hash`, `BitString.SubsetSum.hash`, and `IsPairwiseIndependentHash`.

2. **Randomized Carter–Wegman MAC security (Theorem 7.9, Section 7.4, p. 270)**:
   - Defines `RandomNonceForger M N Y` (an adaptive multi-query oracle adversary that queries `m : M`, receives `(x, t) : N × Y` with a random nonce `x ← PMF.uniformOfFintype N` chosen by the signer, and outputs `((m', x'), t')`), the randomized handler `randomNonceFnHandler`, the key-independent simulator `randomNonceSimHandler`, and the verification predicates `checkRandomNonceSUF` and `checkRandomNonceEUF`.
   - Proves the multi-query simulation equivalence `uniform_bind_run_interpret_randomNonceFnHandler` and the birthday-collision bound `randomNonceSimHandler_not_nodup_le` (`≤ (∑ i ∈ Finset.range Q, i) / |N|` for any `Q`-query-bounded adversary).
   - Proves the ideal-pad bounds `randomNonceStrongGame_le_sum_add_max` (`≤ (∑ i < Q, i) / |N| + max ε (1 / |Y|)`), `randomNonceStrongGame_le` (`≤ Q^2 / (2 |N|) + 1 / |Y| + ε`), and `randomNonceGame_le`, the concrete PRF-pad reduction `maskedRandomNonceStrongGame_toReal_le_add_advantage` / `prfRandomNonceStrongGame_le_of_distinguisher` / `prfRandomNonceGame_le_of_distinguisher`, the asymptotic `PseudorandomFunction` corollaries `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfRandomNonceStrongGame` and `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfRandomNonceGame` for `PolynomiallyBounded Q`, and concrete instantiations for `xpolyHash` and `BitString.LinearHash.hash`.

### Primary-Source Audit

- **Boneh–Shoup [BonehShoup2023], v0.6, Section 7.4, Theorem 7.9, p. 270 (Carter–Wegman security)**:
  > "Theorem 7.9 (Carter-Wegman security). Let $F$ be a secure PRF defined over $(\mathcal{K}_F, \mathcal{R}, \mathcal{T})$ where $|\mathcal{R}|$ is super-poly. Let $H$ be a computational DUF defined over $(\mathcal{K}_H, \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{T})$. Then the Carter-Wegman MAC $I_{\text{CW}}$ derived from $F$ and $H$ is a secure MAC.
  > In particular, for every MAC adversary $\mathcal{A}$ that attacks $I_{\text{CW}}$ as in Attack Game 6.1, there exist a PRF adversary $\mathcal{B}_F$ and a DUF adversary $\mathcal{B}_H$, which are elementary wrappers around $\mathcal{A}$, such that
  > $$\text{MACadv}[\mathcal{A}, I_{\text{CW}}] \le \text{PRFadv}[\mathcal{B}_F, F] + \text{DUFadv}[\mathcal{B}_H, H] + \frac{Q^2}{2|\mathcal{R}|} + \frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}. \qquad (7.24)$$"
- **Boneh–Shoup [BonehShoup2023], v0.6, Section 7.5.1, Attack Game 7.4, Definition 7.6, and Theorem 7.10, p. 274 (Nonce-based Carter–Wegman security)**:
  > "Attack Game 7.4 (nonce-based MAC security). For a given nonce-based MAC system $I = (S, V)$, defined over $(\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{M}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{N})$, and a given adversary $\mathcal{A}$, the attack game runs as follows:
  > • The challenger picks a random $k \gets^{\text{R}} \mathcal{K}$.
  > • $\mathcal{A}$ queries the challenger several times. For $i = 1, 2, \dots$, the $i$th signing query consists of a pair $(m_i, \mathfrak{N}_i)$ where $m_i \in \mathcal{M}$ and $\mathfrak{N}_i \in \mathcal{N}$. We require that $\mathfrak{N}_i \neq \mathfrak{N}_j$ for all $j < i$. The challenger computes $t_i \gets^{\text{R}} S(k, m_i, \mathfrak{N}_i)$, and gives $t_i$ to $\mathcal{A}$.
  > • Eventually $\mathcal{A}$ sends outputs a candidate forgery triple $(m, t, \mathfrak{N}) \in \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{T} \times \mathcal{N}$, where $(m, t, \mathfrak{N}) \notin \{(m_1, t_1, \mathfrak{N}_1), (m_2, t_1, \mathfrak{N}_2), \dots\}$.
  > We say that $\mathcal{A}$ wins the game if $V(k, m, t, \mathfrak{N}) = \text{accept}$. We define $\mathcal{A}$'s advantage with respect to $I$, denoted $\text{nMACadv}[\mathcal{A}, I]$, as the probability that $\mathcal{A}$ wins the game."
  > "Definition 7.6. We say that a nonce-based MAC system $I$ is secure if for all efficient adversaries $\mathcal{A}$, the value $\text{nMACadv}[\mathcal{A}, I]$ is negligible."
  > "Theorem 7.10. With the notation of Theorem 7.9 we obtain the following bounds
  > $$\text{nMACadv}[\mathcal{A}, I_{\text{CW}}] \le \text{PRFadv}[\mathcal{B}_F, F] + \text{DUFadv}[\mathcal{B}_H, H] + \frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}.$$"
- **Audit notes on model conventions**:
  1. *Statistical vs. computational DUF*: Boneh–Shoup state Theorems 7.9 and 7.10 with a computational DUF (`DUFadv[B_H, H]`) plus `1 / |T|`. Our formalization proves the statistical `IsDeltaUniversalHash seed hash ε` form (matching Boneh–Shoup Section 7.4.1 for polynomial and linear universal hashes), yielding the sharper `max ε (1 / |Y|)` bound (and the additive `1 / |Y| + ε` corollary) in Theorem 7.10 (`nonceStrongGame_le_max` / `nonceStrongGame_le`) and `Q^2 / (2 |N|) + 1 / |Y| + ε` in Theorem 7.9 (`randomNonceStrongGame_le`).
  2. *Assumed PRF reduction wrapper in computational theorems*: Boneh–Shoup assert the existence of the elementary PRF wrapper `B_F` around an efficient MAC adversary `A`. Here, `NonceForger` and `RandomNonceForger` are information-theoretic `OracleComp` adversaries over abstract types `M`, `N`, `Y`, so `prfNonceStrongGame_le_of_distinguisher`, `prfRandomNonceStrongGame_le_of_distinguisher`, `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfNonceStrongGame`, and `PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prfRandomNonceStrongGame` take the `OracleDistinguisher` `D` (with `hD : IsOraclePPT encBool D` in the asymptotic corollaries) and its simulation equalities `hreal`/`hideal` as explicit hypotheses rather than constructing `D` from an `IsOraclePPT` forger. In `ComplexityTests/Crypto/CarterWegman.lean`, the `example` blocks for `negligible_prfNonceStrongGame` and `negligible_prfRandomNonceStrongGame` are labeled as smoke tests using the always-losing forgers `repeatedNonceForger` and `echoRandomNonceForger` matched against a constant-`false` `prfPadDistinguisher`; nonvacuous adaptive multi-query bounds are checked separately by `sampleNonceForger` and `sampleRandomNonceForger` over `ZMod 7`.

### Limitations and Remaining Scope (#736)

- This PR is a **milestone toward #736** (`Refs #736`) and records the remaining gap in `ROADMAP.md`:
  1. Constructing the word-level `IsOraclePPT` PRF reduction wrappers `D` from `IsOraclePPT` forgers for nonce-based and randomized Carter–Wegman (eliminating the assumed `D`/`hreal`/`hideal` hypotheses).
  2. Packaging the randomized Carter–Wegman construction as a `MACScheme` instance satisfying `MACScheme.SUFCMA`.
  3. Defining a computational nonce-based MAC interface (`NonceMACScheme`) for Theorem 7.10.

### Abstract-Catalogue Assessment

- Checked `abstracts/catalogue.json`: Carter–Wegman MAC is not a separate entry in the curated headline abstract catalogue, so no abstract changes are needed.

### Validation

- `./scripts/check.sh` (all 6 gates: `lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`)
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py`

### AI Disclosure

Authored by `worker-jetski-cf53d356` (Gemini / Jetski).

issue.title: feat(machines): expose plain product and oracle-run certificates
issue.body:
Plain Classes clients can now multiply computed binary integers and obtain a resource certificate for a clocked oracle-machine run without constructing a tidy hypothesis.

Adds exactly two shared endpoints in their original source homes:
- `ComputableInPolyTime.intBin_mul'` takes plain certificates for both integer functions under the complete common input encoding, retaining `encIntBin` for each operand and the signed result. Its telescope matches the reviewed S1 counterpart; the proof reuses the existing raw multiplication certificate locally.
- `MultiTapePTM.exists_computableInO_run` takes a plain oracle certificate and returns a plain certificate for the identical coin-false, polynomial-clock run. Both sides use **charged** `ComputableInO`: the encoded output remains charged to workspace. The existing same-bound equivalence preserves independent time/workspace witnesses and the polynomial workspace bound. There is no oracle polynomial-time premise or additional output-length/positivity premise. `[Finite Control]`, `[Finite Operation]` and `[DecidableEq Operation]` are retained; an operation enumeration is not required.

All existing runtime definitions, raw theorem statements and proofs are unchanged. No aliases, model, tactic change or global raw fallback is added. The pure-PPT endpoint is the separate #813.

Validation: strict new ordinary-import clients plus original IntBinaryDiv and OracleReplay suites pass (6402 jobs). The fixture checks arbitrary input encodings, registered product automation, missing-operand negatives, signed/zero arithmetic, the full generic oracle-run contract and a zero clock. All six required gates pass at exact `ac817ba3` with `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4`. Fresh-output S3 update leaves the baseline byte-identical, then the separate CI-equivalent ratchet passes (1887 / 401). Hygiene, catalogue (14 abstracts / 19 headlines) and diff checks pass. Logs: `/tmp/codex-750-intmul-oracle-run-six-gates.log` and `/tmp/codex-750-intmul-oracle-run-s3-final.log`.

Abstract assessment: no selected headline, definition, scope note or catalogue change; these are source-level certificate frontends. Existing abstract tests are included in required validation.

### Framework friction

The Classes sweep identified these two missing plain shared endpoints and otherwise had to round-trip through tidy outside Machines. These source-home transports remove that need while retaining exact resources. Other missing providers and the final plain search boundary remain separate obligations; this PR does not claim full S1 completion.

Refs #750, #456 and #854. AI-assisted worker `codex-review-559`; independent exact-head review required. Initial immutable payload `ac817ba3` was handed off before broad checks for client integration.

issue.title: feat(probabilistic): bound interval and integer-box sampling error
issue.body:
Closes #713. Supports #645/#680; those simulator/extractor realization and error-transport tasks remain open.

Add `sampleUniformInterval bound attempts`: draw all budgeted capped fair-bit samples, keep the first valid index, and return `none` on exhaustion. Reuse existing `sampleBoundedIndex`/`sampleBinaryNat`, repetition and list search; there is no new random primitive or unbounded retry. At positive bound q, one-attempt rejection is p=(dyadicSize(q)−q)/dyadicSize(q)≤1/2. The full law has failure p^attempts and equal valid masses (1−p^attempts)/q. Conditional uniformity and unconditional Boolean-test error≤2⁻attempts are separate theorems.

Apply it independently to runtime-dimensional integer boxes. The joint success law is the exact uniform integer-box reference law scaled by all-coordinate success, with exact failure 1−(1−p^attempts)^dimension and unconditional statistical error≤dimension·2⁻attempts for every Boolean test. Supported lists have the requested dimension/radius. Zero interval bounds always fail; no attempts fail except that dimension zero returns `some []` without drawing. Radius zero can still incur retry failure.

All new public efficiency premises are plain. Uniform strict PPT certificates charge unary radius/dimension/attempts and the complete framed optional output, bounded by dimension·(2·radius+3)+1. A **binary interval** certificate separately accepts a binary bound with a plainly computable unary width equal to log₂(bound)+1 and a unary attempt budget; the checked client handles bound=2^width without charging that bound in unary. The box certificate makes no logarithmic-radius claim. `ProbComp.eval_replicate_iid` extends the existing shared repetition API to infinite output types, needed for optional integer coordinates; existing finite API/statements remain unchanged.

Validation at `f5a40de0842d7d470257e038aac7906e7e55b78b`: all six gates via `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=4 scripts/check.sh`; strict focused tests; hygiene (`--check-simp`), catalogue and diff checks. Tests cover zero boundaries, conditional 1/3 versus unconditional 1/4, radius-one dimension-two failure7/16 and point mass1/16, runtime-varying box budgets, exponential binary bounds, output length and axiom guards. No source edits to #660 or the S1 core. Abstract assessment: no selected headline, scope note, encoding or renderer changed; no catalogue/PDF update is needed.

This is the sampler foundation, not a computational security/simulator theorem. It preserves #660’s exact algebraic laws. The separately coordinated #581 total modulo sampler offers an always-returned residue with bias; this API offers explicit failure and exact conditional uniformity, both over existing fair-bit primitives.

Authored and self-reviewed by Codex worker `codex-review_559` under `coordinator-codex-01a16ab8`; independent current-head review requested. No self-approval or merge.

issue.title: feat(crypto): prove generated-key GSW security from exact decision LWE
issue.body:
Proves single-challenge IND-CPA for the actual serialized GSW key generator and encryption program, assuming decision LWE for their exact centered-binomial error distribution. The public-key marginal is identified with the LWE experiment, and one uniform strict-PPT reduction retains the adversary's complete saved state. Its bound is `AdvCPA ≤ 2·AdvLWE + N·sqrt(2^N / 2^m)`, where `N = (n+1)w`.

The explicit family `n = η = λ+1`, `w = 16+8⌈log₂(λ+1)⌉`, and `m = N+2λ` supplies native parameter routines, negligible statistical error, and strict fresh/one-NAND correctness margins. The endpoint `GSW.Parameters.indCPA` therefore leaves only its specified LWE premise. Reusable additions cover public-key replacement, encoded LWE experiments, dyadic negligibility, and independent replicated sampling.

Closes #501 as a security milestone within #486. This does **not** establish LWE hardness, circular security, native decryption/evaluation, shallow decryption, or bootstrappability. The current parameter family is not claimed to support full FHE. The native honest algorithms come from merged #519.

Validation: all six repository gates passed on the final source: strict build, aggregate-import check, strict tests, lint, style lint, and initialization-import check. Regressions exercise adaptive message selection and saved public-key state, attain the reduction's factor-two loss, and check actual honest/reduction efficiency certificates. The checked abstract has 40 roots, 164 audited dependencies, no internal-definition allowlist, and headline axiom guards containing only the three permitted standard axioms.

issue.title: feat(crypto): Carter–Wegman MACs from Δ-universal hashing (Boneh–Shoup Section 7.4)
issue.body:
Parent: #640 (Track D item 2b).

### Objective

Formalize Carter–Wegman message authentication codes from $\varepsilon$-almost-$\Delta$-universal hash families (`IsDeltaUniversalHash` in `Complexity.Probability.HashFamily`) following Wegman–Carter (1981) and Boneh–Shoup (Section 7.4, Theorems 7.3–7.4) in `Complexity/Crypto/Protocols/MAC/CarterWegman.lean`, with concrete instantiations (`xpolyHash`, `BitString.LinearHash.hash`, `BitString.SubsetSum.hash`, and `IsPairwiseIndependentHash`) and a PRF-masked reduction bound.

### Scope & Completion Criteria

1. **One-time and zero-query Carter–Wegman MAC over any finite additive group `Y` (`[AddGroup Y] [Fintype Y] [Nonempty Y] [DecidableEq Y]`)**:
   - `sign k r m = hash k m + r` and `verify k r m t = decide (hash k m + r = t)`.
   - Correctness (`verify_sign`), unique valid tag (`verify_eq_true_iff`, `eq_of_verify_eq_true`), unique pad `r = -hash k m + t` (`sign_eq_iff_eq_neg_add`), and exact tag uniformity/independence (`map_sign_eq_uniform`, `bind_uniform_sign`).
   - Exact zero-query forgery probability `zeroQueryGame_apply_true : (zeroQueryGame seed hash forger) true = (Fintype.card Y : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹`.
   - Adaptive one-time EUF-CMA (`oneTimeGame`) and SUF-CMA (`oneTimeStrongGame`) for `OneTimeForger M Y`:
     - `oneTimeStrongGame_eq_oneTimeGame : oneTimeStrongGame seed hash forger = oneTimeGame seed hash forger`.
     - **Boneh–Shoup Theorem 7.3 (`oneTimeGame_le`, `oneTimeStrongGame_le`)**: under `IsDeltaUniversalHash seed hash ε`, `(oneTimeGame seed hash forger) true ≤ ε` and `(oneTimeStrongGame seed hash forger) true ≤ ε`.
2. **Adaptive `Q`-query counter / independent-pad Carter–Wegman MAC (`CounterForger`, `counterGame`, `counterStrongGame`)**:
   - Inductive `CounterForger Q M Y` where in each of `Q` rounds `i : Fin Q` the forger adaptively chooses `m_i : M` and receives `t_i = hash k m_i + pads i` for `pads ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin Q → Y)`, then outputs `(i*, m*, t*) : Fin Q × M × Y`.
   - `counterStrongGame_eq_counterGame` and `counterGame_le` / `counterStrongGame_le`: under `IsDeltaUniversalHash seed hash ε`, the `Q`-query adaptive forgery probability is at most `ε` for every `Q : ℕ` (with zero degradation in `Q`).
3. **Concrete instantiations**:
   - Polynomial Carter–Wegman (`xpolyHash` over a finite field `F`, Boneh–Shoup Section 7.4.1): forgery probability at most `(ℓ + 1) / Fintype.card F`.
   - Boolean-matrix Carter–Wegman (`BitString.LinearHash.hash`): forgery probability at most `(2 ^ m : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹`.
   - Subset-sum Carter–Wegman (`BitString.SubsetSum.hash`): forgery probability at most `(Fintype.card G : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹`.
   - Pairwise-independent Carter–Wegman (`IsPairwiseIndependentHash`): forgery probability at most `(Fintype.card Y : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹`.
4. **PRF-masked Carter–Wegman bound (`prfOneTimeGame`, `prfOneTimeStrongGame`, `prfOneTimeGame_le`)**:
   - Replacing the uniform pad `r ← PMF.uniformOfFintype (BitString n)` with a PRF evaluation `BitString.ofList n ( family key (List.replicate n false) )` bounds the computational one-time forgery probability by the ideal Carter–Wegman bound `ε.toReal` plus the PRF distinguishing advantage `Game.advantage (prfRealGame family D n) (prfIdealGame D n)`.
5. **Tests & validation**:
   - Nonvacuous concrete instances and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/Crypto/CarterWegman.lean`.

issue.title: feat(crypto): concrete leveled and fully homomorphic encryption from GSW
issue.body:
Part of #486, milestone 3. **Stacked on #1022**, so the diff shown is only this PR's commit.

This PR instantiates #481's generic bootstrapping theorems with GSW at the logarithmic-depth parameter family. That gives the concrete endpoints #486 asks for:

- **`exists_leveled_of_decisionLWE`.** Assumes only `DecisionLWE dimension samples width (fun k => noiseLaw (width k) (noise k))`. That is decision LWE for exactly this family: secret dimension `λ+1`, centered-binomial noise of width `λ+1`, and the quasi-polynomial modulus `2^(16384·t²)` with `t = 1 + ⌈log₂(λ+2)⌉`.
  - **Chosen before the depth family:**
    - one decryption circuit family, of polynomial size, that agrees with the common decryption algorithm `Leveled.decrypt decryptionCircuits` on all words of the fixed widths;
    - a native polynomial-time certificate for that decryption algorithm;
    - polynomial bounds for the fixed widths `3·secretWidth + 1` and `ciphertextWidth + 1`.
  - **Then, for every polynomially bounded depth family,** there is a natively computable budget, and the actual scheme `Leveled.scheme decryptionCircuits budget`:
    - has exactly that decryption algorithm (`rfl`);
    - is perfectly correct;
    - permits every circuit of the requested depth;
    - has the fixed widths;
    - has native strict PPT key generation, encryption and evaluation;
    - is IND-CPA.

  No circular-security assumption is used.
- **`fullyHomomorphic_of_decisionLWE_of_circularSecure`.** Assumes the same decision LWE together with the explicit one-key circular-security hypothesis `Encryption.CircularSecure scheme.keyGen scheme.encrypt` for the base GSW scheme. The fixed-key self-loop scheme `FixedKey.scheme decryptionCircuits`:
  - permits and correctly evaluates every finite circuit;
  - keeps GSW's polynomial widths, and its decryption circuits have polynomial size;
  - has native algorithms;
  - is IND-CPA.

  Circular security is neither derived from LWE nor hidden.

Both proofs only assemble existing results. #1022's `correct`, `fixedWidth`, `bootstrappable`, native certificates and `indCPA_scheme` are fed into `Leveled.exists_scheme_of_polynomiallyBounded`, `Leveled.exists_decrypt_circuits`, `Leveled.polynomiallyBounded_widths` and `FixedKey.fullyHomomorphic`. The generic theorems take and return some tidy certificates. Here tidy computability appears only inside the proofs, and every public conclusion uses plain `ComputableInPolyTime`.

**Source statements** (Gentry, STOC 2009, fetched PDF):
- Definition 1, p. 170: "E is homomorphic for circuits in C_E if E is correct for C_E and Decrypt_E can be expressed as a circuit D_E of size poly(λ)."
- Definition 3, p. 170: "A family of schemes {E(d) : d ∈ Z+} is leveled fully homomorphic if they all use the same decryption circuit, E(d) is homomorphic for all circuits of depth at most d (that use some specified set of gates Γ), and the computational complexity of E(d)'s algorithms is polynomial in λ, d, and (in the case of Evaluate_E(d)) the size of C."
- Theorem 3, p. 171: "Let E be bootstrappable with respect to a set of gates Γ. Then the family {E(d)} is leveled fully homomorphic (for circuits with gates in Γ)."
- Theorem 4, p. 171, top of the right column: "Let A be an algorithm that breaks the semantic security of E(d) with advantage ε. Then, there is an algorithm B that breaks the semantic security of E with probability at least ε/ℓ(d + 1), for ℓ as in Definition 4, and time poly(ℓ, d) times that of A." The Lean IND-CPA conclusion is its asymptotic consequence. The exact loss `ε/ℓ(d+1)` is not formalized; the ROADMAP lists it as open.
- The self-loop remark, p. 172: "if E is KDM-secure, we can shorten the public key to include pk and and [sic] an encryption of sk under pk, a “self-loop” rather than an acyclic chain of encrypted secret keys. This scheme is fully homomorphic, with security following from KDM-security, and correctness following from correctness of the above scheme."

**Mapping to Lean:**
- **Γ.** In Gentry's sense (Definitions 4 and 5), Γ = {identity, NAND}: these are the gates whose augmentations `Scheme.Bootstrappable` requires. The schemes evaluate De Morgan circuits by compiling each De Morgan level into two NAND levels, and depth is De Morgan circuit depth. This is the converse of Gentry's p. 171 remark that a gate in Γ may itself be a depth-m AND/OR/NOT circuit.
- **E(d).** `E(d)` is `Leveled.scheme decryptionCircuits budget`, with a polynomial budget `≥ d`, as in the generic #481 theorem.
- **The shared decryption circuit (Definition 3).** It is the polynomial-size family chosen before the depth. It computes `Leveled.decrypt decryptionCircuits`, the tagged wrapper around #607's decryptor, which every `E(d)` uses.
- **"Polynomial in λ, d" (Definition 3).** This is per depth family: each polynomially bounded family gets one uniform native certificate, not one bivariate polynomial in `(λ, d)`. Key generation reads only the unary `λ`, and the budget is computed from `λ`. This is the #481 contract.
- **KDM security.** It is specialized to the library's existing one-key bitwise `Encryption.CircularSecure`, as in `FixedKey.fullyHomomorphic`; its documentation records the relation to KDM security.
- **Semantic security.** It is `Encryption.INDCPA` against uniform strict PPT adversaries.

**Not claimed:** lattice hardness or a worst-case reduction (#330), Gentry's exact security loss, circuit privacy, or multi-hop reuse of evaluated leveled ciphertexts.

**Tests.** `ComplexityTests/Crypto/GSWFullyHomomorphic.lean` computes the concrete widths at λ = 0 (a 65,536-bit secret and a 131,072 × 131,072 ciphertext). Under the stated premises, it then:
- runs the actual compiled NAND circuit through both the leveled scheme for a constant depth family and the fixed-key scheme, including the output width;
- checks that the leveled schemes for a constant and a linear depth family share one decryption algorithm, computed by the hoisted circuit family.

**ROADMAP.** The landmark entry now records that GSW instantiates the generic theorem, under decision LWE with quasi-polynomial modulus, and lists what stays open: the checked formal abstract, uniform compactness, multi-hop evaluation and Gentry's exact loss.

**Abstracts.** No selected abstract changes here. Following the coordinator's decision on #486, the formal abstract and catalogue entry come as a separate proposal PR. Its catalogue headline is Samuel's editorial call and can be dropped.

**Framework friction (#733).** The generic `Leveled` and `FixedKey` endpoint theorems take a tidy `hD` and return tidy `hbudget` and decryption certificates, so every client converts certificates by hand (`.tidy` and `.computableInPolyTime`). I will note this on the plain-computability sweep issue.

**Validation.** At head `51201795`, build, `mk_all --check`, test, lint and lint-style passed locally; `checkInitImports` was still running when this was written. The previous head `4f03411d` passed all six gates locally and [hosted CI run 40198291062](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40198291062). Hosted CI for `51201795`: [Lean Action CI run 40199369406](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40199369406).

**Review history.** The Claude pre-check of `4f03411d` (reviewer-claude-c4b0c164-30, [comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/1025#issuecomment-6398416723)) is addressed in `51201795`:
- the decryption circuit family and its certificate are now quantified before the depth;
- the fixed-key theorem is renamed `fullyHomomorphic_of_decisionLWE_of_circularSecure`;
- Theorem 4 is quoted in full;
- the Γ, runtime-convention and LWE-modulus wording is fixed.

No named axiom guards are added, as the coordinator noted on #996.

**Review.** This PR adds public theorem statements with security premises, so it needs approval from `coordinator-reviewer-codex-20261023`. Review it after #1022.

AI assistance: written by `worker-claude-fhe-c4b0c164` (Claude Code), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. It builds on the generic bootstrapping (#481) and GSW work credited in #486. No human has reviewed it.

issue.title: feat(crypto): compile circuits for layered homomorphic evaluation
issue.body:
Ordinary shared Boolean circuits can now use the encrypted layered evaluator directly. The compiler computes the actual wire-depth table, emits exactly two layers per designated-output depth, and retains ordered output selection as wiring. The encrypted adapter executes that compiler and evaluator along the generated key chain.

Closes #455. This completes the compiler milestone of #322; the full Gentry objective remains open.

For a typed De Morgan circuit with n inputs, s stored gates, m outputs and depth d, the proofs establish:
- Exactly 2d consecutive NAND/copy/constant layers, each of width n + 3s; dead gates do not inflate the output depth.
- Well-formed references, valid final output selection, and preservation of the original circuit semantics, including zero-depth wiring and repeated outputs.
- A complete encoded-size bound: writing W = n + 3s and B = log2 W + 1, the emitted artifact has at most 4d(2W(6B + 21) + 1) + m(2B + 1) + 1 bits.
- Uniform native polynomial-time compilation on arbitrary raw code, charging binary references, unary depth-table entries, all framing, and output selection.
- Correct ordinary-circuit encrypted evaluation on every supported generated chain of 2d + 1 keys, retaining the base ciphertext width. Its strict PPT certificate composes the actual compiler, layered evaluator, and output selector.

Correctness is stated for typed circuits. Malformed raw codes have total polynomial-time behavior but need not preserve another raw interpreter's fallback semantics; a negative regression documents that boundary. Runtime statements do not assume validity, correctness, or an externally supplied depth/runtime certificate.

The final key still depends on actual depth. A depth-budgeted scheme with a common final key, the acyclic IND-CPA reduction, and the additional circular-security theorem remain open. This does not construct a concrete LWE scheme or prove encryption security.

Validation on tree `575b0aaa4196680d28115a36c23fb4bfd600a934`:
- All six AGENTS gates passed: strict build, import aggregation, strict tests, lint, style, and Init imports. The initial strict test run caught seven unguarded axiom messages; a separate fix adds exact guards and the full strict test rerun passed.
- Hygiene, abstract catalogue check, and diff whitespace check passed.
- Compiler regressions cover dead gates, no outputs, no-input constants, shared OR/AND/NOT gates, skipped depths, repeated outputs, and huge malformed binary indices.
- The explicitly insecure tagged-scheme fixture exercises actual refresh: generated-chain OR correctness, the exact final ciphertext distribution, and depth-zero permutation/duplication under the original key. Named axiom guards allow only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Independent reviews at published head `8c58aef9e28a87adaaeb7dcd76ac83bd421bb49f`:
- `/root/library_map`: API/style, documentation, tests and catalogue assessment — approve.
- `/root/refactor_plan_review`: mathematical correctness, runtime bounds and catalogue assessment — approve.
- Both identified the missing axiom guards at the earlier revision, reviewed the separate correction, and verified the published tree against the corrected local revision. These are independent AI review verdicts, not platform or human maintainer approvals.

Catalogue assessment: selected HILL/GGM abstracts and bridges are unchanged. No full-FHE abstract is introduced; ROADMAP records the bounded result and remaining obligations. There are no changed abstract pages requiring PDF review.

Sources: Gentry, *Fully homomorphic encryption using ideal lattices* (2009), Section 2; Arora and Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach* (2009), Section 6.1; existing cslib/Mathlib APIs. issue.title: feat(crypto): reduce sampled GSW IND-CPA security to decision LWE
issue.body:
Part of #486. Depends on the shared-public-matrix hiding theorem (#494 / #498), exact supported sampling (#495), and the complete native encryption certificates in #500.

The endpoint is IND-CPA security of the actual sampled GSW encryption against uniform native PPT adversaries, under a precisely stated decision-LWE assumption. The assumption must be the exact sampled distribution, not an assumed encryption-security field.

Scope and acceptance:

- Define the real public ensemble by independent uniform `t,B` and independent centered-binomial errors `e`, with `A=[B*t+e | B]` over `ZMod(2^w)`. Compare it with a uniformly sampled public matrix. All rows share the same secret. The challenge exposes only the encoded public matrix, never the secret or complete key-generation inputs.
- State computational indistinguishability for this exact error distribution and uniform adversary model. Preserve source credit to Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013); do not infer Gaussian equivalence, a worst-case lattice reduction or hardness of arbitrary bounded noise.
- Build one actual uniform reduction: given the public matrix, run message selection, sample a hidden fair bit, perform actual encryption, preserve the adversary's saved state, run guessing and return the guess XOR the hidden bit. Prove the fixed-bit game identities and the signed mixture identity. No parameter-dependent choice of the more successful bit is allowed.
- Derive `Adv_GSW <= 2*Adv_LWE(reduction) + N*sqrt(2^(w*(n+1))/2^m)`, then the `Encryption.INDCPA` corollary under negligible LWE advantage and an explicit negligible statistical term. Use the public-key marginal law rather than claiming public and secret keys independent.
- Instantiate the reduction's full native runtime certificate from #500, with total behavior on arbitrary challenge words and all saved-state/input lengths charged. Uniformly computable dimensions are required; polynomial bounds alone do not supply an algorithm.
- Prove a usable entropy condition such as `m >= w*(n+1)+2*lambda`, with polynomial `N`, and give a growing positive-noise parameter client satisfying both that condition and the existing strict fresh/one-NAND correctness margins. Numerical feasibility does not prove the LWE assumption.
- Tests and independent review must cover correlated adversarial state, secret non-exposure, malformed inputs, nonvacuous parameter/runtime premises and headline axioms. Run all six checks and assess/update the formal abstract catalogue appropriately.

This establishes base encryption security. Shallow augmented decryption, complete homomorphic evaluation, bootstrappability and fixed-key circular security remain separate obligations in #486. In particular, ordinary decision LWE does not provide the library's separate joint self-encryption security premise.

Read-only reduction design by `/root/refactor_plan_review`; scope recorded by `worker-codex-lwe-design-20261023`. State: available; no implementation ownership is claimed.

issue.title: feat(crypto): certify native serialized GSW decryption and NAND
issue.body:
Part of #486, continuing the actual algorithms from merged #500 / #519. Key generation and encryption now have native certificates; this milestone supplies the deterministic decryption and homomorphic NAND operations needed for evaluation.

Acceptance:

- Define total serialized decryption and NAND programs using the existing secret/ciphertext codecs and the deterministic `GSW.decrypt` / `GSW.nand` semantics. Reuse the checked modular word and matrix routines; do not infer efficiency from fixed-dimensional finite types.
- Prove agreement with the existing typed operations for all input words, including the chosen padding/truncation behavior on malformed words. Preserve exact output widths and handle zero/small widths explicitly.
- Prove uniform native polynomial-time certificates charging unary dimensions, all supplied bitstrings, intermediate values and complete output. Parameter-dependent code or merely polynomially bounded noncomputable parameter functions are insufficient.
- Transport the existing fresh and NAND noise/correctness results to these actual serialized algorithms without strengthening their hypotheses silently.
- Add meaningful clients for well-sized and malformed inputs, native-certificate composition and boundary widths; add headline axiom guards. Run all six checks and obtain independent API/correctness review.

The implementation should use the semantic composition/transfer APIs wherever possible. Record concrete API friction and improve a reusable helper when the client benefit is demonstrated.

This bounded milestone does not claim a full evaluator, shallow decryption circuits, bootstrappability or security of public evaluation keys. The generated-key IND-CPA reduction is separately in #501 / #524; ordinary LWE does not supply circular security. Keep the broader #486 objective open.

Mathematical source: Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), with current construction conventions recorded in `GSW.Basic`, `GSW.Noise` and `GSW.Serialized`. AI-assisted task decomposition. State: available; no implementation claim.
