issue.title: feat(TFNP): formalize PLS, PPP, PPAD, PPA, inclusions, and circuit problems
issue.body:
## Summary

Implements Milestone 2 of #151:
- **Combinatorial totality principles (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/TFNP/Subclasses/Principles.lean`)**:
  - Defines `zeroVertex` (`0^n`) and proves finite existence and totality (`IsTotalSearch`) on `{0,1}^n` (`List Bool` of length `n`) for:
    - Local optimality (`localOptRel`, `exists_localOpt`, `isTotalSearch_localOptRel`).
    - Pigeonhole (`pigeonRel`, `exists_pigeon`, `isTotalSearch_pigeonRel`).
    - Directed end-of-line (`hasOut`, `hasIn`, `endOfLineRel`, `exists_endOfLine`, `isTotalSearch_endOfLineRel`).
    - Undirected parity / handshake (`undirectedEdge`, `hasOddDegree`, `leafRel`, `exists_leaf`, `isTotalSearch_leafRel`).
  - Proves the reduction soundness lemmas `endOfLineRel_of_pigeonRel` (`PPAD ⊆ PPP` via `ppadToPppMap`) and `endOfLineRel_tail_of_leafRel` (`PPAD ⊆ PPA` via bipartite port doubling `ppadToPpaN₁, ppadToPpaN₂` on `{0,1}^{n+1}`).
- **Uniform subclasses, inclusions, and circuit-presented problems (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/TFNP/Subclasses.lean`)**:
  - Proves polynomial-time computability of `zeroVertex`, `binaryValue` (`encBits → encNat`), and natural-number order `≤` (`encPair encNat encNat → encBool`).
  - Defines `PLS`, `PPP`, `PPAD`, and `PPA` via polynomial-time search reductions to polynomial-time families, proves closure under `SearchReducible` across arbitrary encoded input types, and proves `PLS ⊆ TFNP`, `PPP ⊆ TFNP`, `PPAD ⊆ TFNP`, `PPA ⊆ TFNP`, `PPAD ⊆ PPP`, and `PPAD ⊆ PPA`.
  - Defines `CircuitCode`, `evalCircuitOutputs`, and `evalCircuitCode` on De Morgan circuit codes, proves agreement with `Circuit.eval` (`evalCircuitCode_code`) and polynomial-time computability (`computableTidilyInPolyTime_evalCircuitCode`).
  - Defines the canonical circuit-presented problems `LocalOpt`, `Pigeon`, `EndOfLine`, and `Leaf` with encodings `encLocalOpt`, `encPigeon`, `encEndOfLine`, `encLeaf`, and proves `LocalOpt_mem_PLS`, `Pigeon_mem_PPP`, `EndOfLine_mem_PPAD`, `Leaf_mem_PPA`, their `TFNP` memberships, and `EndOfLine_mem_PPP`, `EndOfLine_mem_PPA`.
- **Tests and documentation**:
  - Extends `ComplexityTests/TFNP.lean` with concrete circuit problem witnesses, reduction examples, and `#print axioms` guards.
  - Updates `references.bib`, `ROADMAP.md`, and `paper/sections/structure.tex`.

### Remaining limitations

issue.title: ci(scripts): advisory check that names in a PR description exist at the head
issue.body:
Closes #1086.

## Change

`scripts/check_pr_names.py` extracts the backticked tokens of a PR description (or any Markdown), keeps those that look like Lean names, and lists the ones the checked-out revision does not declare. It reads source text: `Complexity/`, `ComplexityTests/`, `abstracts/`, `scripts/`, every package under `.lake/packages`, and the toolchain's `Init`/`Std`/`Lean` when `lean` is on the path. Files are preselected with ripgrep when it is installed, otherwise in Python; a run takes 1–5 s on bodies of new names, but 8–45 s when tokens sit in large namespaces such as `Nat.` or when many unresolved names need a base lookup (the follow-up PR brings these under 2 s). Full names come from `namespace` blocks, and a token matches a full name or a dotted suffix of one. Structure fields, constructors, `where` auxiliaries, aliases, generated names (`.mk`, `.ext_iff`, `.eq_1`, …), `to_additive`/`simps` names, module names and `scripts/*.py` names also count. Expressions, paths, numbers, keywords/tactics, all-caps words, single letters, hypothesis names and lowercase words without an underscore are skipped.

Each unresolved name gets a note: *did you mean `X`* (the same last component is declared in this repo under another namespace), *mentioned in N files* (probably a variable or a private name), or *not found in any source file*. A name the repo declared at the base (`--base`, default the merge base with `origin/main`) is marked *removed or renamed here*, because refactoring PRs name what they remove. The script exits 0. `--strict` exits 1 when a reported name was not removed by the change. CLI: `--pr N` (via `gh pr view N --json body`), `--file PATH|-`, `--event PATH`, `--root DIR`, `--github`.

CI: the new step "PR description names (advisory)" runs on `pull_request` after the build, so the package sources are there. It uses the event-payload body, the merge commit, and the merge commit's first parent as base (same base logic as the parallel-definition notice). It has `continue-on-error` and writes to the job summary and a notice. Limitation: the payload body is the one from the latest push, so editing the description does not rerun the step. CONTRIBUTING now asks authors to run `--pr N` before requesting review. The tests (`scripts/test_check_pr_names.py`, hermetic, with and without ripgrep) run in the existing Python test step.

Tooling only: no Lean changes, no public statement changes. This qualifies for review under the delegated-review exception.

## Validation and review

**#1080 at `c69067ba`** (`--root` = a checkout of `pull/1080/head`): 30 names checked, 22 reported, all *not found in any source file*. That includes `nonceSignOracle`, `IsDiffUniversal`, `secureNonceMAC_of_isPRF`, `IsPRF`, `nonceGame_succProbability_le` and `randomNonceGame_succProbability_le*`. `git grep -w` confirms none of the 22 occurs at that head. The 8 names that do exist (`nonceGame`, `randomNonceGame`, `prfPadDistinguisher`, `Nodup`, …) were accepted.

**20 recently merged PRs** (#1036–#1075), each checked at its merge commit with `--base <merge>^`, 471 names in total. 11 bodies are clean. The other reports, apart from names marked *removed or renamed here* by refactors (#1038, #1052, #1056, #1064, #1066, #1073), were:

| PR | reported (not removed) | assessment |
|---|---|---|
| #1067 | `Cslib.Foundations.AffineDisperser.polyOfBits_zipWith_xor` → did you mean `Cslib.AffineDisperser.…` | real slip (wrong namespace) |
| #1073 | `Nat.eventually_pow_lt_two_pow` (not found); `LiuPass.stretchLen_succ_le` → did you mean `Cslib.Crypto.stretchLen_succ_le` | real slip; file-qualified private name |
| #1042 | `IsBipartitePermIndepSet`, `BipartitePermIndepSet`, `encBPIS` | the three slips mentioned in #1086 |
| #1048 | `complexity_subcubeState_le` | real (only `_leaf_le`/`_tree_le` exist) |
| #1056 | `HardnessAmplification.pointOfBits`, `bitsOfPoint_injective` | absent at the merge commit |
| #1036 | `checkCounterGlobal`, `checkCounterStrong` (only in a docstring); `hnonce_len`, `hnonce_inj` | stale docstring names; 2 hypothesis names (false positives) |
| #1057 | `validCert`, `pedersenCommit`, `MCSPAt`, … | names from other PRs, used as calibration examples (expected) |

So the only false positives are the two `hnonce_*` hypothesis names, plus the file-qualified private name, which is arguably imprecise in the description itself. The *removed or renamed* marking accounts for 42 names in the refactors. The *now `X`?* hint after a removed name sometimes points at an unrelated declaration with the same last component; it is phrased as a question.

Commands at the PR head: `python3 -B -m unittest scripts/test_check_pr_names.py` (11 tests OK); `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'` (382 tests). The one error is `test_quick_check.test_ambiguous_base_falls_back`, which fails only because my host has `tag.gpgsign=true` and is unrelated to this change. Also `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp` OK, `lake exe lint-style` OK, workflow YAML parses. No Lean files changed, so the build, test and lint gates are unaffected; CI on this PR runs the new step on this description and will list the example names quoted above, as intended.

## Headline abstracts

- Affected abstracts/catalogue entries, or reason the selection is unaffected: none, tooling only.

## AI assistance

Written and validated by `worker-jetski-d75789e1` (Jetski, Gemini), delegated by `coordinator-jetski-0df14a81`. No human or independent review yet.

issue.title: ci(abstracts): require exact-source Lean success before publication
issue.body:
Abstract PDFs can currently reach the release before Lean CI validates their source commit. This change requires successful **Lean Action CI** for the artifact's exact SHA before any release creation, asset deletion/replacement or release edit. Closes #432.

The gate uses the authoritative workflow-file/ID API, requires this repository's `push` to `main`, selects the latest workflow run and checks its current attempt. It never searches only for green runs. Missing or pending validation can wait up to 20 minutes; failed, cancelled or mismatched evidence denies publication. The run listing and current main are checked again, and each release mutation repeats the gate. Existing artifact provenance, PDF digests, current-main checks and PR review artifacts remain. Only the publication job has release-write permission; its added Actions permission is read-only.

Publication retries download the immutable artifact ID exported by the successful PDF build, so a failed-publish-only rerun does not assume that its new attempt number produced another artifact. No second Lean build is started by the gate.

Validation at exact tree `57aa48eba0aed825d0c9b4cc9a210c54b6a88c27` (public head `4687c9c9c1948b4b6d57d4d9d856b71724ccbf67`, identical to clean private checkpoint `a6bf96e4`):

- All **67 Python tests** pass without skips, including 18 new policy/workflow regressions. They cover wrong SHA/workflow/repository/event/branch, stale green runs/attempts, pagination, unsuccessful conclusions, missing/pending completion/timeout and API errors. The real publication shell, provenance verifier and gate execute against a fake GitHub process boundary; each release mutation is independently blocked when validation is denied.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/abstracts.yml` passes.
- Catalogue selection (12 abstracts/16 headlines), documentation configuration, hygiene and diff checks pass.
- No Lean source or abstract/bridge/catalogue semantic input changes, so no duplicate local six-gate Lean run. Fresh PR CI remains a separate check.

**Abstract impact:** none on selected definitions, statements, bounds, selection or rendered content; this changes release eligibility only. No obsolete paper artifacts are generated or required.

**Limits and review:** GitHub's API checks and release writes are not one atomic transaction. A concurrent main update or rerun can still occur after a check; every subsequent mutation rechecks, but an already-started mutation cannot be rolled back atomically with CI state. Independent exact-revision workflow/security [review by worker_time408](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6354294869) and [coordinator review](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6354337252) approve the exact source/tree with no findings. Main-only publication cannot run in PR CI: the postmerge audit must verify actual Lean-success-before-write ordering, released provenance/source/digests and publication retry behavior. Mocked policy tests and PR artifact generation are not that end-to-end publication claim.

**Sources and AI:** addresses the two codebase reviews supplied by Samuel and recorded in #432. Implementation follows the [workflow-run REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs), [run/attempt semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables), [CLI GET/pagination](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api) and [immutable artifact-ID interface](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/tree/v4). OpenAI Codex worker `worker-codex-abstract-ci432-01a1658b` implemented the workflow, helper, tests and focused documentation. Original renderer/model source credit is unchanged. No author approval or merge is implied.

Integration checkpoint: #437 and #439 are merged; current main `403ea745ab0e866c9f62f18abc2fd46fdddf4f2f` has tree `e775004d563998d437301b9bbdaa1a3f197fd4a7`. Adding this PR produces exact combined tree `5e3be0601e9f02d8caf9e919f7f106641fcf92ee`, already validated with all six strict gates and all 67 Python tests ([combined record](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6354368913)). Fresh Lean CI `39877410074` passed. PDF CI `39877410149` attempt 2 passed after a cancelled-job retry; its original PR-merge source is `daacda1e254f188e9529ff79d2685c7c5a059ff9`. Artifact `12474216457` contains 12 individual PDFs, catalogue and provenance; API/upload logs agree on ZIP digest `91666fd8b4bf065fe21775310b51bfd9ce11acd42d156244235a9d222a11a4ca`. Materializing the connector download is DNS-blocked, so no independent new archive-byte or rendered-page audit is claimed. No source head changes or unresolved source-review findings. Merged as `da9aa17ff255fd172e0788d983491b822bae8da9` under the current coordinator instruction to review/merge PRs; actual main-only publication ordering/provenance remains a separate postmerge audit. See [prior coordinator checkpoint](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6355888246).


Postmerge live audit: [independent audit6361974801](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/pull/438#issuecomment-6361974801) passed on main `19479600b28a6128a641a8063ec9b672f0b8f1cb`. Exact-source Lean run `39931549004` succeeded before the first observed release write; PDF run `39931549058` published 14 assets and the release names that SHA/run. The superseded `50bd9783` attempt waited then denied stale-source publication without writes. This audit checks actual runner ordering and GitHub release metadata/digests; it does not claim independent released JSON/PDF/archive-byte inspection or a live retry/create/deletion experiment. Fixture retry coverage and the documented non-atomic API/write limit remain.

issue.title: feat(tree-eval): prove O(log n * log log n) input-size space bound for Cook-Mertz Tree Evaluation
issue.body:
## Scope

Prove the input-size space corollary from `ROADMAP.md` (Machine-class milestones, line 466):
- In `Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Encoding.lean`:
  - Prove lower bounds on `bodyLength ℓ H` and `(T : Tree ℓ h).encode.length`:
    - `two_pow_mul_le_bodyLength (ℓ H : ℕ) : 2 ^ H * ℓ ≤ bodyLength ℓ H`
    - `tableLength_le_bodyLength_of_pos {ℓ H : ℕ} (hH : 1 ≤ H) : tableLength ℓ ≤ bodyLength ℓ H`
    - `two_pow_le_tableLength {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) : 2 ^ ℓ ≤ tableLength ℓ`
    - `two_pow_ell_le_bodyLength {ℓ H : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) (hH : 1 ≤ H) : 2 ^ ℓ ≤ bodyLength ℓ H`
    - `two_pow_height_le_bodyLength {ℓ H : ℕ} (hℓ : 1 ≤ ℓ) : 2 ^ H ≤ bodyLength ℓ H`
    - `@[simp] theorem Tree.length_encode (T : Tree ℓ h) : T.encode.length = ℓ + h + 2 + bodyLength ℓ h`
- In `Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Instance.lean`:
  - Prove `length_encInstance`, `ell_lt_length_encNat_length_encInstance {I : Instance} (hH : 1 ≤ I.height) : I.ell < (encNat (encInstance I).length).length`, and `height_lt_length_encNat_length_encInstance {I : Instance} (hℓ : 1 ≤ I.ell) : I.height < (encNat (encInstance I).length).length`.
- In `Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/Space.lean`:
  - Prove `spaceBound_add_length_le_log_mul_log_log` for instances satisfying `1 ≤ I.ell` and `1 ≤ I.height` (or more generally `I.ell = 0 ↔ I.height = 0`), bounding `spaceBound I.ell I.height + (encNat ((encInstance I).length + 1)).length` by `O((encNat (encInstance I).length).length * (encNat (encNat (encInstance I).length).length).length)`.
  - Deduce the Cook–Mertz input-size space corollary `computableTidilyInSpace_eval_log_mul_log_log` on nontrivial instances `{I : Instance // 1 ≤ I.ell ∧ 1 ≤ I.height}` (under `encNontrivialInstance := encInstance.comp (Function.Embedding.subtype _)`): Tree Evaluation on instances with positive value length and height is tidily computable in space (\log n \cdot \log \log n)$ in the encoded instance length $.
- Add tests and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/TreeEval.lean`, and update `ROADMAP.md` and `paper/sections/space.tex` (§3.12).

## Completion Criteria

- Independent cslib-style API review, mathematical correctness review, and theorem-index review.

issue.title: ci(scripts): advisory parallel-definition notice; PR template asks for existing notions considered
issue.body:
Samuel approved this guardrail on 2026-10-25. Parallel definitions keep reaching review: the same notion defined again for another carrier, or a copied verifier or game. Recent cases are a third MCSP certificate verifier (#1034), a hiding adversary and games beside `CommitmentReceiver` (#1043), `MCSPAt` as a second name for `GapMCSP.yesSet` (#1048) and the F7 error predicates (#1038). Review caught each of them, but every catch cost a round trip. This PR asks for the reuse argument in the PR description and adds an advisory CI notice that points at candidates. It changes tooling and documentation only; no Lean library file changes.

## Change

Three parts:

1. **PR template** (`.github/pull_request_template.md`). Under "Change", a prompt: for each new public `def`, `structure`, `class`, `abbrev` or `inductive`, list the existing notions considered and why none could be used, extended or generalized (e.g. a language is `PromiseProblem.ofSet A`). An `- Existing notions considered:` line follows it.
2. **AGENTS.md** ("New statements and definitions"). One sentence after "Reuse existing definitions…": a PR that adds a public definition states in its description the existing notions it considered and why none could be reused or generalized, and reviewers treat a definition whose body matches an existing one up to its carrier or argument types as a finding.
3. **Advisory CI notice.**
   - **`scripts/ParallelDefs.lean`**, run with `lake env lean --run`, turns the #884 item-9 survey script into a repository tool. It reads the built `.olean` files without importing them.
     - Anonymization erases variables, universe levels, binder names, the types of `fun` and `let` binders, and metadata. An inductive type's body is its constructors' types, with the type itself replaced by a placeholder.
     - For each examined declaration, it finds the largest subterm shared with another library definition or inductive type, ignoring subterms that more than 4 declarations contain (common plumbing).
     - Pairs where one body mentions the other are skipped, since a wrapper or specialization is what reuse looks like.
     - It also reports definitions that are just another library definition applied to their arguments (a second name).
     - Instances, structure projections, deprecated declarations and generated declarations are left out.
     - Changes from the survey script: traversal is memoized by pointer, so shared terms no longer blow up as trees. Only the examined declarations are tabulated, and the rest of the library is streamed against them. Private counterparts are included, and aliases are reported.
   - **`scripts/parallel_defs.py`** is the wrapper.
     - It examines the public declarations of the `Complexity/` files changed since the merge base whose code contains an added or modified line. "Code" runs from the declared name to the end, so an edit to a docstring alone does not count. It then runs the reader against the whole built library.
     - It keeps cross-module aliases, and cross-module pairs that reach a tier: at least 200 nodes and 30% of the smaller body, or at least 120 nodes and 60% of it (a near copy). Same-module candidates are left out by default (`--same-module` keeps them).
     - Findings go to the job summary as markdown, plus up to 10 `::notice` annotations on the examined declarations.
     - `--decl NAME` examines named declarations, for audits.
     - It always exits 0. It skips itself with a note when build outputs are missing or stale, or when the reader fails.
   - **`.github/workflows/lean_action_ci.yml`** gets a new step, "Parallel-definition notice (advisory)", after "Changed-file lints". It runs on `pull_request` only, with `continue-on-error: true` and `timeout-minutes: 10`. It also runs the compiled-fixture tests, which need Lean; the Python tests at the start of the job skip them, as they do for `test_check_tidy_surface.py`. On hosted CI the step takes about 11 s, tests included.
   - **`scripts/test_parallel_defs.py`** covers:
     - hunk parsing and the changed-line requests, on a scratch repository;
     - tier and same-module selection;
     - reports and annotation escaping;
     - the driver's advisory exits;
     - a compiled fixture module, with a promise-style copy of a predicate, a copied structure, a wrapper that mentions the original and an alias. It also contains a private definition, an instance and a deprecated definition, which are not examined.
   - **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** gets two lines next to the changed-file lints.
   - `check_changed_files.comparison_base` is factored out of `changed_files`, so that both tools use the same base.

- Existing notions considered: `scripts/audit_queries.py duplicates`, through `scripts/LeanOutputs.lean`, finds only alpha-equivalent statements and bodies, so it misses carrier-changed copies such as F7. The near-duplicate pass needs an anonymizing reader and a changed-lines mode. It is therefore a separate reader beside `LeanOutputs.lean` (same `.olean` reading pattern), and it reuses `check_changed_files.changed_files`. No Lean definition is added.

## Calibration

Settings: the default tiers, up to 4 sharing declarations, cross-module only. Each commit was built and compared with its parent, or with its merge base for open-PR heads.

**Known cases**

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| #884 F7 on `main` (`--decl`) | `DecidesWithBoundedError` / `PromiseProblem.SolvesWithBoundedError`: 549 nodes, 48% of the smaller body. The one-sided pair: 525 nodes, 77%. Both flagged. |
| #1048 head `45f21b55` | 1 candidate among 21 examined: `MCSPAt` is `GapMCSP.yesSet` applied to its arguments. The partial verifier pieces `validCert`/`evalCert` are not flagged. |

issue.title: ci: cancel superseded PR runs and restore from the remote build cache
issue.body:
Closes #574.

Lean CI now cancels a pull request's superseded run, and before building it downloads from the remote cache the outputs that `main` CI already built, so a run whose GitHub Actions copy of `.lake` is stale or evicted no longer recompiles them. This is infrastructure only; no Lean source changes.

**Concurrency.** Pull-request runs share the group `lean-ci-pr-<number>` and cancel the run they supersede. Every other run (`main` pushes, merge-queue groups, manual runs) is alone in `lean-ci-<run_id>`, so none of them is cancelled, or replaced while pending as a shared group would do even without `cancel-in-progress`. The `ci-checks` job name is unchanged.

**Remote restore.** lean-action has no hook between installing the toolchain and building, so it now only installs elan and fetches Mathlib's cache (`build`, `test`, `lint` and `use-github-cache` set to false; its own cache restore, build, test, lint and cache save are skipped in the logs). The workflow restores and saves `.lake` itself with lean-action's key, path and save condition (`actions/cache` pinned to the SHA lean-action uses), and runs `lake build`, `lake test` and `lake lint` with the same arguments. The save still runs only after the build succeeds, so an incomplete `.lake` is never saved. Between the two, the new `scripts/cache/get-missing.sh`:

- deepens the depth-1 checkout to 100 generations, since Lake's lookup walks the first 100 commits of `git rev-list HEAD`;
- finds the nearest uploaded revision, as `lake cache get` does;
- drops mapping entries whose input hash already matches a trace in `.lake/build`;
- downloads the rest with `lake cache get <mapping> --repo=cslib-community/complexitylib`.

A miss, a timeout (10 minutes) or an unreachable bucket only leaves the build colder (`continue-on-error`). The filter matters because Lake consults its artifact cache before `.lake` traces, and that cache starts empty on every runner. A plain `lake cache get` would therefore download a complete set (about 75 MB) on every run. At 150–200 runs a day that comes to about 11 GB a day, several times the 100 GB-a-month free egress tier, and it would hit the 10 USD budget whose kill switch makes the bucket private.

**Evidence.** All runs below use this PR's workflow. The `exp/574-*` runs are `workflow_dispatch` runs on throwaway branches. Each differs from the PR only by the toggles shown, and none saves to the Actions cache. Times are `ci-checks` job durations.

| Scenario | Run | `.lake` from the Actions cache | Remote cache | Compiled (build + test) | Restored from remote | Job |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Actions cache miss, remote on | [40034514591](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034514591) | none (forced miss) | 2,354 artifacts, ~75 MB in 3.5 s | no Complexity modules (74 cslib modules, plus native code for lint tools) | 2,354 | **4.7 min** |
| Actions cache miss, remote off | [40034532326](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034532326) | none (forced miss) | disabled | all 2,354 library, abstract and test modules (plus the same cslib and tooling) | 0 | **47.4 min** |
| Stale `.lake`, remote on (×2) | [40034509040](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034509040), [40034511703](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034511703) | `fd5c03e5`, 477 modules behind | 477 artifacts, 12.5 MB | 0 | 477 | **3.0, 3.8 min** |
| Stale `.lake`, remote off | [40034506321](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40034506321) | `fd5c03e5`, same | disabled | 477 | 0 | **13.3 min** |
| This PR, current `.lake` | [40033986765](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033986765) | `0a3b3f66` | 0 missing, nothing downloaded | 6 tooling jobs | 0 | 4.1 min |
| This PR, `main` ahead of its uploads | [40035759067](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40035759067) | `fd5c03e5` | newest upload `fd5c03e5`, 0 missing | 428 | 0 | 13.6 min |

The stale pair builds `a029f89c`'s sources (an uploaded `main` commit) against the newest `main` copy of `.lake`; in recent PR runs a stale copy recompiled 250–480 modules, taking 11–20 minutes. The four controlled runs were dispatched together; the stale ones restored the same Actions cache entry. Toggles: forced miss = cache key prefix `lake-exp574-`; remote off = `COMPLEXITYLIB_CACHE_URL: ""` on the restore step; no save = `if: false` on the save step (e.g. [e9ba42ff](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/commit/e9ba42ff), the forced-miss run with remote on). For reference, recent PR runs under the old workflow took 11–15 minutes (#563 11m10s, #559 11m41s, #497 14m38s), and cold ones 31–47 minutes (40025177553, 40024674388, 40017135006).

Concurrency on real runs: this PR's [40033955224](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033955224) was cancelled by [40033986765](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40033986765) ("Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for lean-ci-pr-582 exists"). The two dispatch runs on `exp/574-stale-rem` above ran at the same time and both succeeded. `actionlint` 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0 passes on the workflow, and shellcheck passes on the script.

**Trust.** CI now reuses outputs that `main` CI produced, so a restored module is not re-checked by the kernel in that run. `scripts/cache/README.md` explains why this adds no party to trust. The Actions cache CI already restores holds copies saved by runs on `main`, a superset of the remote cache's writers, and Lake reuses them in the same way. The README also says what still compiles: every module whose input hash differs from what `main` built, which covers everything a PR changes and every module that imports it. It also corrects the writer description: Workload Identity Federation admits any push run on `main` that requests an OIDC token, not one named workflow, and today only Lean CI requests one.

**Limitations.**
- The remote cache helps only up to the newest commit that `main` CI has finished uploading. During a burst of merges, PR runs still compile the gap, as in 40035759067. `main` runs now restore too, which shortens that lag.
- PR and merge-queue runs still save 2.8 GB `.lake` copies to the Actions cache, unchanged from before. With five entries filling a 13.9 GB cache, they evict `main`'s copies within minutes. Saving only on `main` may now be better; that is left as a follow-up.
- `get-missing.sh` reads Lake's trace (`depHash`) and mapping formats. If they change, the filter keeps every entry and CI downloads a complete set, which stays correct but costs more egress. Like `get.sh`, it passes endpoints by environment variable, which Lake reports as deprecated.
- cslib has no prebuilt cache, so a run without a `.lake` copy still compiles cslib's 74 modules (within the 1.7-minute build step of 40034514591).
- Lake replays no warnings for restored modules. This loses nothing for `--wfail`, because `main` uploads only outputs that passed `--wfail` (see the README).
- The `exp/574-*` branches can be deleted once this is reviewed.

**Abstracts.** No impact: workflow, cache script and documentation only; no Lean statement, definition or catalogue entry changes.

issue.title: Frontier track: Williams' TIME[t] ⊆ SPACE[√(t log t)] via Tree Evaluation
issue.body:
**Status: `available`.** M0 can be claimed now.

## Target
R. Williams, *Simulating Time With Square-Root Space* (STOC 2025): every multitape Turing machine
running in time t(n) ≥ n can be simulated in space O(√(t(n) log t(n))). This is the first major
improvement over Hopcroft–Paul–Valiant (1977) in about 50 years. Include the paper's time–space
corollaries for linear space as stated there; verify the exact form.

## What's already here
- **Cook–Mertz Tree Evaluation**, Williams' key ingredient: `Complexity/Computability/TreeEval/`
  (`CookMertz.lean`, `Iterative.lean`, `Instance.lean`, `Encoding.lean`), by Christian Reitwiessner
  and others. M0 must check its space bound and its machine-level status against what Williams
  needs.
- **Multi-tape machines, space measures, and the space and time hierarchy theorems:**
  `Classes/Hierarchy/{Time,Space}.lean`.

## Milestones
- **M0, design.** Fix the statement for the library's native multitape machines (time and space
  conventions), and say exactly how Cook–Mertz is consumed.
- **M1, block-respecting simulation.** Turn a time-t machine into a block-respecting one with block
  length b, at constant overhead [Hopcroft–Paul–Valiant 1977].
- **M2, encoding.** Encode the block computation graph as a Tree Evaluation instance of height
  about t/b and the matching alphabet. Prove correctness.
- **M3, the theorem.** Apply Cook–Mertz with space accounting, choosing b = √(t log t), to get
  TIME[t] ⊆ SPACE[√(t log t)].
- **M4, corollaries and abstract.** The paper's time–space separation corollaries, plus a headline
  abstract.

## Rules for every track
These follow the frontier program umbrella issue and AGENTS.md.
- **M0 is a short design milestone,** posted as a comment here before any Lean. It pins the exact
  theorem statements, with exact citations (paper, theorem or lemma number), the models and
  encodings, and the open decisions for Samuel. Later milestones follow the design.
- **Faithfulness.** Everything is faithful to the literature, or equivalent in a clear or proven
  way. Label original lemmas. Never state more than is proved.
- **Plain-first (#456, #862).** No tidy computability in statements or proofs outside the Machines
  kernel. Lower the tidy baseline if counts move.
- **PRs.** One reviewable PR (≤ about 40 files) per milestone, with nonvacuous tests and `#print
  axioms` guards. Headline results get a curated abstract under the AGENTS.md rules.
- **Claims.** Claim a milestone with an `active` status comment before starting. Nothing is locked;
  rebase onto whatever lands first.

issue.title: Canonical encodings and encoding independence for the algorithmic framework
issue.body:
Posted by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023` (Claude) at Samuel's direction. **Priority: medium**, after #739.

Encodings are a constant tax on the algorithmic framework:
- every efficiency statement carries `encIn`/`encOut`;
- the Foundations audit (#614) found seven forms of "bits read as a number";
- there are unary/binary choices, framed lists and `Decoder` structures.

Explicit encodings stay right for headline statements, where faithfulness matters, and for model-specific bounds.

**Proposal:**
1. **One canonical encoding per type.** A default for library lemmas, which an explicit encoding can always override.
2. **Encoding independence once.** Extend `EncodingEquiv` so that polynomial-time computability is proved invariant across polynomially equivalent encodings.
3. **Fewer competing representations.** Consolidate them, starting with bits read as numbers: one canonical form, with the others as bridges.

**Design first.** The change touches statements library-wide. Post a design here and get both coordinators' agreement before any sweep, and sequence it after the plain-first sweep (#456), not alongside it.

issue.title: feat(complexity): prove Kadin's polynomial-hierarchy collapse theorem (#683)
issue.body:
Closes #683.

### Mathematical Progress
Proves **Kadin's polynomial-hierarchy collapse theorem** ([Kadin 1988]) in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/BooleanHierarchy/Kadin.lean`: if the Boolean hierarchy over `NP` collapses at any finite level `k` (`coBH k ⊆ BH k`, or equivalently `BH (k + 1) = BH k`), then the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its third level (`PH = Σ₃ᴾ = Σ₃ᴾ ∩ Π₃ᴾ`).

- **Canonical alternating tuple chain (`kadinChain`) and word-block conjunction (`allWordsIn`):**
  - Represents an `r`-tuple of words of length `m(|enc a|)` as a concatenated bit string `s` of length `(r • m)(|enc a|)` paired with `a` under `encPair enc encBits`, proving `kadinChain_mem_BH : kadinChain enc m E r ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) r` and `allWordsIn_mem_NP : allWordsIn enc m E d ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)` for any `E ∈ NP (encPair enc encBits)`.
- **Level-3 collapse at a fixed instance encoding:**
  - `PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`: `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k → PiP 3 enc ⊆ SigmaP 3 enc`, proved by downward induction along the nested difference representation of `(kadinChain enc m E k)ᶜ ∈ BH (encPair enc encBits) k` using Kadin's hard/easy prefix dichotomy.
  - `SigmaP_three_eq_PiP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`: `coBH (encPair enc encBits) k ⊆ BH (encPair enc encBits) k → SigmaP 3 enc = PiP 3 enc`.
  - `PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coDP_subset_DP` and `SigmaP_three_eq_PiP_three_of_coDP_subset_DP`: the `k = 2` (`DP`) specializations.
- **Full polynomial-hierarchy collapses:**
  - `PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`, `PH_eq_SigmaP_three_inter_PiP_three_of_coBH_subset_BH`, and `PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_BH_succ_eq`.
  - `PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coDP_subset_DP` and `PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_DP_eq_coDP`.
  - `DPComplete.coDP_subset_DP_of_mem_coDP`, `DPComplete.DP_eq_coDP_of_mem_coDP`, `DPComplete.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_mem_coDP`, and `PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_SATUNSAT_mem_coDP : SATUNSAT ∈ coDP (encPair encCNF encCNF) → PH enc = SigmaP 3 enc`.

### Validation & Abstract Assessment
- Validated with `lake build Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.BooleanHierarchy.Kadin ComplexityTests.Kadin --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe runLinter Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.BooleanHierarchy.Kadin`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `python3 -B scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`, and `python3 scripts/build_abstracts.py --check`.
- **Headline abstract assessment:** No existing selected abstract in `abstracts/catalogue.json` is affected; `ROADMAP.md` is updated to record Kadin's theorem.

Authored by `worker-jetski-5950b838` (Gemini) with independent pre-PR review by subagent `reviewer-jetski-kadin-683` (`cff89489-614c-46bd-b538-fd1ac18cdd3a`).

issue.title: feat(Algorithms/WordRAM): Dijkstra's algorithm in O((m + 1) log n) time with a formal abstract
issue.body:
## Change

**Depends on** #1091 (`refactor(Computability/WordRAM): scope the word-RAM statement syntax and
ram_eval`, one commit, 7c68492f). This branch has that commit as its parent; until #1091 merges,
the diff here includes it.

This PR adds Dijkstra's algorithm with a binary heap on the word RAM, and a formal abstract for it.
Upstream has no issue about Dijkstra's algorithm (`gh issue list --search Dijkstra --state all`
finds none). This draft proposes the development.

**Result.** `Cslib.Algorithms.WordRAM.Dijkstra.logLinearStatement : LogLinearStatement`
(`Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/Dijkstra/LogLinear.lean`): there are a word-RAM program over the
exact basis, with a fixed number of registers, and a constant `K` such that the following holds.
For every directed graph with `n` vertices, `m` edges and natural-number weights (parallel edges
and self-loops allowed), given by adjacency lists with offsets, and every word size `w` with
`8 (n + m + 2) (W + 2) < 2 ^ w` (`W` the largest weight), the program halts after at most
`K (m + 1) (⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)` instructions. It then holds the encoded distance from the source to
each vertex `v` at `outAddr v` (`0` for unreachable, `d + 1` for distance `d`). The proof gives
`K = 230` with 27 registers. One program works for every word size.

**Source and mapping.** Dijkstra (1959), *Numerische Mathematik* 1, p. 270, states the problem:
"Problem 2. Find the path of minimum total length between two given nodes P and Q." It also says:
"In the solution presented, the minimal paths from P to the other nodes are constructed in order of
increasing length until Q is reached." Remark 1 on the same page: "The above
process can also be applied in the case where the length of a branch depends on the direction in
which it is traversed." (Quoted from the scan at
https://courses.cs.cornell.edu/cs2110/2017sp/online/shortestPath/1959dijkstra.pdf.) The bound is
in Jeff Erickson, *Algorithms*, 1st ed. (June 2019), Chapter 8 "Shortest Paths", Section 8.6
"Best-First: Dijkstra's Algorithm", subsection "No Negative Edges", p. 288 (free from the author at
https://jeffe.cs.illinois.edu/teaching/algorithms/; quoted from
https://jeffe.cs.illinois.edu/teaching/algorithms/book/08-sssp.pdf): "Altogether Dijkstra
performs at most E DecreaseKey operations, and at most V Insert and ExtractMin operations. Thus,
if we implement the underlying priority queue using a standard binary heap, which supports each
operation in O(log V) time, Dijkstra runs in O(E log V) time." (The procedure names are set in
small capitals there.) There `G = (V, E, w)` is "a weighted directed graph" (p. 273). The bound
is also in Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, *Introduction to Algorithms*, 3rd ed. (2009),
Section 24.3 (`CLRS2009`), which we could not open.

How the Lean statement maps the source:
- `V` is `n` (the vertices are `Fin n`). `E` is `m`, the total length of the adjacency lists, so
  parallel edges count separately.
- `log V` becomes `Nat.log 2 n + 1`, that is `⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1`. The `+ 1` keeps the factor positive
  for `n ≤ 1`.
- Weights are natural numbers, so they are nonnegative, as the subsection with the bound assumes
  ("No Negative Edges"). Edges are directed, as in Erickson's `G` and Dijkstra's Remark 1.
- The input is the adjacency-list representation, encoded as words: `n`, the source, the `n + 1`
  offsets of the lists in an edge array, then each edge as target and weight (`encode`).
- The model is the word RAM over the exact basis with `w`-bit words. One instruction is one step,
  whatever its operands. The bound counts every instruction executed, the final `halt` included.
- Quantifiers: one program `p` with `r` registers and one constant `K`, then all `n`, graphs,
  sources and word sizes that satisfy the word-size condition.
- Output: the distance from the source to every vertex, one memory cell per vertex past the
  input (`outAddr`). An unreachable vertex (distance `⊤`) is encoded as `0`, and distance `d` as
  `d + 1`.

The bound `(m + 1) (⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1)` has no `n` term and assumes no reachability. Erickson's
`O(E log V)` has no `V` term either, but his initialization `InitSSSP` (Section 8.3, p. 276) sets
`dist(v) ← ∞` "for all vertices v ≠ s". Here memory past the input starts at `0`, so the
per-vertex arrays need no initialization, and the offsets give the adjacency list of any vertex
directly. So the program touches only the vertices it reaches
(`Dijkstra/HeapStatement.lean:19-21`). The `m + 1` keeps the bound positive for `m = 0`. This
accounting, with no initialization pass and an explicit constant, is ours, not the sources'.
Dijkstra (p. 269) restricts to graphs "where at least one path exists between any two nodes"; the
theorem does not.

**Machine.** The program is a `Program .exact r`: every operation computes its exact value, and an
instruction faults on `x - y` with `y > x`, on `/` and `%` by zero, and on a value that is not a
word. The algorithm is written as structured `Code` and compiled with `Code.program`. The
instruction bound is proved for the structured code with `ExecWithin`: rules for sequences,
branches and loops (with `ExecWithin.loop_potential` for the main loop), and symbolic interpretation
(`ram_exact_eval`, through `ExecWithin.of_eval`) for individual loop-free blocks. `Exec.runs` then
transfers the run and its step count to the compiled program. The only change to an existing
library implementation module is `ExecWithin.loop_potential` in
`Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Structured.lean`. It is a loop rule with a potential function
that bounds the total cost of all iterations. The aggregators (`Complexity.lean`,
`abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts.lean`) and `references.bib` also change.

Files under `Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/Dijkstra/`:
- `Statement`: the problem (`Instance`, `dist`, `maxWeight`, `encodeDist`).
- `HeapStatement`, `ListEncode`: the adjacency-list input layout, `LogLinearSpec` and
  `LogLinearStatement`.
- `Invariant`: Dijkstra's invariant on the abstract distances.
- `ExactNotation`, `HeapProgram`: scoped syntax for exact-basis structured code, and the program.
- `BinaryHeap`, `HeapSift`, `HeapRelax`: correctness and cost of the heap and the relax step.
- `LogLinear`: the main theorem.

**Abstract.** `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/DijkstraAbstract.lean` states `dijkstra_logLinear`
with its own graph, distance, input and output layout, word-size condition and machine. Apart from
`Runs`, its machine definitions are those of `WordRAMAbstract`. `#check_abstract` passes with no
allowlist (218 root declarations, 229 dependencies). `DijkstraBridge.lean` proves that the
abstract's distance is the library's and that the abstract's machine runs as `Cslib.WordRAM` over
the exact basis. It then applies `logLinearStatement`.

**Syntax in the bridge's imports.** The bridge imports `LogLinear`, whose imports include
`ExactNotation` and `Computability/WordRAM/Notation`. These declare the syntax the programs are
written in. With the scoping commit, all their syntax rules, `macro_rules` and tactics are
`scoped`: `Notation`'s to `Cslib.WordRAM`, and `ExactNotation`'s (`ram_exact[`,
`ram_exact_block%`, `ram_exact_stmt%`, `ram_exact_eval`) to `Cslib.Algorithms.WordRAM.Dijkstra`.
Only the syntax category `wramStmt` and the syntax abbreviation `wramBlock` stay global, because
Lean has no `scoped` form for them. Outside those namespaces `wramStmt` has no rules, so they parse
nothing. `DijkstraAbstract.lean` opens neither namespace. A scan of the bridge's import closure
finds no other global syntax, `macro_rules`, elaborator or unification hint from these files.

**Tests.** `ComplexityTests/WordRAMDijkstra.lean` (in the test library's glob) checks:
- a three-vertex graph with a parallel edge and a shorter two-edge path: its input encoding and
  the word-size condition at `w = 10`;
- `logLinearSpec` applied to that graph: the run halts within `230 · 5 · 2` steps and the source's
  output cell holds `1`;
- the interpreter on that graph: it finds the outputs `[1, 4, 2]` (distances `0, 3, 1`) within the
  cost bound of `heapDijkstra_spec` (`decide +kernel`);
- the interpreter on a graph with two vertices and no edges: it finds `[1, 0]` (vertex `1`
  unreachable) within the bound `200 · 1 · 2 + 27` of `heapDijkstra_spec` (`decide +kernel`).
There are no named axiom guards: the global audit `ComplexityTests/Axioms.lean` covers these
declarations, as for the guards removed in #1004.

**Not in this PR (follow-ups).**
- The quadratic version (adjacency-matrix input, `O(n²)` time) and its files.
- Moving `ExactNotation`, `appendCode` and `execWithin_append` to `Computability/WordRAM`.
- Narrowing the `@[expose] public section` in `LogLinear`.
- Splitting `HeapSift` (862 lines).
- A ROADMAP note.

- Existing notions considered (upstream/main a512b10b; CSLib 6ff325e and Mathlib 625d8914, as
  pinned in `lake-manifest.json`):
  - Problem and distance (`Instance`, `Instance.Vertex`, `Instance.arrowWeight`, `Instance.dist`,
    `Instance.maxWeight`, `encodeDist`): Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.dist`
    (`Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Metric.lean:206`) is the length of a shortest walk in an
    undirected graph without weights, and `Quiver.shortestPath`
    (`Mathlib/Combinatorics/Quiver/Arborescence.lean:105`) minimizes the number of arrows.
    Upstream has no weighted graph or shortest-path distance: `Cslib.InductiveCounting.Graph`
    (`Complexity/Algorithms/Reachability/InductiveCounting/Semantics.lean:48`) is an unweighted
    `Bool` edge relation, the `Graph` of `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Problems/Graph.lean:91`
    is an unweighted edge list, and `Complexity/Foundations/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Metric.lean`
    extends Mathlib's unweighted graph metric API. Mathlib's `Digraph`
    (`Mathlib/Combinatorics/Digraph/Basic.lean:48`) is an unweighted relation without parallel
    edges. CSLib has none either. So `dist` reuses Mathlib's `Quiver.Path` and
    `Quiver.Path.addWeight` (`Mathlib/Combinatorics/Quiver/Path/Weight.lean:48`) on the quiver
    whose arrows are the edges (`Dijkstra/Statement.lean:67-79`), with no new path type.
    `maxWeight` and `encodeDist` are this problem's size parameter and output convention.
  - Input encoding (`ListInstance` with `lightest`, `toInstance`, `dist`, `m`, `maxWeight`,
    `offset`, `encode`, `outAddr`; `ListInstance.dbase`): the input is a `List ℕ` placed by
    upstream's `State.init`, as for every upstream word-RAM program. Upstream has no adjacency-list
    encoding of a weighted graph; its graph encodings (the adjacency matrix of `USTCONBridge`, the
    edge list above) carry no weights. `toInstance` maps the lists to the weight-matrix
    `Instance`, so the distance is defined once.
  - Invariants and heap predicates (`decodeDist`, `Instance.relax`, `Instance.Inv`, `edgeWord`,
    `edgesWord`, `heapKey`, `HeapShape`, `Ordered`, `UpOrdered`, `DownOrdered`, `HeapInv`, and in
    `LogLinear` `distOf`, `visitedOf`, `remaining`, `potential`, `OuterInv`): invariants of this
    proof. The heap predicates describe three arrays in raw word-RAM memory (`ℕ → ℕ`). Upstream has
    no word-RAM binary heap: `Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Heap.lean` is a footprint and frame
    calculus for memory, `Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/` is a van Emde Boas tree with
    its own layout, and `Queue` and `Stack` are FIFO and LIFO. Batteries' `BinaryHeap`
    (`Batteries/Data/BinaryHeap/Basic.lean:13`) is a max-heap held in a Lean `Array`, not a
    predicate on machine memory. Its `decreaseKey` (`Basic.lean:185`) takes a heap index, and it
    keeps no position array from vertex to index, which Dijkstra's decrease-key needs.
  - Programs and register names (`swapCode`, `siftUpBody`, `siftUp`, `siftDownChoose`,
    `siftDownSink`, `siftDownBody`, `siftDown`, `extractMin`, `pushNew`, `edgeBody`, `relaxEdges`,
    `heapRound`, `heapSetup`, `heapDijkstra`; the 27 `HeapReg` abbrevs): the programs are
    `Code .exact 27` values written in `ram_exact[…]`. The abbrevs name registers as elements of
    `Fin 27`, as upstream's word-RAM programs do (for example
    `Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/PackedCount.lean:46-54` and
    `Complexity/Algorithms/WordRAM/VanEmdeBoas/Program.lean:65-69`).
  - `appendCode`: runs one structured program after another, nesting the `Code.seq` chain to the
    right as `ram[…]` nests it. Upstream has `Code.seq` and the notation, but no function that
    appends two `Code` values. Moving it to `Computability/WordRAM` is a listed follow-up.
  - `LogLinearSpec`, `LogLinearStatement`: the nearest upstream notions are
    `Program.ComputesInTime` (`Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Function.lean:61`), whose program
    returns one word `f a` with `halt`, and `Program.Answers` and `Program.DecidesInTime`
    (`Complexity/Computability/WordRAM/Time.lean:70`, `:196`), which return one bit. The output
    here is `n` memory cells, which neither can state without packing them into one word or running
    once per vertex. The spec is built from upstream's `Runs`, `step`, `Fits` and `State.init`, and
    `LogLinearStatement` quantifies over programs as `UniformComputableInTime` does over
    `Program.ComputesInTime` (`Function.lean:81`).
  - The abstract's restated model (`Graph`, `IsWalk`, `dist`, `numEdges`, `maxWeight`, `offset`,
    `encode`, `outAddr`, `encodeDist`, `AluOp`, `Instr`, `Program`, `State`, `Outcome`, `step`,
    `init`, `Runs`): restated because upstream's abstract rules ask for it. Every public reference
    in an abstract must resolve to the abstract itself, a background library or an allowlisted
    module (`.agents/skills/lean-abstract/SKILL.md:34-39`), and problem definitions stay in each
    abstract, with only `ComplexityAbstracts.Encoding` and `ComplexityAbstracts.Computation`
    shared (`:50`); neither has a word RAM. Apart from `Runs`, the machine definitions are those of
    `WordRAMAbstract`. `DijkstraBridge` proves the correspondence with the library; its helpers
    `WalkLaws`, `walkDist`, `haltsVia` and `stateOf` serve only that proof.
  - Upstream's advisory parallel-definition notice: `scripts/parallel_defs.py` of upstream/main
    a512b10b, run locally on this branch built at 1edeec07, with `--base upstream/main`, reports
    no candidate parallel definitions among the 101 examined declarations. The local run compares
    with the library at this branch's base 0b838c43, not with the merge into upstream/main that CI
    checks.

`git merge-tree --write-tree` against upstream/main 91448407 shows no conflict.

issue.title: feat(abstracts): Immerman–Szelepcsényi headline abstract (#885)
issue.body:
Item 3 of #885. This adds a headline formal abstract for the Immerman–Szelepcsényi theorem `NL = coNL`, with directed non-reachability in `NL` as a supporting corollary.

## Change

New `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/ImmermanSzelepcsenyiAbstract.lean` and `…Bridge.lean`, catalogue entry `immerman-szelepcsenyi`:

- `nl_eq_conl {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : NL enc = coNL enc` (headline).
- `stcon_compl_mem_nl : STCONᶜ ∈ NL encInstance` (supporting).

The abstract states the conventions explicitly:

- **Model.** Each problem has one fixed finite-state binary multi-tape `Turing.MultiTapeNTM` (upstream cslib). Acceptance means some computation path halts with output `[true]`.
- **Space.** Along every computation prefix, rejecting branches included, the machine visits at most `c * (floor(log₂ n) + 1)` work-tape cells (upstream `RunsInSpace`). Read-only input and write-only output are not charged.
- **Termination.** Every branch terminates: on each input some finite time bounds all paths (`RunsInTime`). A stuck branch rejects.
- **Encoding.** `NL = coNL` holds for an arbitrary injective encoding `enc`, and `coNL` uses the same encoding. The corollary uses the explicit adjacency-matrix encoding with unary header `1^n 0 1^s 0 1^t 0`, the same layout as the Reingold abstract, shown in the representation appendix.

`Accepts` and `DecidesInSpace` are copied verbatim from the Savitch abstract, and the bridge proves the public `NL` and `coNL` definitionally equal to the library's `Cslib.Complexity.NL` and `coNL` (`rfl`). The abstract and the new regression tests pin this. `#check_abstract` passes without an allowlist: 15 root declarations and 71 dependencies, all upstream (cslib, Mathlib).

The library proof is Erik Demaine's streaming inductive-counting construction (#465), and the abstract credits it. Directed connectivity's `compl_mem_NL` comes from #887.

Other edits:

- `README.md`: the existing "Immerman–Szelepcsényi" selected-results bullet now links to the abstract rather than the library file.
- `ROADMAP.md`: one clause.
- `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/ImmermanSzelepcsenyiTests.lean`: concrete clients.

  - The single arc `1 → 0` is in `STCONᶜ`, and the path `0 → 1 → 2` is in `STCON`, so the corollary is nonvacuous.

issue.title: feat(ordered): prove native first-order model checking in logspace
issue.body:
Implement native logarithmic-space model checking for each fixed Mathlib first-order sentence over `FO.Ordered.language L`, where the input vocabulary `L` is finite and relational. This is the next bounded child of #30 after #126 / #121.

Endpoint: an actual encoded query language belongs to `Complexity.L encStructure`. Membership requires the existing relation-table shape predicate, cardinality `n >= 2`, and truth of the sentence in the canonical expansion of `v.decode a : L.Structure (Fin n)`. Numeric `0`, `1`, `max`, order and BIT are computed from cardinality/indices; no numeric tables or assumed evaluator occur in the input or theorem hypotheses. The sentence is fixed, including its quantifier depth; this is data complexity, not combined formula/input complexity.

Encoding: retain `EncodedStructure = Nat × List (List Bool)` and `encStructure`, with unary cardinality and framed raw relation tables in the existing `tupleIndex` order. Space is measured in the full binary encoding length `N`; malformed table shapes and sizes zero/one are rejected. No claim about arbitrary raw bit strings outside the image of `encStructure` is implicit in membership at this encoding.

Construction plan for independent review:
- Reuse the proved shape checker and counter/query/native-Turing-machine simulation.
- Factor the existing formula-control/quantifier proof into a shared compiler with explicit atomic handlers, then instantiate it for both the existing order-free API and canonical ordered terms/atoms. Preserve old public names/statements and order-free semantics.
- Compile terms to counter expressions (variables, zero, one, truncated predecessor of cardinality for max); input atoms use existing table addressing and order uses comparison.
- Prove binary BIT evaluation in linear space using existing binary encoding and bounded iteration or bit-list access, then expose only the proved operation to counter expressions. No exponential `2^i` register or unit-cost unbounded arithmetic assumption. Subtraction reuses the existing native `natSub` certificate.
- Use the same polynomial register bound from the shape/assignment compiler; the fixed-expression native simulation charges arithmetic intermediates in binary work space.

Completion criteria: closed native sentence membership theorem; quantified clients mixing input predicates with constants/order/BIT; malformed/zero/one rejection, `n=2`, non-power-of-two sizes, high bit indices, and constants in relation/equality arguments; axioms guards; all six gates; source/API/correctness and theorem-index independent reviews; exact declaration pins and generated CI PDF review.

Source: Immerman, *Descriptive Complexity*, Theorem 3.1 and proof, printed pp.57–59, https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/book/ch3.pdf . Reuse/credit the existing model-checker and Christian Reitwiessner's native arithmetic. The encoding conventions above are the library's explicit framing/cardinality conventions, not a claim of identical textbook bit layout.

Still open after this issue: actual ordered interpretation-to-logspace transducers/reduction closure, standard projections and NL/P/capture endpoints. Arbitrary restricted-domain automatic BIT remains outside scope. The existing #86 unpublished-source exception remains unchanged.

issue.title: feat(abstracts): Partial MCSP ETH hardness formal abstract (#798)
issue.body:
Adds a self-contained formal abstract and proof bridge for Ilango's Exponential Time Hypothesis lower bound on the Partial Minimum Circuit Size Problem (`PartialMCSP` / $\mathrm{MCSP}^*$), completing Candidate Abstract 3 from [#798](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/798) Comment 4 ([Ilango, FOCS 2020, Theorem I.3; ECCC TR20-183, Theorem 3 and Theorem 11][Ilango2020FOCS]).

### Summary of Changes

- **`abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/PartialMCSPAbstract.lean`**:
  - Self-contained presentation of `ThreeSAT`, `numVars`, `DecidableInTimeO`, `DecidableInExpTime`, `DecidableInSubexpTime`, `ETH`, `DeMorganCircuit`, `evalCircuit`, `binaryGateCount`, `tableIndex`, `Instance`, `tableSize`, `AgreesWith`, `PartialMCSP`, `PartialMCSPBinaryGate`, and `NP`, audited by `#check_abstract` with only `[ComplexityAbstracts.Encoding, ComplexityAbstracts.Computation]` allowlisted (zero `Complexity.*` implementation modules allowlisted; `60 root declarations, 180 dependencies checked`).
  - Headline theorems:
    - `ComplexityAbstracts.PartialMCSPAbstract.not_decidableInSubexpTime_partialMCSP`: assuming `ETH`, `PartialMCSP` on $m$-variable partial Boolean functions cannot be decided in time $2^{o(m \log_2 m)}$ under unary threshold encoding `encInstance`.
    - `ComplexityAbstracts.PartialMCSPAbstract.not_decidableInSubexpTime_partialMCSP_tableSize`: assuming `ETH`, `PartialMCSP` on partial truth tables of size $N = 2^m$ cannot be decided in time $2^{o(\log_2 N \log_2 \log_2 N)} = N^{o(\log \log N)}$.
  - Supporting theorems:
    - `ComplexityAbstracts.PartialMCSPAbstract.not_decidableInSubexpTime_partialMCSP_encBinary`: ETH lower bound $2^{o(m \log_2 m)}$ under binary threshold encoding `encInstanceBinary`.
    - `ComplexityAbstracts.PartialMCSPAbstract.not_decidableInSubexpTime_partialMCSPBinaryGate`: ETH lower bound $2^{o(m \log_2 m)}$ under Ilango's binary-gate cost measure `binaryGateCount`.
    - `ComplexityAbstracts.PartialMCSPAbstract.partialMCSP_mem_NP` and `ComplexityAbstracts.PartialMCSPAbstract.partialMCSP_mem_NP_encBinary`: `NP` membership under both unary and binary threshold encodings.
- **`abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/PartialMCSPBridge.lean`**:
  - Connects the abstract's self-contained definitions to `Complexity.Computability.MCSP.PartialETH` and `Complexity.Computability.MCSP.Partial`.
- **`ComplexityTests/Abstracts/PartialMCSPTests.lean`**:
  - Concrete non-vacuity and alignment checks (`ThreeSAT = Cslib.Complexity.ThreeSAT`, `ETH ↔ Cslib.Complexity.ETH`, `sampleFormula`, `allStarInstance`, `notCircuit`, and `negationInstance` separating `PartialMCSP` at threshold $0$ from `PartialMCSPBinaryGate` at threshold $0$).
- **`abstracts/catalogue.json`, `abstracts/README.md`, `README.md`, `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts.lean`**:
  - Registers the `partial-mcsp` entry in the formal abstracts catalogue.

### Faithfulness and scope

> MCSP* cannot be solved in deterministic time N^{o(log log N)} on truth tables of length-N assuming ETH.

Ilango, [ECCC TR20-183](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2020/183/download), Theorem 11, p. 20 (mathematical typography normalized).

The bridge uses the library's formalized Section 3 reduction from `2n × 2n` Bipartite Permutation Independent Set to a `6n`-variable partial truth table with threshold `6n - 1`, together with the LMS ETH lower bound for the source problem. The ETH-to-graph lower-bound chain includes sparsification. The abstract distinguishes all-gates circuit size from binary AND/OR gate count and spells out both threshold encodings. Its subexponential-time convention permits the machine and input-length polynomial degree to depend on the positive exponent; ETH is an explicit open assumption.

### Validation

- `./scripts/check.sh` (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`)

issue.title: feat(counting): characterize UP and FewP by native machines
issue.body:
The verifier-defined UP and FewP classes now have exact native finite-machine characterizations. Both directions reuse the actual parsimonious #P bridge: a bound of one or a polynomial on accepting witness counts becomes the same bound on accepting occurrence traces, with a polynomial all-branches clock.

Closes #131.

- Endpoints: `Cslib.Complexity.mem_UP_iff_exists_machine` and `Cslib.Complexity.mem_FewP_iff_exists_machine`. The fixed tape count, finite control, closed List-choice machine and polynomial clock precede every input; FewP has a separate ambiguity polynomial in encoded input length. Tables are globally nonblocking, while the halting/correctness contract is on the encoding image (`encBits` covers all binary inputs).
- Ambiguity bounds accepting branches only. Rejecting and total branch counts are unrestricted by that bound. Repeated equal transition occurrences count separately; early-halt clock padding introduces no new paths. No new machine semantics, compiler or shared counting helper was needed.
- Actual 0-tape Unit-state clients have 0, 1 or 3 copied possible accepting occurrences plus two always-rejecting occurrences. They prove exact accept/reject counts, nonblocking and one-step all-branches halting for arbitrary inputs, clock padding, a nonconstant language in UP/FewP and the zero ambiguity polynomial. A multiply accepting machine is not a language separation claim. Both headline axiom guards use only the standard allowed axioms.

issue.title: feat(LogSpace): directed s-t connectivity is NL-complete
issue.body:
Item 1 of #885. Directed s–t connectivity is NL-complete under logspace many-one reductions [Sipser, Theorem 8.25], and its complement is in NL, and NL-complete, through `NL_eq_coNL`.

## What is proved

`STCON : Set STCONInstance` holds when there is a directed path from `s` to `t`, the empty path included. This is Sipser's `PATH`. An instance is an adjacency matrix on `Fin n` with two vertices. It is encoded by `encSTCON` as the unary header `1^n 0 1^s 0 1^t 0` followed by the matrix row by row, the same layout as `encUSTCON`. `USTCON` now encodes an instance as its directed graph, so that layout lives in one place.

- `STCON.mem_NL : STCON ∈ NL encSTCON` [Sipser, Example 8.19].
- `STCON.logSpaceReducible_of_mem_NL`, `STCON.logSpaceHard`, and `STCON.logSpaceComplete : LogSpaceComplete NL encSTCON STCON` [Sipser, Theorem 8.25].
- `STCON.compl_mem_NL` and `STCON.compl_logSpaceComplete`, through `NL_eq_coNL`, which rests on Erik Demaine's inductive-counting construction (#465). The second is the form used for 2SAT in item 2.
- `STCON.mem_L_iff_forall_NL_eq_L`: `STCON ∈ L` exactly when `NL = L` for every encoding [Sipser, Corollary 8.24].

The classes are the existing native ones. NL means one finite-state NTM with every-prefix work space `c * (log₂ n + 1)` that halts on every branch. The reductions are deterministic logspace functions (`LogSpaceReducible`).

## How

- **Membership.** `Machines/…/LogSpace/CounterProgram/Nondeterministic.lean` adds *nondeterministic counter programs*: a counter program whose register `0` receives a fresh choice bit after every step. `CounterProgram.exists_decidesInLogSpace` compiles one to a native NTM through `NondeterministicQueryMachine.exists_decidesInSpace`. The hypotheses are halting of every branch, polynomially bounded registers and correct acceptance. A rank and an invariant give the first two (`haltsWithin_of_rank`, `forall_run_of_rank`). `Problems/STCON/Search.lean` is the search: it reads the header, then guesses the next vertex by counting, and gives up after `n` steps. Its invariant records that the current vertex is reachable, which gives soundness. For completeness, a shortest path, with fewer than `n` arcs, is followed.
- **Hardness.** `Problems/STCON/Reduction.lean` maps an instance to the compact configuration graph of the decider (`ConfigurationGraph`), with one extra sink vertex and an arc to it from each accepting halted vertex. `configurationInstance_mem_iff` reduces correctness to the existing `accepts_iff_reachable_bad_of_runsInSpace`. A counter program with output writes the encoded instance; it stores the input length, two vertex identifiers and one symbol code. For that, `CounterProgram/Boolean.lean` and `ConfigurationGraph/Expr.lean` express the local edge test, `bad`, `startID`, `vertexBound` and `queryIndex` as counter-program expressions. Each comes with a lemma giving its value. The program runs on the framed input (`computableInLogSpace_frame`), so its registers stay below `(|input| + 1) ^ d` even on the empty encoding.

## Plain-first note

All new public statements are plain; the tidy ratchet is unchanged at 1301. The only tidy use is in the private compiler glue of `Nondeterministic.lean` (`withChoice_inSpace`, `next_inSpace`, `accept_inSpace`). It feeds `NondeterministicQueryMachine.exists_decidesInSpace`, whose callbacks are `ComputableTidilyInSpace` and which has no plain counterpart. The STCON program and the reduction use no tidy notion: the transducer uses the existing plain `CounterProgram.computableInLogSpace_of_reachesOut`. The missing plain rule is a plain-callback variant of `exists_decidesInSpace`, the Machines conversion of #862 step 5.

## Formal abstracts

No impact on statements. `USTCONBridge` used `USTCONInstance.matrix`, which moved to `STCONInstance.matrix`; I updated its proof. The abstract statement and its encoding are unchanged. `scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` selects 14 abstracts and 19 headline theorems, as before. Item 3 of #885 adds the NL = coNL headline.

## Validation

At 1e44041c: `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates. `check_hygiene.py --check-simp` and `check_tidy_surface.py` (1301, matching the baseline) pass, as does `build_abstracts.py --check`. `ComplexityTests/STCON.lean` exercises concrete instances: `0 → 1 → 2` is in `STCON`, the single arc `1 → 0` does not connect `0` to `1`, and the search accepts the first and rejects the second. It pins the encoding bit by bit, instantiates hardness on `USTCON ∈ L`, and guards the headline theorems with `#print axioms` (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`).

Citations: Sipser, 3rd edition. Example 8.19 (p. 350), Theorem 8.23 (p. 352) and Theorem 8.25 (p. 353) were checked against course notes quoting those page numbers. Corollary 8.24 follows Theorem 8.23 in the same section.

## AI disclosure

Written by `worker-claude-nl-c4b0c164` (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`. Self-reviewed by the author; this is not an independent review.

issue.body:

The plain polynomial-time certificate includes parsing arbitrary words, list/default handling, arithmetic, framing and every output coordinate. issue.title: Kadin's theorem: Boolean Hierarchy collapse implies PH = Σ₃ᴾ
issue.body:
Tracks the Boolean Hierarchy collapse theorem from `ROADMAP.md` (line 508, `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/BooleanHierarchy/Basic.lean`).

## Objective & Scope

Prove **Kadin's Theorem** ([Kadin1988]): if the Boolean Hierarchy collapses at level $k \ge 1$ (`BH (k + 1) encBits = BH k encBits`, or equivalently `BH k encBits = coBH k encBits`), then the Polynomial Hierarchy collapses to $\Sigma_3^{\mathsf{P}}$ (`PH enc = SigmaP 3 enc`, i.e., $\mathsf{PH} = \mathsf{NP}^{\Sigma_2^{\mathsf{P}}}$):

1. **`DP = coDP → PH = Σ₃ᴾ` ($k = 1, 2$) and General `BH_k = coBH_k → PH = Σ₃ᴾ`**:
   * Formalize Kadin's easy/hard case analysis in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/BooleanHierarchy/Kadin.lean`.
   * Use `PH_eq_SigmaP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP` (`Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/PH/Collapse.lean`) to reduce `PH enc = SigmaP 3 enc` to `PiP 3 enc ⊆ SigmaP 3 enc`.
   * Prove both the base levels (`NP = coNP → PH = Σ₃ᴾ`, `DP = coDP → PH = Σ₃ᴾ`) and the general inductive step (`BH k encBits = coBH k encBits → PH enc = SigmaP 3 enc` and `BH (k + 1) encBits = BH k encBits → PH enc = SigmaP 3 enc`).
2. **Tests & Nonvacuity (`ComplexityTests/Kadin.lean`)**:
   * Concrete checks and `#print axioms` guards for the headline collapse theorems.

issue.title: feat(circuit): construct uniform logarithmic-depth binary addition
issue.body:
Adds an actual prefix-doubling De Morgan adder for two unsigned words and carry-in, including the output carry at every width. Its depth is at most `7 + 2*ceil(log₂(w+1))`, with an exact gate count and a polynomial size bound. The modular interface and carry-save finisher have depth at most `8 + 2*ceil(log₂(w+1))`; the checked finishing client preserves the existing 4-to-2 reducer’s modular value and clears its second word.

One native polynomial-time algorithm generates each complete circuit code from unary width, charging binary gate/output references and framing. The generator reuses shared code composition through a fixed-formula template API and bounds its complete intermediate codes. Existing arithmetic APIs remain compatible. Source credit: Ladner–Fischer, [Parallel Prefix Computation](https://doi.org/10.1145/322217.322232), §4; this implementation uses the simple doubling network and its own proved De Morgan constants.

Closes #526. Stacked on #534. This supplies the arithmetic primitive for #528; shallow GSW decryption, bootstrappability, and stronger uniformity remain open.

All six `scripts/check.sh` gates passed together on tree `92bdb95cf9d37f4a657fdeaa6e8c9f1f2fc84213`, identical to this published head.
