issue.title: feat(circuit): polynomial identity testing, Schwartz-Zippel, and Kabanets-Impagliazzo
issue.body:
Closes #326

## Summary

Formalizes **Polynomial Identity Testing (`PITInt`)**, the **multivariate Schwartz–Zippel lemma** ([Schwartz 1980][Schwartz1980]; [Zippel 1979][Zippel1979]; [DeMillo and Lipton 1978][DeMilloLipton1978]), **Laplace cofactor expansion and downward self-reducibility of the permanent to `PITInt`** ([Kabanets and Impagliazzo 2004, Lemma 4.2][KabanetsImpagliazzo2004]), and the **Kabanets–Impagliazzo derandomization-to-lower-bounds dichotomy** ([Kabanets and Impagliazzo 2004, Theorem 4.1][KabanetsImpagliazzo2004]) in `Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Arithmetic/IdentityTesting.lean`.

### Main Definitions & Results
- **Integer Arithmetic Circuit Encoding & `PITInt` (`encArithOpInt`, `encArithGateInt`, `encArithCodeInt`, `encArithCircuitInt`, `PITInt`)**:
  - Injective bit-string encoding of bundled single-output integer arithmetic circuits `(Σ n, Circuit (arithSignature ℤ) n 1)` and the polynomial identity testing language `PITInt := { c | c.2.polynomial 0 = 0 }`.
- **Multivariate Schwartz–Zippel Lemma (`MvPolynomial.card_mul_card_roots_le`, `MvPolynomial.card_roots_le`, `MvPolynomial.exists_eval_ne_zero_of_totalDegree_lt_card`, `card_roots_eval_le_of_notMem_PITInt`, `exists_eval_ne_zero_of_notMem_PITInt`)**:
  - Over any integral domain `R`, a nonzero polynomial $P \in R[\mathrm{Fin}\,n]$ has at most $(\mathrm{totalDegree}\,P) \cdot |S|^{n-1}$ roots on $S^n$, yielding a non-vanishing evaluation point whenever $\mathrm{totalDegree}\,P < |S|$ and bounding the error of randomized `PITInt`.
- **Laplace Permanent Expansion & Downward Self-Reducibility to `PITInt` (`Matrix.permanent_succ_column_zero`, `Matrix.permanent_succ_row_zero`, `permFamily`, `intPermFamily`, `isPFamily_permFamily`, `permanent_genericMatrix_succ`, `permBaseDiff`, `permStepDiff`, `forall_polynomial_eq_permanent_iff_mem_PITInt`, `IsLaplacePermChain`, `laplacePermCircuit`, `PermPITCertified`, `exists_certified_perm_family_of_PITInt_mem_P_of_mem_VP`)**:
  - Proves Laplace cofactor expansion of the permanent over any `CommSemiring R`.
  - Constructs explicit arithmetic difference circuits `permBaseDiff` and `permStepDiff` certifying that a candidate circuit family `C` computes the generic permanent for all $m \le n$ if and only if `⟨0, permBaseDiff (C 0)⟩ ∈ PITInt` and `⟨(m + 1) * (m + 1), permStepDiff m (C m) (C (m + 1))⟩ ∈ PITInt` for all $m < n$ (`forall_polynomial_eq_permanent_iff_mem_PITInt`).
  - Proves that `PITInt ∈ P encArithCircuitInt` and `intPermFamily ∈ VP ℤ` imply `PermPITCertified` (`exists_certified_perm_family_of_PITInt_mem_P_of_mem_VP`).
- **`NEXP` Circuit Lower Bound & Kabanets–Impagliazzo Dichotomy (`SigmaP_subset_EXP`, `SigmaP_subset_NEXP`, `exists_mem_NEXP_notMem_SIZE`, `kabanets_impagliazzo`, `kabanets_impagliazzo_of_EXP_subset_P`)**:
  - Proves unconditionally that for every degree $k$, some language in `NEXP` requires Boolean circuits of size strictly greater than $n^k$ infinitely often (`exists_mem_NEXP_notMem_SIZE`, via Kannan's theorem).
  - Derives the Kabanets–Impagliazzo dichotomy `(∃ L, L ∈ NEXP encBits ∧ L ∉ PPoly) ∨ intPermFamily ∉ VP ℤ` from `PITInt ∈ P encArithCircuitInt` and the collapse step `hCollapse` (`kabanets_impagliazzo` and `kabanets_impagliazzo_of_EXP_subset_P`).

### Scope & Limitations
- `permBaseDiff` and `permStepDiff` are constructed as combinatorial `Circuit (arithSignature ℤ)` values with proved polynomial gate-size bounds (`c₀.size + 4` and `cm1.size + (m + 1) * (cm.size + 2) + 4`), and `kabanets_impagliazzo` / `kabanets_impagliazzo_of_EXP_subset_P` take the collapse implication from `(∀ L ∈ NEXP, L ∈ PPoly) ∧ PermPITCertified` to `NEXP ⊆ SigmaP 2` (or `EXP ⊆ P`) as an explicit hypothesis `hCollapse`. Formalizing the machine-level polynomial-time transducer for `permStepDiff` and discharging `hCollapse` via Nisan–Wigderson easy-witness extraction and Toda/Valiant `#P`-completeness of the permanent remain future work recorded in `ROADMAP.md`.

## Validation
All 6 checks in `./scripts/check.sh` passed cleanly:
- `lake build --wfail --iofail`
- `lake exe mk_all --check`
- `lake test --wfail --iofail`
- `lake lint`
- `lake exe lint-style`
- `lake exe checkInitImports`

## Review Provenance & AI-Assistance Disclosure
- **Authoring agent**: `worker-agy-765830f1` (delegated worker subagent `b9b381a4-f656-47b7-9273-6cc7afaa05ea`, Gemini / Antigravity).
- **Independent cslib-Style & API Review** (`2a309c05-c3b3-45b7-8a19-683a9685b609`):
  - Initial review at `16eb011309e6cb0a60bb41edada63808861865c1`: `APPROVED` (0 blocking issues; suggested generalizing `permFamily R` over `[CommSemiring R]` and turning `PermPITCertified` into a `structure`).
  - Re-review at `9d1b45a56cc40a1454667cd798fcc178196c2774` (Lean commit `860b6595115e5fc139815e34908765c4e044eca9`): `APPROVED`.
- **Independent Correctness & Theorem-Index Review** (`1545138d-90f8-4878-b374-e077ad7d8587`):
  - Initial review at `16eb011309e6cb0a60bb41edada63808861865c1`: `CHANGES REQUESTED` — verified all Lean mathematics, proofs, non-vacuity instances, and `ROADMAP.md`, and requested (1) replacing Unicode `ℤ` with ASCII `Int` in declaration names (`PITInt`, `encArithCircuitInt`, etc.) to avoid UTF-8 mojibake inside `\nolinkurl` under `pdflatex`, and (2) replacing `\decl` with `\declat{<sha>}` in `paper/sections/synthesis.tex`.
  - Resolution: Renamed `ℤ`-suffixed declarations to `Int`, generalized `permFamily R`, converted `PermPITCertified` into a `structure` in `860b6595115e5fc139815e34908765c4e044eca9`, and updated all 17 `\declat{860b6595115e5fc139815e34908765c4e044eca9}` links in `9d1b45a56cc40a1454667cd798fcc178196c2774`.
  - Re-review at `9d1b45a56cc40a1454667cd798fcc178196c2774`: `APPROVED`.

issue.title: feat(awpp): prove uniform input-dependent error reduction
issue.body:
Prove uniform AWPP error reduction: for every polynomially bounded requested exponent `r(x)`, one GapP numerator with a length-polynomial dyadic denominator has error at most `2^-r(x)`. This completes #31 beyond the existing fixed three-round amplification.

The construction takes strict majority of `12q(n)` trials for a fixed length polynomial `q` dominating `r`, with exact denominator exponent `12q(n)p(n)`. The requested rate need not itself be computable. Uniform GapP sums and powers establish membership; a finite cardinality identity transfers the majority bound without assuming an efficient sampler for a GapP numerator. Counting-machine characterizations and PP-lowness remain outside this result.

Prerequisite #36 has merged. This branch incorporates the independently reviewed #29 and #37 heads, preserving stack topology; coordinator integration order is #29, #37, then this PR. Source revision `c7d716f413c92d69597f5f6dee1863e9cb095a68` passes all six project checks. Nonconstant clients cover genuine quarter error, input-dependent rates, a possibly noncomputable dominated rate, zero exponent and denominator one. Named axiom guards contain only the three permitted axioms. Independent exact-source correctness/API review by coordinator `/root` and an additional early read by reviewer `fusion-barrier` found no findings.

Index assessment: added a standalone uniform-amplification entry and corrected stale outstanding statements in earlier entries and ROADMAP. The combined index preserves the ordered-FO and WPP entries, with 122 entries total. All three new declaration links are pinned to the checked source lines. The PDF builds without undefined citations or overfull boxes; pages 25 and 26 were rendered and inspected. Independent coordinator review of the quantitative prose found no findings; final document-head approval is requested on `2c6f5cacff2aeea0efde34c5f01f9a6139dd7855`.

All six checks also pass on the combined final source tree, including the reviewed prerequisite branches. The source and documentation are committed separately; no custom axioms, `sorry`, or `native_decide` are introduced.

Sources: Stephen Fenner, *PP-Lowness and a Simple Definition of AWPP* (2003), and Arora–Barak §7.4.1 for the majority framework; the factor 12 is the checked quantitative bound reused from the existing BPP development. The GapP aggregation prerequisite credits Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz (1994).

Closes #31. AI assistance: OpenAI Codex worker `awpp-amplification-20261020`, with independent coordinator review under #30. This is AI-assisted formalization and review, not human editorial approval.

issue.title: feat(fusion): prove quadratic completeness for pair covers
issue.body:
Prove Cavalar–Oliveira Theorem 24 using the existing Fusion closure/compiler APIs: from a pair cover of length t construct an ordinary acyclic monotone set circuit with at most t^2 AND gates, then derive the source-complexity inequality. Make source/constant and trivial-target conventions explicit. Use a bounded-iteration/closure lemma reusable by later cover encoding. Include a nonvacuous example. This task is independent of the graph and approximation tasks.

Sources: Igor Carboni Oliveira, *Notes on the Method of Approximations and the Emergence of the Fusion Method* (2018), https://www.dcs.warwick.ac.uk/~igorcarb/documents/papers/approximation-method-fusion-note.pdf; Bruno P. Cavalar and Igor C. Oliveira, *Boolean Circuit Complexity and Two-Dimensional Cover Problems*, ECCC TR25-033 (2025), https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2025/033/. Credit earlier results to their original authors as identified there.

Workflow: follow AGENTS.md, claim with a distinct agent/session ID, use an isolated worktree and separate mutable build outputs, report hourly while active, open a focused PR and await coordinator review. Reuse native Circuit/Program, source complexity, Semifilter, PairCover and cyclic APIs. issue.title: feat(stateful): compose data-structure proofs with Word-RAM realizations
issue.body:
This adds a first substantial prototype for proving a data structure once and reusing its behavior and resource contracts in larger adaptive algorithms. Mathematical semantics, implementation refinement, native execution evidence, and performance certificates are separate.

Refs #160. Samuel explicitly authorized submission of this broader prototype; the earlier local-only restriction is superseded. Coordinator review is requested before integration.

## What is implemented

- **Stateful interfaces and composition:** typed operations, admissibility, adaptive clients using upstream `PFunctor.FreeM`, semantic modules, hidden representation relations, Hoare rules, and realization at an arbitrary backend.
- **Independent resource proofs:** additive natural-number weights on native traces, worst-case certificates, concrete-state potentials, and amortized composition retaining initial and final credit. Linking preserves flattened traces in both directions, so bounds cover every supplied terminating execution.
- **Reusable constructions:** a polymorphic two-stack FIFO queue with amortized charge `3K` when each stack call costs at most `K`; tests reuse the same proof over two different stack representations and trace types. Timeline editing explicitly charges editing, reset and replay, giving `E(H,e) + R + |e(H)| T`.
- **Concrete Word-RAM realizations:** finite-footprint assertions and frame rules, faithful read/write transcripts, disjoint array copying, and a fixed-program operation interface preserving machine state across calls. A nine-register bounded stack costs at most 12 instructions per operation. A fourteen-register prefix-sum program uses a complete binary aggregation tree with `n = 2^h` leaves, `2n-1` representation words, and at most `13(h+1)+12` instructions per operation, including dispatch and halt.
- **Non-vacuous clients:** adaptive histories, polymorphic payloads, distinct concrete representations, nonzero initial potentials, valid/invalid replay edits, actual persistent machine interpretation, boundary indices, and overflow rejection.

The implementation is 18 library modules and five test modules. The commit sequence isolates the required cslib main-pin refresh, the feature, and documentation.

## Boundaries

Machine theorems start from a bounded represented state and enforce operation-specific capacity, address and word-fit conditions. Initial representation construction, external argument encoding/delivery, result decoding, and pure Lean client-controller computation are not charged. The queue/replay controllers are not compiled RAM programs. Prefix sums use a segment tree, not a Fenwick tree.

This does not yet provide reusable allocation/deallocation, peak-space accounting, doubling arrays, a shared-heap compiled queue, historical-query operations, randomized semantics, cache models, or a general cell-probe model. Realizations prove existence and correctness of supplied terminating executions, not demonic termination of arbitrary nondeterministic backends. Outstanding work is recorded in ROADMAP.md.

## Validation and review

All six required local gates passed on final head `1d072fa180cd42bc80549dc7e01e7aba4f296131`:

issue.title: feat(counting): prove uniform bounded wide-gap closure
issue.body:
Closes #55. Includes refreshed PR53, PR57 and PR59 at the current cslib pin; preserve ancestry with a merge commit because PR61 stacks on this head.

Prove uniform bounded conjunction and disjunction closure for both WPP and LWPP. The input is one jointly uniform language on `(x,i)`, encoded with a unary index, and any polynomial-time unary bound `r(x)`. This does not replace joint membership with separate slice membership, and `r` may vary between inputs of the same length.

Conjunction multiplies the indexed gaps using PR53's certified product theorem. For WPP, multiply the corresponding FP targets. For LWPP, joint encoded length is `2|x|+1+i`; all possible targets are `T(n,k) = product_{i<k} f(2n+1+i)` for `0 ≤ k ≤ p(n)`, where a fixed polynomial bounds `r`. This nonzero, uniformly FP family permits polynomial-family robustness to normalize the selected input-dependent index `k=r(x)`. Complement closure gives disjunction. Empty ranges produce the full and empty languages respectively.

Source credit: this is a formalized deduction from Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz counting algebra and the polynomial-family robustness theorem of Edith Hemaspaandra, Lane A. Hemaspaandra, Holger Spakowski and Osamu Watanabe, *The Robustness of LWPP and WPP, with an Application to Graph Reconstruction*, Theorem 3.1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1711.01250. It does not claim that source states these exact encoded interfaces. The classes retain the verifier model; adaptive oracle closure, PP-lowness and counting-machine characterization remain separate.

issue.title: feat(MCSP): add Oliveira-Santhanam Theorems 1/17 and Lemma 26/Theorems 5/27 (#798)
issue.body:
## Summary

Packages Lemma 16 of Oliveira and Santhanam [OliveiraSanthanam2018] (#1062) with `SuccinctMCSP.mem_NP` (#1034) into `FormulaPoly` (`Formula[poly]`) separations for **Milestone M5.2** of [#798](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/798), and adds the deterministic finite-counting form of Lemma 26 and one-sided zero-error average-case formula magnification (Theorem 27):

### Source Statements (ECCC TR18-139)

Verbatim from [OliveiraSanthanam2018, Section 3.1, Theorem 17, p. 15] (also stated as [OliveiraSanthanam2018, Section 1.2, Theorem 1, pp. 5–6]):

> **Theorem 17** (Magnification of Weak Formula Lower Bounds). For convenience, let
> Π[s, δ] = (1, 1 − δ)-MCSP[s]. The following implications hold.
> (i) Let s(n) = n^k and δ(n) = n^{−k}, where k ∈ ℕ. If Π[s, δ] ∉ Formula[N · (log N)^{O(1)}]
>     then there is L ∈ NP over m-bit inputs such that L ∉ Formula[poly(m)].
> (ii) For the same choice of parameters, if Π[s, δ] ∉ Formula[N^{1+ε}] for some ε > 0, then
>     there is L ∈ NP over m-bit inputs and δ > 0 such that L ∉ Formula[2^{m^δ}].
> (iii) Let s(n) = 2^{o(n)} and δ(n) = 2^{−o(n)}. If Π[s, δ] ∉ Formula[N^{1+ε}] for some ε > 0,
>     then there is L ∈ NP over m-bit inputs such that L ∉ Formula[poly(m)].

Verbatim from [OliveiraSanthanam2018, Section 1.2, Theorem 5, p. 8], [OliveiraSanthanam2018, Section 3.3, Lemma 26 and Theorem 27, p. 21], and [OliveiraSanthanam2018, Appendix A, Definition 43, p. 34]:

> **Theorem 5.** If MCSP[2^{√n}] on N-bit inputs cannot be solved on average with zero error by
> formulas of size o(N), then NP does not have polynomial size formulas.

> **Lemma 26.** Let n ≤ s(n) ≤ 2^{o(n)} and t(n) = 4s(n) log s(n). Let I be a random collection
> of t(n) pairs of the form (x_i, b_i), where each b_i ∼ {0, 1}, and all x_i are fixed but
> distinct elements of {0, 1}^n. Then, for every n sufficiently large,
> Pr_I[ There is a circuit of size ≤ s(n) consistent with I ] < 2^{−n}.

> **Theorem 27** (Magnification from sub-linear average-case lower bounds for MCSP). Let C be a
> typical circuit class, and consider MCSP[s] for a size parameter n ≤ s(n) ≤ 2^{o(n)}. Assume
> that there exists δ > 0 such that solving MCSP[s] on average on N-bit inputs requires C-circuits
> of size Ω(N^δ). Then there is a language L in NP such that L on inputs of length
> m = Θ(n · s(n) · log s(n)) requires C-circuits of size ℓ(m) = 2^{Ω(n)}.

> **Definition 43** (Average-case MCSP [HS17]). We say that MCSP-C[s] is computed on average by a
> device D (an algorithm or a family of circuits) if for every large enough n, the following holds:
> • D is never incorrect. For each y ∈ {0, 1}^{2^n}, D(y) ∈ {MCSP-C[s](y), “?”}.
> • D rarely outputs “?”. Pr_{z∼{0,1}^{2^n}}[D(z) ∈ {0, 1}] ≥ 1 − 1/n.
> We say that MCSP-C[s] is average-case hard for a class of devices A if no D ∈ A computes
> MCSP-C[s] on average.

### Mathematical Progress

1. **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Formula/Poly.lean`**:
   - Defines non-uniform formula-size classes in `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean`, mirroring `SIZE`/`PPoly`:
     - `FormulaSIZE (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (Language Bool)` (`∀ n, formulaSize (L.slice n) ≤ s n`, measured by leaf count `formulaSize` on fan-in-2 De Morgan formulas) and `FormulaPoly : Set (Language Bool)` (`PolynomiallyBounded fun n => formulaSize (L.slice n)`).
     - `FormulaSIZEOn (enc : α ↪ List Bool) (s : ℕ → ℕ) : Set (Set α)` and `FormulaPolyOn (enc : α ↪ List Bool) : Set (Set α)`.
   - Proves leaf-size bounds for Boolean operations (`formulaSize_not_le`, `formulaSize_not`, `formulaSize_and_le`, `formulaSize_or_le`), monotonicity (`FormulaSIZE_mono`), characterizations (`mem_FormulaPoly_iff_exists_formulas`, `mem_FormulaPoly_iff_exists_mem_FormulaSIZE`, `mem_FormulaPolyOn_iff_exists_mem_FormulaSIZEOn`, `mem_FormulaSIZEOn_encBits_iff`, `mem_FormulaPolyOn_encBits_iff`), and Boolean closure properties (`FormulaPoly.zero_mem`, `FormulaPoly.top_mem`, `FormulaPoly.compl`, `FormulaPoly.sup`, `FormulaPoly.inf`, `FormulaPolyOn.compl`, `compl_mem_FormulaPolyOn_iff`).

2. **`Complexity/Computability/MCSP/SuccinctNP.lean` & `Complexity/Computability/MCSP/FormulaMagnification.lean`**:
   - **Monotonicity of query length**: `Cslib.SuccinctMCSP.ofFunctionEncLength_mono` (`Monotone (fun q => SuccinctMCSP.ofFunctionEncLength n q s)`) and `Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.approxMCSPQueryEncLength` / `ofFunctionEncLength_le_approxMCSPQueryEncLength`.
   - **Language-generalized projection and Lemma 16**:
     - `exists_formula_ofFunction_SuccinctMCSP_of_agrees`, `exists_formula_all_ofFunction_SuccinctMCSP_of_agrees`, and `exists_formula_separating_approxMCSP_of_agrees` generalize the word-level formula projection to any language `L : Language Bool` agreeing with `SuccinctMCSP` along `SuccinctMCSP.enc`.
   - **Contrapositive of Lemma 16 and Theorem 1(i) / Theorem 17(i)**:
     - `exists_formula_separating_approxMCSP_of_mem_FormulaSIZEOn`, `not_succinctMCSP_mem_FormulaPolyOn_of_approxMCSP_hard`, and `not_NP_subset_FormulaPolyOn_of_approxMCSP_hard`: general-parameter contrapositive of Lemma 16 combined with `SuccinctMCSP.mem_NP`, concluding `¬ (Complexity.NP SuccinctMCSP.enc ⊆ FormulaPolyOn SuccinctMCSP.enc)` (underlying Theorem 17(i)/(iii)).
     - `computableFunctionsLogBound_le_poly`, `polynomiallyBounded_computableFunctionsLogBound`, `polynomiallyBounded_approxMCSPQueryEncLength`, `exists_poly_formula_separating_approxMCSP_of_mem_FormulaPolyOn`, `not_succinctMCSP_mem_FormulaPolyOn_of_approxMCSP_poly_hard`, and `not_NP_subset_FormulaPolyOn_of_approxMCSP_poly_hard`: when `s₂` and `k` are polynomially bounded in `n`, a `Formula[N · (log N)^{O(1)}]` lower bound (`(2 ^ n + 1) * (c * (n + 1) ^ c) < F.leafSize`) implies `SuccinctMCSP ∉ FormulaPolyOn SuccinctMCSP.enc` and `¬ (Complexity.NP SuccinctMCSP.enc ⊆ FormulaPolyOn SuccinctMCSP.enc)` (Theorem 1(i) / Theorem 17(i)).
   - **Lemma 26 and one-sided Theorem 27 (zero-error average-case formula magnification)**:
     - `card_filter_agreesOn_eq_two_pow`, `card_filter_ofFunction_mem_succinctMCSP_le`, and `card_filter_ofFunction_mem_succinctMCSP_le_two_pow`: deterministic finite-counting form of Lemma 26 showing that for any fixed sample set `S : Finset (BitString n)` with `M + r ≤ S.card` (where `(computableFunctions n s).card ≤ 2 ^ M`), at most `2 ^ (2 ^ n - r)` truth tables `T : BitString (2 ^ n)` have `SuccinctMCSP.Instance.ofFunction ((MCSP.truthTable n).symm T) S s ∈ SuccinctMCSP`.
     - `avgCaseMCSPQueryEncLength`, `exists_formula_zero_error_average_case_of_sample`, `exists_formula_zero_error_average_case_of_agrees`, `exists_formula_zero_error_average_case_of_succinctMCSP`, `lt_formulaSize_succinctMCSP_of_zero_error_average_case`, `not_succinctMCSP_mem_FormulaPolyOn_of_zero_error_average_case_hard`, and `not_NP_subset_FormulaPolyOn_of_zero_error_average_case_hard`: one-sided zero-error average-case formula magnification from `GapMCSP.yesSet s` to `SuccinctMCSP ∉ FormulaPolyOn SuccinctMCSP.enc` and `¬ (Complexity.NP SuccinctMCSP.enc ⊆ FormulaPolyOn SuccinctMCSP.enc)`.

### Limitations & Remaining Work
- The `NP ⊄ FormulaPolyOn` conclusions are stated over `SuccinctMCSP.enc` (`¬ (Complexity.NP SuccinctMCSP.enc ⊆ FormulaPolyOn SuccinctMCSP.enc)`).
- In the average-case theorems, hypotheses are stated directly for one-sided `{0, 1}`-valued De Morgan formulas accepting all `GapMCSP.yesSet s` yes-instances and at most `2 ^ (2 ^ n - r)` truth tables overall (the projection device constructed in the proof of Theorem 27 before relabeling `1 ↦ "?"`, as documented alongside Definition 43 in `FormulaMagnification.lean`).
- The subexponential-formula consequence Theorem 17(ii) (`Formula[2^{m^δ}]`) and the specific asymptotic parameter instantiations of Theorem 17(iii) (`s(n) = 2^{o(n)}`) and Theorem 5 (`s(n) = 2^{√n}`) remain recorded in `ROADMAP.md`.
- Headline formal abstract assessment: `#798` Comment 4 selects the McKay–Murray–Williams (STOC 2019) circuit magnification (`Complexity/Computability/MCSP/Magnification.lean`) as the hardness-magnification formal abstract candidate, which is developed in a separate PR.

### Validation
- `./scripts/check.sh` passed (`lake build --wfail --iofail`, `lake exe mk_all --check`, `lake test --wfail --iofail`, `lake lint`, `lake exe lint-style`, `lake exe checkInitImports`).
- `python3 scripts/check_hygiene.py --check-simp`, `python3 scripts/check_tidy_surface.py`, `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only`, and `python3 -B scripts/build_abstracts.py --check` passed.
- Non-vacuity tests in `ComplexityTests/FormulaMagnification.lean` check `FormulaPoly` memberships, `card_filter_agreesOn_eq_two_pow`, `card_filter_ofFunction_mem_succinctMCSP_le`, `computableFunctionsLogBound`, `exists_formula_zero_error_average_case_of_succinctMCSP` at `n = 4, s = 0, r = 1`, and `exists_formula_ofFunction_SuccinctMCSP_of_agrees`.

*AI disclosure: authored by `worker-jetski-9fbb7ac4` (Gemini).*

issue.title: feat(counting): prove uniform indexed product closure
issue.body:
Prove uniform indexed product closure for #P and GapP. A jointly uniform family `f : α × ℕ → ℕ/ℤ`, encoded with a unary index, and a polynomial-time unary bound `r(a)` yield `a ↦ ∏ i < r(a), f(a,i)` in the same class. This extends homogeneous powers and specialized WPP interpolation products.

The #P verifier pads index-dependent certificates to width `p(2|a|+1+r(a))` and checks indexed rows. The GapP proof expands over Boolean sign choices using this #P closure, an efficiently computed parity sign, and uniform word summation. The family must be jointly uniform and the bound must have a unary FP output. Oracle lowness remains open.

Tests cover varying certificate lengths, empty products, zero-width rejecting factors, negative factors, and exact cancellation. Named axiom guards use only the permitted axioms. All six checks in `scripts/check.sh` pass on final revision `8ab40dc2fc6972190f70e809569d0214ed1bd66c`, including the current cslib pin `b5f3b77d9f045ed8f2dfec05505b159c2417e1c6`. issue.title: feat(counting): prove uniform indexed product closure
issue.body:
Prove actual uniform polynomially indexed product closure for jointly uniform #P and GapP functions. For `f : α × ℕ → ℕ` (respectively ℤ) in #P (GapP) under `encPair enc encUnary`, and `r : α → ℕ` computed in polynomial time with unary output, prove that `a ↦ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range (r a), f (a,i)` belongs to the same class.

This goes beyond homogeneous powers and PR44's special products of FP targets minus one fixed GapP value. Do not assume product closure. No overlap with #49's two-sided WPP/LWPP specialization; use a new SharpP/Products module and leave shared Aggregation and WPP files unchanged.

Construction: for #P, pad the index-i certificate of length `p(2|a|+1+i)` with false bits to common width `p(2|a|+1+r(a))`, check all indexed rows, and use exact cardinality factorization. Total certificate length before final padding is row count times common width. For GapP, expand the product of positive/negative differences over Boolean choices, use the proved uniform #P products on the selected joint family, and sum with a certified polynomial-time parity sign. Verify the actual encoding-length formula, including zero index, in source.

Completion criteria: both full closure theorems, efficient verifier and count identity, nonvacuous tests for varying index-dependent factors/certificate lengths, empty product, zero and signed factors and cancellation, named axiom guards, all six gates, source credit, exact declaration links and index/PDF assessment, independent correctness/API/index review. This is a useful class-algebra prerequisite for future AWPP PP-lowness, not a claim that lowness has been proved.

Source credit: Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz, *Gap-definable counting classes* (1994); explicit verifier/padding and Boolean-expansion implementation follows the existing uniform counting algebra. Parent coordinator #30 approved this API/resource plan. issue.title: feat(FineGrained): the satisfiability coding lemma and PPZ for unique k-SAT (#894)
issue.body:
This PR covers part of **M3 of #894**: the **PPZ satisfiability coding lemma and its unique k-SAT bound**, from R. Paturi, P. Pudlák and F. Zane, *Satisfiability Coding Lemma* (FOCS 1997). It is independent of #908 (Schöning).

**Algorithm** (`FineGrained/PPZ.lean`, namespace `Cslib.Complexity.PPZ`). `round φ` draws a uniformly random order `π` of the `n` variables and processes them in that order:
- if a clause becomes a unit clause on the current variable under the values chosen so far (`IsUnitOn`, `forced`), set the variable to satisfy it;
- otherwise draw a uniform bit.

Tautological clauses never force.

**Results:**
- `forced_eq`: along a run that agrees with a satisfying `σ`, forced values agree with `σ`.
- `run_apply_restrict`: in a fixed order, the run produces `σ` with probability exactly `2^{−u}`, where `u` (`unforcedCount`) is the number of unforced steps along the run that agrees with `σ`.
- `exists_critical`: if `σ` is the unique solution, every variable `x` has a **critical clause**, in which the literals on `x` are true under `σ` and every other literal is false.
- `forced_ne_none_of_isLast`: a variable that comes after the other variables of its critical clause is forced.
- `card_isLast_mul`: a fixed member of a set `S` comes last in exactly a `1/|S|` fraction of the `n!` orders. The proof uses swap involutions, plus the fact that every order has exactly one last element.
- `round_success`: for the unique solution of a CNF whose clauses have at most `k ≥ 1` literals, one round succeeds with probability at least `2^{−(1−1/k)n}`. On average at most `(1−1/k)n` steps are unforced, and the weighted AM–GM inequality gives `E[2^{−u}] ≥ 2^{−E[u]}`.

**Scope.** This is PPZ for **unique** k-SAT.
- The general (non-unique) PPZ bound via isolated solutions is a natural follow-up, and I plan it next.
- PPSZ's `s`-implication bound (the rest of M3), Hertli's general case (M4), and amplification and the time model (M2) remain open on #894.
- I'll add a `ROADMAP.md` line after #908 lands, to avoid conflicting edits to the same row.

**Faithfulness.** This follows the PPZ unique-SAT analysis. The algorithm processes variables in a random order with unit-clause forcing, and the bound `2^{−(1−1/k)n}` is the paper's.

**Abstracts.** No impact.

**Validation** at `c8cf27bd`:
- `scripts/check.sh`: all six strict gates pass.
- `scripts/check_hygiene.py` passes.
- `ComplexityTests/PPZ.lean`:
  - a uniquely satisfiable 2-CNF, where `round_success` gives at least `1/2`;
  - the `1/3` fraction of orders for `S = Fin 3`;
  - axiom guards.

Also adds the `PPZ1997` bibliography entry.

issue.title: NP ∩ coNP oracle lowness for NP and Low₁ characterization (Schöning 1983)
issue.body:
### Objective

Formalize the oracle lowness of $\mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$ for $\mathsf{NP}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ (and of $\mathsf{UP} \cap \mathsf{coUP}$ for $\mathsf{P}$) in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/Oracle/Lowness.lean`, using the deterministic instruction-indexed oracle replay infrastructure in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/Oracle/Replay.lean` and the uniform `#P` product/sum closure in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/SharpP/Products.lean` and `Aggregation.lean`.

### Deliverables

1. **Boolean closure of `PWithOracle`**:
   - `compl_mem_PWithOracle`, `inter_mem_PWithOracle`, `union_mem_PWithOracle`, and `mem_PWithOracle_compl_self`.
2. **Certified oracle replay in `NP` and `UP`**:
   - `ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle.mem_NP`: for  \in \mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$,  : \alpha \to \beta$ computable in polynomial time relative to $, and  : \alpha \times \beta \to \mathsf{Bool}$ computable in polynomial time, $\{a \mid P(a, f(a)) = \mathsf{true}\} \in \mathsf{NP}$.
   - `ComputableInPolyTimeWithOracle.mem_UP`: the analogous unambiguous result for  \in \mathsf{UP} \cap \mathsf{coUP}$.
3. **$\mathsf{P}^{\mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}} = \mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$ and $\mathsf{P}^{\mathsf{UP} \cap \mathsf{coUP}} = \mathsf{UP} \cap \mathsf{coUP}*:
   - `PWithOracle_subset_NP`, `PWithOracle_subset_coNP`, `PWithOracle_subset_NP_inter_coNP`, and the iff characterization `PWithOracle_subset_NP_inter_coNP_iff : PWithOracle A encBits ⊆ NP encBits ∩ coNP encBits ↔ A ∈ NP encBits ∩ coNP encBits`.
   - `iUnion_PWithOracle_NP_inter_coNP` and `P_eq_NP_inter_coNP_iff_forall_PWithOracle_eq_P`.
   - `PWithOracle_subset_UP`, `PWithOracle_subset_coUP`, `PWithOracle_subset_UP_inter_coUP`, `PWithOracle_subset_UP_inter_coUP_iff`, and `iUnion_PWithOracle_UP_inter_coUP`.
4. **$\mathsf{NP}^{\mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}} = \mathsf{NP}$ and the $\mathsf{Low}_1$ characterization [Schöning 1983, Arora–Barak Ch. 3]**:
   - `NPWithOracle_subset_NP_of_PWithOracle_subset_NP`: general reduction from `NPWithOracle` collapse to `PWithOracle` on paired encodings.
   - `NPWithOracle_eq_NP_of_mem_NP_of_mem_coNP`: for  \in \mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$, $\mathsf{NP}^A = \mathsf{NP}$ for every instance encoding `enc`.
   - `NPWithOracle_eq_NP_iff`: $\mathsf{NP}^A = \mathsf{NP} \iff A \in \mathsf{NP} \cap \mathsf{coNP}$.
5. **Regression tests and axiom guards**:
   - Nonvacuous tests and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/OracleLowness.lean`.

issue.title: feat(logic): add compositional first-order projection core
issue.body:
This adds the compositional semantic foundation for first-order projections on the path to Circuit Value completeness. Numeric tests and input relations have separate vocabularies: for a fixed numeric structure and assignment, one constant or signed input literal works for every interpretation of the input relations. Arbitrary quantifier-free formulas do not enforce that restriction.

The core is vocabulary-parametric and relativized. It reuses Mathlib formulas and the existing tuple-based `FO.Interpretation`, proves a finite mutually exclusive numeric-case normal form, truth-preserving substitution, identity/composition isomorphisms preserving both vocabularies, and quantifier-free closure under explicit numeric hypotheses. A graph-complement client reuses Mathlib's graph language. Tests include a concrete nonvacuous example, empty universes, composition, axiom guards, and a proof that two independent nullary input bits cannot be projected to their conjunction.

This is the first independently useful milestone. Classical positive-dimensional full tuple universes with canonical numeric predicates, projection reducibility on finite structure classes, a certified logspace encoding transducer, the alternating-logspace simulation, `REACHa → MCVP → CVP`, and the native Circuit Value P-completeness theorem remain outstanding in `ROADMAP.md`. No resource bound or completeness theorem is claimed here. The classical quantifier-free convention of the cited source excludes BIT.

Validation and reviews:

- All six project gates passed, including strict build/tests and the imported-declaration axiom audit. The final expected-output guards also passed strict tests after formatting.
- The upstream synchronization check reports CURRENT for the CSLib main pin and every copied dependency revision.
- Independent Codex API review (`proof_api`) and correctness review (`proof_correctness`) approved exact Lean revision `811ad02abdab6bc2b9f945d58d2a1ff2ed1c282b`. Findings about precise source credit and scope wording were fixed and re-reviewed; no findings remain.
- Independent statement-index review (`resume_alternation`) approved the new exposition against that Lean revision. The 19-page PDF was rebuilt and visually inspected; all 81 declaration names, source anchors, and actual PDF URLs were verified. The 50 numbered entries remain unchanged. Exact review evidence and source hashes are in `paper/review.md`.

Mathematical sources: [Immerman, Descriptive Complexity](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-0539-5) and [Immerman–Landau, The Complexity of Iterated Multiplication, Definitions 3.3–3.6](https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/pub/mult.pdf). The latter bibliography entry is a separate commit.

issue.title: feat(kolmogorov): time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity K^t, Levin's Kt, and MINKT ∈ NP (#798)
issue.body:
## Summary Implements **M1a** of the metacomplexity track (#798, [assignment comment](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/798#issuecomment-6385933977)) in two new Kolmogorov modules (`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/TimeBounded.lean` and `Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/MINKT.lean`) plus regression tests (`ComplexityTests/KolmogorovTimeBounded.lean`), without modifying any existing Kolmogorov module: 1. **Universal multi-tape description method and time-bounded Kolmogorov measures (`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/TimeBounded.lean`):** - Plain `ComputableInPolyTime` wrappers for `decodeDesc`, `List.map eBit`, `eBit`, and `Universal.universal`. - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTMRunFor` and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.DescriptionMethod.universalTM : DescriptionMethod (List Bool)`: clocked evaluation of binary programs `p` by parsing `decodeDesc (unframe p)` and `dropFrame p`, simulating the described multi-tape machine for `t` steps (Decision D1), and mapping the global output tape contents to `List Bool` via `(· != 0)` (Decision D2), together with `computableInPolyTime_universalTMRunFor`, `computable_universalTMRunFor`, and `partrec_universalTMEval`. - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.plain` / `plainNat` ($K(x)$), `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded` / `timeBoundedNat` ($K^t(x)$), and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKt` / `levinKtNat` ($\mathrm{Kt}(x)$) in `ℕ∞` and `ℕ` (Decision D3), with proved equivalence bridges between the `ℕ∞` and finite `ℕ` formulations (`timeBounded_le_natCast_iff`, `timeBoundedNat_le_iff`, `exists_length_eq_timeBoundedNat`, `timeBoundedNat_eq_sInf`, `levinKt_eq_iInf_pos`, `levinKt_le_natCast_iff`, `levinKtNat_le_iff`). - Clock-preserving simulation of every finite-state binary `MultiTapeTM` with constant program overhead and zero time overhead (`universalTMSimulation`, `exists_simulation_ofMultiTapeTM`, `simulation_ofMultiTapeTM`, `exists_etimeBoundedComplexity_universalTM_le_ofMultiTapeTM`). - Basic properties of $K^t$ and $\mathrm{Kt}$: - monotonicity in $t$ (`timeBounded_mono_of_le`, `timeBounded_anti`); - trivial upper bound $K^t(x) \le |x| + \mathrm{copyOverhead}$ whenever $t(|x|) \ge |x| + 1$ (`timeBounded_le_length_add`, `timeBounded_le`, `exists_timeBounded_le`); - relation to plain Kolmogorov complexity: directly under `universalTM` (`plain_le_timeBounded : plain x ≤ timeBounded t x`, `plainNat_le_timeBoundedNat`, `plain_le_levinKt`) and up to an additive constant `+ c` via a computable decoder `dec : List Bool → ℕ` under `Partrec.universal` (`exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded`, `exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded_bits`); - counting and incompressibility facts for $K^t$ (`encard_setOf_timeBounded_lt`, `encard_setOf_length_eq_timeBounded_lt`, `exists_length_eq_forall_le_timeBounded`, `exists_length_eq_le_timeBounded`, `two_pow_lt_ncard_setOf_length_eq_le_timeBounded_add`). 2. **The `MINKT` and `MINKTAt` decision problems and `GapMINKT` (`Complexity/Computability/Kolmogorov/MINKT.lean`):** - `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINKT.Instance`, `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINKT`, and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINKT.enc` (with `time` and `size` encoded in unary per Decision D4), plain `ComputableInPolyTime` projections/constructors, polynomial-time witness check `MINKT.check` (`computableInPolyTime_check`), and `MINKT.mem_NP : MINKT ∈ NP MINKT.enc`. - Fixed-threshold formulation `Cslib.Kolmogorov.MINKTAt t s : Set (List Bool)` (Decision D4), equivalence bridge `mem_MINKTAt_iff_mem_MINKT`, finite-form bridge `mem_MINKTAt_iff_timeBoundedNat_le`, polynomial-time reduction `MINKTAt.polyTimeReducible_MINKT`, and `NP` membership for polynomial-time unary thresholds (`MINKTAt.mem_NP`, `MINKTAt.mem_NP_polynomial`, `MINKTAt.mem_NP_polynomial₂`). - Hirahara's promise problem `Cslib.Kolmogorov.GapMINKT` (`GapMINKT.yes`, `GapMINKT.no`, `GapMINKT.disjoint_yes_no`, `GapMINKT.no_eq`, `GapMINKT.id_eq`). ## Faithfulness | Concept / Theorem | Source & Locator | Library Statement | Convention Differences & Bridge Lemmas | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity $K^t(x)$ | [Liu and Pass, *On One-way Functions and Kolmogorov Complexity*, FOCS 2020, Section 2.2][LiuPass2020]: $K^t(x) = \min\{\lvert\Pi\rvert : U(\Pi, 1^{t(\lvert x\rvert)}) = x\}$ where $\Pi$ encodes $(M, w)$ and $U(\Pi, 1^t)$ is the output of $M(w)$ emulated for $t$ steps | `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBounded` (`ℕ∞`-valued) and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.timeBoundedNat` (`ℕ`-valued) over `DescriptionMethod.universalTM` | **D1 (clock):** `universalTM` parses `p` into `decodeDesc (unframe p)` and `dropFrame p` and counts steps of the described multi-tape machine (`Desc.runFor`), matching the reading required by [Liu and Pass, Theorem 5.2][LiuPass2020] and clocked-simulation optimality `simulation_ofMultiTapeTM`. The universal simulator's polynomial overhead appears only in algorithmic results (`computableInPolyTime_universalTMRunFor`, `MINKT.mem_NP`).
**D2 (output):** global output tape contents upon halting (`universalTMRunFor_eq_ite`), matching [Ko][Ko1986], [Liu and Pass, Section 2.2][LiuPass2020], and [Hirahara][Hirahara2018].
**D3 (value type):** `timeBounded t x : ℕ∞` is `⊤` when no program halts in `t |x|` steps. Whenever a witness exists (`timeBounded t x ≠ ⊤`, in particular for `t |x| ≥ |x| + 1` via `timeBounded_ne_top`), `natCast_timeBoundedNat`, `timeBoundedNat_le_iff`, `exists_length_eq_timeBoundedNat`, and `timeBoundedNat_eq_sInf` prove exact agreement with the `ℕ`-valued minimum $\min\{\lvert p\rvert : x \in (\mathrm{universalTM.run}\;p).\mathrm{runFor}(t(\lvert x\rvert))\}$. | | Trivial upper bound $K^t(x) \le \lvert x\rvert + c$ | [Liu and Pass, FOCS 2020, Fact 2.1][LiuPass2020] | `timeBounded_le_length_add`, `timeBounded_le`, `exists_timeBounded_le` | In Liu–Pass's single-tape model where the input starts on the output tape, a 0-step halting machine witnesses $K^t(x) \le \lvert x\rvert + c$ for $t > 0$. In the library's multi-tape model where the input tape is separate from the output tape, copying $x$ to the output tape and halting takes $\lvert x\rvert + 1$ steps (`exists_simulation_literal`), giving $K^t(x) \le \lvert x\rvert + \mathrm{copyOverhead}$ for all $t(\lvert x\rvert) \ge \lvert x\rvert + 1$. | | Relation to plain Kolmogorov complexity $K(x) \le K^t(x)$ | [Li and Vitányi, Chapter 7][LiVitanyi2019] | `plain_le_timeBounded`, `plainNat_le_timeBoundedNat`, `exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded`, `exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded_bits` | Bridged both directly against `plain = universalTM.ecomplexity` (`plain_le_timeBounded : plain x ≤ timeBounded t x`) and, for any computable decoder `dec : List Bool → ℕ`, up to an additive constant `+ c` against `Partrec`'s universal description method `DescriptionMethod.universal` on `ℕ` (`exists_ecomplexity_universal_le_timeBounded : ∃ c, ∀ t x, universal.ecomplexity (dec x) ≤ timeBounded t x + c`). | | Levin's time-bounded complexity $\mathrm{Kt}(x)$ | [Levin, 1973][Levin1973]; [Liu and Pass, CRYPTO 2021, Section 2.2][LiuPass2021Crypto]: $\mathrm{Kt}(x) = \min\{\lvert\Pi\rvert + \lceil \log t\rceil : U(\Pi, 1^t) = x\}$ | `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKt` and `Cslib.Kolmogorov.levinKtNat` | Defined as `⨅ s : ℕ, universalTM.etimeBoundedComplexity s x + Nat.clog 2 s`. Because no program halts in $0$ steps (`etimeBoundedComplexity_universalTM_zero`), `levinKt_eq_iInf_pos` proves equality with the infimum over $s > 0$, and `levinKt_le_natCast_iff` / `levinKtNat_le_iff` bridge to the finite witness form $\exists p\;s,\;x \in (\mathrm{universalTM.run}\;p).\mathrm{runFor}\;s \wedge \lvert p\rvert + \lceil \log_2 s\rceil \le k$. | | `MINKT`, `MINKTAt`, and `MINKT ∈ NP` | [Ko, Section 2][Ko1986]; issue.title: feat(crypto): certify native GSW key generation and encryption
issue.body:
GSW key generation and encryption now have native polynomial-time certificates for the actual serialized algorithms. Dimensions use unary encodings; residues and signed errors use binary encodings. Exact bridges identify the total computations with the existing typed construction, including the full joint public/secret-key law and the encryption distribution.

The representation is fixed-width, row-major and little-endian. Public keys contain `m*(n+1)*w` bits, secret keys `n*w` bits, and ciphertexts `((n+1)*w)^2` bits. The algorithms specify padding, truncation and modular normalization for arbitrary inputs. Generic matrix encodings, signed remainder and traversal certificates live below crypto; the moved bit-reconstruction lemmas retain deprecated aliases.

Closes #500. This completes the key-generation/encryption efficiency milestone under #486. Native decryption/NAND, cryptographic security, parameter selection and bootstrappability remain separate work. issue.title: feat(fo): define BIT on arbitrary-base full tuples
issue.body:
Closes #112.

Defines `tupleBit L k`, an actual native first-order formula over canonical order and BIT, and proves exact BIT semantics for the lexicographic ranks of full base-n tuples on every `Fin n`, `n >= 2`. Both the represented value and index can exceed the source universe. High indices are rejected; dimension zero is explicitly false.

The construction uses checked radix-word affine arithmetic, multiplication, conversion, and a cardinality word obtained from `max + 1`. Its witnessed binary radix satisfies `B^3 < n`; seven digits encode the cardinality and `7k` digits encode each rank. Full-word index matching uses base-one conversion, so no out-of-domain scalar index is assumed. A fixed finite disjunction covers source sizes 2 through 8. No formula-size efficiency, restricted-domain BIT, or completed numeric-preserving composition is claimed.

Source: Neil Immerman, *Descriptive Complexity*, [Remark 1.32 and Exercise 1.33(3), printed p.25 / PDF p.37](https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/book/ch0_1_2.pdf#page=37). This is an explicit implementation of the full-domain exercise, not a claimed transcription of its arithmetic hint. Existing PLUS/TIMES source credit is preserved.

Validation at source `92915665afb129fbdbe0051fcb4a56c4b994be96`: all six repository gates passed; fresh focused Lean MCP diagnostics and the headline axiom guard are clean. Clients cover n = 2, 8, 9, 64; a true index 9 over Fin 9; MSB orientation; the seventh cardinality digit; high rejection; zero dimension; relabeling; inclusive carries; and exact overflow. Current main `68b94b2817a812b43069aff9558393af622ec71b` integrated cleanly at final head `c90ddbe0fdcfa21af2e239656ec73039e5c5ef3b`; all six combined gates also passed. issue.title: feat(complexity): #P and UP ∩ coUP oracle lowness, Low(#P) = UP ∩ coUP, Low(GapP) = SPP, and modular counting lowness
issue.body:
### Objective

Complete the unsigned and signed counting oracle-lowness hierarchy in `Complexity/Computability/Complexity/Classes/SharpP/Lowness.lean` (following `SharpP/Oracle.lean`, `WPP/Lowness.lean`, and #719):

1. **Precomposition of `#P` and `GapP` with `FP^(UP ∩ coUP)` functions**:
   - Prove `SharpP.encoded_comp_mem_of_computableInPolyTimeWithOracle` and `SharpP.comp_mem_of_computableInPolyTimeWithOracle`: for `A ∈ UP encBits ∩ coUP encBits`, `f : α → β` computable in polynomial time relative to `A`, and `F : α × List Bool → ℕ` in `SharpP (encPair enc encBits)`, `(fun a => F (a, output (f a))) ∈ SharpP enc`.
   - Prove the signed `GapP` analogues `GapP.encoded_comp_mem_of_computableInPolyTimeWithOracle` and `GapP.comp_mem_of_computableInPolyTimeWithOracle`.
2. **Exact `#P` oracle lowness characterization (`Low(#P) = UP ∩ coUP`, [Köbler–Schöning–Torán 1989; Hemachandra 1989])**:
   - `SharpPWithOracle_eq_SharpP_of_mem_UP_of_mem_coUP`: for `A ∈ UP encBits ∩ coUP encBits`, `SharpPWithOracle A enc = SharpP enc` for every instance encoding `enc`.
   - `SharpPWithOracle_eq_SharpP_iff : SharpPWithOracle A encBits = SharpP encBits ↔ A ∈ UP encBits ∩ coUP encBits` (and `forall_SharpPWithOracle_eq_SharpP_iff`, `iUnion_SharpPWithOracle_UP_inter_coUP`).
3. **Relativized `UP`, `coUP`, `FewP`, `US`, and `SBPWithFixedTarget` and their `UP ∩ coUP` lowness**:
   - Define `UPWithOracle`, `coUPWithOracle`, `FewPWithOracle`, `USWithOracle`, and `SBPWithFixedTarget` (retaining an unrelativized `FP` threshold, analogous to `LWPPWithFixedTarget` and `WPPWithFixedTarget`), with verifier characterizations `mem_UPWithOracle` and `mem_FewPWithOracle`, base inclusions, and `P`-oracle elimination.
   - Prove `UP ∩ coUP` lowness for `UP`, `coUP`, `FewP`, `US`, and `SBPWithFixedTarget`, and prove the exact iff characterizations `UPWithOracle_eq_UP_and_coUPWithOracle_eq_coUP_iff` and `UPWithOracle_inter_coUPWithOracle_eq_iff` (`Low(UP ∩ coUP) = UP ∩ coUP`).
4. **Exact `GapP` and `SPP` oracle lowness characterizations (`Low(GapP) = Low(SPP) = SPP`, [Fenner–Fortnow–Kurtz 1994, Theorem 5.14])**:
   - Prove `GapPWithOracle_eq_GapP_iff : GapPWithOracle A encBits = GapP encBits ↔ A ∈ SPP encBits` and `SPPWithOracle_eq_SPP_iff : SPPWithOracle A encBits = SPP encBits ↔ A ∈ SPP encBits` (plus `forall_*` and `iUnion_*` corollaries).
5. **Relativized modular counting (`ModPWithOracle`, `coModPWithOracle`, `ParityPWithOracle`) and `SPP` / `FewP` / `UP ∩ coUP` lowness**:
   - Define `ModPWithOracle`, `coModPWithOracle`, and `ParityPWithOracle` (`ModPWithOracle 2 A enc = ParityPWithOracle A enc`).
   - Prove `UP ∩ coUP` lowness for all `k : ℕ`, the `GapPWithOracle` residue characterizations for `0 < k`, and `SPP` (hence `FewP`) lowness for `ModPWithOracle k`, `coModPWithOracle k`, and `ParityPWithOracle` (`0 < k`).
6. **Tests, axiom guards, and documentation**:
   - Add nonvacuous tests and `#print axioms` guards in `ComplexityTests/SharpPLowness.lean` and update `ROADMAP.md`.

issue.title: feat(counting): realize signed GapP by native finite machines
issue.body:
Complete the signed reverse endpoint of #106 using the actual native verifier machines in #116 / PR #119. This is separate from the already proved #P iff; no arbitrary signed GapP endpoint is claimed until this construction and its clocks are proved.

Construction and API:

1. Add an actual fixed finite Boolean verdict router. A successful verifier output `[true]` makes one terminal branch of the selected sign; an unsuccessful `[false]` makes exactly one accepting and one rejecting branch. Its one native transition has nonempty choices on every local view. Buffered composition charges every output handoff; an unsuccessful witness contributes gap zero, and a successful one contributes exactly +1 or -1. Preserve both counts, not only their difference.
2. Add an actual initial two-occurrence choice between two closed finite machines, preserving each component's List occurrences and native labelled counts. Reserve disjoint work tapes, keep the input unchanged and charge the selector transition. Reuse the shared action/state/tape compilers and FreeM/List bridge; do not introduce another branch semantics.
3. Apply the router separately to the two #P verifier machines supplied by a GapP decomposition. They retain their own witness lengths, including unequal and zero lengths. Use a polynomial sum clock and native halted-clock stability; do not add witness bits or discarded coin choices to align branches. The resulting machine's accepting-minus-rejecting count must be the original arbitrary integer function, including odd, negative and zero values.
4. Combine this actual reverse construction with the existing certified forward checker to prove `Cslib.Complexity.mem_GapP_iff_exists_machine`, with one fixed finite state type, tape count, machine and polynomial clock before `forall a`. All branches halt on encoded inputs. Raw `encBits` covers every binary input; no inverse encoding, input advice, oracle, simulation certificate or runtime-uniform supplied machine description is assumed.

Expected files: `Counting/Alternative.lean` for native initial choice and clocks; `Counting/Verdict.lean` for the one-versus-two router and exact counts; `Classes/SharpP/GapMachine.lean` (or a comparably small dedicated module) for the reverse GapP construction/iff; focused clients and affected index/roadmap entries. Completion criteria: actual constructors; List/native correspondence; explicit nonblocking/finite-control instances; exact routed accepting/rejecting counts; charged polynomial bounds including every buffer and initial choice; full signed iff; adversarial clients for false-branch cancellation, unequal witness lengths, duplicate outcomes, early halting, zero/odd/negative gaps; six local gates; source credit; exact-source API/correctness and changed-index review plus generated PDF artifact review. issue.title: feat(ram): certify relocation of length-prefixed inputs
issue.body:
## Change

Add a concrete RAM program that relocates a length-prefixed input from address 5 to a fixed address `R ≥ 5`, copying backwards to handle overlapping blocks and then clearing every register below `R`. `RAM.Input.run_prepare_append` proves the exact register state and program counter before arbitrary appended code after `6 + 6*(input.length+1) + R` instructions.

`RAM.Input.time_prepare_append_le` charges every preparation instruction under `RAM.logCost` and proves the bound

```
(24 + R) * (bitLength (R + 5) + 2) * (input.length + 1) * b
```

from `bitLength input.length ≤ b` and `∀ v ∈ input, bitLength v ≤ b`. The first hypothesis derives `b ≥ 1`. This is supporting infrastructure for #81, with no WordRAM dependency or assumed simulation/resource certificate.

The external convention is `List.replicate 5 0 ++ input.length :: input`. Installing that convention is explicitly uncharged; this does not certify an encoding reduction or a Turing-machine simulation. The source credits Cook–Reckhow for the model/cost convention and retains the existing natural-number and free-input adaptation boundary.

Closes #84.

## Validation and review

- Lean MCP: source and tests checked, no errors or warnings.
- Executable clients: `R=5`, genuinely overlapping shift to `R=7`, empty input, and the exact boundary before an appended instruction.
- Symbolic clients: arbitrary appended code, exact whole-register state, and nonvacuous cost bounds for empty and nonempty input.

issue.title: feat(abstracts): McKay–Murray–Williams hardness magnification abstract (#798)
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds the formal abstract for **McKay–Murray–Williams (STOC 2019) hardness magnification for MCSP** (`abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/MagnificationAbstract.lean`, `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts/MagnificationBridge.lean`, and `ComplexityTests/Abstracts/MagnificationTests.lean`). It is Candidate Abstract 2 from [#798 (comment)](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/issues/798#issuecomment-2777231279) and bridges to `Complexity.Computability.MCSP.Magnification` (#1048):

> Barely superlinear circuit lower bounds for $\mathrm{MCSP}[n^k]$ on $N = 2^n$-bit truth tables separate $\mathrm{NP}$ from $\mathrm{P/poly}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ from $\mathrm{NP}$.

(This one-line summary is a paraphrase, not a quotation.)

### Declarations in `ComplexityAbstracts.MagnificationAbstract`

- **Self-contained circuit and MCSP definitions**:
  - `DeMorganCircuit` (`Cslib.Circuits.Circuit Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.signature n 1`), `evalCircuit`, `ComputesFunction` and `HasCircuitOfSize`: plain fan-in-2 De Morgan circuits over `{AND, OR, NOT}`, counting all operation gates via `Circuit.size`.
  - `tableIndex`, `tableFunction` and `DecidesMCSPSlice`: exact decision $\mathrm{MCSP}[s(n)]$ on $N = 2^n$-bit truth tables ordered by `tableIndex`.
- **Self-contained complexity classes**:
  - `P`, `IsVerifier` and `NP` use native multi-tape Turing machines over `List Bool`, via `ComplexityAbstracts.Encoding` and `ComplexityAbstracts.Computation`. `PPoly` is the class of nonuniform polynomial-size De Morgan circuit families.
- **Headline theorems (in `abstracts/catalogue.json`)**. Both take a fixed degree `k` and the threshold `fun m => m ^ k`:
  - `np_not_subset_ppoly_of_mcsp_hard (k : ℕ)`: suppose that for every exponent $c > 0$ there is an arity $n$ at which every De Morgan circuit deciding the $2^n$-bit slice of $\mathrm{MCSP}[m \mapsto m^k]$ has more than `2 ^ n * c * (n + 1) ^ c` gates. Then `¬ (NP ⊆ PPoly)`.
  - `p_ne_np_of_mcsp_hard (k : ℕ)`: under the same hypothesis, `P ≠ NP`.
- **Supporting theorems (in `abstracts/catalogue.json`)**:
  - `mcsp_circuit_of_np_subset_ppoly` is the general upper bound. If `NP ⊆ PPoly`, there is $c > 0$ such that, for every size schedule $s$ and every arity $n$, some De Morgan circuit of size at most `2 ^ n * c * (n + s n + 1) ^ c` decides the $2^n$-bit slice of $\mathrm{MCSP}[s]$. It is proved by merge-tree synthesis over subcubes.
  - `mcsp_pow_circuit_of_np_subset_ppoly (k : ℕ)` is the polynomial-regime specialization $s(m) = m^k$. If `NP ⊆ PPoly`, there is $c > 0$ such that for every $n$ some circuit of size at most `2 ^ n * c * (n + 1) ^ c` decides the slice. With $N = 2^n$, this is $N \cdot (\log_2 N)^{O(1)}$.
- **Audit**:
  - `#check_abstract ComplexityAbstracts.MagnificationAbstract allowing [ComplexityAbstracts.Encoding, ComplexityAbstracts.Computation]` checks all 17 root declarations and 103 transitive dependencies. The allowlist is exactly the two shared foundations.
- **Regression tests (`ComplexityTests/Abstracts/MagnificationTests.lean`)**:
  - They check `P = Cslib.Complexity.P encBits` (`rfl`), `NP = Cslib.Complexity.NP encBits`, `PPoly = Cslib.Circuits.Boolean.PPolyOn encBits`, `tableIndex` and `HasCircuitOfSize`, and the infinitely-often lower-bound corollaries (`∃ᶠ n in atTop`).

### Source statement and specialization

[McKayMurrayWilliams2019, Section 1, Theorem 1.4, third bullet, p. 3 of the STOC ’19 version](https://people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf). The proof is in Section 5, p. 9.

> "Theorem 1.4 (Section 5). Let s(n) ≥ n, and let A ∈ PH. […] If search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on inputs of length N = 2^n does not have circuits of N · poly(s(n)) size and poly(s(n)) depth, then NP ⊄ P/poly."

Superscripts are written with `^`, as in the source PDF's typeset `MCSP^A` and `2^n`.

Notation mapping and specialization (this matches the abstract's corrected module docstring):
- `A = ∅`: oracle-free `MCSP`.
- Decision `MCSP[s]` (`DecidesMCSPSlice`) instead of `search-MCSP^A[s(n)]`. A decision lower bound implies a search lower bound, so this hypothesis is stronger.
- A size-only lower bound instead of a lower bound against circuits of size `N · poly(s(n))` and depth `poly(s(n))`. This hypothesis is also stronger.
- `s(n) = n ^ k`, with `poly(s(n))` instantiated as `c * (n + 1) ^ c` for every `c > 0`, and fan-in-2 De Morgan circuits counting all gates.
- The upper bound under `NP ⊆ P/poly` provides decision circuits with a size bound only. It asserts no search circuits and no depth bound.
- Proof route: the library adapts [Lemma 3.1, p. 6] and the `C = P/poly` case of the Section 5 proof of Theorem 1.4 to a binary tree of subcubes. Its merge language `Cslib.MCSP.CircuitMinMergeLanguage` is a polynomial-hierarchy language (adapted from `Circuit-Min-Merge`, Section 2.1, p. 5). It selects the lexicographically least valid fixed-threshold certificate of size at most `s` that agrees with both halves, rather than a minimum-size circuit. Under `NP ⊆ P/poly`, nonuniform quantifier elimination gives it polynomial-size circuits.

### Coordinator fix-up (`04ed2f4b`)

The authoring worker became inactive, so `worker-claude-fixups-c4b0c164` (delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`) addressed review 5645802735:
- The abstract's module docstring, which is rendered on PDF page 1, now describes the actual proof. The merge problem is a polynomial-hierarchy language. Under `NP ⊆ P/poly`, closure under polynomially bounded quantifiers gives it polynomial-size circuits. It selects the lexicographically least valid fixed-threshold certificate, not a minimum-size circuit. The binary-subcube construction is identified as the library's adaptation of Lemma 3.1 and Section 5.
- The module docstring states the specialization of Theorem 1.4 (third bullet): oracle-free decision MCSP and a size-only lower-bound hypothesis, with no search or depth conclusion.
- This PR description now gives the correct headline bullets: fixed `k`, threshold `fun m => m ^ k` and bound `2 ^ n * c * (n + 1) ^ c`. The general arbitrary-`s` bound is listed as a supporting theorem.
- The branch is restacked onto `main` (`a919571e`). The `gsw-fhe` and `partial-mcsp` catalogue entries and README rows are kept, `magnification` is appended as the 19th entry, the README count reads "nineteen", and `abstracts/ComplexityAbstracts.lean` passes `mk_all --check`.
- No formal statement, definition, bridge, test or allowlist changed. Outside the module docstring, README rows, catalogue and aggregator, the diff against `main` is byte-identical to the reviewed head `463d19bb`. The `magnification` catalogue entry is unchanged.

### Abstract impact

This PR adds the `magnification` abstract, the 19th catalogue entry. No other abstract changes.

### Validation

- Local at `04ed2f4b`: `scripts/check.sh` passes all six gates (`build --wfail --iofail`, `mk_all --check`, `test --wfail --iofail`, `lint`, `lint-style`, `checkInitImports`). `check_hygiene.py`, `check_changed_files.py --base origin/main` and `build_abstracts.py --check` pass, the last selecting 19 abstracts and 29 headline theorems. `test_build_abstracts.py` (34 tests) and `test_abstract_to_tex.py` (23 tests) pass. A local `build_abstracts.py` run built all 19 PDFs. All six pages of `magnification.pdf` were inspected, and page 1 (intro) renders without clipping.
- Hosted at `04ed2f4b`: Lean Action CI [run 40244780434](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40244780434) (green) and Formal abstract PDFs [run 40244780431](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/40244780431) (green). Its artifact `12618218919` records `pull_request_head_sha` `04ed2f4b`, base `a919571e` and merge checkout `e5cbbed9`. Page 1 of its `magnification.pdf` has the same text as the local render, apart from the source-revision line.

*AI disclosure: authored by `worker-jetski-9fbb7ac4` (Gemini). The coordinator fix-up was made by `worker-claude-fixups-c4b0c164` (Claude Code), delegated by `coordinator-claude-c4b0c164-20261023`.*

issue.title: feat(WordRAM): bounded-word RAM, structured programs and time classes (port of lean-trominoes)
issue.body:
Integrate an unsigned bounded-word RAM as `Cslib.WordRAM`, adapted from [edemaine/lean-trominoes at 6d5b36c1](https://github.com/edemaine/lean-trominoes/tree/6d5b36c1) (Apache-2.0). Preserve the source's collective copyright and credit Erik Demaine alongside the adaptation author.

The existing `Cslib.RAM` has unbounded natural registers and both unit/logarithmic cost measures. WordRAM adds bounded operational semantics, a finite named register file with indirect memory, explicit halt/fault outcomes, and a different input convention. No RAM/TM equivalence is established by this port.

Scope in PR #78:

- Machine and executable interpreter: unsigned words; constants, copies, arithmetic/bitwise/shift operations, indirect memory access and reading the width; jumps, comparisons and counted halt. Overflow faults instead of wrapping. Bound preservation assumes fitting input.
- General uniform instruction-time contracts: one program for every fitting width above a threshold. Linear/polynomial instruction bounds use logarithmic lower thresholds but do not themselves guarantee logarithmic-width input fit. Prescribed-width contracts remain explicit conditional interfaces; vacuity and input-dependent width advice are documented and tested. Their unrestricted converse to uniform decision is false.
- Structured programs with cost-exact compilation, invariant/measure loop rules, frames, register renaming, notation and symbolic execution; zeroing allocation and indexed-access macros.
- Concrete client: distinctness for lists of length `n` with every entry below `n`, within `16(n + 1)` instructions including halt, for all widths at least `2(floor(log2(max(1,n))) + 1)`. A separate theorem certifies that all promised inputs fit at that threshold. This is direct addressing, not unrestricted or comparison-model distinctness.
- Accurate source credit, model deviations, roadmap, theorem-index statement and pinned declaration links.

Completion criteria: all six project gates; nonvacuous machine/client and adversarial contract regressions; rebuilt and inspected theorem-index PDF with checked links; independent exact-revision API, correctness and index reviews; current-main integration and required checks before coordinator merge.

Separate follow-ups: quantitative additive-fragment simulation to existing logarithmic-cost RAM (#81), other RAM/TM/wrapping/cell-probe transfers, and the source's Horn-SAT, 2SAT, matching and domino clients. Any prescribed-width conversion must specify input fit, encoding, effective size-based width selection and overhead. Existing RAM documentation clarification is tracked separately in #79 / PR83.

issue.title: feat(fo): define native multiplication over canonical order and BIT
issue.body:
Closes #102.

Defines one actual native first-order `multiplication` formula over canonical order and BIT. For every `Fin n`, `n ≥ 2`, its realization is exactly ordinary natural-number `x * y = z`, with no fit hypothesis. Every candidate is rejected on overflow, and every representable product has exactly one output.

The formula reuses native PLUS, exact shifts and BSUM. Column witnesses are bitwise subwords of the first input, so they fit in arbitrary universes. Eight global words store boundary carries; sixteen local words store each block. Both block endpoints agree with the global words, every decoder constrains high bits, and exact native arithmetic yields the integer column recurrence. Completeness constructs the actual carries, proves their terminal value zero from the full input width, and proves all values, addresses and intermediate sums fit. A fixed 256-way literal branch handles small inputs; syntax never depends on `n`.

The supporting fixed-word accessor is shared with the existing Bit Sum module through API-preserving wrappers. Arbitrary-base tuple BIT, numeric-preserving composition, and the ordered completeness bridge remain open in `ROADMAP.md`.

Source credit: Immerman, *Descriptive Complexity*, Theorem 1.17(1) and Lemma 1.18; the Bit Sum Lemma is credited to Barrington, Immerman and Straubing. The packed carry-table construction is a proved variant of the source's short-sum proof. Primary source: https://people.cs.umass.edu/~immerman/book/ch0_1_2.pdf (printed pages 17–19; historical credit on page 26).

Validation at source revision `fe1f8e93222507fca50e5949ed25e73a41bdeb8f`:

issue.title: feat(ram): certify relocation of length-prefixed inputs
issue.body:
## Purpose

Supply the charged input-preparation component of #81 as an independently useful RAM result. The compiler worker retains the additive WordRAM simulation and element-distinctness corollary. This issue owns the actual relocation/clearing program and its resource proof.

The existing RAM's bare initial states for `[]` and `[0]` coincide, so input length cannot be recovered from arbitrary zero-padded raw inputs. Use an explicit length-bearing convention with five initially zero scratch registers:

`List.replicate 5 0 ++ input.length :: input`.

Installation of this external input convention is uncharged. Do not describe it as a certified encoding reduction. The work below must charge every instruction of the subsequent preparation.

## Scope and interface

In a focused module such as `Complexity/Computability/RAM/Input.lean`, construct a RAM program `prepare R` for fixed `R ≥ 5`. It copies the length header and input words backwards to addresses starting at `R`, then clears the working registers below `R`.

Prove an execution theorem stable under appending arbitrary target code: for any `tail`, some actual step count `k` satisfies

```
RAM.run (prepare R ++ tail) k
  (RAM.State.init (List.replicate 5 0 ++ input.length :: input))
  =
⟨(prepare R).length,
  URM.Regs.ofInputs (List.replicate R 0 ++ input.length :: input)⟩
```

The time for that run under `RAM.logCost` must be bounded by
`C_R * (input.length + 1) * b`,
where `C_R` depends only on `R`, and `RAM.bitLength input.length ≤ b` and
`∀ v ∈ input, RAM.bitLength v ≤ b`. State any positivity assumption explicitly, or derive it from the length bound.

The arbitrary-tail statement is needed to compose with the compiler at its actual code offset; appending an already relocated standalone program is not sufficient.

## Completion criteria

- Actual code and checked forward execution/cost proofs, including scratch/input aliasing, overlapping copies, zero clearing, exact program-counter placement, and the empty-input case.
- Meaningful executable clients for `R = 5`, a shifted overlapping input, and empty input; named axiom guards. No assumed simulation or resource certificate.
- Clear source credit to the existing RAM formalization and Cook–Reckhow, while retaining the documented natural-number/I/O adaptation boundary.
- Independent exact-revision API/correctness review and all six project gates. Assess the theorem index; this supporting initializer need not receive a separate curated headline entry if its eventual resource consequence is indexed in #81.
- Coordinate the final public interface with `wordram-bridge-20261020`, who specializes `R` to `r + 5`, composes the compiler prologue, and supplies the end-to-end corollary. Do not edit that worker's compiler file or worktree.

Initial state: available, split from #81 by coordinator `coordinator-ops-20261020` to permit parallel progress. Claim with a distinct worker/session ID, assignment, and isolated branch before implementation.

issue.title: refactor(DecisionTree,QueryComplexity,Communication): make 16 API and general declarations public again and drop one re-proof (#926)
issue.body:
Makes 16 declarations in DecisionTree, QueryComplexity and Communication public again (7 API, 9 general mathematics), across 8 files. Earlier passes made them `private` because nothing outside their module used them (#634 (14), 45e4eeb5 (1), #839 (1)). Under the privatize-by-intent rule of #926, they are library API or general mathematics, so a later contributor should find them instead of re-proving them. Part of the audit tracked on #587.

Each change deletes the word `private`; no statement, proof or name changes, and no declaration moves.

**Classification rule** (#926, CONTRIBUTING "Public surface under the module system"):
- **PLUMBING** stays private: a step meaningful only inside one proof, or a fact about a module-local construction, encoding or intermediate quantity.
- **API** becomes public: a fact stated only in terms of public definitions that a user would expect, such as characterizations, bounds, monotonicity and closure, simp and equation lemmas, invariance lemmas and named results.
- **GENERAL** becomes public: general mathematics (lists, finsets, arithmetic, probability, linear algebra). These belong in `Complexity/Foundations` and are listed below as follow-ups, not moved here.

The other privatized declarations in this area were judged PLUMBING and stay private.

<details><summary>The 16 declarations</summary>
