### #614 Item C6 Checklist Status

- [x] *"Add `Sudan.WeightedDegreeLE`; the raw quantifier has 13 copies (↔ 4 Circuit clients). Give `IsInterpolant` a single weight convention."* — **Done in this PR.** Defined `Cslib.Code.Sudan.WeightedDegreeLE (d D : ℕ) (Q : F[X][Y]) : Prop`, replaced all 13 copies of the raw `(1, d)`-weighted degree quantifier across `SudanInterpolant.lean`, `Sudan.lean`, and `HintDecoding.lean` (the 4 `Circuit` importers of `HintDecoding.lean` use `Sudan.monomials` / `Sudan.interpolantCoeffs` and needed no edits), and moved `Sudan.IsInterpolant` to `SudanInterpolant.lean` parameterized by weight `d : ℕ` (`1 ≤ d`, reparametrizing `Sudan.lean`'s former dimension `k` via `d = k - 1`).
- [x] *"Add `Code.IsAsymptoticallyGood` for code families, and restate Justesen with it; today it is a 4-way conjunction for each `s`."* — **Done in this PR.** Defined `Cslib.Code.IsAsymptoticallyGood` in `Complexity/Foundations/Data/Code/AsymptoticallyGood.lean` (with `[Nontrivial α]` and explicitly bound `R : ℕ` and `Δ : ℕ` so `Δ` cannot elaborate as `⊤ : ℕ∞`), proved `Cslib.Code.isAsymptoticallyGood_justesenCode` in `Justesen.lean` (alongside the explicit per-level theorems `nonempty_justesenCode_index`, `tendsto_card_justesenCode_index`, `le_mul_log_card_justesenCode`, and `card_le_mul_minDist_justesenCode`), and added a checked negative test in `ComplexityTests/Code/M3.lean` showing `¬ IsAsymptoticallyGood (fun s : ℕ => (Set.univ : Set (Fin (s + 2) → Bool)))`.
- [x] *"Build the decoders from the explicit interpolant rather than `Classical.choose`."* — **Done in this PR.** `Cslib.Code.sudan` now factors `Sudan.interpolant α w (k - 1) D` directly instead of calling `Classical.choose` on `exists_isInterpolant` (`HintDecoding.hintDecode` already used `Sudan.interpolant`; `BerlekampWelch.berlekampWelch` solves an inhomogeneous monic constraint `E.Monic ∧ E.natDegree = e` rather than a homogeneous kernel system `A *ᵥ v = 0`, so it is outside the `Sudan.interpolant` / `kernelVec` scope). Because `isInterpolant_interpolant` requires positive weight `1 ≤ d`, completeness (`mem_sudan_iff` and `mem_sudan_iff_of_lt`) now takes `2 ≤ k` (so `1 ≤ k - 1`), while soundness (`degree_lt_and_lt_card_of_mem_sudan`) and the list-size bound (`card_sudan_mul_le`) hold for all `k`.
- [x] *"Name the Hadamard result `minDist_range_hadamardCode`."* — **Already on `main`** (`Cslib.BitString.minDist_range_hadamardCode`, `Complexity/Foundations/Data/Code/Hadamard.lean`).

Part of #614 (completes Item C6).

### Framework friction

Replacing 13 repeated copies of `∀ j ≤ Q.natDegree, Q.coeff j ≠ 0 → (Q.coeff j).natDegree + d * j ≤ D` with `Sudan.WeightedDegreeLE d D Q` and moving `Sudan.IsInterpolant` into `SudanInterpolant.lean` under a single weight convention `d` removes the split `(k : ℕ)` vs `(d : ℕ)` convention between the two Sudan modules. Building `Code.sudan` directly from `Sudan.interpolant` eliminates the `Classical.choose` indirection and aligns full list decoding with `HintDecoding.hintDecode`.

issue.title: chore(scripts): follow-ups from #374 review (worktree remote tracking, pin diagnostics, full-name matching)
issue.body:
Closes #388

## Summary

These are the follow-ups from the independent review of #374 (reviewer `6f9639fa`, at `1f38e7c1`). Each item in #388 is handled as follows.

1. **`worktree.sh create` and remote-only branches (safety).** Before, when a branch existed only on `origin` (the usual takeover case), `create` silently made a fresh branch from `origin/main`. Now it fetches `origin/<branch>` first, so a branch pushed after the local clone is still found. If the branch exists on `origin` but not locally, `create` makes the local branch tracking it (`git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> origin/<branch>`). If you pass a `base_ref` for such a branch, it refuses with a hint, because that would discard the pushed work. `--force-reset` overrides the refusal. Without a `base_ref`, `--force-reset` still tracks `origin/<branch>`. If the fetch fails, a local `origin/<branch>` ref is used if present, even if it is stale. Brand-new branches are now created with `--no-track`. Before, they silently tracked `origin/main`, so a plain `git push` could target the base branch.
2. **`pin_paper_links.py --pin` diagnostics.** A link that cannot be resolved no longer produces a traceback. The error names the `.tex` file, the Lean path, the revision and the failing declaration, and lists any declarations that share its short name. It adds a hint that the declaration may have been moved or renamed. It exits with status 1 and does not modify any `.tex` file (writes were already all-or-nothing).
3. **Full-name matching.** `--check` and `--pin` now require the link name to equal the full declaration name (namespace included); the old suffix match is gone. On current `main`, all 1468 links already use full names, so no link changes.
4. **`main.tex` exclusion.** Before, `main.tex` was skipped entirely. Now it is scanned like every other file under `paper/`. Only the two lines that define the `\decl` and `\declat` macros are skipped; links inside other user macros are still checked.
5. **`--copy-cslib` hard-links the other packages.** This is now documented, and there is a new `--copy-packages` flag (for `create` and `seed`) that copies every package. It is mutually exclusive with `--copy-cslib`.
6. **`--pin` SHA validation.** `--pin` now requires a full 40-character lowercase SHA that names a commit and is an ancestor of `HEAD`.
7. **CI (optional item).** The **Theorem index PDF** workflow now runs `pin_paper_links.py --check` with `fetch-depth: 0`. It also triggers on changes to `scripts/pin_paper_links.py` and `scripts/proof_lengths.py`. That workflow is the right place: pinned links name immutable commits, so the result can only change when `paper/` or the checker changes. Locally, every pinned SHA on `main` is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so they are all reachable in a full-history checkout.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` is updated to describe the takeover behaviour of `worktree.sh`, the full-name requirement and the `--pin` SHA rule.

### Changes after the coordinator review of `4d8eacae` (reviewer `daa3f64f`), in `99c20e2c`
- **Blocking:** the CI `--check` step ran before `build_paper.py` and wrote `scripts/__pycache__`, so `build_paper.py` recorded `source_dirty: true`. The step now runs `python3 -B`, and `.gitignore` ignores `__pycache__/`. Re-run [39844083208](https://github.com/cslib-community/complexitylib/actions/runs/39844083208), artifact `12453813447`, has `provenance.json` with `source_dirty: false` (merge revision `7e35ddc8`, PR head `99c20e2c`).
- **Non-blocking 1:** `replace_declat`/`replace_decl` now look up macro-definition lines in the string their own regex pass matched (`m.string`), not in the original content.
- **Non-blocking 2:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` now says to pin only to commits that land on `main` unchanged, and to re-pin to the merged commit after a squash or rebase merge.
- **Optional 3:** `--copy-packages` and `--copy-cslib` use `cp -a`, which preserves mtimes.

## Tests

- New `scripts/test_worktree.py`, which runs against throwaway git repos with a bare `origin`, covers item 1:
  - a remote-only branch is tracked;
  - a branch pushed after the clone is fetched and tracked;
  - a `base_ref` given for a remote-only branch is refused, and no branch is created;
  - a new branch starts from `origin/main` with no upstream;
  - conflicting copy flags are refused.
  
  All 5 tests fail against the old script.
- `scripts/test_pin_paper_links.py`, new tests:
  - **Item 2:** `main(["--pin", …])` on a stale link reports the `.tex` file, the Lean path, `not found` and the hint, prints no traceback, and leaves the files unchanged.
  - **Item 6:** an abbreviated SHA, an unknown SHA and a non-ancestor SHA are each rejected without writing anything; pinning to an ancestor full SHA succeeds.
  - **Item 3:** a short-name link fails `--check` and the error names the full name.
  - **Item 4:** links in `main.tex` are checked, including links inside a user `\newcommand` macro.

## Validation

On `99c20e2c` (the same results also held on `4d8eacae`):
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`: 37 tests OK.
- `python3 scripts/pin_paper_links.py --check`: verified 1468 declaration links (strict full-name matching, `main.tex` included).
- `python3 scripts/check_docs.py --config-only`: consistent. The full `check_docs.py` needs built documentation (`index.html`), and it fails the same way on `main`.
- `bash -n scripts/worktree.sh`: OK.
- No Lean files changed, so the Lean gates are unaffected; CI runs them.

## Theorem index assessment

**No impact.** No Lean declarations or paper prose change. Only the link checker becomes stricter, and every existing link passes it.

## Review record

- Independent review `995e8e06` (fresh AI review subagent that did not author these changes):
  - **`ec70a54f`: APPROVE**, no blocking findings. It ran the unit tests and `--check`, confirmed that the new worktree tests fail against the old script, confirmed that every pinned SHA is an ancestor of `main`, and checked edge cases by hand in throwaway repos (`--force-reset`, the existing-local-branch path, conflicting `seed` flags, a deleted remote branch). Non-blocking items 1–4 were fixed in `4d8eacae`: documenting `--force-reset` without `base_ref`, documenting the stale/deleted remote-ref fallback, narrowing the macro-line skip to `\decl`/`\declat`, and a PEP 8 blank line.
  - **Re-review of `ec70a54f..4d8eacae`: APPROVE**, no blocking findings.
  - **Remaining notes, not acted on:**
    - No test exercises the positive skip of the `\decl`/`\declat` definition lines. Those lines never match the link regexes anyway, so the skip is defensive only; not added.
    - If the project ever switches to rebase or squash merges and deletes PR branches, `\declat` SHAs pinned to PR-branch commits would become unreachable for the CI `--check`. This is fine under the current merge-commit policy.
    - `--copy-packages` copying and the `seed` flag parsing are not unit-tested; both were checked by hand.

## AI assistance disclosure

Written with AI assistance by Jetski worker `worker-jetski-8a8d8213`. The independent review was done by a separate AI review subagent, listed above. No human editorial review is implied.

   - Define multi-output ordered-syntax circuit counting (`Signature.lineCount`, `Signature.orderedBudget`, `Circuit.functionsAtMost`, `Circuit.mem_functionsAtMost_iff`, `Circuit.card_functionsAtMost_le`, `Circuit.exists_hard_in_family`) and prove the De Morgan specialization (`boolean_lineCount_le`, `boolean_orderedBudget_le`, `boolean_orderedBudget_le_pow`, `square_le_exponential`, `lowerBudget`, `lowerBudget_description_exponent`, `lowerBudget_wire_bound`).

   - Define `easyCounterPowers` and prove `easyCounterPowers_card_le`, `lowerBudget_description_margin`, and `almost_every_counter_power` (`(easyCounterPowers k (lowerBudget k)).card * 2 ^ (2 ^ (k - 1)) ≤ ModulusCounter.period k`).

3. **`Complexity/Computability/Circuit/Boolean/Iteration/PrimeCycles.lean`**:

4. **`ComplexityTests/Iteration/HardPowers.lean`**:
   - Add nonvacuous tests and `#print axioms` guards for all headline theorems.
   - Update `ROADMAP.md` and `paper/sections/iteration.tex` (§14).
